EDCS-00380732.summary: This is a personal name, likely the owner of the object or the author of the inscription.

EDCS-00380736.summary: This is a personal name, likely the owner of the object or the author of the inscription, with a possible uncertain ending.

EDCS-00380737.summary: This is a personal name, likely the owner of the object or the author of the inscription.

EDCS-00380747.summary: This is a personal name, likely the owner of the object or the author of the inscription.

EDCS-00380755.summary: This is a personal name, likely the owner of the object or the author of the inscription.

EDCS-00380765.summary: This inscription likely records a name, possibly 'Maddurus', possibly referring to a person or a place.

EDCS-00380774.text_edition: \n Manliani f(orma) ad Gantunas novas Alfius fecit\n
EDCS-00380774.translation: Alfius made [this] at the new Gantunas, Manliana's property.
EDCS-00380774.summary: This inscription records that Alfius built something at a location called 'Gantunas novas', possibly on Manliana's land.

EDCS-00380778.text_edition: \n Quintus Calpurnius Luci filius Lemonia Festus \n
EDCS-00380778.translation: Quintus Calpurnius Festus, son of Lucius, of the Lemonia tribe.
EDCS-00380778.summary: This inscription records the full name and tribal affiliation of Quintus Calpurnius Festus.

EDCS-00380783.text_edition: \n Idibus Septembribus Macrino et Celso consulibus\n
EDCS-00380783.translation: On the Ides of September, in the consulship of Macrinus and Celsus.
EDCS-00380783.summary: This inscription records a date specified by the Roman Ides of September and the consuls Macrinus and Celsus.

EDCS-03000659.summary: This inscription fragment likely refers to the possessive form of a personal name, 'Felicio'.

EDCS-03000665.text_edition: \n Venulanto Nonio militi legionis XIII geminae centuria Socci\n
EDCS-03000665.translation: To Venulantus Nonius, a soldier of the Thirteenth Legion Gemina, in the century of Soccius.
EDCS-03000665.summary: This inscription records a military dedication to a soldier of the Thirteenth Legion, dating to the period when this legion existed.

EDCS-03000666.text_edition: \n Dabis Lucio Finitio Dubitato centuria Taciti\n
EDCS-03000666.translation: To Dabis Lucius Finitius Dubitatus, in the century of Tacitus.
EDCS-03000666.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Finitius Dubitatus, likely a soldier, indicating his service in the century of Tacitus.

EDCS-03000667.translation: To Gaius Seius Raeticus, in the century of Pontius.
EDCS-03000667.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument or marks a grave for Gaius Seius Raeticus, serving in the century of Pontius.

EDCS-03000668.text_edition: \n Sornio Secundo centuria is aut Sornio Firmo centuria Proculi dabis\n
EDCS-03000668.translation: You will give to Sornius Secundus in the century of Sornius Firmus, in the century of Proculus.
EDCS-03000668.summary: This inscription seems to be a request or a statement regarding two individuals, Sornius Secundus and Sornius Firmus, and their respective centuries, possibly related to a debt or legal matter.

EDCS-03000669.text_edition: \n Tullo centuria Gai quaeris in quas vias curas agam quidquid egi Marci curae attributum tum faustus Tullus qui de amoribus ignoras VS\n
EDCS-03000669.translation: Tullus, in the century of Gaius, you ask what concerns I should take up, whatever I have done has been attributed to Marcus' concerns; then, Faustus Tullus, you who do not know of love, [something].
EDCS-03000669.summary: This enigmatic inscription appears to be a personal or philosophical message, possibly from a soldier named Tullus, discussing responsibilities and knowledge of love.

EDCS-03000670.summary: This fragment appears to be a dedication or memorial to a physician named Gaius.

EDCS-03000673.text_edition: \n dabis a Veturio Melo o amico \n
EDCS-03000673.translation: You will give to Veturia Mela, from a friend.
EDCS-03000673.summary: This inscription is a short message, possibly a request or a dedication, to Veturia Mela, sent by a friend.

EDCS-03000676.text_edition: \n Tiberi Claudi Verati diamesus sic ad claritatem\n
EDCS-03000676.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Veratus, the diamesus, so that he may have clarity.
EDCS-03000676.summary: This inscription dedicates something to Tiberius Claudius Veratus, referring to him as a 'diamesus,' possibly a medical term or a title, seeking clarity.

EDCS-03000682.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Eucerilla placed this for Bellinius Rhethicus.
EDCS-03000682.summary: This is a funerary inscription (Dis Manibus) recording that Eucerilla erected this monument for her deceased husband, Bellinius Rhethicus.

EDCS-03000686.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucilius Avento beneficiarius consularis ex iussu posuit Commodo Augusto III consule\n
EDCS-03000686.translation: In honor of the divine house. To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Lucilius Avento, beneficiary of a consular official, placed this by order, when Commodus Augustus was consul for the third time.
EDCS-03000686.summary: This is a public dedication honoring the emperor and the gods, placed by a military official named Lucilius Avento during the third consulship of Commodus.

EDCS-03000687.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Genio loci Caius Secundinius Dignus beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Secundinius Dignus beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-03000687.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, to the Genius of the place, Gaius Secundinius Dignus, a beneficiarius consularis, for himself and his family, happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-03000687.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Gaius Secundinius Dignus to Jupiter, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place.

EDCS-03000690.text_edition: \n II Lucius Primius Cavio miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis VII Kalendas Ianuarias Geta II et Plautiano consulibus\n
EDCS-03000690.translation: Lucius Primius Cavio, soldier of the XXII Primigenia pious faithful legion, a beneficiarius consularis, on the 7th day before the Kalends of January, when Geta II and Plautianus were consuls.
EDCS-03000690.summary: This inscription records a military appointment or service date of Lucius Primius Cavio, a soldier in the XXII Primigenia legion, during the consulship of Geta II and Plautianus.

EDCS-03000692.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci et Marti Consservatori Gaius Carantius Severianus pro se et suis beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito dominis nostris Severi sic III et Antonino consulibus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Iarionus\n
EDCS-03000692.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place and Mars the Preserver, Gaius Carantius Severianus, a beneficiarius consularis, for himself and his family, happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow, to our lords Severus III and Antoninus consuls, soldier of the XXII Primigenia pious faithful legion, Iarionus.
EDCS-03000692.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Gaius Carantius Severianus, a soldier in the XXII Primigenia legion, in honor of the imperial family and various deities during the consulship of Severus III and Antoninus.

EDCS-03000693.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Caius Iulius Hibernalis beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-03000693.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, Gaius Julius Hibernalis, a beneficiarius consularis, for himself and his family, deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-03000693.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Gaius Julius Hibernalis to Jupiter, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place.

EDCS-03000694.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci dis deabusque omnibus Caius Covventinius \n
EDCS-03000694.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the place, and to all the gods and goddesses, Gaius Covventinius.
EDCS-03000694.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Covventinius to Jupiter, the Genius of the place, and all the gods and goddesses.

EDCS-03000695.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Secundius Secundinus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis pro salute sua et suorum Fabiano et Muciano consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-03000695.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, Secundius Secundinus, soldier of the XXII Primigenia pious faithful legion, a beneficiarius consularis, for his safety and that of his family, when Fabianus and Mucianus were consuls, happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-03000695.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Secundius Secundinus, a soldier in the XXII Primigenia legion, for his and his family's well-being during the consulship of Fabianus and Mucianus.

EDCS-03000696.text_edition: \n dis deabusque omnibus et Genio loci Titus Flavius Amandus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis Idibus Iuliis Geta II et Plautiano II connsulibus\n
EDCS-03000696.translation: To all the gods and goddesses and to the Genius of the place, Titus Flavius Amandus, soldier of the XXII Primigenia pious faithful legion, a beneficiarius consularis, on the Ides of July, when Geta II and Plautianus II were consuls.
EDCS-03000696.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Titus Flavius Amandus, a soldier in the XXII Primigenia legion, to all deities and the Genius of the place during the consulship of Geta II and Plautianus II.

EDCS-03000698.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo salutique Auggustorum nnostrorum Iunoni Reginae Genio loci Lucius Titianius Titus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis egit stationes duas Victorino et Proculo consulibus IX Idibus Ianuariis insequente Muciano consule\n
EDCS-03000698.translation: In honor of the divine house and for the health of our Emperors, to Juno Regina, the Genius of the place, Lucius Titianius Titus, soldier of the XXII Primigenia pious faithful legion, a beneficiarius consularis, performed two stations when Victorinus and Proculus were consuls, on the 9th day before the Ides of January, with Mucianus as the following consul.
EDCS-03000698.summary: This inscription records the performance of duties by Lucius Titianius Titus, a soldier in the XXII Primigenia legion, in honor of the imperial family and for the health of the emperors during the consulship of Victorinus and Proculus.

EDCS-03000704.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Caius Iulius Petunnatius beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-03000704.translation: Sacred to Mercury, Gaius Julius Petunnatius, a beneficiarius consularis, happily and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-03000704.summary: This inscription records a vow made by Gaius Julius Petunnatius to the god Mercury.

EDCS-03000708.text_edition: \n Gnaeus Horatinius Gnaei libertus Araricus Flavia Finita\n
EDCS-03000708.translation: Gnaeus Horatinius Araricus, son of Gnaeus, and Flavia Finita.
EDCS-03000708.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative inscription mentioning Gnaeus Horatinius Araricus and Flavia Finita.

EDCS-03000710.text_edition: \n Garum scombri flos aannorum Claudi Valeri Caldoni Domestici Publi Pomponi Secundi legati Augusti\n
EDCS-03000710.translation: The flower of garum from mackerel, from the years of Claudius Valerius Caldon Domesticus, legate of Publius Pomponius Secundus Augusti.
EDCS-03000710.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely related to the production or sale of garum by Claudius Valerius Caldon Domesticus, a legate under Publius Pomponius Secundus.

EDCS-03000712.text_edition: \n centuria Cai Valeri Primi Cai Valeri Primi centuria Cai Valeri Primi Caius Ranius Cai Valeri Primi\n
EDCS-03000712.translation: Century of Gaius Valerius Primus, century of Gaius Valerius Primus, century of Gaius Valerius Primus, Gaius Ranius, century of Gaius Valerius Primus.
EDCS-03000712.summary: This inscription seems to be a list or record of military units or land divisions associated with Gaius Valerius Primus and Gaius Ranius.

EDCS-03000713.translation: Century of Gaius Valerius Primus, Gaius Ranius, century of Gaius Valerius Primus.
EDCS-03000713.summary: This fragmentary inscription records names associated with military centuries, likely indicating land ownership or administrative divisions related to Gaius Valerius Primus and Gaius Ranius.

EDCS-03300699.text_edition: \n Lagona Nicomedes qui illam emeruit TI\n
EDCS-03300699.summary: This inscription records Nicomedes acquiring a slave woman named Lagona.

EDCS-03300707.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide a definitive summary, but the numbers and letters may refer to military units or quantities.

EDCS-03300710.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci et Marco Aurelio Antonino Auggustis et Getae Caesari balneum cohortis I Germanorum vetustate dilabsum a solo restitutum ex praecepto Caesoni Rufiniani legati Auggustorum pro praetore cura agente Iulio Clodiano tribuno cohortis supra scriptae\n
EDCS-03300710.translation: During the reigns of Emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, and Geta Caesar, the bath of the first cohort of Germans, which had fallen into ruin from age, was restored from the ground up by order of Caesonius Rufinianus, legate of the Augusti, pro-praetor, under the care of Julius Clodianus, tribune of the aforementioned cohort.
EDCS-03300710.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a bathhouse for the first cohort of Germans, ordered by the legate Caesonius Rufinianus during the joint reign of Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta.

EDCS-03300711.text_edition: \n Titus Cirrius Deciminus veteranus domo Arelate vivos sic fecit\n
EDCS-03300711.translation: Titus Cirrius Deciminus, a veteran from Arelate, made this while alive.
EDCS-03300711.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Cirrius Deciminus, a veteran from Arles, who dedicated his own tomb during his lifetime.

EDCS-03300712.text_edition: \n Caius Licinius Luci filius Pomptina Dertona annorum XXX stipendiorum XVII hic situs est heres ex testamento posuit\n
EDCS-03300712.translation: Gaius Licinius, son of Lucius, of the Pomptina tribe, from Dertona, aged 30, with 17 years of service, lies here; his heir placed this according to his will.
EDCS-03300712.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Licinius, a soldier from Dertona, detailing his age, service length, and that his tomb was erected by his heir.

EDCS-03300713.text_edition: \n Mercator Tabi filius cives Remus annorum L Pusina uxor annorum XL Dercoieda filia annorum XII hic siti sunt\n
EDCS-03300713.translation: Mercator, son of Tabius, a citizen of Remus, aged 50, his wife Pusina, aged 40, and their daughter Dercoieda, aged 12, lie here.
EDCS-03300713.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a family: Mercator, his wife Pusina, and daughter Dercoieda, likely from the area of Remus.

EDCS-03300716.summary: This inscription, though brief, likely refers to a group of soldiers or people identified as 'Hastici' and 'Numidians'.

EDCS-03700629.text_edition: \n Iulio Decimi filio Cornelia IIvirum flamini Augusti Capitoni\n
EDCS-03700629.translation: To Iulius, son of Decimus, of the Cornelia tribe, for Capitōnus, former *duumvir* and *flamen Augusti*.
EDCS-03700629.summary: This is a funerary or honorary inscription for Iulius Capitōnus, who held significant local magistracies.

EDCS-03700631.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carinus Pius Felix Augustus leugas XX\n
EDCS-03700631.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carinus Pius Felix Augustus, 20 *leugae*.
EDCS-03700631.summary: This inscription likely marks a distance of 20 *leugae* (Roman miles) from a certain point, possibly indicating the extent of an imperial road or territory under Carinus.

EDCS-03700633.translation: In honor of the divine house. To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Acceptius Severinus, veteran, [offers this].
EDCS-03700633.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, likely by a veteran named Acceptius Severinus, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-03700634.translation: In honor of the divine house. Martius dedicated [this] to the goddess Juno.
EDCS-03700634.summary: A dedication to Juno, made by Martius in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-04900730.translation: Flaviusviusarpus took care to have this made.
EDCS-04900730.summary: This is a dedication or construction notice, with Flaviusviusarpus being the person responsible for its creation.

EDCS-04900733.text_edition: \n Asinio Celere Nonio consulibus XI Kalendas Augustas supra scriptus Clua eques Raetorum turma Albi Pudentis accepi |(denarios) L et stipendii proximi |(denarios) LXXV\n
EDCS-04900733.translation: In the consulship of Asinius Celer and Nonius (on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August), the above-named Clua, an *eques* from Raetia, troop of Albus Pudentis, received 50 denarii and 75 denarii of the next stipend.
EDCS-04900733.summary: A financial record detailing a payment of denarii received by Clua, an *eques* from Raetia, during the consulship of Asinius Celer and Nonius.

EDCS-04900735.text_edition: \n Apollini Augusto sacrum Caius Caelius Tertius ex voto\n
EDCS-04900735.translation: Sacred to Apollo Augustus. Caius Caelius Tertius, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-04900735.summary: This is a votive dedication to Apollo Augustus, made by Caius Caelius Tertius.

EDCS-04900736.summary: This is a simple funerary or identification marker for Caius Caecilius Septumus.

EDCS-04900741.text_edition: \n Genio Martis Cenabetii Gaius Amonius Quintus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-04900741.translation: To the Genius of Mars Cenabetius, Gaius Amonius Quintus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-04900741.summary: A votive inscription by Gaius Amonius Quintus to the Genius of Mars Cenabetius.

EDCS-04900742.text_edition: \n Sevvo Secconis Publius Attius Primulus Aulus \n
EDCS-04900742.translation: Sevvo Secconis. Publius Attius Primulus, Aulus [dedicated this/was honored].
EDCS-04900742.summary: This inscription possibly records a dedication or is a funerary marker involving individuals named Sevvo Secconis, Publius Attius Primulus, and Aulus.

EDCS-04900743.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Valerius Quartus veteranus ex cohorte II Hispanorum pro salute sua et suorum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-04900743.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Valerius Quartus, a veteran from the 2nd cohort of Spaniards, paid his vow for his own safety and that of his family, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-04900743.summary: A vow paid by a veteran to Jupiter Optimus Maximus for his well-being and that of his family.

EDCS-04900744.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Quinciana Paterna votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-04900744.translation: Quinciana Paterna paid her vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-04900744.summary: A vow paid by Quinciana Paterna to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina.

EDCS-04900746.translation: Of the century of Rufinus, son of Sacra.
EDCS-04900746.summary: An indication of property belonging to a century named after Rufinus, son of Sacra.

EDCS-04900747.translation: From the troop of Ursinius Priscus, a cavalryman.
EDCS-04900747.summary: Identifies a cavalryman, Ursinius Priscus, and his troop.

EDCS-04900750.translation: Titus, from the century of Vitrius.
EDCS-04900750.summary: Identifies Titus and his century, that of Vitrius.

EDCS-04900751.translation: Under Emperor Commodus Augustus, from the 1st cohort of the Bituriges, troop of Veroniani(?), [named] A[---]isus.
EDCS-04900751.summary: Records military personnel from the 1st cohort of Bituriges, troop of Veroniani, under Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-04900752.translation: Under Emperor Commodus Augustus, from the 1st cohort of the Bituriges, century of Gaius [---]nsanus, son of Sattonis.
EDCS-04900752.summary: Records military personnel from the 1st cohort of Bituriges, century of Gaius [---]nsanus, under Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-04900753.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest and the Genius of the place, Arcius Severus, soldier of the 22nd legion Pia Fidelis, a deputy to the governor, and Vervicia Candida, his wife, for the safety of themselves and of Arcius Severinus, his father, and his family, on the Ides of July in the consulship of Apro and Maximo.
EDCS-04900753.summary: A dedication by Arcius Severus and his wife Vervicia Candida to Jupiter and the Genius loci, for their well-being and that of his father, during the consulship of Apro and Maximo.

EDCS-05000639.text_edition: \n Mars Gradive pater hanc patriam civesque inclute bellator T imperio monitus merito Sextus Tetricius donum dedit\n
EDCS-05000639.translation: Father Mars Gradivus, renowned warrior, prompted by your command, Sextus Tetricius deservedly gave this gift to this homeland and its citizens.
EDCS-05000639.summary: A dedication by Sextus Tetricius to Mars Gradivus for the homeland and its citizens.

EDCS-05000640.text_edition: \n Livillae deae sacrum Genialis Flavi Erotis libertus\n
EDCS-05000640.translation: Sacred to the goddess Livilla, from Genialis, freedman of Flavius Erotis.
EDCS-05000640.summary: A dedication to the goddess Livilla by Genialis, a freedman.

EDCS-05000641.text_edition: \n Silvano et Neptuno Aprilis Cai Camilli Paterni servus\n
EDCS-05000641.translation: To Silvanus and Neptune, Aprilis, slave of Caius Camillus Paternus.
EDCS-05000641.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the gods Silvanus and Neptune by Aprilis, a slave of Caius Camillus Paternus.

EDCS-05000647.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Attio Severo Severianus filius\n
EDCS-05000647.translation: To the Divine Manes, Severianus, son of Marcus Attius Severus.
EDCS-05000647.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Divine Manes for Marcus Attius Severus by his son Severianus.

EDCS-05000648.text_edition: \n Quadrubiis sic Valeria Secundina votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-05000648.translation: Valeria Secundina willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow at the crossroads.
EDCS-05000648.summary: This inscription records Valeria Secundina fulfilling a vow at a crossroads.

EDCS-05000649.text_edition: \n Dis Inferis Manibus Atto piisimis patribus\n
EDCS-05000649.translation: To the Underworld Gods, the Manes, for the most dutiful fathers, Atto.
EDCS-05000649.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Underworld Gods and Manes by Atto for his fathers.

EDCS-05000650.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae anianus\n
EDCS-05000650.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, Anianus.
EDCS-05000650.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Anianus.

EDCS-05000652.text_edition: \n |Centuria Farronis Praesentis Caius Vilius M VIIX\n
EDCS-05000652.translation: From the century of Farro Praesens, Gaius Vilius [erected this for?] 78 miles.
EDCS-05000652.summary: This inscription appears to relate to a centuria and a distance marker, possibly erected by Gaius Vilius.

EDCS-05000654.text_edition: \n CRO Cai Valeri Iucundi diazmyrnes ad aspritudinem CCC EG\n
EDCS-05000654.translation: CRO. Gaius Valerius Iucundus [presented?] diazmyrnes for roughness, 300 units.
EDCS-05000654.summary: This inscription seems to record a transaction or offering by Gaius Valerius Iucundus related to diazmyrnes.

EDCS-05000660.summary: This inscription is a dedication or dedication of property by Lucius G. I. V. Argynnus.

EDCS-05200514.text_edition: \n rianius Celer ex voto posuit libens merito\n
EDCS-05200514.translation: Aterianus Celer willingly and deservedly set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-05200514.summary: This inscription records Aterianus Celer fulfilling a vow by setting up a monument.

EDCS-05200516.text_edition: \n Caius Valerius Leucadius decurio civium Romanorum Mogontiaci collegis donum dedit\n
EDCS-05200516.translation: Gaius Valerius Leucadius, decurion of the Roman citizens at Mogontiacum, gave this gift to his colleagues.
EDCS-05200516.summary: This inscription records Gaius Valerius Leucadius, a decurion at Mogontiacum, giving a gift to his colleagues in a civic or collegial context.

EDCS-05200517.text_edition: \n arius Luci filius inna miles legionis annrum L stipendiorum hic situs est ]\n
EDCS-05200517.translation: Arius, son of Lucius, a soldier of the legion, aged 50 years, with 25 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-05200517.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Arius, a soldier of a Roman legion, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-05200518.text_edition: \n Caius Cai filius nus miles legionis \n
EDCS-05200518.translation: Caius, son of Caius, a soldier of the legion.
EDCS-05200518.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Caius, son of Caius, as a soldier of a Roman legion.

EDCS-05200519.text_edition: \n Cai Crispi Genialis diabsoricum sic ad claritatem Cai Crispi Genialis chelidonium ad caliginem\n
EDCS-05200519.translation: Caius Crispius Genialis, a diasmyrin (scent/perfume) for brightness, Caius Crispius Genialis, a chelidonium for darkness.
EDCS-05200519.summary: This inscription seems to record the dedication of perfumed substances or unguents by Caius Crispius Genialis, possibly in a religious or ritual context.

EDCS-05200522.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Apollini Maiorius Iuvenis votum solvit laetus libens merito Victorino et Sancto [consulibus] XVI Kalendas Iulias posuit\n
EDCS-05200522.translation: In honor of the divine house, Maiorius Iuvenis happily, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Apollo, and placed this [this dedication] in the consulship of Victorinus and Sanctus on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of July.
EDCS-05200522.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo by Maiorius Iuvenis in honor of the imperial family, likely dating to the late 2nd or 3rd century CE based on the consul names.

EDCS-05200527.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Bellius Plautus beneficiarius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-05200527.translation: Bellius Plautus, a beneficiary, happily, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-05200527.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Bellius Plautus, who held a position as a beneficiary, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05200528.text_edition: \n Claudius Paternus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae et Iulia Emerita uxor ambo ex nnia superiore libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-05200528.translation: Claudius Paternus, a centurion of the Legio VIII Augusta, and Iulia Emerita, his wife, both from upper [Italy?], willingly, happily, and deservedly [dedicated this].
EDCS-05200528.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial made by Claudius Paternus, a centurion of Legio VIII Augusta, and his wife Iulia Emerita, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200529.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Victoriae Augustae Marcus Ianuarinius Secundinus haruspex et Romulus filius donum dederunt\n
EDCS-05200529.translation: In honor of the divine house, Victoria Augusta, Marcus Ianuarinius Secundinus, a haruspex, and his son Romulus, gave this gift.
EDCS-05200529.summary: This inscription records a gift dedicated to Victoria Augusta in honor of the imperial family by Marcus Ianuarinius Secundinus, a diviner, and his son.

EDCS-05200530.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae hoc Eponae signum Publius Iunius Floridus votum libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-05200530.translation: In honor of the divine house, Publius Iunius Floridus willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled his vow with this statue of Epona.
EDCS-05200530.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Epona in honor of the imperial family by Publius Iunius Floridus.

EDCS-06100454.text_edition: \n Cai Iuli Castrensis diasmyrines sic Cai Iuli Castrensis nardinum Cai Iuli Castrensis diapsporicum sic Cai Iuli Castrensis euuodes VQVOQVE S Cai Iuli Castrensis\n
EDCS-06100454.translation: Caius Iulius Castrensis, diasmyrin (scent/perfume) for brightness, Caius Iulius Castrensis, nardinum, Caius Iulius Castrensis, diapsporicum for brightness, Caius Iulius Castrensis, euuodes VQVOQVE S Caius Iulius Castrensis.
EDCS-06100454.summary: This inscription lists various perfumed substances or unguents associated with Caius Iulius Castrensis, possibly related to trade or personal use.

EDCS-06100459.translation: To the Domestic Goddesses, Arertonius Atticus [dedicated this].
EDCS-06100459.summary: This is an altar inscription dedicated to the Domestic Goddesses by Arertonius Atticus, likely a private devotion from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-06100460.text_edition: \n in? h(onorem) domus divinae BE simus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-06100460.translation: In honor of the divine house, we have fulfilled our vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-06100460.summary: A dedication honoring the imperial family, likely erected by a group or household, expressing gratitude for divine favor.

EDCS-07000793.summary: This inscription likely records the name and origin of Gaius Coelius Venustus, possibly as part of a funerary monument or a personal dedication.

EDCS-07400579.text_edition: \n Sulpicia Vepa mater et Sulpicia Pervinca filia de suo testamento antas in solo Caesaris posuerunt Fusciano et Silano II consulibus III Kalendas Apriles libentes laetae merito\n
EDCS-07400579.translation: Sulpicia Vepa, mother, and Sulpicia Pervinca, daughter, placed the ants from their own property in Caesar's soil, in the consulship of Fuscianus and Silanus, three days before the Kalends of April, willingly and joyfully, as deserved.
EDCS-07400579.summary: A funerary inscription recording the placement of funerary monuments ('antas') by a mother and daughter in imperial land, dated to the consulship of Fuscianus and Silanus.

EDCS-07400583.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Magnentius Augustus Lucubrio pondo III\n
EDCS-07400583.summary: This inscription records a weight of 3 pounds associated with Emperor Magnentius, possibly related to a supply or a votive offering.

EDCS-07600326.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Flavio Valerio Constantino Pio nobilissimo Caesari divi Constanti Pii Augusti filio\n
EDCS-07600326.translation: To Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the Pious, most noble Caesar, son of the deified Constantius Pius Augustus.
EDCS-07600326.summary: A dedication to Emperor Constantine, honoring his titles and divine lineage, likely part of a larger monument.

EDCS-07600327.text_edition: \n Fortunae Brittones Elantienses balineum vetustate conlabsum sic adiecta concha et camaris opere figlino restitutis item vasis novis positis iubente Calpurnio Agricola legato Augusti pro praetore curam agente Veranio Saturnino |(centurione) legionis VIII Augustae votum solverunt Tertullo et Sacerdote consulibus\n
EDCS-07600327.translation: To Fortuna, the Brittones Elantienses restored the bathhouse, which had collapsed with age, with an added shell and vaulted brickwork, and also with new vessels, by order of Calpurnius Agricola, the emperor's legate with praetorian power, with Veranius Saturninus, centurion of the Eighth Augustan Legion, overseeing the work; they fulfilled their vow in the consulship of Tertullus and Sacerdos.
EDCS-07600327.summary: A public works inscription detailing the restoration of a bathhouse by the Brittones Elantienses, commissioned by Governor Calpurnius Agricola and overseen by Centurion Veranius Saturninus, dated to the consulship of Tertullus and Sacerdos.

EDCS-07600328.text_edition: \n Genio praepositorum et Genio conlegiis secutorum eorum sub cura Verani Saturnini |(centurionis) legionis VIII Augustae \n
EDCS-07600328.translation: To the Genius of the overseers and to the Genius of their collegia, under the supervision of Veranius Saturninus, centurion of the Eighth Augustan Legion.
EDCS-07600328.summary: A dedication to the guardian spirits ('genii') of officials and their associations, overseen by Centurion Veranius Saturninus.

EDCS-07600329.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Victor Abascanti Augusti dispensatoris vicarius dono dedit\n
EDCS-07600329.translation: The god Unconquered, Victor, deputy of Abascanti, steward of Augustus, gave as a gift.
EDCS-07600329.summary: A dedication to the Unconquered God, presented by Victor, a deputy steward for Augustus.

EDCS-08300471.summary: This inscription likely records the name and age of Marcus Iulius Martialis, who died at 104 years old, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-08300472.text_edition: \n Deae Candidae Reginae bene merenti pro se et suis Caius Paulinius Iustus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300472.translation: To the Goddess Candida Regina, who has deserved well, for himself and his family, Gaius Paulinius Iustus, a soldier of the Twenty-Second Primigenia Legion, pious, faithful, a beneficiary of the consular legate, fulfilled his vow willingly, joyfully, and as deserved.
EDCS-08300472.summary: A votive dedication to the goddess Candida by Gaius Paulinius Iustus, a soldier of the Twenty-Second Legion, expressing gratitude for divine favor.

EDCS-08300473.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo dis deabusque omnibus Titus Ianuarinius Tertius miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Idibus Ianuariis Mamertino et Rufo consulibus\n
EDCS-08300473.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to all the gods and goddesses, Titus Ianuarinius Tertius, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow on the Ides of January during the consulship of Mamertinus and Rufus.
EDCS-08300473.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter and all gods by Titus Ianuarinius Tertius, a soldier and staff officer of the Eighth Legion, dated to 199 CE.

EDCS-08300474.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae dis deabusque omnibus et Genio loci Publius Aelius Gemellus beneficiarius consularis Imperatore [Commodo] [Augusto et] Victorino II consulibus Idibus Iuliis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300474.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and all the gods and goddesses, and to the Genius of the place, Publius Aelius Gemellus, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow on the Ides of July during the consulship of Emperor Commodus Augustus and Victorinus.
EDCS-08300474.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, all gods, and the Genius of the place by Publius Aelius Gemellus, a staff officer, dated to 187 CE.

EDCS-08300475.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Genio loci dis deabusque omnibus Lucius Annamatius Atrectus beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300475.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, the Genius of the place, and all the gods and goddesses, Lucius Annamatius Atrectus, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300475.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, the Genius of the place, and all gods by Lucius Annamatius Atrectus, a staff officer, for himself and his family.

EDCS-08300476.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Titus Essimnius Tertius beneficiarius consularis pro se et suos sic votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300476.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, Titus Essimnius Tertius, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300476.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter and Juno by Titus Essimnius Tertius, a staff officer, for himself and his family.

EDCS-08300477.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci dis deabusque omnibus Gaius Iulius Iullinus miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300477.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, and to all the gods and goddesses, Gaius Iulius Iullinus, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300477.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, the Genius of the place, and all gods by Gaius Iulius Iullinus, a soldier and staff officer of the Eighth Legion, for himself and his family.

EDCS-08300478.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Quintus Cornelius Sabatina Severianus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08300478.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, Quintus Cornelius Sabatina Severianus, a soldier of the Twenty-second Primigenian Legion, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300478.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius of the place by Quintus Cornelius Sabatina Severianus, a soldier and staff officer of the Twenty-second Legion, for himself and his family.

EDCS-08300479.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae et Marti Exalbiovici dis deabusque omnibus et Genio loci pro se et suis Quintus Melicius Respectus miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08300479.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, Mars Exalbiovicius, and to all the gods and goddesses and the Genius of the place, Quintus Melicius Respectus, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300479.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, Mars, all gods, and the Genius of the place by Quintus Melicius Respectus, a soldier and staff officer of the Eighth Legion, for himself and his family.

EDCS-08300480.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Titius Tacitus miles legionis III Italicae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito Flacco et Gallo consulibus\n
EDCS-08300480.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, Titius Tacitus, a soldier of the Third Italian Legion, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family during the consulship of Flaccus and Gallus.
EDCS-08300480.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius of the place by Titius Tacitus, a soldier and staff officer of the Third Italian Legion, for himself and his family, dated to 225 CE.

EDCS-08300481.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Fortunae Reduci dis deabusque omnibus Genio loci Publius Iunius Secundus beneficiarius consularis pro se et suos sic votum solvit\n
EDCS-08300481.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, Fortuna Redux, and all the gods and goddesses and the Genius of the place, Publius Iunius Secundus, a staff officer of the governor, thus fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300481.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the imperial family, Jupiter, Juno, Fortuna Redux, and the Genius of the place by Publius Iunius Secundus, a staff officer.

EDCS-08300482.text_edition: \n Diae sic Candidae Reginae et numini eius Lucius Traianius Ibliomarus miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300482.translation: To the thus radiant Queen Dia and her divine power, Lucius Traianius Ibliomarus, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, a staff officer of the governor, gratefully, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-08300482.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Dia and her divine power by Lucius Traianius Ibliomarus, a soldier and staff officer of the Eighth Legion, for himself and his family.

EDCS-08300483.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Mansuetius Constans beneficiarius consularis pro se et suos sic votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08300483.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius Mansuetius Constans, aide of the governor, fulfilled his vow for himself and his family, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-08300483.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Lucius Mansuetius Constans, an aide of a governor.

EDCS-08501419.summary: This is a boundary inscription indicating land dimensions, likely agricultural.

EDCS-08600540.text_edition: \n Maximius Acceptus sibi vivus et Connougae uxori defunctae faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-08600540.translation: Maximius Acceptus had this made for himself while alive and for his deceased wife Connouga.
EDCS-08600540.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Maximius Acceptus for himself and his deceased wife.

EDCS-08600541.text_edition: \n ius us excussor sic vivus sibi et Masioni fratri defuncto faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-08600541.translation: Ius was the excussor. While alive, he had this made for himself and his deceased brother Masion.
EDCS-08600541.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Ius, identified as an excussor, for himself and his deceased brother.

EDCS-08900490.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio ius Iuvenalis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-08900490.translation: To the god Mercury, Iuvenalis fulfilled his vow, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08900490.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mercury by Iuvenalis.

EDCS-08901056.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinace Augusto Arabico Adiabenico Parthico Maximo patre patriae consule III et Imperatore Caesare Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Pio et Publio Septimio Geta Caesare a colonia Augusta Treverorum leugae XLVIII\n
EDCS-08901056.translation: Under Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, Arabicus, Adiabenicus, Parthicus, Maximus, father of the country, consul for the third time, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus Pius, and Caesar Publius Septimius Geta, 48 leagues from the colony Augusta Treverorum.
EDCS-08901056.summary: This inscription records a distance of 48 leagues from Augusta Treverorum, under the consulship of Septimius Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, placing it between 198 and 209 AD.

EDCS-08901059.text_edition: \n D(is)? M(anibus) Caio Iulio Aprili Iuliae Acceptae Iulio Accepto \n
EDCS-08901059.translation: To the departed spirits: to Gaius Julius Aprilis, Iuliae Acceptae, [and] Iulius Acceptus.
EDCS-08901059.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus), listing several names, likely funerary.

EDCS-08901060.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio |(centuriae) Iuli Marti Publius Contessius Vitalis custos armorum donum dedit dedicavit Praesente II et Condiano consulibus\n
EDCS-08901060.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the centuria of Iulius Martius, Publius Contessius Vitalis, keeper of arms, gave and dedicated this gift, in the presence of the consuls II and Condianus.
EDCS-08901060.summary: This is a dedication of a gift to Jupiter and the Genius of a centuria by Publius Contessius Vitalis, keeper of arms, during the consulship of II and Condianus.

EDCS-08901062.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae et Marti Secundinius Amantius cornicularius praefecti legionis XXII permittente Primulo patre ex voto posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-08901062.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras and to Mars, Secundinius Amantius, a junior officer of the XXII legion, with the permission of his father Primulus, set this up according to his vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-08901062.summary: This is a dedication to Mithras and Mars by Secundinius Amantius, a military officer, made with his father's permission.

EDCS-08901063.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Conservatori M(arcus)? Satrius Saturninus ex iussu posuit\n
EDCS-08901063.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Unconquered God Conservator, Marcus Satrius Saturninus set this up by order.
EDCS-08901063.summary: This inscription honors the divine house and the god Mithras Conservator, set up by Marcus Satrius Saturninus by order.

EDCS-08901064.text_edition: \n Caius Albucius Cai filius Claudia Firmus Apro miles leg(ionis) I adiutricis? annorum stipendiorum IX hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-08901064.translation: Gaius Albucius Firmus, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, a soldier of the I adiutrix legion with 9 years of service, is buried here. His heir arranged for his burial.
EDCS-08901064.summary: A tombstone for a soldier of the I adiutrix legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901066.text_edition: \n Iucunda Luci Tiberi liberta Felicis nnorum natu XX et Primio filius annorum VIII hic siti sunt Quintus Ancharius Castus de suo posuit\n
EDCS-08901066.translation: Iucunda, freedwoman of Lucius Tiberius, aged 20, and her son Primus, aged 8, are buried here. Quintus Ancharius Castus placed this monument at his own expense.
EDCS-08901066.summary: A tombstone for a freedwoman and her son, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08901071.text_edition: \n Legio XIIII gemina Martia victrix centuria Laecani\n
EDCS-08901071.translation: The XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix legion, the century of Laecanius.
EDCS-08901071.summary: An inscription possibly marking a military structure or a dedication by a century of the XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix legion.

EDCS-09001539.text_edition: \n In honorem domus <divinae> Deo Marti Laeno sic Saturninius Quintus ex voto posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-09001539.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Mars Laenus. Saturninius Quintus placed this in accordance with his vow, gladly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-09001539.summary: A votive dedication to the god Mars Laenus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, possibly associated with the imperial family.

EDCS-09200393.text_edition: \n Priminiae Maturae et Amando filio heredes ponendum curaverunt nati\n
EDCS-09200393.translation: Her heirs arranged for this monument to be erected for Priminia Matura and her son Amandus.
EDCS-09200393.summary: A tombstone for Priminia Matura and her son Amandus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200394.text_edition: \n Sulevis Vettius Aventini filius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-09200394.translation: Sulevis, son of Vettius Aventinus, fulfilled his vow, gladly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-09200394.summary: A votive inscription by Sulevis, son of Vettius Aventinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200395.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marci Nervini Saturnini Mucius Doryphorus IIIIO ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-09200395.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Mucius Doryphorus arranged for the monument to be erected for Marcus Nervinius Saturninus, dedicating four hundred (units?).
EDCS-09200395.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Nervinius Saturninus, erected by Mucius Doryphorus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09200396.text_edition: \n Quinto Severio Quinti Severi Marcelli filio Cornelia Marciano decurioni Coloniae Iuliae Equestris aedili praefecto pro IIviris praefecto arcendis latrociniis IIviro bis flamini Augusti\n
EDCS-09200396.translation: For Quintus Severius Marcianus, son of Quintus Severius Marcellus, decurion of the colony of Iulia Equestris, aedile, prefect for suppressing brigands, twice as aedile, and imperial flamen.
EDCS-09200396.summary: An epitaph for Quintus Severius Marcianus, detailing his extensive career as a local magistrate and official in Colonia Iulia Equestris, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09300445.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Divixta Macionis I Camelus Sanuanus annorum LXX Bello Cameli LX\n
EDCS-09300445.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Divixta Macionis. Camelus Sanuanus, aged 70. Bello Cameli, aged 60.
EDCS-09300445.summary: A tombstone for Divixta Macionis, Camelus Sanuanus, and Bello Cameli, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09300450.translation: Legio XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis. Manlius Candidus made this.
EDCS-09300450.summary: An inscription possibly related to the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis legion, indicating it was made by Manlius Candidus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09300452.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Minervae Marcus Aurelius Iustius Belatullus magister plumariorum votum solvit libens laetus merito Aspro et Aspro consulibus\n
EDCS-09300452.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Minerva, Marcus Aurelius Iustius Belatullus, master of the plumarii (embroiderers), willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow under the consulship of Asprius and Asprius.
EDCS-09300452.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva by Marcus Aurelius Iustius Belatullus, master of the plumarii, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09300453.text_edition: \n Maximo et Condiano consulibus Silvano deo et Genio loci Marcus Petronius Maximinus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-09300453.translation: Under the consulship of Maximinus and Condianus, to the god Silvanus and the Genius of the place, Marcus Petronius Maximinus, a beneficiary of the governor, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09300453.summary: This is a votive inscription to Silvanus and the Genius Loci by Marcus Petronius Maximinus, a military official, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09300454.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Silvano et Dianae sanctae Genio catabuli consularis ceterrisque sic diis inmortalibus pro se suisque Titus Maximius Felix miles legionis XXII Primigeniae beneficiarius consularis Idibus Ianuariis Imperatore Antonino Augusto Pio III et Geta Caesare II consulibus\n
EDCS-09300454.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Silvanus, and the holy Diana, the Genius of the consular stable, and the other immortal gods, Titus Maximius Felix, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia legion, a beneficiary of the governor, for himself and his family, on the Ides of January, under Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius (consul for the 3rd time) and Geta Caesar (consul for the 2nd time).
EDCS-09300454.summary: This is a complex dedication to multiple deities by Titus Maximius Felix, a soldier and beneficiary of the governor, dating to the period of Antoninus Pius and Geta Caesar (likely 136-161 CE).

EDCS-09300455.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Silvano et Genio loci et Deanae Caius Iulius Super miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Imperatore Antonino Augusto II et Geta Caesare consulibus Idibus Iuliis\n
EDCS-09300455.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Silvanus, the Genius of the place, and Diana, Caius Julius Super, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia legion, pious and faithful, a beneficiary of the governor, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow under Emperor Antoninus Augustus (consul for the 2nd time) and Geta Caesar, on the Ides of July.
EDCS-09300455.summary: This is a votive inscription to Silvanus, the Genius Loci, and Diana by Caius Julius Super, a soldier and beneficiary of the governor, dating to the joint consulship of Antoninus Pius and Geta Caesar (likely 136-140 CE).

EDCS-09300456.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tiberio Claudio Augusti liberto Zosimo procuratori praegustatorum Imperatoris Domitiani Caesaris Augusti Germanici hoc monumentum heredem non sequetur\n
EDCS-09300456.translation: To the spirits of the dead: Tiberius Claudius Zosimus, freedman of Augustus, procurator of the Emperor Domitian Caesar Augustus Germanicus's tasters, this monument shall not pass to his heir.
EDCS-09300456.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius Zosimus, a freedman and procurator for Emperor Domitian, indicating the monument is not inheritable.

EDCS-09300459.text_edition: \n Quarta Titunai filia et Marinus Longini filius hic siti sunt Longinus coniux et Capito frater posuerunt\n
EDCS-09300459.translation: Quarta, daughter of Titunius, and Marinus, son of Longinus, are buried here. Longinus (her husband) and Capito (her brother) erected this.
EDCS-09300459.summary: This is a tombstone for Quarta and Marinus, set up by Longinus and Capito, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-09301147.text_edition: \n Marcus Cassius Marci filius Oufentina Mediolano veteranus legionis XIIII geminae annorum Caius Cassius Marci filius Oufentina Mediolano frater miles legionis XIIII geminae annorum XLV stipendiorum hic siti sunt\n
EDCS-09301147.translation: Marcus Cassius, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, from Mediolanum, a veteran of the XIV Gemina legion, aged [approx. 45?], and Caius Cassius, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, from Mediolanum, a soldier of the XIV Gemina legion, aged 45, are buried here.
EDCS-09301147.summary: This tombstone records the burial of two brothers, Marcus Cassius (veteran) and Caius Cassius (soldier), both from Mediolanum and serving in the XIV Gemina legion, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09301149.text_edition: \n Legio XIIII gemina Martia victrix centuria Severi\n
EDCS-09301149.translation: The XIV Gemina Martia Victrix legion, century of Severus.
EDCS-09301149.summary: This inscription likely refers to a unit or property belonging to the XIV Gemina Martia Victrix legion, associated with the century of Severus, probably from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-09301151.text_edition: \n Lucio Ferridio Balbi liberto Felici et Modesto servo natione Trevero sic nnorum XIIX heres eius curavit\n
EDCS-09301151.translation: Lucius Ferridius Felix, freedman of Balbus, and Modestus, a slave of Treveran origin, aged 18, his heir took care of this.
EDCS-09301151.summary: This is a funerary monument for Lucius Ferridius Felix, a freedman, and Modestus, a slave, with an indication that the heir arranged for the monument, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-09301154.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Victoriae perpetuae sacrum sub cura Sexti Cati Clementini consularis provinciae Germaniae superioris Caius Sempronius Martialis praefectus\n
EDCS-09301154.translation: Sacred to the perpetual divine house, under the supervision of Sextus Catius Clementinus, governor of the province of Upper Germany, Caius Sempronius Martialis, prefect.
EDCS-09301154.summary: This is a dedication to the 'perpetual divine house' and Victoria by Caius Sempronius Martialis, a prefect, under the supervision of the governor of Upper Germany, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-09401126.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Saturninus.
EDCS-09401126.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Saturninus.

EDCS-09401133.summary: This inscription records a dedication or memorial, possibly by Quintuvius Servandus for Firmius.

EDCS-09500082.summary: This inscription records that Amaranthus created the monument.

EDCS-09500086.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Adiantus, son of Pudentis.
EDCS-09500086.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Adiantus, son of Pudentis.

EDCS-09500087.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial, possibly by Lagoena for Natalis.

EDCS-09500092.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Totia Luci filia votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-09500092.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Totia, daughter of Lucius, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-09500092.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury, dedicated by Totia daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-09500094.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription to Mercury by Adnamus.

EDCS-09500097.text_edition: \n Mercurio Quillenio Aulus Ibliomarius Placidus negotiator castello Mattiacorum lanius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-09500097.translation: To Mercury Quillenius. Aulus Ibliomarius Placidus, a merchant from the fort of the Mattiaci, a butcher, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-09500097.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury Quillenius by Aulus Ibliomarius Placidus, a merchant and butcher from the fort of the Mattiaci.

EDCS-09500098.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Verecundinia Voba sibi fecit et Cerialinio Mulioni filio faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-09500098.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld for Verecundinia Voba; she made this for herself and arranged for it to be made for her son Cerialinius Mulio.
EDCS-09500098.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Verecundinia Voba, who commissioned it for herself and her son Cerialinius Mulio.

EDCS-09500100.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or memorial, possibly by Lagoena for Severa.

EDCS-09500101.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely identifies a small bowl belonging to someone named Marcinus.

EDCS-09500293.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XVI imperator II consul IIII proconsul fortissimus felicissimusque magnus princeps pacator orbis vias et pontes vetustate collabsos! restituit\n
EDCS-09500293.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, the greatest victor in Parthia and Britannia, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 16th time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 4th time, the bravest and happiest proconsul, the great prince, the pacifier of the world, restored roads and bridges that had collapsed from age.
EDCS-09500293.summary: This inscription records the restoration of roads and bridges by Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely during his reign from 161 to 180 CE.

EDCS-09500294.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate III consul pater patriae vias et pontes vetustate conlapsos restituit milia passuum XII\n
EDCS-09500294.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul, father of the fatherland, restored roads and bridges that had collapsed from age, 12 miles.
EDCS-09500294.summary: This inscription records the restoration of roads and bridges, covering 12 miles, by Emperor Gordian III, likely during his reign from 238 to 244 CE.

EDCS-09500296.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate III consul pater patriae vias et pontes vetustate conlabsos sic restituit milia passuum VI\n
EDCS-09500296.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul, father of the fatherland, restored roads and bridges that had collapsed from age, 6 miles.
EDCS-09500296.summary: This inscription records the restoration of roads and bridges, covering 6 miles, by Emperor Gordian III, likely during his reign from 238 to 244 CE.

EDCS-09500300.text_edition: \n Imperatori Marco Iulio Philippo Pio Felici Augusto et Marco Iulio Philippo nobilissimo Caesari mille passus I\n
EDCS-09500300.translation: To Emperor Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus and Marcus Julius Philippus, the most noble Caesar, 1 mile.
EDCS-09500300.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Philip I and his son Philip II, likely commemorating the construction or restoration of one mile of road, possibly from the 240s CE.

EDCS-09700220.text_edition: \n Caeno I filius |(centurio) cohortis Hispanorum domo Tancia Norbana nnorum XL stipendiorum IIII hic situs est Cundigus Boeli filius heres posuit\n
EDCS-09700220.translation: Caeno, son of I, a centurion of the Spanish cohort, from Tancia Norbana, aged 40, with 4 years of service, is buried here. Cundigus, son of Boelius, his heir, set this up.
EDCS-09700220.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caeno, a centurion of the Spanish cohort, set up by his heir Cundigus, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09701088.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cubi Sacrati filius eiius\n
EDCS-09701088.translation: To the departed spirits: Cubus, son of Sacratus.
EDCS-09701088.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirits (Dis Manibus), likely a funerary inscription for Cubus, son of Sacratus.

EDCS-09701090.text_edition: \n Mercurio Titus Cammianius Bacchus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-09701090.translation: To Mercury, Titus Cammianius Bacchus willingly, happily, deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-09701090.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Titus Cammianius Bacchus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701092.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to identify a person named Cera, daughter of Felix, possibly on a tomb or object.

EDCS-09701102.translation: Tiberianus, a citizen of Arles, made this for Soiona.
EDCS-09701102.summary: This is a dedication by Tiberianus, a citizen of Arles, to a deity or person named Soiona, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09701103.text_edition: \n Rheno Patri Oppius Severus legatus Augusti\n
EDCS-09701103.translation: To Father Rhenus, the legate of the emperor Oppius Severus.
EDCS-09701103.summary: This is a dedication to the river god Rhenus by a legate of the emperor, likely from the Roman frontier.

EDCS-09701104.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Catto Calodubni filiio Ne<m=II>odlianus \n
EDCS-09701104.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Nemodlianus, son of Catto Calodubnus.
EDCS-09701104.summary: This is a funerary dedication (dis manibus) for Nemodlianus, the son of Catto Calodubnus.

EDCS-09701582.translation: Long live Tonancius! Maxo made me very well; I made and I make.
EDCS-09701582.summary: This is a dedication, possibly for a tombstone, made by Maxo for Tonancius, indicating the maker's skill.

EDCS-09701585.text_edition: \n Deabus Sanctis sacrum Caius Geminius ens\n
EDCS-09701585.translation: Sacred to the Holy Goddesses. Caius Geminius ens...
EDCS-09701585.summary: This is a sacred dedication to unknown "Holy Goddesses" by Caius Geminius.

EDCS-09800264.text_edition: \n Turma Grati Ulpi Aprilis turma Tulli\n
EDCS-09800264.translation: The troop of Gratus, son of Ulpius Aprilis, the troop of Tullius.
EDCS-09800264.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two cavalry troops, perhaps associated with a military unit or a specific location.

EDCS-09800265.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marcellus Bolgedonis miles cohortis I Ligurum civis Sequanus stipendiorum XXIII heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-09800265.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Marcellus, son of Bolgedo, a soldier of the I Cohort of Ligurians, a citizen of the Sequani, after 23 years of service, arranged for this to be made as heir.
EDCS-09800265.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcellus, a soldier of the I Cohort of Ligurians, who served for 23 years.

EDCS-10700396.summary: This is a very brief inscription that may record a dedication or marking of places by Secundius.

EDCS-10700397.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Florentinius Quintianus veteranus cohortis XXIIII voluntariorum ex corniculario praefecti votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10700397.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Florentinius Quintianus, a veteran of the XXIIII Cohort of Volunteers, formerly a clerk to the prefect, paid his vow willingly, happily, deservedly.
EDCS-10700397.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter by a veteran soldier named Florentinius Quintianus.

EDCS-10700403.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae bonis Cassibus eo quod post summersamm bonae saluti sit redditus et suis Lucius Licinius Divixtus negotiator ex voto posuit A<l=B>bino et Maximo consulibus libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-10700403.translation: In honor of the divine house, because after the shipwreck, it was returned to good health and to its own [people]. Lucius Licinius Divixtus, a merchant, set this up by vow, willingly, happily, deservedly, under the consulship of Albino and Maximo.
EDCS-10700403.summary: This is a votive offering by a merchant, Lucius Licinius Divixtus, dedicated to the imperial family after surviving a shipwreck, dating to the consulship of Albino and Maximo.

EDCS-10700404.text_edition: \n Divixta Argentias Litta Celori dono dederunt laetae libentes merito\n
EDCS-10700404.translation: Divixta and Argentias Litta and Celori gave [this] as a gift, happy, willing, deservedly.
EDCS-10700404.summary: This records a gift given by Divixta, Argentias Litta, and Celori.

EDCS-10700405.text_edition: \n Aram pro salutem sic Publi Petronii Caesii Rufi io C Apro et Maximo consulibus Kalendis Decenbribus sic\n
EDCS-10700405.translation: An altar for the safety [of Publius Petronius Caesius Rufus], under consuls io and Apro and Maximus, on the Kalends of December.
EDCS-10700405.summary: This inscription records an altar dedicated for the safety of Publius Petronius Caesius Rufus, dated by consuls to December 1st.

EDCS-10700407.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Herculi collegium convenarum Lupo et Maximo consulibus Idibus Decembribus\n
EDCS-10700407.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Hercules, by the association of convenae, under consuls Lupo and Maximus, on the Ides of December.
EDCS-10700407.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Hercules by an association of convenae, honoring the imperial family and dated by consuls to December 13th.

EDCS-10700408.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Dianae collegium convenarum Lupo et Maximo consulibus Idibus Decembribus\n
EDCS-10700408.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Diana, by the association of convenae, under consuls Lupo and Maximus, on the Ides of December.
EDCS-10700408.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Diana by an association of convenae, honoring the imperial family and dated by consuls to December 13th.

EDCS-10700409.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Sev\n
EDCS-10700409.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Sev[...
EDCS-10700409.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-10700410.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with an incomplete personal name.

EDCS-10700416.text_edition: \n CIS Publius Allius Proculus domo Roma praefectus cohortis III Aquitanorum \n
EDCS-10700416.translation: Publius Allius Proculus, from Rome, prefect of the 3rd Aquitanian cohort.
EDCS-10700416.summary: This inscription records Publius Allius Proculus, a Roman citizen and prefect of a cohort, likely marking his service or a funerary monument.

EDCS-10700418.text_edition: \n Bonis Casibus Quintinius libertus Lector ex voto\n
EDCS-10700418.translation: To the Good Fortunes, Quintinius, freedman, Lector, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10700418.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the Bonis Casibus (Good Fortunes) by Quintinius, a freedman and lector.

EDCS-10700420.translation: To the Only Unconquered God Mithras, Eternal (?), by Appuleius.
EDCS-10700420.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Mithras by Appuleius, possibly dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700422.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Paternius Amandus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10700422.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Paternus Amandus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10700422.summary: This inscription records Paternus Amandus fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus with joy and gratitude.

EDCS-10700423.translation: Candida gave [this] as a gift to the townspeople of Vangiones.
EDCS-10700423.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Candida to the municipium of Vangiones.

EDCS-10700425.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Attius Tertius |(centurio) cohortis II Hispanorum pro salute sua et Cissonis coniugis suae et filiorum suorum votum susceptum posuit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10700425.translation: In honor of the divine house, Attius Tertius, a centurion of the II Cohort of Spaniards, placed this offering, freely, willingly, and deservedly, for his own health, that of his wife Cissonis, and his sons.
EDCS-10700425.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by a centurion of the II Cohort of Spaniards for the health of his family, likely from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-10700427.text_edition: \n Ruto Mattiaci filius cives sic Cairacas curia Flacci annorum XXV Allia mater annorum sibi et filio suo posuit\n
EDCS-10700427.translation: Ruto, son of Mattiacus, a Roman citizen from Cairacas, 25 years old, his mother Allia, 25 years old, set this up for herself and her son.
EDCS-10700427.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Ruto, a 25-year-old Roman citizen, set up by his mother Allia.

EDCS-10700428.text_edition: \n Marcus Laetorius Marci filius Publilia Firmus Verona miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XXXV stipendiorum X hic situs est testamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700428.translation: Marcus Laetorius Firmus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 14th Legion Gemina Martia Victrix, 35 years old with 10 years of service, lies here; he ordered this to be made in his will, and his heir had it carried out.
EDCS-10700428.summary: This is a soldier's tombstone for Marcus Laetorius Firmus of the 14th Legion, who died after 10 years of service at age 35, with instructions for his burial specified in his will.

EDCS-10700429.text_edition: \n Caius Titius Cai filius Maecia Mestrius Pelagonia miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XXX stipendiorum XII hic intus situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700429.translation: Caius Titius Mestrius, son of Caius, of the Maecia tribe, from Pelagonia, a soldier of the 14th Legion Gemina Martia Victrix, 30 years old with 12 years of service, lies here within; his heir had this carried out.
EDCS-10700429.summary: This epitaph records Caius Titius Mestrius, a 30-year-old soldier of the 14th Legion with 12 years of service, and states that his heir was responsible for the monument.

EDCS-10700430.text_edition: \n Titus Valerius Titi filius Galeria Luna miles legionis XVI annorum XXV stipendiorum V hic situs est\n
EDCS-10700430.translation: Titus Valerius Luna, son of Titus, of the Galeria tribe, a soldier of the 16th Legion, 25 years old with 5 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10700430.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Valerius Luna, a 25-year-old soldier of the 16th Legion with 5 years of service.

EDCS-10700431.text_edition: \n Caius Helvius Cai filius Voltinia Sabinus Viana miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXX stipendiorum X hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700431.translation: Caius Helvius Sabinus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Viana, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, 30 years old with 10 years of service, lies here; his heir had this carried out.
EDCS-10700431.summary: This epitaph commemorates Caius Helvius Sabinus, a 30-year-old soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion with 10 years of service, whose heir arranged for the monument.

EDCS-10700432.text_edition: \n Marcus Dipponius Marci filius Claudia Icco Iuvavo miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXVI stipendiorum VI hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700432.translation: Marcus Dipponius Icco, son of Marcus, of the Claudia tribe, from Juvava, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, 26 years old with 6 years of service, lies here; his heir had this carried out.
EDCS-10700432.summary: This tombstone records Marcus Dipponius Icco, a 26-year-old soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion who served for 6 years, with his heir responsible for the monument.

EDCS-10700433.text_edition: \n Theander Aristomeni filius Cretensis miles cohortis I Noricorum optio annorum XLV stipendiorum XXVI hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700433.translation: Theander, son of Aristomenes, a Cretan, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Noricum, a optio, 45 years old with 26 years of service, lies here; his heir had this carried out.
EDCS-10700433.summary: This is the tombstone of Theander, a Cretan optio in the 1st Cohort of Noricum, who died at age 45 after 26 years of service, with his heir responsible for the monument.

EDCS-10700434.text_edition: \n Caius Valerius Cai filius Offentina Virillio Mediolani miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XL stipendiorum XX hic situs est heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10700434.translation: Caius Valerius Virillio, son of Caius, of the Offentina tribe, from Milan, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, 40 years old with 20 years of service, lies here; his heirs had this carried out.
EDCS-10700434.summary: This epitaph marks the burial place of Caius Valerius Virillio, a 40-year-old soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia with 20 years of service, whose heirs arranged for the monument.

EDCS-10700435.text_edition: \n Caius Coelius Cai filius Voltinia Passus Tolossa sic miles legionis IIII Maacedonicae annorum XXX stipendiorum VIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-10700435.translation: Caius Coelius Passus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Tolosa, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, 30 years old with 8 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10700435.summary: This is a soldier's tombstone for Caius Coelius Passus of the 4th Macedonian Legion, who was 30 years old and had served for 8 years.

EDCS-10700436.translation: Alphius made [this] for [the] new posts at Ga[n(tunas)].
EDCS-10700436.summary: This is a milestone marking the construction of new posts near Gantu[nas].

EDCS-10700437.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Luci Caesi Restituti\n
EDCS-10700437.translation: From the first legion Adiutrix, from the century of Lucius Caelsius Restitutus.
EDCS-10700437.summary: This inscription identifies a soldier from the first legion Adiutrix, belonging to the century of Lucius Caelsius Restitutus.

EDCS-10700439.text_edition: \n Flavius Proculus eques singularis Augusti domo Philodelphia sic annorum XXI faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700439.translation: Flavius Proculus, an equestrian soldier of the emperor, from Philadelphia, twenty-one years of age, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10700439.summary: This is a tombstone for Flavius Proculus, a 21-year-old equestrian soldier from Philadelphia, who arranged for his monument before his death.

EDCS-10700440.text_edition: \n Caius Octavius Cai filius Voturia Octavius Placentia miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XXVI stipendiorum VI hic situs est titulum fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700440.translation: Gaius Octavius Octavius, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the legion XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, twenty-six years old, with six years of service, lies here; he ordered this inscription to be made, and his heir arranged for it to be made.
EDCS-10700440.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Octavius Octavius, a 26-year-old soldier of the legion XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, who arranged for his monument and had it made by his heir.

EDCS-10700441.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Do...
EDCS-10700441.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter, possibly incomplete.

EDCS-10700444.text_edition: \n Serenus legatus legionum IIII Flaviae et XXII Primigeniae voti compos\n
EDCS-10700444.translation: Serenus, legate of the legions IIII Flavia and XXII Primigenia, having fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10700444.summary: This inscription records Serenus, a legate of two legions, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10700445.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Titi Aeli Hadriani Antonini Augusti Pii patris patriae Aulus Iunius Pastor Lucius Caesennius Sospes legatus Augusti\n
EDCS-10700445.translation: For Jupiter Best and Greatest, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the fatherland, Aulus Iunius Pastor and Lucius Caesennius Sospes, imperial legates...
EDCS-10700445.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter for the health of Emperor Antoninus Pius, made by two imperial legates.

EDCS-10700446.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely a dedication made by a married couple.

EDCS-10700447.text_edition: \n A cum Claudia Alexandria uxore et liberis\n
EDCS-10700447.translation: ...with Claudia Alexandria his wife and children.
EDCS-10700447.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, likely recording a family dedicating something.

EDCS-10700449.text_edition: \n Libero et Apollini pro salute Imperatoris Caesaris Marci [Aureli] Commodi[3] [[]] [] Quintus Aurelius Polus Terentianus cum Quinto Aurelio Polo Syriaco filio fetialis legatus legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis item legionis II Augustae\n
EDCS-10700449.translation: To Liber and Apollo, for the health of the Emperor Caesar Marcus [Aurelius] Commodus, Quintus Aurelius Polus Terentianus, fetialis, legate of the legion XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis, and also of the legion II Augusta, with his son Quintus Aurelius Polus Syriacus.
EDCS-10700449.summary: This is a dedication to Liber and Apollo for the health of Emperor Commodus, made by Quintus Aurelius Polus Terentianus, a fetialis and legate of two legions, along with his son.

EDCS-10700453.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Octaviae Capitolinae domo Aelia Capitolina castissimae ac pudicissimae coniugi et incomparabili vixit nnos XXXII menses V dies IIII et Gaio Iulio Nepotiano equiti Romano filio eius vixit annos II menses XI dies XIIX Iulius Valens |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10700453.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. For Octavia Capitolina, most chaste and modest wife, of the Aelia Capitolina tribe, who lived 32 years, 5 months, and 4 days; and for her son Gaius Julius Nepotianus, a Roman knight, who lived 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days. Julius Valens, centurion of the 8th Augustan Legion, had this made.
EDCS-10700453.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a centurion for his wife and son, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10700454.text_edition: \n Marcus C Con cent I legionis XX\n
EDCS-10700454.translation: Marcus [son of] Con, centurion of the 20th Legion.
EDCS-10700454.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning a centurion of the 20th Legion, possibly indicating his name and affiliation.
