EDCS-10700455.text_edition: \n Caius Tallius Cai Fabia Priscus veteranus ex legione XIIII gemina nnrum XLIIX stipendiorum XXVII vexsillo sic Publi Atili Crispi hic situs est frater pro pietate posuit\n
EDCS-10700455.translation: Caius Tallius Priscus, a veteran of the 14th Gemina Legion, with 48 years of service and 27 years of full pay, is buried here. His brother erected this out of filial devotion.
EDCS-10700455.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a veteran of the 14th Gemina Legion, erected by his brother.

EDCS-10700459.text_edition: \n Abaius filius natione Pannonnius eques alae Picentianae \n
EDCS-10700459.translation: Abaius, son of [?], a Pannonian by birth, a cavalryman of the Picentian Ala.
EDCS-10700459.summary: This is an inscription identifying a cavalryman serving in the Picentian Ala, likely a soldier's tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-10700460.text_edition: \n No et annonae quoi sic Carthaginienses ex Hispania honores qui erant maximi in colonia sua grati decreverunt et pleps sic eorum ex aere conlato decreto decurionum statuam posuerunt Quintus Vibius Quinti filius Rufus et Marcus Iguinus Marci filius Valens decuriones Placentini amico et sodali carissimo posuerunt\n
EDCS-10700460.translation: The Carthaginians from Hispania bestowed honors upon the god of the grain supply and the Annona, which were the greatest in their colony, and the people, from a collection of money, decreed by the decurions, erected a statue for their friend and most dear comrade. Quintus Vibius Rufus, son of Quintus, and Marcus Iguinus Valens, son of Marcus, decurions of Placentia, erected this for their very dear friend and comrade.
EDCS-10700460.summary: This is a dedication by local officials of Placentia for a deity, honoring them with a statue, likely erected in the late Roman period.

EDCS-10700461.text_edition: \n denuntiavi Tito Elvissio Secundo uti adsit Mogontiaci ante praetorium Poblici M<a>rcelli ad hiberna legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis\n
EDCS-10700461.translation: I have notified Titus Elvissius Secundus to be present at Mogontiacum, before the praetorium of Publicus Marcellus, for the winter quarters of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, the dutiful and faithful.
EDCS-10700461.summary: This inscription records an official notification concerning the winter quarters of the 22nd Primigenia Legion at Mogontiacum (modern Mainz).

EDCS-10700462.text_edition: \n Legionis I adiutricis |(centuriae) Cai Mummi Lolliani Luci Lucreti Celeris Luci Lucreti Celeris legionis I\n
EDCS-10700462.translation: Of the 1st Adjutant Legion, [of the] century of Caius Mummius Lollianus, [of the] century of Lucius Lucretius Celer, [of the] century of Lucius Lucretius Celer, of the 1st Legion.
EDCS-10700462.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing officers or soldiers belonging to the 1st Adjutant Legion, possibly part of a larger monument or list.

EDCS-10700463.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely refers to a group of soldiers identified as 'Black Spaniards'.

EDCS-10700464.summary: This is a brief inscription possibly recording a legal summons or a debt, mentioning Amine Aulinus and Marcellinus.

EDCS-10700465.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly indicating ownership of a vessel or a tomb marker for a woman named Severa.

EDCS-10700466.text_edition: \n Antiochus Antiochi filius Parthus Anazarbaeus eques alae Parthorum et Araborum evocatus triplicarius stipendiorum X donis donatus Belesippus frater posuit\n
EDCS-10700466.translation: Belesippus, his brother, dedicated this; Antiochus, son of Antiochus, a Parthian from Anazarba, a cavalryman in the ala of the Parthians and Arabs, a volunteer with triple pay, honored with ten military decorations.
EDCS-10700466.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Antiochus, a Parthian cavalryman, erected by his brother Belesippus.

EDCS-10700467.text_edition: \n Quintus Marius Quinti libertus Felix hic situs est\n
EDCS-10700467.translation: Quintus Marius Felix, freedman of Quintus, is buried here.
EDCS-10700467.summary: A simple tombstone marking the burial of Quintus Marius Felix, a freedman.

EDCS-10700468.text_edition: \n Molaecus Samuti filius annorum L ex cohorte III Ituraius sic stipendiorum XIIII hic situs est ]] [] libert-- annorum XXV hic sit-- est Phoenix conliberto ob pietatem de suo posuit\n
EDCS-10700468.translation: Molaecus, son of Samutus, aged 50, from the 3rd cohort of Ituraea, a soldier with 14 years of service, is buried here. Phoenix, his fellow freedman, dedicated this at his own expense out of piety for his freedman [name missing], aged 25, who is buried here.
EDCS-10700468.summary: This inscription records the burial of Molaecus and the posthumous dedication of his tomb by his fellow freedman Phoenix.

EDCS-10700469.translation: Freedman, aged 25, is buried here. Phoenix, his fellow freedman, dedicated this at his own expense out of piety.
EDCS-10700469.summary: A tombstone indicating the burial of a freedman and dedicated by his fellow freedman Phoenix.

EDCS-10700470.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Aurelio Rufino equiti Romano Valeria Rufina mater\n
EDCS-10700470.translation: To the Divine Shades. Valeria Rufina, his mother, [dedicated this] to Marcus Aurelius Rufus, a Roman equestrian.
EDCS-10700470.summary: A funerary dedication to Marcus Aurelius Rufus, an equestrian, by his mother.

EDCS-10700472.text_edition: \n Deae Candidae Reginae Lucius Augustius Iustus |(centurio) cohortis II Raetorum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10700472.translation: Lucius Augustius Justus, centurion of the 2nd cohort of Raetians, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Goddesses of Purity, Regina.
EDCS-10700472.summary: A votive inscription to the Goddesses of Purity by Lucius Augustius Justus, a centurion.

EDCS-10700473.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Sextius Ursus veteranus ex decurione cohortis I Damascenorum in suo ex voto posuit Albino et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-10700473.translation: Sextius Ursus, a veteran, formerly a decurion in the 1st cohort of Damascenes, dedicated this on his own property, fulfilling a vow, during the consulship of Albinus and Maximus.
EDCS-10700473.summary: A votive dedication by Sextius Ursus, a veteran decurion, during the consulship of Albinus and Maximus.

EDCS-10700474.translation: To the Goddess Proserpina. Primitiva [dedicated this].
EDCS-10700474.summary: A dedication to the goddess Proserpina, likely by a woman named Primitiva.

EDCS-10700476.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Tertinius Noan\n
EDCS-10700476.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina. Tertinius Noan [dedicated this].
EDCS-10700476.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Tertinius Noan.

EDCS-10700477.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Ambirenius Fronto sibi et FauVI FAV\n
EDCS-10700477.translation: To the Divine Shades. Ambirenius Fronto [dedicated this] for himself and Fau[stus?].
EDCS-10700477.summary: A funerary dedication for Ambirenius Fronto and possibly another individual, Fau[stus?].

EDCS-10700478.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Aprilius Saturninus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10700478.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Aprilius Saturninus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10700478.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter and Juno by Aprilius Saturninus.

EDCS-10700480.summary: This inscription records the name of Titus Ceionius Pacatus, likely on a tomb or property marker.

EDCS-10700481.translation: Of the century of Valerius Flavinius Secundus.
EDCS-10700481.summary: This inscription refers to a military unit, specifically a century belonging to Valerius Flavinius Secundus.

EDCS-10700482.text_edition: \n Imperatore Commodo Augusto cohortis XXXII voluntariorum |(centuriae) C Q Valeri Pri\n
EDCS-10700482.translation: Under Emperor Commodus Augustus, of the 32nd cohort of volunteers, century of Gaius Valerius Primus.
EDCS-10700482.summary: This inscription dates to the reign of Emperor Commodus and records a military unit, the 32nd cohort of volunteers.

EDCS-10700483.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Titus Carminius Scrainius momoriae sic Quinti Quinti dono dedit\n
EDCS-10700483.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Titus Carminius Scrainius gave this memorial with the consent of Quintus Quintius.
EDCS-10700483.summary: This is a memorial inscription dedicated to Jupiter and Juno by Titus Carminius Scrainius.

EDCS-10700489.text_edition: \n Rogo Manes Inferi ut Marius Fronto adversarius Sexti sit vanus neque loqui possit contra Sextum ut Fronto fiat mutus quum accesserit Consularem ut sit mutus neque possit loqui neque quicquam agere tanquam sic nullo sic ab inferis\n
EDCS-10700489.translation: I pray to the gods of the underworld that Marius Fronto, adversary of Sextus, may be in vain and unable to speak against Sextus, that Fronto may be mute when he approaches the consular, so that he may be mute and unable to speak or do anything, as if thus he were nothing from the underworld.
EDCS-10700489.summary: This is a magical curse inscription, likely intended to disable an opponent named Marius Fronto.

EDCS-10700494.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Genio loci Marcus Cossius Florentinus miles legionis VIII Augustae Severianae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit <l=I>(ibens) <l=I>(aetus) merito XVII Kalendas Februarias Maximo et Aeliano consulibus \n
EDCS-10700494.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, Marcus Cossius Florentinus, a soldier of the VIII Augusta Severiana legion, a beneficiarius consularis, fulfilled his vow for himself and his family willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, on the 17th day before the Kalends of February, when Maximo and Aelianus were consuls.
EDCS-10700494.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius loci by Marcus Cossius Florentinus, a soldier, during the consulship of Maximo and Aelianus.

EDCS-10700495.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae dis deabusque omnibus Genio loci Claudius Pompeianus miles legionis VIII Antoninianae Augustae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis omnibus posuit Idibus Ianuariis Grato et Seleuco consulibus\n
EDCS-10700495.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, and all the gods and goddesses, and the Genius of the place, Claudius Pompeianus, a soldier of the VIII Antoniniana Augusta legion, a beneficiarius consularis, erected this for himself and all his family on the Ides of January, when Gratus and Seleucus were consuls.
EDCS-10700495.summary: This is an inscription erected by Claudius Pompeianus, a soldier, to various deities and the Genius loci, during the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus.

EDCS-10700497.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Titus Vettius Augustalis praefectus equitum pro sal(ute) sua et ivi fili votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10700497.translation: To the god Mercury, Titus Vettius Augustalis, prefect of cavalry, fulfilled his vow for the health of himself and his son willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-10700497.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Titus Vettius Augustalis, a cavalry prefect, for his and his son's health.

EDCS-10700506.translation: Of the troop of Gratus / Of Ulpius / Of Aprilis / Of the troop of Tullius.
EDCS-10700506.summary: This inscription lists troop commanders or units, likely related to a military context.

EDCS-10700507.text_edition: \n iae sacrum Otia s Victor legionis XXII Primigeniae \n
EDCS-10700507.translation: Sacred to Iae. Otia, Victor of the twenty-second Primigenia legion.
EDCS-10700507.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to the deity Iae by a soldier named Victor, who belonged to the twenty-second Primigenia legion.

EDCS-10700510.text_edition: \n Maximo et Urbano? co(n)s(ulibus) Victorinus tesserarius fecit\n
EDCS-10700510.translation: In the consulship of Maximo and Urbano (perhaps), Victorinus, a tesserarius, made this.
EDCS-10700510.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Victorinus, a tesserarius, during the consulship of Maximo and Urbano, likely in the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-10700512.text_edition: \n Nimphis sic e<t=I> Apollini sacrum L(ucius) Iunius Elaus |(centurio) cohortis I civium Romanorum votum solvit libens merito \n
EDCS-10700512.translation: Lucius Iunius Elaus, a centurion of the first cohort of Roman citizens, gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Apollo and the Nymphs.
EDCS-10700512.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Lucius Iunius Elaus, a centurion of the first cohort of Roman citizens, to Apollo and the Nymphs.

EDCS-10701813.text_edition: \n Lucius Cornelius Adiutor crocodes ad aspritudines Luci Corneli Adiutoris diazmyrnes ad cicatrices veteres\n
EDCS-10701813.translation: Lucius Cornelius Adiutor's crocodes for roughness, for the old scars of Lucius Cornelius Adiutor's diazmyrnes.
EDCS-10701813.summary: This inscription appears to be a label for medicinal substances, likely crocus and diazmyrnes, intended for treating the scars of Lucius Cornelius Adiutor.

EDCS-10800404.text_edition: \n Caesia Vegeta Apollini v votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800404.translation: Caesia Vegeta gladly and deservedly paid her vow to Apollo.
EDCS-10800404.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Apollo by Caesia Vegeta.

EDCS-10800405.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iulia Pusinna flaminica Augustae votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800405.translation: Iulia Pusinna, priestess of Augusta, gladly and deservedly paid her vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-10800405.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Iulia Pusinna, who served as a priestess for the imperial cult.

EDCS-10800406.text_edition: \n Mercurio votum solvit libens merito Ocellio\n
EDCS-10800406.translation: Ocellio gladly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-10800406.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Mercury made by Ocellio.

EDCS-10800407.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli civitas Equestrium\n
EDCS-10800407.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power, consul, the community of Equestrium.
EDCS-10800407.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the community of Equestrium to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely during his reign (161-180 AD).

EDCS-10800408.text_edition: \n Caio Antistio Crescenti CLIA NHOR D CTNFDEN Caius Antistius ritu filio unico pater infelix\n
EDCS-10800408.translation: To Gaius Antistius Crescens. Caius Antistius, an unhappy father, to his only son.
EDCS-10800408.summary: This inscription is a dedication from an unhappy father, Caius Antistius, to his deceased son, Gaius Antistius Crescens.

EDCS-10800409.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucio Aurelio Reperto iuveni erudito causidico bis civitatibus Vallinsae sic et Equestri defuncto annorum XVIIII filio pientissimo Aurelius Respectus pater ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800409.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Respectus, a devoted father, arranged for the burial of his most pious son, Lucius Aurelius Reperto, a learned young advocate, who died having been honored by two communities, at the age of nineteen.
EDCS-10800409.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Aurelius Respectus for his son Lucius Aurelius Reperto, a young advocate who died at nineteen, having been honored by two communities.

EDCS-10800410.text_edition: \n Decimo Iulio Luci filio Voltinia Ripano Capitoni Bassiano equo publico honorato praefecto fabrum tribuno militum cohortis I Gal[lica in Hispania] Lucius Iulius Brocchus Valerius Bassus filio\n
EDCS-10800410.translation: To Decimus Julius Ripanus Bassianus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, a respected member of the equestrian order, prefect of the engineers, tribune of the soldiers of the 1st Gallic cohort in Spain. Lucius Julius Brocchus Valerius Bassus (erected this) to his son.
EDCS-10800410.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Julius Brocchus Valerius Bassus to his son, Decimus Julius Ripanus Bassianus, who had a distinguished military and political career.

EDCS-10800412.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Cai filio Voltinia Sedato IIviro iterum flamini Augusti Decimus Iulius Capito amico optimo\n
EDCS-10800412.translation: To Gaius Julius Sedatus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, twice duovir, priest of Augustus. Decimus Julius Capito (erected this) to his excellent friend.
EDCS-10800412.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Decimus Julius Capito to his friend, Gaius Julius Sedatus, a prominent local official.

EDCS-10800413.text_edition: \n Cai Lucconi Cornelia Tetrici praefecti arcendorum latrociniorum praefecti pro IIviro IIviri bis flaminis Augusti\n
EDCS-10800413.translation: To Caius Lucconius, son of Cornelia Tetricus, prefect of the suppression of brigandage, prefect, twice duovir, priest of Augustus.
EDCS-10800413.summary: This inscription records the career of Caius Lucconius, a local official who held positions such as prefect of the suppression of brigandage and duovir.

EDCS-10800414.text_edition: \n Lucio Sergio Luci filio Cornelia Lustrostaio Domitino omnibus honoribus in colonia Equestrium et in colonia Viennensium functo Titus Iulius Pompeius Tertullus socero optimo\n
EDCS-10800414.translation: To Lucius Sergius Lustrostaïus Domitianus, son of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, who held all the honors in the colony of Equestrium and in the colony of Vienna. Titus Iulius Pompeius Tertullus (erected this) to his excellent father-in-law.
EDCS-10800414.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Titus Iulius Pompeius Tertullus to his father-in-law, Lucius Sergius Lustrostaïus Domitianus, who had a distinguished career in two colonies.

EDCS-10800415.text_edition: \n Decimo Valerio Asiatici liberto Sissi sic IIIIIIviro coloniae Equestris ex testamento\n
EDCS-10800415.translation: To Decimus Valerius Asiaticus, freedman of Sissi, Sextumvir of the colony of Equestris, by his will.
EDCS-10800415.summary: This inscription records a bequest made by Decimus Valerius Asiaticus, a freedman and a Sextumvir of the colony of Equestris, through his will.

EDCS-10800416.text_edition: \n no filio Cornelia ? Cantabro curatori civium Romanorum conventus Helvetici IIviro Iuliae Cai filiae Marcellae Corneliae Quinti filiae Marcellae\n
EDCS-10800416.translation: To... son, of the Cornelia tribe, Cantabrus, curator of Roman citizens of the Helvetian district, duovir, (and) to Julia Marcella, daughter of Caius, of the Cornelia tribe, (and) Marcella, daughter of Quintus, of the Cornelia tribe.
EDCS-10800416.summary: This inscription honors multiple individuals, including a curator of Roman citizens, a duovir, and two women named Marcella, suggesting a familial or civic dedication.

EDCS-10800419.text_edition: \n Memoriae Antiphili annorum XVIII Lucina patrona\n
EDCS-10800419.translation: To the memory of Antiphilus, aged 18. Lucina, patroness.
EDCS-10800419.summary: This is a tombstone commemorating Antiphilus, an 18-year-old, dedicated by his patroness Lucina.

EDCS-10800420.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cai Camilli Quintilli Marcia Cocceia Sicuniana viri sic carissimo\n
EDCS-10800420.translation: To the departed gods. Marcia Cocceia Sicuniana (erected this) to her most beloved husband, Caius Camillus Quintillus.
EDCS-10800420.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Marcia Cocceia Sicuniana to her husband, Caius Camillus Quintillus.

EDCS-10800421.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Corneli Bilcaisionis filii Publicia Perpetua coniugis incomparabilis\n
EDCS-10800421.translation: To the departed gods. Publicia Perpetua (erected this) to her incomparable wife, the son of Cornelius Bilcaïs.
EDCS-10800421.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Publicia Perpetua to her wife, the son of Cornelius Bilcaïs.

EDCS-10800422.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a partial name, Lutatius.

EDCS-10800423.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Phileti Brittae annorum XXIIII defuncti Dossius Claudianus filii unici et piissimi ponendum curavit sub ascia dedicavit\n
EDCS-10800423.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Dossius Claudianus, out of love for his only and most devoted son Phileta Britta, who died at the age of twenty-four, arranged for this monument to be set up and dedicated it under the axe.
EDCS-10800423.summary: A funerary epitaph for Phileta Britta, set up by her father Dossius Claudianus.

EDCS-10800424.text_edition: \n Cornelius Primus Maecenas Aquila Maecenas Amphio maceriem \n
EDCS-10800424.translation: Cornelius Primus Maecenas Aquila Maecenas Amphio [dedicated] the wall.
EDCS-10800424.summary: A dedication of a wall by Cornelius Primus Maecenas Aquila and Maecenas Amphio.

EDCS-10800425.text_edition: \n Publius Saedius Hospes Sextus Iulius Philargurus\n
EDCS-10800425.translation: Publius Saedius Hospes [and] Sextus Iulius Philargurus.
EDCS-10800425.summary: An inscription listing two names, possibly a dedication or a list of property owners.

EDCS-10800429.text_edition: \n Soli Genio Lunae sacrum ex voto pro salute Augustorum Publius Clodius Cornelia Primus curator vikanorum Lousonnensium II IIIIIIvir Augustalis curator civium Romanorum conventus Helvetici de suo dedit\n
EDCS-10800429.translation: Sacred to Sol, the Genius, and Luna, in fulfillment of a vow for the safety of the Augusti. Publius Clodius [and] Cornelia Primus, curator of the Lousonnenses villagers, IIIIIIvir Augustalis, curator of the conventus of Roman citizens in Helvetia, gave this from their own funds.
EDCS-10800429.summary: A dedication to Sol, Genius, and Luna by officials of the Lousonnenses villagers and Roman citizens in Helvetia for the safety of the emperors.

EDCS-10800430.text_edition: \n Banira et Dolvinda et Daedalus et Tato Icari filii Suleis suis qui sic curam vestram agunt iden sic Cappo Icari filius\n
EDCS-10800430.translation: Banira and Dolvinda and Daedalus and Tato, sons of Icari, [dedicate this] to their Suleis, who take care of you in this way, and in the same way Cappo, son of Icari.
EDCS-10800430.summary: A dedication to household deities (Suleis) by several individuals, possibly a family group.

EDCS-10800431.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Toccae filius Rufus aquam \n
EDCS-10800431.translation: Gaius Julius Rufus, son of Toccae, [dedicated] the water.
EDCS-10800431.summary: A dedication of water by Gaius Julius Rufus, son of Toccae.

EDCS-10800432.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Lucanus emeritus testamento poni iussit Iulia Censorina faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800432.translation: Gaius Julius Lucanus, a veteran, ordered this to be set up in his will. Iulia Censorina took care of its construction.
EDCS-10800432.summary: A funerary monument ordered by the veteran Gaius Julius Lucanus and constructed by Iulia Censorina.

EDCS-10800435.text_edition: \n Libero Patri Cocliensi Publius Severius Lucanus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800435.translation: To Liber Pater of Coclium, Publius Severius Lucanus willingly paid [his] vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10800435.summary: A votive inscription to Liber Pater of Coclium by Publius Severius Lucanus.

EDCS-10800436.text_edition: \n ------] DOM Tit--- App Sanctin-- annorum IX \n
EDCS-10800436.translation: [...] DOM Tit[...] App Sanctin[us] [...] aged nine.
EDCS-10800436.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely commemorating a child named Sanctinus, who died at the age of nine.

EDCS-10800437.text_edition: \n quae vixit annos XXV Maturius Caratilius pater ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800437.translation: who lived for 25 years. Maturius Caratilius, [her] father, arranged for this monument to be set up.
EDCS-10800437.summary: A funerary epitaph for an unnamed woman who lived 25 years, set up by her father Maturius Caratilius.

EDCS-10800445.text_edition: \n Pro salute domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae aram Quintus Aelius Aunus IIIIIIvir Augustalis de suo item donavit vicanis nnibus |(denarios) DCCL ex quorum ussuris sic gymnasium in derecto tempore per triduum eisdem vicanis dedit in aevum quod si in alios ussus sic transferre voluerint sic hanc pecuniam incolis coloniae Aventicensium dari volo locus datus decreto vicanorum Minnodunensium\n
EDCS-10800445.translation: For the safety of the divine house, Quintus Aelius Aunus, a high priest of the Augustales, dedicated an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina at his own expense. He also donated 750 denarii to the villagers. From the interest of this sum, he established a gymnasium for them to use for three days in perpetuity. If they wish to transfer this money to other uses, I want this money to be given to the inhabitants of the colony of Aventicum, by decree of the villagers of Minnodunum.
EDCS-10800445.summary: This dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Quintus Aelius Aunus also establishes a gymnasium for the villagers of Minnodunum, funded by interest from his donation, and specifies how the funds should be used.

EDCS-10800446.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Tiberius Pomponius |(denarios) mille ex quorum usuris sive reditu hoc templum redd TRIV a vicanis L SIIN\n
EDCS-10800446.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Tiberius Pomponius, from the interest or income of one thousand denarii, restored this temple for the villagers.
EDCS-10800446.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Tiberius Pomponius, funded by the interest from a donation of 1000 denarii for the benefit of the villagers.

EDCS-10800448.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iulio Decumino et Pompeiae Reginae Iulius Valerianus fecit\n
EDCS-10800448.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, Iulius Valerianus made [this monument] for Iulius Deciminus and Pompeia Regina.
EDCS-10800448.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Iulius Valerianus for Iulius Deciminus and Pompeia Regina.

EDCS-10800449.text_edition: \n Marti Caturigi Lucius Camillius Aetolus templum a novo instituit\n
EDCS-10800449.translation: Lucius Camillius Aetolus established a new temple to Mars Caturix.
EDCS-10800449.summary: Lucius Camillius Aetolus founded a new temple dedicated to the god Mars Caturix.

EDCS-10800450.text_edition: \n Daeo Mercurio Iulia Iuliana votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800450.translation: Iulia Iuliana willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the god Mercury.
EDCS-10800450.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulia Iuliana to the god Mercury.

EDCS-10800451.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Titius Capitonius Surdo.

EDCS-10800454.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulia Festilla to the god Apollo.

EDCS-10800456.text_edition: \n Marti Augusto Caius Sentius Diadumenus medicus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800456.translation: Gaius Sentius Diadumenus, the physician, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Augustus.
EDCS-10800456.summary: This is a votive inscription by Gaius Sentius Diadumenus, a physician, to Mars Augustus.

EDCS-10800457.text_edition: \n Marti Caturigi sacrum pro salute et incolumitate Decimi Valeri Camilli Sextus Cri<s>pinius Nigrinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800457.translation: For the safety and well-being of Decimus Valerius Camillus, Sextus Crispinius Nigrinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Caturix.
EDCS-10800457.summary: Sextus Crispinius Nigrinus made a votive offering to Mars Caturix for the safety and well-being of Decimus Valerius Camillus.

EDCS-10800458.text_edition: \n Mercurio Apollini Minervae Togirix Metiae filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800458.translation: Togirix, son of Metia, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, Apollo, and Minerva.
EDCS-10800458.summary: This is a votive inscription by Togirix, son of Metia, dedicated to the gods Mercury, Apollo, and Minerva.

EDCS-10800459.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto Lucius Silanius Candidus nomine suo et Marci Silani Sabini et Titi Silvi Similis fratrum suorum ex HS nummum IIIImilibus testamento poni iussit Marcus Domitius Magnus heres ponendum curavit et eo amplius de suo adiecit HS nummum milleCCCC dona venibunt ad ornamenta eius et ex stipibus ponentur\n
EDCS-10800459.translation: To Mercury Augustus, Lucius Silanius Candidus, in his own name and in the names of his brothers Marcus Silanius Sabinus and Titus Silvius Similis, ordered this to be set up by a will from 4,000 sesterces. Marcus Domitius Magnus, the heir, arranged for its erection and added 1,400 sesterces of his own money. The gifts will be sold for its adornment and will be set up from the offerings.
EDCS-10800459.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the erection of a monument to Mercury Augustus funded by a will and additional personal contributions, with items to be sold to complete the adornment.

EDCS-10800461.text_edition: \n Victoriae Iustius Vatto votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800461.translation: Iustius Vatto willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Victory.
EDCS-10800461.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to the goddess Victory by Iustius Vatto.

EDCS-10800464.text_edition: \n SOIHS SIIS ex HS nummis IIImilibus E N Iulius heres ponendum curavit et dedicavit adiectis HS nummis CC AD\n
EDCS-10800464.translation: To the gods, from 3,000 sesterces. Julius, the heir, arranged for this to be set up and dedicated, adding 200 sesterces of his own.
EDCS-10800464.summary: This inscription records the erection and dedication of a monument by an heir, funded by a will and additional personal contributions.

EDCS-10800466.text_edition: \n Caio Flavio Camillo IIviro coloniae Helvetiorum flamini Augusti quem ordo patronum civitatis cooptavit eique ob merita eius erga rem publicam scholam et statuas decrevit vikani Eburodunenses amico et patrono\n
EDCS-10800466.translation: To Gaius Flavius Camillus, duovir of the colony of the Helvetii, flamen Augusti, whom the town council co-opted as patron of the city and decreed a school and statues for him because of his merits towards the state, the vicikani of Eburodunum [dedicate this] to their friend and patron.
EDCS-10800466.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated by the vicikani of Eburodunum to Gaius Flavius Camillus, honoring his public service and patronage.

EDCS-10800467.text_edition: \n Iuliae Cai Iuli Camilli filiae Festillae flaminicae primae Augustae vicinae optimae ob egregia eius merita vikani Eburodunenses\n
EDCS-10800467.translation: To Julia Festilla, daughter of Gaius Iulius Camillus, first flaminica Augustae, the best neighbor, the vicikani of Eburodunum [dedicate this] for her outstanding merits.
EDCS-10800467.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated by the vicikani of Eburodunum to Julia Festilla, recognizing her merits as a neighbor and priestess.

EDCS-10800469.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Genio loci Fortunae reduci Decimus Appius Augustus dedicavit\n
EDCS-10800469.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to the Genius of the place, and to Fortune the Restorer, Decimus Appius Augustus dedicated this.
EDCS-10800469.summary: This is a religious dedication by Decimus Appius Augustus to Jupiter, the Genius of the place, and Fortuna Redux.

EDCS-10800474.text_edition: \n Deae Aventiae Caius Iulius Primus Trevir curator coloniae item curator IIIIIIvirorum de suo posuit IIA RII locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-10800474.translation: To the goddess Aventia, Gaius Iulius Primus, curator of the colony and also curator of the IIIIvirate, set this up from his own funds. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10800474.summary: This inscription records a private dedication to the goddess Aventia by Gaius Iulius Primus, a colonial official, with the location provided by the town council.

EDCS-10800475.text_edition: \n Deae Aventiae Titus Tertius Severus curator coloniae idemque allector cui incolae Aventicenses primo omnium ob eius erga se merita tabulam argenteam publice posuerunt donum de sua pecunia ex HS VmilibusCC locus datus a decurionibus\n
EDCS-10800475.translation: To the goddess Aventia, Titus Tertius Severus, curator of the colony and also elector, to whom the inhabitants of Aventicum first of all publicly presented a silver tablet for his merits towards them, [dedicated this] as a gift from his own money, from 5,200 sesterces. The place was granted by the decurions.
EDCS-10800475.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Aventia by Titus Tertius Severus, a colonial official, funded by his own money and in response to a public honor.

EDCS-10800476.text_edition: \n Deae Aventiae et Genio incolarum Titus Ianuarius Florinus et Publius Domitius Didymus curatores coloniae ex stipe annua adiectis de suo |(sestertiis) nummum |(milia) D\n
EDCS-10800476.translation: To the goddess Aventia and to the Genius of the inhabitants, Titus Ianuarius Florinus and Publius Domitius Didymus, curators of the colony, [added] 5,000 sesterces from the annual offerings from their own funds.
EDCS-10800476.summary: This inscription records a joint dedication to the goddess Aventia and the Genius of the inhabitants by two colonial curators, supplementing annual offerings with their own money.

EDCS-10800477.text_edition: \n Avetae A Aug CANAE Servius Sulpicius Publius Plaut votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800477.translation: To Aveta Augusta Canae, Servius Sulpicius and Publius Plautus willingly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-10800477.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Aveta Augusta Canae by Servius Sulpicius and Publius Plautus.

EDCS-10800479.text_edition: \n Genio pagi Tigorini Publius Graccius Paternus testamento poni iussit Scribonia Lucana heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800479.translation: To the genius of the Tigorini district, Publius Graccius Paternus ordered this to be set up in his will; Scribonia Lucana, his heir, saw to its construction.
EDCS-10800479.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument set up by an heir to the genius of a local district.

EDCS-10800482.text_edition: \n Numinibus Augustorum et Genio coloniae Helvetiorum Apollini sacrum Quintus Postumius Hyginus et Postumius Hermes libertus medicis et professoribus de suo dederunt\n
EDCS-10800482.translation: To the divine powers of the Emperors and the genius of the Helvetii colony, to Apollo, Quintus Postumius Hyginus and his freedman Postumius Hermes, doctors and teachers, dedicated this from their own funds.
EDCS-10800482.summary: This inscription records a dedication to imperial deities and the genius of a colony by two doctors and teachers.

EDCS-10800483.text_edition: \n Deae Victoriae Marcus Iunius Primitius ex voto\n
EDCS-10800483.translation: To the goddess Victoria, Marcus Iunius Primitius, according to his vow.
EDCS-10800483.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the goddess Victoria.

EDCS-10800484.translation: To the goddess Victoria, Sabinia Marcella.
EDCS-10800484.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Victoria.

EDCS-10800486.text_edition: \n Camillius Iucundus X\xc2\xa0 votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800486.translation: Camillius Iucundus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10800486.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10800488.text_edition: \n Iuliae Dominae Augustae matri castrorum Helvetii publice\n
EDCS-10800488.translation: To Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the camps, on behalf of the Helvetii, publicly.
EDCS-10800488.summary: This inscription records a public dedication to Julia Domna, mother of the camps, by the people of the Helvetii.

EDCS-10800494.text_edition: \n IEIVI quaestura in provincia Asia functus est incolae Aventicenses ob egregia eius erga se merita patrono publico cui singuli adque universi obligatos se esse praeferunt adque etiam parum sibi videntur praedicare cura Titi Nigrini Modesti IIIIIIviri Augustalis\n
EDCS-10800494.translation: Having completed his quaestorship in the province of Asia, the inhabitants of Aventicum, because of his outstanding services to them, and considering themselves unable to sufficiently praise him, have appointed him their public patron, to whom they individually and collectively acknowledge themselves indebted, with the care of Titus Nigrinus Modestus, one of the IIIIvirii Augustales.
EDCS-10800494.summary: This inscription records the appointment of a former quaestor as patron of the inhabitants of Aventicum, likely in the 2nd century CE, in recognition of his services.

EDCS-10800495.text_edition: \n Donato Caesaris Augusti Salviano exactori tributorum in Helvetiis Communis vicarius\n
EDCS-10800495.translation: To Donatus, Caesar Augustus Salvianus's tax collector in the Helvetii region, from Communis, his deputy.
EDCS-10800495.summary: This inscription records a dedication to a tax collector by his deputy.

EDCS-10800496.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Cai filio Fabia Camillo sacerdoti Augusti magistro tribuno militum legionis IIII Macedonicae hasta pura et corona aurea donato a Tiberio Claudio Caesare Augusto Germanico cum ab eo evocatus in Britannia militasset colonia pia Flavia constans Emerita Helvetiorum ex decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-10800496.translation: To Gaius Julius Camillus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, priest of Augustus, master, tribune of the soldiers of the IV Macedonian Legion, honored by Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus with a pure spear and a golden crown when he served under him in Britain; by the loyal, constant, Flavian colony of the Helvetii, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10800496.summary: This inscription records a military honor awarded to Gaius Julius Camillus by Emperor Claudius, likely in the mid-1st century CE.

EDCS-10800497.text_edition: \n OV Aniensi ius miles cohortis I Montanorum civium Romanorum centuria Senecae annorum XL stipendiorum XVIII hic situs est testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-10800497.translation: OV Aniensi, soldier of the I Cohort of Montani, Roman citizens, of the century of Senecae, aged 40, with 18 years of service, is buried here; he ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-10800497.summary: This inscription records the burial and testament of a soldier in the I Cohort of Montani.

EDCS-10800499.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucius Camillius Faustus IIIIIIvir Augustalis vivus fecit in anno LXX vixit annis LXXXXII\n
EDCS-10800499.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Camillius Faustus, a Six-member official of the Augustales, made this while alive in his 70th year; he lived 92 years.
EDCS-10800499.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Camillius Faustus, recording his membership in a college and his age at death and completion of the monument.

EDCS-10800500.text_edition: \n Quinto Cluvio Quirina Macro omnibus honoribus apud suos functo cui primo omnium in duumviratu scholam et statuas ordo decrevit Helvetii publice inpendium sic remiserunt Macrius Nivalis et Macrius Macer liberi\n
EDCS-10800500.translation: Quinto Cluvius Macro, who held all offices among his people, for whom the council first decreed a school and statues in their duumvirate, the Helvetii publicly remitted the expenses, his children Macrius Nivalis and Macrius Macer.
EDCS-10800500.summary: This inscription records the remission of public expenses by the Helvetii for Quinto Cluvius Macro, a prominent local official, likely relating to the funding of public buildings or honors.

EDCS-10800501.text_edition: \n Cluvi Macri uxori Afrani Professi pronepti qui curiam donavit Helvetii publice inpendium remiserunt Macrius Nivalis et Macrius Macer liberi\n
EDCS-10800501.translation: To the wife of Cluvius Macro, great-granddaughter of Afranius Professor, who donated the curia, the Helvetii publicly remitted the expenses, his children Macrius Nivalis and Macrius Macer.
EDCS-10800501.summary: This inscription, likely a funerary monument or dedication, records the remission of public expenses by the Helvetii for the wife of Cluvius Macro, related to a donated curia.

EDCS-10800502.text_edition: \n Quinto Macrio Cluvi Macri filio Quirina Nivali omnibus honoribus apud suos functo \n
EDCS-10800502.translation: To Quinto Macrius Cluvius Macro's son, of the Quirina tribe, who held all offices among his people.
EDCS-10800502.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription honoring Quinto Macrius, son of Cluvius Macro, noting his holding of local offices.

EDCS-10800504.text_edition: \n Tiberio Iulio Tiberi filio Quirina Abucino IIviro praefecto operum publicorum flamini Augusti sacerdoti perpetuo primo omnnium patrono publico coloni Aventicenses ex aere conlato ob egregia ius erga se merita patrono\n
EDCS-10800504.translation: To Tiberius Iulius Abucinus, son of Tiberius, of the Quirina tribe, duumvir, prefect of public works, Augustalis priest, perpetual patron, first of all to receive the honor of public patron from the colonists of Aventicum for his outstanding merits towards them.
EDCS-10800504.summary: This inscription honors Tiberius Iulius Abucinus of Aventicum, listing his various civic and religious offices and recognizing him as the first public patron of the colony.

EDCS-10800509.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Otaciliae Faventinae uxori Marcus Otacilius IIIIIIvir Augustalis ibsa sic viva\n
EDCS-10800509.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Otacilius, a Six-member official of the Augustales, made this for his wife Otacilia Faventina while she was alive.
EDCS-10800509.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Marcus Otacilius, a Six-member official of the Augustales, commissioned a monument for his wife Otacilia Faventina during her lifetime.

EDCS-10800510.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Paulini-- Sapid-- IIIIIIvir- Augustal--- Paulinius Primitius filius et Donatus libertus faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10800510.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Paulinius Primitius, son [of Paulinius], a Six-member official of the Augustales, and Donatus, a freedman, had this made.
EDCS-10800510.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Paulinius Primitius and his freedman Donatus commissioned a monument for a deceased member of the Augustales college.

EDCS-10800512.text_edition: \n Caio Valerio Cai filio Fabia Camillo quoi sic publice funus Haeduorum civitas et Helvetii decreverunt et civitas Helvetiorum qua pagatim qua publice statuas decrevit Iulia Cai Iuli Camilli filia Festilla ex testamento\n
EDCS-10800512.translation: To Gaius Valerius Camillus, son of Gaius, of the Fabia tribe, for whom the state of the Haedui and the Helvetii publicly decreed funeral rites, and the Helvetian state, both by village and publicly, decreed statues, erected by Iulia Festilla, daughter of Gaius Iulius Camillus, according to his will.
EDCS-10800512.summary: This inscription records that Gaius Valerius Camillus was honored with public funeral rites and statues by the Haedui and Helvetii, with the monument erected by his daughter Iulia Festilla.

EDCS-10800513.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Valeriae Seccae quae iucunde vixit annis LXV Lucius Severius Martius IIIIIIvir Augustalis maritus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800513.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Severius Martius, a Six-member official of the Augustales, saw to the making of this for his wife Valeria Secca, who lived pleasantly for 65 years.
EDCS-10800513.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Valeria Secca, recording her age at death and that her husband, Lucius Severius Martius, a Six-member official of the Augustales, commissioned the monument.

EDCS-10800514.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Severiae Martiolae Severius Marcianus frater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800514.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Severius Marcianus, brother, had this made for Severia Martiola.
EDCS-10800514.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Severius Marcianus commissioned a monument for his sister Severia Martiola.

EDCS-10800523.text_edition: \n Pompeiano et Avito consulibus Kalendis Augustis\n
EDCS-10800523.translation: In the consulship of Pompeianus and Avitus, on the Kalends of August.
EDCS-10800523.summary: This inscription records a date: August 1, AD 207.

EDCS-10800524.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription, stating that Prosthasius erected the monument.

EDCS-10800531.text_edition: \n Aeliae Modestinae quae vixit annis II menses VI Aelius Cladaeus et Caninia Modestina parentes filiae dulcissimae posuerunt\n
EDCS-10800531.translation: Aelius Cladaeus and Caninia Modestina set this up for their sweetest daughter, Aelia Modestina, who lived for 2 years and 6 months.
EDCS-10800531.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl, Aelia Modestina, set up by her parents.

EDCS-10800532.translation: To the departed spirits of Marcus Alpinus Virilis.
EDCS-10800532.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the memory of Marcus Alpinus Virilis.

EDCS-10800533.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a funerary monument, mentioning names.

EDCS-10800534.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flaviae Severillae quae vixit annos XXXVI Flavius Severinus coniux coniugi faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800534.translation: Flavius Severinus erected this for his wife, Flavia Severilla, who lived for 36 years.
EDCS-10800534.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Severilla, erected by her husband.

EDCS-10800535.translation: To the departed spirits of Hibernial[ia] Valentina.
EDCS-10800535.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Hibernialia Valentina.

EDCS-10800537.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Decimi Iuli Iuni Iulia Titullina uxor\n
EDCS-10800537.translation: Iulia Titullina, wife [of?], to Decimus Iulius Iunius.
EDCS-10800537.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly a dedication from a wife to her deceased husband, Decimus Iulius Iunius.

EDCS-10800538.text_edition: \n Iuliae Censorinae Cnaeus Iulius Caupius pater\n
EDCS-10800538.translation: To Iulia Censorina, [from her] father Gnaeus Iulius Caupius.
EDCS-10800538.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely a dedication from a father to his daughter, Iulia Censorina.

EDCS-10800539.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titi Nigri Saturnini Saturninia Gannica liberta et coniunx faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800539.translation: Saturninia Gannica, freedwoman and wife, saw to the making of this for Titus Niger Saturninus.
EDCS-10800539.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Niger Saturninus, erected by his freedwoman and wife.

EDCS-10800540.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Pompeiae Gemellae Pompeia Dionysias et Primus Augusti nostri educatrici \n
EDCS-10800540.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Pompeia Gemella. Pompeia Dionysias and Primus placed this on behalf of their 'nurse' (or foster mother), Augusti nostri.
EDCS-10800540.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeia Gemella, set up by Pompeia Dionysias and Primus, likely former slaves of the household, dedicating it to their 'nurse' who was also possibly associated with the imperial household.

EDCS-10800543.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Gaius Laelius, possibly a dedication or an honorific. Dating is uncertain due to its fragmentary nature.

EDCS-10800550.text_edition: \n Marti sacrum Titus Frontinius Genialis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800550.translation: Sacred to Mars. Titus Frontinius Genialis willingly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10800550.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mars by Titus Frontinius Genialis, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10800551.text_edition: \n Nariae Nousantiae Titus Frontinius Hibernus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800551.translation: To Naria Nousantia. Titus Frontinius Hibernus willingly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10800551.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Naria Nousantia by Titus Frontinius Hibernus, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-10800553.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus - Severi Commendati dendrophori Augustia Asinula coniux faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800553.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Augustia Asinula, wife, arranged for this to be made for Severus Commendatus, a dendrophorus (tree-bearer).
EDCS-10800553.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Severus Commendatus, a dendrophorus, arranged by his wife Augustia Asinula.

EDCS-10800554.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Camillius Polynices natione Lydus artis aurifex corporis fabrum tignuariorum apud eosdem omnibus honoribus functus us vixit nnos LX et Camillio Paulo filio eiusdem artis et corporis qui vixit annos aetatis XXXIII\n
EDCS-10800554.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Camillius Polynices, a Lydian by nation, a goldsmith by trade, who served with all honors among the carpenters and timbersmiths of the same guild, lived 60 years. And to his son, Camillius Paulus, of the same trade and guild, who lived 33 years of age.
EDCS-10800554.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Camillius Polynices and his son Camillius Paulus, detailing their professions as goldsmith and carpenter/timsersmith respectively, and their ages at death.

EDCS-10800555.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flaviae Pusinnae uxori karissimae ac pudicae piissimae quae vixit nnis XVIII diebus IIII Otacilius Thesaeus perinde karissimus maritus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800555.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Flavia Pusinna, his dearest, chaste, and most dutiful wife, who lived 18 years and 4 days. Otacilius Thesaeus, her equally dearest husband, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10800555.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavia Pusinna, set up by her husband Otacilius Thesaeus, emphasizing her virtues and young age at death.

EDCS-10800556.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Matidiae Pusinnae quae vixit annos XXV- Matidius Pervincus pater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800556.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Matidia Pusinna, who lived 25 years. Matidius Pervincus, her father, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10800556.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Matidia Pusinna, set up by her father Matidius Pervincus, recording her age at death.

EDCS-10800557.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Pompeiae Hospitae feminae sanctissimae quae vixit nnos XXXII Geminius Victullus coniugi incomparabili faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800557.translation: To the Divine Spirits. To Pompeia Hospita, a most virtuous woman, who lived 32 years. Geminius Victullus arranged for this to be made for his incomparable wife.
EDCS-10800557.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pompeia Hospita, set up by her husband Geminius Victullus, highlighting her virtue and their marital bond.

EDCS-10800565.translation: To the goddess Artio. Licinia Sabinilla.
EDCS-10800565.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Artio by Licinia Sabinilla.

EDCS-10800566.text_edition: \n Deae Nariae regio Arurensis curante Feroce liberto\n
EDCS-10800566.translation: To the goddess Naria, the Arurensian region, under the care of Ferox, freedman.
EDCS-10800566.summary: A dedication to the goddess Naria by a freedman named Ferox, likely from the Arurensis region.

EDCS-10800568.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto Sextus Taanincanus ex voto pecunia sua fecit\n
EDCS-10800568.translation: Sextus Taanincanus made this to Mercury Augustus, according to his vow, with his own money.
EDCS-10800568.summary: A dedication to Mercury Augustus made by Sextus Taanincanus using his own funds, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10800570.translation: To Melissus, Caprasius made this for his son.
EDCS-10800570.summary: A dedication to Melissus by Caprasius on behalf of his son.

EDCS-10800571.text_edition: \n Numini Augustorum via ducta per Marcum Dunium Paternum IIvirum coloniae Helvetiorum\n
EDCS-10800571.translation: To the divine will of the Emperors, for the aqueduct constructed by Marcus Dunius Paternus, IIvir of the colony of the Helvetii.
EDCS-10800571.summary: An inscription related to an aqueduct construction project overseen by Marcus Dunius Paternus, a magistrate in the colony of the Helvetii.

EDCS-10800572.translation: Silvanus Victorinus made this during his lifetime.
EDCS-10800572.summary: A self-funded dedication made by Silvanus Victorinus during his lifetime.

EDCS-10800573.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Florentina vixit nnos C Tiberius Sanctius Ingens coniux faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800573.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Florentina lived 100 years. Tiberius Sanctius Ingens, her husband, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10800573.summary: A funerary monument for Florentina, who lived to 100 years, erected by her husband Tiberius Sanctius Ingens.

EDCS-10800574.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Apollini Augusto Titus Crassicius Pattusius templum de suo donum dedit\n
EDCS-10800574.translation: In honor of the divine house, Titus Crassicius Pattusius dedicated a temple to Apollo Augustus as a gift from his own resources.
EDCS-10800574.summary: Titus Crassicius Pattusius dedicated a temple to Apollo Augustus as a gift, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-10800575.text_edition: \n Deae Eponae Marcus Aurelius Aprilius Restio miles legionis XXII Antoninianae Primigeniae piae fidelis immunis consularis curas agens vico Saloduro XIII Kalendas Septembres Imperatore domino nostro Antonino Augusto II et Sacerdote II consulibus votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10800575.translation: To the goddess Epona, Marcus Aurelius Aprilius Restio, a soldier of the XXII Legion Antoniniana Primigenia, pious, faithful, exempt, serving as consular legate, carrying out duties in the vicus of Salodurum, on the 13th day before the Kalends of September, during the consulship of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus II and Sacerdos II, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10800575.summary: A soldier, Marcus Aurelius Aprilius Restio, dedicated a vow to the goddess Epona in the vicus of Salodurum during the consulship of Antoninus II and Sacerdos II.

EDCS-10800576.text_edition: \n Genio publico in honorem domus divinae aram cum signo Suecconius Demecenus de suo posuit Imperatore domino nostro Antonino II et Sacerdote II consulibus\n
EDCS-10800576.translation: To the public genius, in honor of the divine house, Suecconius Demecenus placed an altar with a symbol at his own expense, during the consulship of our lord Emperor Antoninus II and Sacerdos II.
EDCS-10800576.summary: Suecconius Demecenus dedicated an altar to the public genius, honoring the imperial family, during the consulship of Antoninus II and Sacerdos II.

EDCS-10800577.summary: A dedication to Jupiter by Decimanus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10800578.text_edition: \n Laribus Augustis Marcus Valerius Marci libertus Zethus Lucius Marius Luci libertus Privatus Quintus Quintus Vassi Quinti liberti Zethus et Clarus de suo fecerunt\n
EDCS-10800578.translation: Marcus Valerius Zethus, freedman of Lucius Marius, and Quintus Privatus, freedman of Vasius, and Clarus Zethus, freedman of Quintus, made this at their own expense for the Augustan Lares.
EDCS-10800578.summary: This is a dedication to the Augustan Lares made by three freedmen at their own expense, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10800579.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto Valerius Hispanus IIIIIIvir Augustalis Luguduni exs sic voto\n
EDCS-10800579.translation: To Mercury Augustus, Valerius Hispanus, one of the six priests of the Augustan cult at Lugdunum, by vow.
EDCS-10800579.summary: This is a votive offering to Mercury Augustus by a local priest from Lugdunum (modern Lyon), likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10800582.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Parduliani Ripari filii qui vixit nnos X Quieta mater et Principalis frater et pater supra scriptus faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10800582.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Quieta, his mother, and Principalis, his brother, and his father, who is named above, arranged for this to be made for Pardulianus Riparius, who lived for 10 years.
EDCS-10800582.summary: This is a funerary monument for a boy named Pardulianus Riparius, who died at the age of 10, arranged by his mother, brother, and father, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800583.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Luci Crassici Corbulonis IIIIIIviri Auggustalis Publii Primus et Seccalus filii eius ponendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10800583.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: his sons Publius Primus and Seccalus arranged for this to be placed for Lucius Crassicius Corbulonis, a priest of the Augustan cult.
EDCS-10800583.summary: This is a funerary monument for Lucius Crassicius Corbulonis, a local priest, arranged by his sons, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800584.text_edition: \n Tito Crassicio Avito filio annorum XXXV\n
EDCS-10800584.translation: To Titus Crassicius Avitus, son, aged 35 years.
EDCS-10800584.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Crassicius Avitus, who died at the age of 35, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800585.translation: To Caia Decima, by Decimus Decimanus, her brother.
EDCS-10800585.summary: This is a tombstone for Caia Decima, dedicated by her brother, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800586.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sexti Iuni Maiorini filii eius curaverunt\n
EDCS-10800586.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: his son arranged for this to be made for Sextus Iunius Maiorinus.
EDCS-10800586.summary: This is a funerary monument for Sextus Iunius Maiorinus, arranged by his son, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800587.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: his son arranged for this to be made for Sextus Iunius Maiorinus.
EDCS-10800587.summary: This is a funerary monument for Sextus Iunius Maiorinus, arranged by his son, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800588.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Memorinae Severianus pater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800588.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Severianus, his father, arranged for this to be made for Memorina.
EDCS-10800588.summary: This is a funerary monument for Memorina, arranged by her father, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800589.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Severi curaverunt fratres eius\n
EDCS-10800589.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: his brothers arranged for this to be made for Severus.
EDCS-10800589.summary: This is a funerary monument for Severus, arranged by his brothers, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10800590.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus vivi fecerunt Statili Aproni Matugeniae Marcellinae Statili Paterni\n
EDCS-10800590.translation: The living [Statilius Apronius and Matugenia Marcellina] dedicated this to the Divine Shades for Statilius Paternus.
EDCS-10800590.summary: A funerary dedication for Statilius Paternus by living relatives, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10800596.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae Cinneni Secundi vixit annos XXI menses VIII Cinnenius Secunnus sic filius et nnenius Secundinus frater faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10800596.translation: To the Divine Shades and memory of Cinnennius Secundus, who lived 21 years and 8 months. Cinnenius Secunnus, his son, and Cinnenius Secundinus, his brother, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-10800596.summary: A funerary monument for Cinnennius Secundus, erected by his son and brother, indicating a life cut short in youth.

EDCS-10800597.text_edition: \n D(is)? M(anibus) et memoriae Rogatini Romuli fratris Senati Romani interceptus vixit annos XXV Sat Aventina et Sat Senatus patres posuerunt\n
EDCS-10800597.translation: To the Divine Shades and memory of Rogatinus Romulus, brother of Senatus Romanus, intercepted [in death]. He lived 25 years. Aventina Sat and Senatus Sat, his parents, erected this.
EDCS-10800597.summary: A funerary dedication for Rogatinus Romulus, who died at age 25, by his parents.

EDCS-10800598.text_edition: \n Dianae sacrum Stllaccius filius us veteranus legionis T \n
EDCS-10800598.translation: Sacred to Diana. Stllaccius, son of Stllacius, a veteran of the Legio X [Gemina], [dedicated this].
EDCS-10800598.summary: A dedication to the goddess Diana by a veteran of Legio X Gemina, likely erected during his lifetime or shortly after his death.

EDCS-10800600.text_edition: \n Imperatore Tito Vespasiano Caesare Augusto VII consule Marti Apollini Minervae arcum vicani Vindonissenses curantibus Tito Urbanio Mattoni Tito Valerio Albano Lucio Veturio Melo Caio Cottio Rufo Quinto Sextio \n
EDCS-10800600.translation: During the consulship of Emperor Titus Vespasianus Caesar Augustus (for the 7th time), the villagers of Vindonissa arranged for this arch to be made for Mars, Apollo, and Minerva, under the supervision of Titus Urbanus Mattonus, Titus Valerius Albanus, Lucius Veturtius Melos, and Gaius Cottius Rufus.
EDCS-10800600.summary: A public works dedication for an arch honoring Mars, Apollo, and Minerva, commissioned by the villagers of Vindonissa during the reign of Vespasian.

EDCS-10800602.text_edition: \n Aram Avertentibus Marcus Mas Ter miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Crispi libens posuit\n
EDCS-10800602.translation: Marcus Masterus, a soldier of the Legio XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Crispus, willingly placed this altar for the gods who avert [evil].
EDCS-10800602.summary: A dedication of an altar to protective deities by a soldier of Legio XI Claudia, likely during his service.

EDCS-10800603.text_edition: \n Quadr<i=U>vis pro se et suis votum solvit Quintus Nicennius us veteranus legionis I-- fecit libens merito \n
EDCS-10800603.translation: Quintus Nicennius, a veteran of Legio I [Germanica?], paid his vow for himself and his family, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10800603.summary: A votive offering for Quintus Nicennius and his family, made by him as a veteran of Legio I.

EDCS-10800611.text_edition: \n Caius Allius Cai filius Pomptina Oriens domo Dertona |(centurio) legionis XIII geminae\n
EDCS-10800611.translation: Gaius Allius Oriens, son of Gaius, from Dertona, a centurion of Legio XIII Gemina, [from the tribe] Pomptina.
EDCS-10800611.summary: An epigraphic record identifying Gaius Allius Oriens, a centurion of Legio XIII Gemina, with his tribal affiliation and origin.

EDCS-10800612.text_edition: \n Marcus Apronius Marci f<i=V>lius V<ol=IV>(tinia) S Secundus Luco Augusti miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Veli Fusci nnrum XXXVII stipendiorum XVII hic situs est testamento fieri iussit heredes faciundum curaverunt \n
EDCS-10800612.translation: Marcus Apronius Secundus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Luco Augusti, a soldier of the Legio XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Velus Fuscus, 37 years old and 17 years of service, lies here. He ordered this to be made by his will, and his heirs arranged for it to be done.
EDCS-10800612.summary: A funerary monument for Marcus Apronius Secundus, a soldier of Legio XI Claudia who died at 37 after 17 years of service, erected by his heirs as per his will.

EDCS-10800613.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Hymno medico legionis XXI Claudiae Quietae eius Atticus patronus\n
EDCS-10800613.translation: To Tiberius Claudius Hymnus, doctor of the Legio XXI Rapax, his patron Atticus [dedicated this].
EDCS-10800613.summary: A dedication to Tiberius Claudius Hymnus, a doctor serving in Legio XXI Rapax, by his patron Atticus.

EDCS-10800614.text_edition: \n Marco Iulio Marci filio Quirina Maximo Augusto Nemeto militi legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis stipendiorum VIII structorus Vegetus miles legionis eiusdem heres eius fecit\n
EDCS-10800614.translation: To Marcus Julius Maximus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, with 8 years of service, Vegetus, a soldier of the same legion, his heir, made this.
EDCS-10800614.summary: A soldier's heir erects a monument to a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis with 8 years of service.

EDCS-10800615.translation: Quintus Lucilius Pudens, son of Quintus, of the Voturia tribe, from Bergomum, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Gellus Agricola, aged 33, with 14 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-10800615.summary: The heir of Quintus Lucilius Pudens, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis aged 33 with 14 years of service, arranged for his burial monument.

EDCS-10800616.text_edition: \n Marcus Magius Marci Poblilia Maccaus Verona miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Marci Modesti nnorum XXXIII ex testamento heredes faciendum curaverunt Lucius Ennius Secundus Quintus Romanius Verecundus hic situs est\n
EDCS-10800616.translation: Marcus Magius Maccaus, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, from Verona, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Marcus Modestus, aged 33, by his will his heirs had this made; Lucius Ennius Secundus and Quintus Romanius Verecundus are buried here.
EDCS-10800616.summary: Heirs of Marcus Magius Maccaus, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis aged 33, fulfilled his will by erecting his tombstone.

EDCS-10800618.text_edition: \n Lucius Titennius Luci filius Lemonia Victorinus Bononia miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Valeriana nnum XXV stipendiorum V heres testamento faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800618.translation: Lucius Titennius Victorinus, son of Lucius, of the Lemonia tribe, from Bononia, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the Valeriana century, aged 25, with 5 years of service, his heir had this made by his will.
EDCS-10800618.summary: The heir of Lucius Titennius Victorinus, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis aged 25 with 5 years of service, arranged for his tombstone to be made according to his will.

EDCS-10800619.text_edition: \n Caius Valerius Cai filius Voltinia Campanus Vienna miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria olni nnrum stipendiorum XI testamento fieri iussit Caius Cominius Nemausus heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800619.translation: Caius Valerius Campanus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vienna, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Volnius, aged [---], with 11 years of service, ordered by his will that this be made; Caius Cominius Nemausus, his heir, had this made.
EDCS-10800619.summary: The heir of Caius Valerius Campanus, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis with 11 years of service, fulfilled his will by erecting his tombstone.

EDCS-10800620.text_edition: \n Lucio Vecnatio Pollia Maximo Foro Corneli miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Gusori nnorum XLVIII stipendiorum hic situs est Gaius Roscius Omullus heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800620.translation: To Lucius Vecnatius Maximus, of the Pollia tribe, from Forum Corneli, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Gusorius, aged 48, with [---] years of service, is buried here; Gaius Roscius Omullus, his heir, had this made.
EDCS-10800620.summary: The heir of Lucius Vecnatius Maximus, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis aged 48, arranged for his burial monument.

EDCS-10800621.text_edition: \n Caius Vegelo Cai filius Aniensi Rufus Cremona miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Metti Firmi nnorum XL stipendiorum XXI hic situs est sit tibi terra levis Caius Graccius Saturninus heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800621.translation: Caius Vegelo Rufus, son of Caius, of the Aniensi tribe, from Cremona, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, in the century of Mettius Firmus, aged 40, with 21 years of service, is buried here; may the earth lie lightly upon you. Caius Graccius Saturninus, his heir, had this made.
EDCS-10800621.summary: The heir of Caius Vegelo Rufus, a soldier of the legion XI Claudia Pia Fidelis aged 40 with 21 years of service, arranged for his burial monument with a wish for peace.

EDCS-10800627.translation: Attilius made this; he conquered Cexa.
EDCS-10800627.summary: Attilius erected this monument, possibly commemorating a victory or athletic achievement, possibly related to the name Cexa.

EDCS-10800631.text_edition: \n Iuliae Venustae Tiberius Iulius Secundus libertae suae de se bene meritae\n
EDCS-10800631.translation: To Julia Venusta, from Tiberius Julius Secundus, for his freedwoman who deserved well of him.
EDCS-10800631.summary: Tiberius Julius Secundus dedicated this monument to his freedwoman, Julia Venusta, for her good service.

EDCS-10800637.text_edition: \n Deae Isidi templum a solo Lucius Annusius Magianus de suo posuit vikanis Aquensibus ad cuius templi ornamenta Alpinia Alpinula coniunx et Peregrina filia |(denarios) C dederunt locus datus decreto vicanorum\n
EDCS-10800637.translation: Lucius Annusius Magianus personally placed this temple to the goddess Isis from the ground up; for the villagers of Aquae; for the adornment of this temple, Alpinia Alpinula, his wife, and Peregrina, his daughter, gave 100 denarii; the site was granted by decree of the villagers.
EDCS-10800637.summary: Lucius Annusius Magianus funded and built a temple to Isis for the villagers of Aquae, with additional contributions from his wife and daughter, on a site approved by the villagers.

EDCS-10800638.text_edition: \n Deo Marti Militari Legenti REGLY BENIGNES\n
EDCS-10800638.translation: To the Soldier God Mars, Regly Benignes.
EDCS-10800638.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars Militaris, likely by a soldier named Regly Benignes, with the date inferable from the style of the inscription.

EDCS-10800639.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or a funerary marker, to Rinioni, son of Boltius.

EDCS-10800640.text_edition: \n Mercurio Matutino pondo |(unciae) |(novem) |(semuncia) |(scripula) VII Gai Helvi Privati\n
EDCS-10800640.translation: To Mercury Matutinus, nine ounces, a half-ounce, and seven scruples. By Gaius Helvius Privatus.
EDCS-10800640.summary: This inscription records a votive offering of a specific weight to Mercury Matutinus by Gaius Helvius Privatus.

EDCS-10800642.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Tiberius Cassius Sanctus et Tiberius Sancteius Valens posuerunt e visu libentes\n
EDCS-10800642.translation: Tiberius Cassius Sanctus and Tiberius Sancteius Valens gladly set this up to the Unconquered God, having seen a vision.
EDCS-10800642.summary: This is a dedication to the Unconquered God (likely Sol Invictus or Mithras) by Tiberius Cassius Sanctus and Tiberius Sancteius Valens, who claimed to have received a vision.

EDCS-10800644.text_edition: \n Marci filio Voltinia Certo domo Vienna veterano legionis XIII Geminae et Amianthus liberti et heredes fecerunt\n
EDCS-10800644.translation: For Marcus, son of Marcus, Certo of the Voltinian tribe, from Vienna, a veteran of the 13th Gemina legion, his freedmen and heirs, Amianthus and others, made this.
EDCS-10800644.summary: This funerary monument was erected by freedmen and heirs for Marcus Certo, a veteran of the 13th Gemina legion from Vienna.

EDCS-10800645.text_edition: \n iugiacus filius Pollia Super Pollentia miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Saeni imi nnm XXXI\n
EDCS-10800645.translation: Iugiacus, son of Iugiacus, of the Pollia tribe, from Super Pollentia, a soldier of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, in the century of Saenius, aged 31.
EDCS-10800645.summary: This is a military inscription recording the name, tribal affiliation, origin, legion, century, and age of a soldier named Iugiacus.

EDCS-10800646.text_edition: \n Quintus Valerius Quinti filius Fabia Libens Brixia miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Attieni Maximi IX\n
EDCS-10800646.translation: Quintus Valerius Libens, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, from Brixia, a soldier of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, in the century of Attienus Maximus, [serving his] 9th [year? or rank?].
EDCS-10800646.summary: This military inscription identifies Quintus Valerius Libens, a soldier of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, noting his origin and century.

EDCS-10800649.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus hic situs est Lucius Aelius Urbicus qui vixit anno uno mensibus V diebus V Unio Augusti libertus praepositus stationis Turicensis XL Galliarum et Aelia Secundina parentes dulcissimo filio\n
EDCS-10800649.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Here lies Lucius Aelius Urbicus, who lived for one year, five months, and five days. Unio, a freedman of Augustus, prefect of the supply post of Turicensis XL Galliarum, and Aelia Secundina, his parents, [set this up] for their dearest son.
EDCS-10800649.summary: This is a touching funerary epitaph for a child, Lucius Aelius Urbicus, set up by his parents, one of whom held a significant administrative position in Gaul.

EDCS-10800650.translation: Flavius Areobindus Dagalai(f)us Areobindus, illustrious man, formerly count of the sacred stable and master of the soldiers throughout the East, ordinary consul.
EDCS-10800650.summary: This is a career summary inscription for Flavius Areobindus Dagalai(f)us Areobindus, detailing his high-ranking military and administrative offices, including ordinary consul.

EDCS-10800652.text_edition: \n Cocceius Provincialis signo Eulogius visu libens laetus posuit pro se suisque omnibus\n
EDCS-10800652.translation: Cocceius Provincialis, by the name Eulogius, gladly and joyfully set this up in a vision for himself and all his family.
EDCS-10800652.summary: This inscription records a personal dedication made by Cocceius Provincialis (named Eulogius) for himself and his family, prompted by a vision.

EDCS-10800663.text_edition: \n Mercurio Marcus et Quintus? Sanucii Atti Sanuci filii Quirina Messor et Maelo ex voto quod pater eorum susceperat\n
EDCS-10800663.translation: To Mercury, Marcus and Quintus, sons of Atti Sanuci, Quirina, Messor and Maelo, fulfilling the vow that their father had undertaken.
EDCS-10800663.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by two individuals, likely brothers, fulfilling a vow made by their father.

EDCS-10800664.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto Quintus Attius Messor votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800664.translation: Quintus Attius Messor willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury Augustus.
EDCS-10800664.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Mercury Augustus by Quintus Attius Messor.

EDCS-10800665.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto sacrum Lucius <C=G>iltius Celtilli filius Quirina Cossus IIIIIIvir Augustalis loco dato decreto decurionum \n
EDCS-10800665.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus, Lucius Ciltius, son of Celtillus, Quirina, Cossus, a six-man official of the Augustales, in a place granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10800665.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to Mercury Augustus by Lucius Ciltius Cossus, an Augustalis, on land granted by local officials.

EDCS-10800667.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication to the Unconquered God by Secundus.

EDCS-10800674.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Valentis Mucaporae fili nnorum XIII Mucapora veteranus pater ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800674.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Valens, son of Mucapora, aged thirteen. Mucapora, the veteran father, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10800674.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Valens, a thirteen-year-old, set up by his father, Mucapora, a veteran.

EDCS-10800681.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio SuaD3? do ex civitate Biturigum \n
EDCS-10800681.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Caius Suadodus, from the territory of the Bituriges.
EDCS-10800681.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Spirits of the Departed for Caius Suadodus, who came from the region of the Bituriges.

EDCS-10800682.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tiberi Ingenui Sattonis et Sabiniani fili medici C\n
EDCS-10800682.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Tiberius Ingenui, son of Sattonis, and Sabinianus, a physician.
EDCS-10800682.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Spirits of the Departed for Tiberius Ingenui, son of Sattonis, and also mentions Sabinianus, a physician.

EDCS-10800683.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Adiantoni Toutio et Marulinae Maruli coniugi Adledus et Adnamtus filii eorum ponendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-10800683.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Adianton, husband of Toutius, and Marulina. Adledus and Adnamtus, their sons, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10800683.summary: This tombstone inscription is dedicated to Adianton and his wife Marulina by their sons, Adledus and Adnamtus.

EDCS-10800684.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Attonio Aproniano Lucius Carassounius Panturo fratri\n
EDCS-10800684.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Marcus Attonius Apronianus. Lucius Carassounius Panturus, for his brother.
EDCS-10800684.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Spirits of the Departed for Marcus Attonius Apronianus, set up by his brother Lucius Carassounius Panturus.

EDCS-10800685.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Publio Aulio Memuso Prittusa Liberi fratri pientissimo ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800685.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. For Publius Aulius Memusus, for his most devoted brother Liberius. He arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10800685.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Spirits of the Departed for Publius Aulius Memusus, set up by his brother Liberius.

EDCS-10800686.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Bellinus, son of Divixtus.
EDCS-10800686.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Bellinus, son of Divixtus, dedicated to the gods of the underworld.

EDCS-10800687.text_edition: \n Blandus Vindaluconis hic situs est filii pro pietate pos<u=I>erunt \n
EDCS-10800687.translation: Blandus, son of Vindaluco, lies here; his children placed this out of dutiful affection.
EDCS-10800687.summary: A tombstone recording that Blandus, son of Vindaluco, is buried here, with the monument erected by his children.

EDCS-10800689.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Castio Peregrino Castia coniux fecit\n
EDCS-10800689.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Castius Peregrinus; his wife Castia made this.
EDCS-10800689.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Castius Peregrinus by his wife Castia.

EDCS-10800690.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Comus, for eternal remembrance.
EDCS-10800690.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Comus for eternal memory.

EDCS-10800691.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Ioincatia Nundina.
EDCS-10800691.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Ioincatia Nundina.

EDCS-10800693.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Marcus Iulius [---]mo.
EDCS-10800693.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Iulius, with part of the name missing.

EDCS-10800694.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai libertus Fecu annorum L hic situs est Urbana Iulia filia posuit patri pietatis causa\n
EDCS-10800694.translation: Gaius Julius Fecu, freedman of Gaius, aged 50 years, lies here; his daughter Urbana Iulia placed this for her father out of dutiful affection.
EDCS-10800694.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Julius Fecu, a freedman, erected by his daughter Urbana Iulia.

EDCS-10800695.translation: For Marinus, son of Cossus, Attilius [dedicated this].
EDCS-10800695.summary: A dedication, likely funerary, for Marinus, son of Cossus, by Attilius.
