EDCS-10800696.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Masucon, for his brother Liber.
EDCS-10800696.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by Liber to his brother Masucon.

EDCS-10800698.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus aeternae memoriae Sabinus vixit nnos LXV\n
EDCS-10800698.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Sabinus, for eternal remembrance; he lived 65 years.
EDCS-10800698.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the name, age at death, and eternal remembrance for Sabinus.

EDCS-10800699.text_edition: \n Tettonis Omulli filii occissi in Vocrullo Visurix mater ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800699.translation: Visurix, mother of Tettonis, son of Omullus, who was killed at Vocrullus, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10800699.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a mother for her son killed in battle.

EDCS-10800712.translation: To the spirits of the departed. In this tomb rests in peace the good memory of Baudoaldus, who lived for 55 years and died on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-10800712.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Baudoaldus, recording his age and date of death.

EDCS-10800713.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription for Radoara.

EDCS-10800715.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cai Induti Sallustiani C(audia) Victorinia coniunx\n
EDCS-10800715.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caudia Victorinia, wife of Cai Indutius Sallustianus.
EDCS-10800715.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a tomb to Cai Indutius Sallustianus by his wife.

EDCS-10800716.text_edition: \n Prima Cai Cotei liberta nnorum XVI et soror ill<i=AE>us Araurica nnula et mensium VI hic sitae sunt patronus posuit \n
EDCS-10800716.translation: Prima, freedwoman of Cai Coteius, aged 16 years, and her sister Araurica, aged 1 year and 6 months, are buried here; their patron set them up.
EDCS-10800716.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of a freedwoman, Prima, and her sister, Araurica, placed by their patron.

EDCS-10800717.text_edition: \n Tauricus Carati de suo donum dedit\n
EDCS-10800717.translation: Tauricus Carati gave this gift of his own accord.
EDCS-10800717.summary: This is a dedication of a gift made by Tauricus Carati.

EDCS-10800719.text_edition: \n Apollini Granno Mogouno aram Quintus Licinius Trio de suo dedit\n
EDCS-10800719.translation: Quintus Licinius Trio gave this altar to Apollo Grannus Mogounus of his own accord.
EDCS-10800719.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating an altar to Apollo Grannus Mogounus by Quintus Licinius Trio.

EDCS-10800720.summary: This is a dedication of a monument to Apollo by Boudillus.

EDCS-10800721.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deae Victoriae pro salute vicanorum Cetturo Induti votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800721.translation: In honor of the divine house, Cetturo Induti paid his vow willingly and deservedly to the Goddess Victoria for the safety of the villagers.
EDCS-10800721.summary: This is a votive inscription by Cetturo Induti to the Goddess Victoria for the well-being of the villagers and in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-10800722.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae aram Birrius Martius de suo dedit\n
EDCS-10800722.translation: In honor of the divine house, Birrius Martius dedicated this altar of his own accord.
EDCS-10800722.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to the imperial cult by Birrius Martius.

EDCS-10800724.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His mother made this for Firmus.
EDCS-10800724.summary: This funerary epitaph records that a mother dedicated a monument to her son, Firmus.

EDCS-10800725.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Maccio PaternIano et Tertio Divixto\n
EDCS-10800725.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Maccius Paternianus and Tertius Divixtus.
EDCS-10800725.summary: This funerary epitaph records a dedication to Maccius Paternianus and Tertius Divixtus.

EDCS-10800726.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pa Suavis.
EDCS-10800726.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name Pa Suavis.

EDCS-10800727.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Prittillius Banucanis Natalis Lutonis de suo donavit\n
EDCS-10800727.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Prittillius Banucanis donated this at his own expense, on behalf of Natalis Lutonis.
EDCS-10800727.summary: This funerary epitaph records a donation made by Prittillius Banucanis for Natalis Lutonis.

EDCS-10800728.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Saci.
EDCS-10800728.summary: This funerary epitaph records the name Saci.

EDCS-10800729.summary: This inscription records the name Geta Decemberus.

EDCS-10800735.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo fontem et aram Titus Pompeius Nocturnus plumbarius votum solvit libens merito Dedicata Chilone et Libone consulibus cuiius aquam inde duxit usque villam Flaviacam tubo plumbeo TAR numero DX\n
EDCS-10800735.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Titus Pompeius Nocturnus, a plumber, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to provide a spring and an altar. Dedicated when Chilone and Libo were consuls. He led the water from it to the Flaviacan villa through a lead pipe, number 50.
EDCS-10800735.summary: This votive inscription records the dedication of a spring and altar to Jupiter by Titus Pompeius Nocturnus, including details about the water supply and consuls of an unspecified date.

EDCS-10800736.text_edition: \n Publius Valerius Salu EV TRIB VII\n
EDCS-10800736.translation: Publius Valerius Salvu[s?], tribune of the seventh legion.
EDCS-10800736.summary: This inscription records the name and rank of Publius Valerius Salvu[s?], a tribune of the seventh legion.

EDCS-10800737.summary: This inscription records the name and age of Saturninus Boudilli.

EDCS-10800738.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gai Vindilli Adiovi heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800738.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Vindilius Adiovi's heir had this made.
EDCS-10800738.summary: This funerary epitaph records that the heir of Gaius Vindilius Adiovi commissioned a monument.

EDCS-10800739.text_edition: \n Dianae Abnobae Marcus Sennius Fronto solvit libens ex voto\n
EDCS-10800739.translation: To Diana Abnoba, Marcus Sennius Fronto willingly paid a vow.
EDCS-10800739.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to the goddess Diana Abnoba by Marcus Sennius Fronto.

EDCS-10800742.translation: To Sabaoath, Adonai, Ablanathanalba, Akramakhamaari, Semesilam, Sesengem, barpharangis, io io io, protect Lucius, whom his mother Libia bore from all harm. Protect Lucius, servant. Protect Mercussa, servant.
EDCS-10800742.summary: This inscription is a complex magical or invocation text, likely a phylactery or amulet, invoking divine names and seeking protection for individuals named Lucius and Mercussa.

EDCS-10800744.text_edition: \n Marti Segomoni sacrum Paternus Dagusae filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800744.translation: Sacred to Mars Segomon. Paternus, son of Dagusae, willingly fulfilled his vow deservedly.
EDCS-10800744.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Mars Segomon by Paternus, son of Dagusae.

EDCS-10800745.summary: This inscription is a dedication or memorial to Benusa, daughter of Miucenus.

EDCS-10800747.text_edition: \n Marti Augusto Quintus Petronius Metellus Marcus Petronius Magnus IIviri Caius Iulius Respectus Caius Iulius Metellus NIIVI votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-10800747.translation: To Mars Augustus. Quintus Petronius Metellus and Marcus Petronius Magnus, the two *duoviri*, and Caius Iulius Respectus and Caius Iulius Metellus, the two *aediles*, willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10800747.summary: This inscription records a joint votive offering to Mars Augustus by two pairs of magistrates (duoviri and aediles) in a city, likely dated to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-10800748.text_edition: \n Marti Caius Iulius Veranius ex voto\n
EDCS-10800748.translation: To Mars. Caius Iulius Veranius, according to his vow.
EDCS-10800748.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to the god Mars by Caius Iulius Veranius.

EDCS-10800750.text_edition: \n Catilia Paula Catili Paterni filia aram\n
EDCS-10800750.translation: Catilia Paula, daughter of Catilius Paternus, an altar.
EDCS-10800750.summary: This inscription appears to record the dedication of an altar by Catilia Paula, daughter of Catilius Paternus.

EDCS-10800751.summary: This inscription is a simple epitaph or dedication identifying Tiberius Claudius Martialis.

EDCS-10800752.summary: This inscription is likely an incomplete epitaph or dedication for Quintus Claudius, with the filiation partially preserved.

EDCS-10800757.text_edition: \n Caio Licinio Pomptina Latini filio Campano Haeduo sacerdoti III provinciarum Galliarum officis et honoribus omnibus domesticis functo Sequani publice\n
EDCS-10800757.translation: To Caius Licinius Pomptina, son of Latinus, the Campanian Aeduan, priest, who served in all provincial offices and honors of the three Gallic provinces, the Sequani publicly [honored him].
EDCS-10800757.summary: This inscription records public honors bestowed by the Sequani people upon Caius Licinius Pomptina, a Campanian Aeduan priest who had held various provincial offices.

EDCS-10800758.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a label or a dedication by someone named Hector, celebrating three victories, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800760.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Iulius Senecianus thurarius bases donavit quattuor votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800760.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Caius Iulius Senecianus, the incense seller, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow by dedicating four bases.
EDCS-10800760.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by a thurarius (incense seller) named Caius Iulius Senecianus, who fulfilled a vow by dedicating four bases, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800762.text_edition: \n Matri Deum Camellius Tutor ex voto\n
EDCS-10800762.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, Camellius Tutor, according to his vow.
EDCS-10800762.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the Mother of the Gods by Camellius Tutor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800763.translation: Here rests Auxilius, thirty years old.
EDCS-10800763.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Auxilius, who died at the age of thirty, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800765.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gaio Iulio Flac filio Gaius Iulius Resp\n
EDCS-10800765.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, Caius Iulius Resp to his son Gaius Iulius Flaccus.
EDCS-10800765.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gaius Iulius Resp to his son Gaius Iulius Flaccus, addressed to the Dis Manibus (Spirits of the Departed), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800766.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, Martina.
EDCS-10800766.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Dis Manibus (Spirits of the Departed) for Martina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800767.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, Senobena.
EDCS-10800767.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Dis Manibus (Spirits of the Departed) for Senobena, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800768.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed, Gentilis.
EDCS-10800768.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Dis Manibus (Spirits of the Departed) for Gentilis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800771.text_edition: \n Apollini et Mercurio Esuccus Minerv et Biccus Veri votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-10800771.translation: To Apollo and Mercury, Esuccus, Minerva, and Biccus Veri gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10800771.summary: This is a votive inscription by Esuccus, Minerva, and Biccus Veri, dedicating something to Apollo and Mercury, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800773.text_edition: \n Genio Martis Vesonti Lucius Catlius Co\xc4\x91\xc4\x91acatus Catulli filius maceriam refecit porticum posuit votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800773.translation: To the Genius of Mars of Vesontio, Lucius Catlius Co[---]dacatus, son of Catullus, rebuilt the wall, set up the portico, and gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10800773.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Genius of Mars of Vesontio by Lucius Catlius Co[---]dacatus, who rebuilt a wall and erected a portico, fulfilling a vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800775.text_edition: \n Matrabus sic sacrum Oxia Messoris filia votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800775.translation: Oxia Messoris, daughter of Messor, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Matres.
EDCS-10800775.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Matres by Oxia Messoris, likely a freedwoman fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10800776.text_edition: \n Matrabus Auggustis Martialis Auggustorum nnostrorum verna ex dispensatore ex voto monitus\n
EDCS-10800776.translation: Martialis, a house-born slave from the emperor's household management, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the August Matres.
EDCS-10800776.summary: This is a votive inscription to the August Matres by Martialis, a freedman who previously served as an imperial steward.

EDCS-10800777.text_edition: \n Mercurio Marcus Mammaius Scottus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800777.translation: Marcus Mammaius Scottus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-10800777.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Marcus Mammaius Scottus.

EDCS-10800778.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Cissonio Dubitatia Castula natione Syria templum et porticus vetustate conla<p=B>sum denuo de suo restituit \n
EDCS-10800778.translation: Dubitatia Castula, by nation a Syrian, restored at her own expense this temple and portico to the god Mercury Cissinius, which had been destroyed by age.
EDCS-10800778.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple and portico dedicated to Mercury Cissinius by Dubitatia Castula, a Syrian woman, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10800779.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Apollini votum solvit libens merito Albanus Iuli filius\n
EDCS-10800779.translation: Albanus, son of Iulius, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury and Apollo.
EDCS-10800779.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury and Apollo by Albanus Iulius, likely a freedman.

EDCS-10800783.translation: Suadurix willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10800783.summary: This is a votive inscription by Suadurix, likely a local deity or hero.

EDCS-10800785.summary: This is a funerary epitaph or a dedication identifying Publius Cornelius Scipio.

EDCS-10800786.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely identifying an individual named Pompeius, possibly on a tomb or a dedication.

EDCS-10800787.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. For Marcus Tituleius Victor, prefect of the Sixth Cohort of Raeti.
EDCS-10800787.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Tituleius Victor, who served as prefect of the Sixth Cohort of Raeti, dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10800788.text_edition: \n rginiae Marius Vitalis coniunx |(centurio) legionis et Marius Nigidianus filius quaestor matri e longinquo adportatae et hic conditae sex et triginta nnos vixit inculpata marito obsequio raro solo contenta marito\n
EDCS-10800788.translation: Marius Vitalis, husband, a centurion of the legion, and Marius Nigidianus, his son, a quaestor, lived thirty-six years with their mother, who was brought from afar and buried here, praised for her rare devotion to her husband and contentment with him.
EDCS-10800788.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman, commemorating her devotion and contentment, as stated by her husband, a centurion, and son, a quaestor.

EDCS-10800789.text_edition: \n Geminia Titulla Arausiensis mater sacrorum hic adquiescit Decimus Iulius Publi libertus Auctus coniugi piissimae et Aurae Severi quem pro filia observavit\n
EDCS-10800789.translation: Geminia Titulla of Arausio, mother of priests, rests here. Decimus Iulius Auctus, freedman of Publius, [placed this] for his most devoted wife and for Aura Severa, whom he cared for as a daughter.
EDCS-10800789.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Geminia Titulla, placed by her husband or a devoted admirer.

EDCS-10800790.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Epichari XIII vixs(it) nnos XLIII menses V dies VII Martialis Augusti nostri verna ex dispensatore\n
EDCS-10800790.translation: To the departed spirits. Epicharis lived 43 years, 5 months, and 7 days. Martialis, our freedman from August, [dedicated this] from the steward's office.
EDCS-10800790.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Epicharis, dating to the imperial period based on the mention of 'Augusti nostri verna'.

EDCS-10800791.text_edition: \n Caesoniae Donatae quae vixsit annis XXXXVII mensibus diebus XI horis IIII Candidus Augusti nostri verna ex testamento coniugi bene merenti posuit Eusebi have et vale loco libero Vale Eusebi Ave Eusebi\n
EDCS-10800791.translation: For Caesia Donata, who lived 47 years, 11 months, and 4 days. Candidus, our freedman from August, erected [this] in accordance with his will for his deserving wife. Farewell and be well, Eusebius. Farewell, Eusebius. Be well, Eusebius.
EDCS-10800791.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Candidus for his wife, Caesia Donata, according to his will, dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-10800792.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus memoriai sic Aureliai sic Vin\n
EDCS-10800792.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Aurelia and Vin[---].
EDCS-10800792.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph intended to honor Aurelia and another individual.

EDCS-10800794.translation: To the departed spirits of Claudia Viduca.
EDCS-10800794.summary: A simple funerary epitaph dedicated to Claudia Viduca.

EDCS-10800795.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Clodio Onesimo Iulia Carrotala uxor\n
EDCS-10800795.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulia Carrotala, his wife, [dedicated this] for Clodius Onesimus.
EDCS-10800795.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a wife to her husband, Clodius Onesimus.

EDCS-10800796.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae aeternae Ianussi Ianuaris Iunioris qui vixit annos VIIII menses VI dies VIIII Ianussius Ianuaris Gedus pater et Luciola Lucustae mater filio dulcissimo ad asciam dedicaverunt posuerunt\n
EDCS-10800796.translation: To the departed spirits and eternal memory. For Ianussius Ianuaris Gedus, his father, and Luciola Lucustae, his mother, dedicated and placed [this] for their sweetest son, who lived 9 years, 6 months, and 9 days.
EDCS-10800796.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their young son, Ianussius Ianuaris Gedus, indicating a loving remembrance.

EDCS-10800797.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus memoriai sic Iliomari Vanatasti nnos V\n
EDCS-10800797.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Iliomarus Vanatastus, [who lived] 5 years.
EDCS-10800797.summary: A funerary epitaph commemorating Iliomarus Vanatastus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-10800798.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus memoria Invetius Domitianus annos LXXV\n
EDCS-10800798.translation: To the departed spirits, in memory of Invetius Domitianus, [who lived] 75 years.
EDCS-10800798.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated to Invetius Domitianus, recording his lifespan.

EDCS-10800799.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucius Lepidius Solutor vixit annis VIII mensibus II \n
EDCS-10800799.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Lepidius Solutor lived 8 years and 2 months.
EDCS-10800799.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the brief life of Lucius Lepidius Solutor.

EDCS-10800800.summary: This is a dedication to Licinius Silvanus and Regina.

EDCS-10800801.summary: This is a funerary marker for a boy named Magnillus who died at the age of 10.

EDCS-10800802.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus memoria Megethius Mineti annos XXIII\n
EDCS-10800802.translation: To the Divine Shades, in memory of Megethius, son of Minetus, aged 23.
EDCS-10800802.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Megethius, son of Minetus, who died at the age of 23.

EDCS-10800812.translation: Silvester, bishop, who lived in peace for 47 years and remained in his episcopate for 22 years. Flavius [...]
EDCS-10800812.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for bishop Silvester, detailing his lifespan and tenure in office.

EDCS-10800813.translation: To the goddess Bellona, from Scantrus, son of Oxta.
EDCS-10800813.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Bellona by Scantrus, son of Oxta.

EDCS-10800814.text_edition: \n Castori sacrum Tiberius Iulius Sancti filius Celsus voto\n
EDCS-10800814.translation: Sacred to Castor, from Tiberius Iulius Celsus, son of Sanctus, fulfilling his vow.
EDCS-10800814.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Castor by Tiberius Iulius Celsus.

EDCS-10800816.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Vireius Camulatus et Titus Vireius Iucundus\xc2\xa0\n
EDCS-10800816.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius Vireius Camulatus and Titus Vireius Iucundus.
EDCS-10800816.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Vireius Camulatus and Titus Vireius Iucundus.

EDCS-10800817.text_edition: \n Decantilla Cobnerti filia votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800817.translation: Decantilla, daughter of Cobnertus, gladly and deservedly paid her vow.
EDCS-10800817.summary: This is a votive inscription where Decantilla, daughter of Cobnertus, fulfilled her vow.

EDCS-10800818.translation: Mutacus gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10800818.summary: This is a votive inscription where Mutacus fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10800821.text_edition: \n Flavius Catullus testamento ad marmorandum balneum legavit rei publicae |(denarios) LXXVmilia quod Caius Flavius Gallus heres perficiendum curavit additis summis et tributis legati supra scripti ad consummationem\n
EDCS-10800821.translation: Flavius Catullus by his will bequeathed 75,000 denarii for the construction of a bathhouse for the public treasury, which Caius Flavius Gallus, his heir, took care to have completed, adding funds from the aforementioned legacy for its completion.
EDCS-10800821.summary: This inscription records a bequest of 75,000 denarii by Flavius Catullus for a public bathhouse, completed by his heir Caius Flavius Gallus.

EDCS-10800823.translation: Catullus with statues of Tiberius Claudius
EDCS-10800823.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely recording the dedication of statues by Catullus to Tiberius Claudius, possibly in the imperial period.

EDCS-10800826.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription, likely a dedication or memorial to a person named Amantia.

EDCS-10800827.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, of Iulius Vestalis
EDCS-10800827.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Iulius Vestalis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800830.translation: To Apollo and Sirona, Taurus himself [dedicated this]
EDCS-10800830.summary: This is a votive inscription where Taurus dedicates something to the deities Apollo and Sirona, likely from a provincial Roman context.

EDCS-10800831.text_edition: \n Lussoio et Brictae Divixtius Constans votum solvit <l=T>(ibens) merito \n
EDCS-10800831.translation: Divixtius Constans willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Lussoius and Bricta
EDCS-10800831.summary: This is a votive inscription from Divixtius Constans dedicated to the deities Lussoius and Bricta, likely from a provincial Roman context.

EDCS-10800832.text_edition: \n Luxovio et Brixtae Gaius Iulius Firmanus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800832.translation: Gaius Iulius Firmanus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Luxovius and Brixta
EDCS-10800832.summary: This is a votive inscription from Gaius Iulius Firmanus dedicated to the deities Luxovius and Brixta, likely from a provincial Roman context.

EDCS-10800833.text_edition: \n Marcus Nu Mepilla INOC votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10800833.translation: Marcus Nu Mepilla willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow
EDCS-10800833.summary: This is a votive inscription where Marcus Nu Mepilla fulfilled a vow, likely from a provincial Roman context.

EDCS-10800835.translation: To the memory of Aminia Olata
EDCS-10800835.summary: This is a memorial inscription dedicated to Aminia Olata, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800837.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cassianus Maronianus filius uxsor Vinilla\n
EDCS-10800837.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Cassianus Maronianus, son, and his wife Vinilla
EDCS-10800837.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Cassianus Maronianus and his wife Vinilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800838.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, of Censorinus
EDCS-10800838.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Censorinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10800839.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Cerialis, son of Donicatus.
EDCS-10800839.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Cerialis, son of Donicatus.

EDCS-10800840.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Divicus et Samilla mater\n
EDCS-10800840.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Divicus and his mother Samilla.
EDCS-10800840.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Divicus and his mother Samilla.

EDCS-10800842.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iunianus Carrotalus filius ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10800842.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Iunianus Carrotalus arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10800842.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, commissioned by Iunianus Carrotalus.

EDCS-10800843.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lagussa et Lupula filia\n
EDCS-10800843.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Lagussa and her daughter Lupula.
EDCS-10800843.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Lagussa and her daughter Lupula.

EDCS-10800844.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Mariciainus.
EDCS-10800844.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Mariciainus.

EDCS-10800845.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Meliudius.
EDCS-10800845.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Meliudius.

EDCS-10800846.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Musinius, son of Irelis.
EDCS-10800846.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Musinius, son of Irelis.

EDCS-10800847.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Oxtaia.
EDCS-10800847.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Oxtaia.

EDCS-10800848.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Salicilla, daughter of Venustus.
EDCS-10800848.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Salicilla, daughter of Venustus.

EDCS-10800849.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Tascilla.
EDCS-10800849.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed for Tascilla.

EDCS-10800850.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Victorinus Coactilus.
EDCS-10800850.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the departed for Victorinus Coactilus.

EDCS-10800855.translation: Here lies Cadmus, son of Hisagogus.
EDCS-10800855.summary: A tombstone recording the burial of Cadmus, son of Hisagogus.

EDCS-10800861.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus mon<u=I>mentum Amandi simul Carae uxoris Amandini filii cura Amandi liberti \n
EDCS-10800861.translation: To the spirits of the departed, a monument for Amandus, and also for Cara, his wife, and Amandinus, his son, by the care of Amandus, freedman.
EDCS-10800861.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Amandus, his wife Cara, and son Amandinus, erected by Amandus, a freedman.

EDCS-10800862.translation: To the spirits of the departed, in memory of Cucumilla, his daughter.
EDCS-10800862.summary: A funerary dedication in memory of Cucumilla, a daughter.

EDCS-10800863.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tiberi Masc ano AS\n
EDCS-10800863.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Tiberius Mascanus.
EDCS-10800863.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the departed for Tiberius Mascanus.

EDCS-10800864.summary: An inscription identifying Paulla as the daughter of Annus.

EDCS-10800865.translation: Of Quintus Ramus, son of Op[---].
EDCS-10800865.summary: A fragmented inscription possibly recording a dedication or ownership by Quintus Ramus.

EDCS-10800866.summary: A dedication or memorial for Sambatiola.

EDCS-10800867.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Lucius Solinius Cestus.
EDCS-10800867.summary: A funerary dedication to the spirits of the departed for Lucius Solinius Cestus.

EDCS-10801067.translation: Bert[---] this family order[---] / when I had wished to seek the holy tombs first / [too fortunate] if I had left my children and husband safe by the gift of such a vow / but since of the four born, one survives / [I pray] that he may live here always and honor these bones / a distinguished woman here ena[---] / [---]to, on the 10th day before the Kalends of May, Severinus, a most illustrious man, being consul / fifty-two years.
EDCS-10801067.summary: A poetic epitaph, likely from the late Roman period, lamenting the premature death of a woman and expressing a wish for her surviving son, who lived to be 52.

EDCS-10801370.text_edition: \n Matrabus agrum ex macerie circumductum Sextus Clementis filius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10801370.translation: To the Matres, Sextus, son of Clementis, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow concerning the field enclosed by a stone wall.
EDCS-10801370.summary: This is a votive inscription from Sextus, son of Clementis, dedicating an enclosed field to the Matres, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-10801373.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Iulius Romulus.
EDCS-10801373.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Iulius Romulus, possibly a soldier or a freedman.

EDCS-10801376.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury by Tiberius Pabenn[...], likely an incomplete inscription.

EDCS-10801377.translation: To the Genius of the Argentorates people, Phrunicus.
EDCS-10801377.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of the people of Argentoratum by Phrunicus.

EDCS-10801378.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio vici canabarum et vicanorum canabensium Quintus Martius Optatus qui columnam et statuam dono dedit\n
EDCS-10801378.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Genius of the crossroads and of the inhabitants of the crossroads, Quintus Martius Optatus, who gave a column and a statue as a gift.
EDCS-10801378.summary: This inscription records Quintus Martius Optatus dedicating a column and statue to the Genius of a crossroads and its inhabitants, likely honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-10801379.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iassus ex voto posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10801379.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Iassus erected this, having vowed it, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-10801379.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iassus dedicating a monument to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-10801380.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Augustus Tocissae filius ex voto votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10801380.translation: To the god Mercury, Augustus, son of Tocissa, fulfilled his vow, having vowed it, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-10801380.summary: This is a votive inscription by Augustus, son of Tocissa, dedicating something to the god Mercury.

EDCS-10801381.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Minervae sanctae et Genio loci Caius Amandius Finitus optio principis et Titus Celsius Victorinus librarius principis refecerunt Muciano et Fabiano consulibus Caius Quintius Catilus optio principis inchoatum de suo perfecit duobus Auggustis Severo III et Antonino consulibus\n
EDCS-10801381.translation: In honor of the divine house, to holy Minerva and the Genius of the place, Caius Amandius Finitus, chief optio, and Titus Celsius Victorinus, chief scribe, restored it; Caius Quintius Catilus, optio, completed what was begun at his own expense under the consuls Mucianus and Fabianus, during the reign of the two Augusti, Severus (for the third time) and Antoninus.
EDCS-10801381.summary: This is a dedication and restoration inscription for Minerva and the Genius Loci, commissioned by imperial officials and completed under the consuls Severus and Antoninus, suggesting a date around 200 CE.

EDCS-10801382.text_edition: \n Quadruviis Septiminius Victor ara cum templo restituit votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10801382.translation: To the crossroads, Septiminius Victor restored the altar with its temple, and fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-10801382.summary: This inscription records Septiminius Victor restoring an altar and temple dedicated to the crossroads.

EDCS-10801385.text_edition: \n Lucius Autronius Luci filius Sergia Norba Silo veteranus ex legione II heredes ex testamento\n
EDCS-10801385.translation: Lucius Autronius, son of Lucius, of the Sergia tribe, from Norba, Silo the veteran of the II Legion, his heirs by his will.
EDCS-10801385.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Autronius, a veteran of the II Legion, whose heirs erected the monument according to his will.

EDCS-10801386.text_edition: \n Tiberius Babuleius Garrulus Tiberi Oufentina Medioleanio miles legionis II centuria Scaevae Petroni annorum XXXXV stipendiorum XXII hic situs est Pater Tiberius Babuleius Brocus materi sic Pupae et sorori Priscae Tiberius Babuleius Albanus libertus heres ex testamento faciendum <c=Q>uravit! \n
EDCS-10801386.translation: Tiberius Babuleius Garrulus, soldier of the II Legion, in the century of Scaeva Petronius, aged 45, with 22 years of service, lies here. His father Tiberius Babuleius Brocus, his mother Pupae and sister Priscae, and his freedman heir Tiberius Babuleius Albanus, made this monument by will.
EDCS-10801386.summary: This is a tombstone for Tiberius Babuleius Garrulus, a soldier in the II Legion, erected by his father, mother, sister, and freedman heir.

EDCS-10801387.text_edition: \n Titus Iulius Titi filius Camilia Alba miles legionis II centuria Bieni nnorum XXXV stipendiorum XVI hic situs est\n
EDCS-10801387.translation: Titus Iulius Alba, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe, soldier of the II Legion, in the century of Biennus, aged 35, with 16 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10801387.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Iulius Alba, a soldier in the II Legion.

EDCS-10801388.text_edition: \n Caius Largennius Cai Fabia Luca miles legionis II centuria Scaevae annorum XXXVII stipendiorum XVIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-10801388.translation: Caius Largennius Luca, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe, soldier of the II Legion, in the century of Scaeva, aged 37, with 18 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-10801388.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Largennius Luca, a soldier in the II Legion.

EDCS-10801389.text_edition: \n Titus Flavius Titi filius Ouf<e=F>ntina Peregrinus Mediolanni sic miles legionis VIII Augustae centuria Marci Postumi Celerini vixit annos XXV stipendiorum IIII frater heres faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-10801389.translation: Titus Flavius Peregrinus, son of Titus, of the Oufentina tribe, from Mediolanum, soldier of the VIII Augusta Legion, in the century of Marcus Postumius Celer, lived 25 years, with 4 years of service. His brother and heir had this made.
EDCS-10801389.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Flavius Peregrinus, a soldier in the VIII Augusta Legion, erected by his brother and heir.

EDCS-10801391.text_edition: \n Caius Anienus fecit et testamento filios instituit et rogavit\n
EDCS-10801391.translation: Caius Anienus made this and appointed his sons as heirs in his will, and requested this.
EDCS-10801391.summary: This inscription records the actions of Caius Anienus regarding his will and the appointment of heirs.

EDCS-10801392.text_edition: \n Lucius Licinius Luci filius Claudia Maximus Aequo miles legionis VIII Augustae\n
EDCS-10801392.translation: Lucius Licinius Maximus, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, from Aequum, soldier of the VIII Augusta Legion.
EDCS-10801392.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Licinius Maximus as a soldier of the VIII Augusta Legion.

EDCS-10801393.text_edition: \n Caiae Lucaniae Caratae Ianuconius Primanus veteranus coniugi \n
EDCS-10801393.translation: Ianuconius Primanus, a veteran, to his wife Caia Lucania Carata.
EDCS-10801393.summary: This is an epitaph for Caia Lucania Carata, dedicated by her husband, Ianuconius Primanus, a veteran.

EDCS-10801394.translation: To his wife Maximina, by Maximinus.
EDCS-10801394.summary: This is an epitaph for Maximina, dedicated by Maximinus, presumably her husband.

EDCS-10801396.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et memoriae Terentiae Augustulae coniugi sanctissimae Iustius Iustinus maritus et Iusti Oceanus et Florida matri pientissimae\n
EDCS-10801396.translation: To the divine spirits and memory of Terentia Augustula, most holy wife. Her husband Iustius Iustinus and her children Iusti Oceanus and Florida, to their most devoted mother.
EDCS-10801396.summary: This is a tombstone for Terentia Augustula, dedicated by her husband Iustius Iustinus and her children Iusti Oceanus and Florida.

EDCS-10801397.text_edition: \n Dianae Caius Ligurius Victor votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10801397.translation: Caius Ligurius Victor willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Diana.
EDCS-10801397.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Diana by Caius Ligurius Victor, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10801400.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo votum solvit laetus libens merito Liberalis Virillionis filius\n
EDCS-10801400.translation: Liberalis, son of Virillio, gladly, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10801400.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Jupiter by Liberalis, son of Virillio.

EDCS-10801402.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Apollini Magiorix et Quintus Secundi filii votum solverunt libens merito\n
EDCS-10801402.translation: Magiorix and Quintus, sons of Secundus, gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Mercury and Apollo.
EDCS-10801402.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Mercury and Apollo by Magiorix and Quintus.

EDCS-10801403.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Secundius Belatulus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10801403.translation: In honor of the divine house, Secundius Belatulus fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-10801403.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Mercury, in honor of the imperial family, by Secundius Belatulus.

EDCS-10801405.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Bella, daughter of Dagomar.
EDCS-10801405.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Bella, daughter of Dagomar, dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Underworld).

EDCS-10801406.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Carantilla.
EDCS-10801406.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Carantilla, dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Underworld).

EDCS-10801407.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Casata, daughter of Caratus.
EDCS-10801407.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Casata, daughter of Caratus, dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Underworld).

EDCS-10801408.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Codolna Senurus.
EDCS-10801408.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Codolna Senurus, dedicated to the 'Dis Manibus' (Spirits of the Underworld).

EDCS-10801409.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et perpetuae securitati Corneliae Divixtae Cornelius Iuvenilis maritus\n
EDCS-10801409.translation: For the Spirits of the Underworld and for the eternal security of Cornelia Divixta, her husband Cornelius Iuvenilis [erected this].
EDCS-10801409.summary: This inscription is a tombstone dedication by Cornelius Iuvenilis for his wife Cornelia Divixta, intended for the 'Dis Manibus' and her eternal security.

EDCS-10801410.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Divixtae Materni Cidius maritus Sexto ci Cidius pater\n
EDCS-10801410.translation: For the Spirits of the Underworld, her husband Sextus Cidius [erected this] for Divixta, Cidius her father [erected this].
EDCS-10801410.summary: This inscription is a tombstone dedication by Sextus Cidius for his wife Divixta, and also mentions Cidius, possibly her father.

EDCS-10801411.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Laeto Catulini Cintussa et Cintusmus fili ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-10801411.translation: For the Spirits of the Underworld, Cintussa and Cintusmus, sons of Laetus Catulinus, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-10801411.summary: This inscription is a tombstone dedication arranged by Cintussa and Cintusmus, sons of Laetus Catulinus, for the 'Dis Manibus'.

EDCS-10801412.translation: To the departed spirits of Matta, daughter of Carasius.
EDCS-10801412.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Matta, daughter of Carasius.

EDCS-10801414.text_edition: \n OIIAIV APVIILEIVS Camerino Ianuario Carasio PITERVTT\n
EDCS-10801414.translation: Olliaivus Aviius Camerinus, son of Ianuarius, dedicated this to Carasius PITERVTT.
EDCS-10801414.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Olliaivus Aviius Camerinus to Carasius.

EDCS-10801415.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Latti Materni fili monimentum\n
EDCS-10801415.translation: To the departed spirits. A monument to Lattius, son of Maternus.
EDCS-10801415.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Lattius, son of Maternus.

EDCS-10900253.text_edition: \n Titus Iulius Cai filius Postumus VIvir \n
EDCS-10900253.translation: Titus Iulius Postumus, son of Caius, a member of the college of six (VIvir).
EDCS-10900253.summary: This inscription records the name and office of Titus Iulius Postumus, a VIvir.

EDCS-10900257.text_edition: \n Cereri sacrum pro salute Caesarum Aptus Trionis libertus\n
EDCS-10900257.translation: Sacred to Ceres, for the safety of the Emperors. Aptus, freedman of Trion, made this offering.
EDCS-10900257.summary: This is a religious dedication to Ceres by Aptus, a freedman, for the safety of the emperors.

EDCS-10900258.text_edition: \n Herculi sacrum Caius Maecius Firmus IIIIIIvir Augustalis curator civium Romanorum designatus ex voto pecunia s(ua) posuit\n
EDCS-10900258.translation: Sacred to Hercules. Caius Maecius Firmus, a IIIIIIvir Augustalis and curator of Roman citizens, set this up at his own expense according to his vow.
EDCS-10900258.summary: This is a religious dedication to Hercules by Caius Maecius Firmus, who held multiple civic and religious offices.

EDCS-10900260.text_edition: \n Ex voto suscepto Neptuno sacrum Titus Nontrius Vanatactus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900260.translation: Sacred to Neptune. Titus Nontrius Vanatactus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly, as he had undertaken.
EDCS-10900260.summary: This inscription records Titus Nontrius Vanatactus fulfilling a vow made to Neptune.

EDCS-10900264.text_edition: \n Nonios Suleis suis voto libens merito <p=R>(osuit) \n
EDCS-10900264.translation: Nonios Suleis dedicated this willingly and deservedly according to his vow.
EDCS-10900264.summary: This inscription records Nonios Suleis fulfilling a vow to his household gods (Suleis).

EDCS-10900265.translation: To Sul(e)is. [---]NAI fulfilled the vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-10900265.summary: This fragmented inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Sul(e)is by an individual whose name is partially lost.

EDCS-10900272.translation: To the departed spirits. [---]atus, son of Otacilius...
EDCS-10900272.summary: This is a fragmented funerary dedication to a person named Otacilius [---]atus.

EDCS-10900273.text_edition: \n Marti Caturigi Iulius Silvester lapidarius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900273.translation: To Mars Caturix, Julius Silvester, stonecutter, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900273.summary: A stonecutter named Julius Silvester dedicates an offering to Mars Caturix, likely on a votive monument, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10900277.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Tiberi filius Maternus aedilis sphaeristerium de suo dedit\n
EDCS-10900277.translation: Tiberius Claudius Maternus, son of Tiberius, the aedile, gave the gymnasium at his own expense.
EDCS-10900277.summary: An aedile named Tiberius Claudius Maternus funded the construction of a gymnasium, likely a public building for athletic training.

EDCS-10900282.translation: The property of Dirogis. Masso, slave of Gratus, made this. Maternus Maccius Gratus.
EDCS-10900282.summary: This inscription likely marks a property boundary or a tombstone, mentioning the owner Dirogis and the maker Masso, possibly with a client name Gratus.

EDCS-10900283.translation: Cantexta, from the Suleis tribe, [---] Mode[---]
EDCS-10900283.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions a woman named Cantexta and possibly a tribal affiliation or place name, with the text being incomplete.

EDCS-10900287.text_edition: \n Marti Marti Aulus Q S votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900287.translation: To Mars! Aulus, son of Q S, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900287.summary: Aulus, son of Q S, dedicates an offering to Mars, likely on a votive monument, having willingly fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-10900288.translation: Fulfilled his vow to Mars. Aulus [---]
EDCS-10900288.summary: This is a partial inscription indicating that Aulus fulfilled a vow to Mars, likely on a votive monument, but the text is incomplete.

EDCS-10900297.translation: Century of Cassius Quintius, AP-SRI Hisponis.
EDCS-10900297.summary: This inscription refers to a military unit, specifically a century named after Cassius Quintiuse, possibly indicating its origin or affiliation with Hisponis.

EDCS-10900298.translation: Century of Lucius Bilienus, the reaper.
EDCS-10900298.summary: This inscription identifies a military unit, a century named after Lucius Bilienus, possibly associated with a role or nickname related to harvesting or a military role.

EDCS-10900300.translation: Century of Olneus, of Lucius Cornelius Sabinus.
EDCS-10900300.summary: This inscription denotes a military unit, a century named Olneus, linked to Lucius Cornelius Sabinus, possibly indicating command or ownership.

EDCS-10900301.translation: Century of Victorinus, of Marcus Julius Festus.
EDCS-10900301.summary: This inscription marks a military unit, a century called Victorinus, belonging to or commanded by Marcus Julius Festus.

EDCS-10900303.translation: The century of Pir Severus. Quintus Saturius.
EDCS-10900303.summary: This inscription appears to record names, possibly of soldiers or officials, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-10900304.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that likely recorded ownership or dedication by Lucius Soranus.

EDCS-10900305.translation: From Aulus Vettius Priscus, legate of the Emperor.
EDCS-10900305.summary: This inscription indicates a dedication or commission by Aulus Vettius Priscus, who held the significant imperial office of legate.

EDCS-10900306.summary: This inscription likely records the name and office of a Roman official, possibly a quaestor, from an uncertain period.

EDCS-10900307.translation: Marcus M. I. erected (this) to Mars?.
EDCS-10900307.summary: This fragmentary inscription suggests a dedication to the god Mars, possibly by an individual named Marcus.

EDCS-10900308.translation: Lucius Pupius Masius made (this); soldier of the Eleventh Legion.
EDCS-10900308.summary: This inscription records that Lucius Pupius Masius, a soldier of the Eleventh Legion, commissioned or created this object.

EDCS-10900309.translation: Of Lucius Calvus, century of Justus.
EDCS-10900309.summary: This inscription likely refers to a unit or individual within a military context, possibly a century commanded by Justus and associated with Lucius Calvus.

EDCS-10900314.summary: This inscription records the establishment or dedication of a forum named after Emperor Tiberius.

EDCS-10900315.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Flavia Sacrilla, dearest mother, and Valeria Sancta, most devoted mother, Julius Marcellus and Valeria Sancta have arranged for this to be erected at their own expense.
EDCS-10900315.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a son-in-law and a daughter to their respective mothers, Flavia Sacrilla and Valeria Sancta, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-10900317.summary: This inscription seems to record a personal transaction or permission granted by Masclus to his son, likely related to property or legal matters.

EDCS-10900318.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription recording a gift made by Lentinus.

EDCS-10900320.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented epitaph, possibly mentioning a person named Frontonis.

EDCS-10900324.text_edition: \n Apollini Caius Iulius Domitinus Sequanus voto\n
EDCS-10900324.translation: To Apollo, Gaius Iulius Domitinus Sequanus, fulfilling his vow.
EDCS-10900324.summary: This dedication to Apollo was made by Gaius Iulius Domitinus Sequanus, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10900326.translation: Genialis willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Apollo and Sirona.
EDCS-10900326.summary: This inscription records Genialis fulfilling a vow to the deities Apollo and Sirona.

EDCS-10900337.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the eternal memory of Eusstata, my sweetest wife, who lived 65 years. Amatus erected this.
EDCS-10900337.summary: This is a tomb inscription dedicated by Amatus to his wife Eusstata, who lived 65 years.

EDCS-10900340.translation: To the spirits of the departed, to Marcellinus and Paullina.
EDCS-10900340.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the memory of Marcellinus and Paullina.

EDCS-10900341.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Vassitus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900341.translation: To the god Mercury, Vassitus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10900341.summary: This inscription records Vassitus fulfilling a vow to the god Mercury.

EDCS-10900342.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple name and patronymic, possibly an owner's mark or a very brief epitaph.

EDCS-10900343.translation: [As] decurion of the civitas of the Nemetes(?) and Gaius Constantius [---]us, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-10900343.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by a decurion of the Nemetes and another individual, Gaius Constantius.

EDCS-10900344.text_edition: \n Lucius Valerius Sera miles legionis XXII Marti votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900344.translation: Lucius Valerius Sera, a soldier of the XXII Legion Martia, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-10900344.summary: This inscription records Lucius Valerius Sera, a soldier of the XXII Legion Martia, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10900345.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Sextus Seneianius Micio and Pacata willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-10900345.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter by Sextus Seneianius Micio and Pacata.

EDCS-10900346.translation: Avvo, son of Saturn, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900346.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Avvo, son of Saturn.

EDCS-10900347.text_edition: \n aniae Delibriae iuveni infelici quae vixit annos XVIII ridia mater misera quae contra votum suum et quae sibi a filia optaverat faciendum kuravit!\n
EDCS-10900347.translation: His wretched mother had made this for her beloved, unfortunate young man, who lived 18 days, a fate against her vow and what she had wished for herself from her daughter.
EDCS-10900347.summary: This funerary inscription, possibly from the 2nd century CE, records a monument erected by a mother for her infant son.

EDCS-10900348.translation: Here rests in peace, chaste. His father possibly placed this title.
EDCS-10900348.summary: This funerary inscription possibly records a father placing a tombstone for his son.

EDCS-10900349.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae D VI In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio pro salute Sabini ex voto posuit aram Lucius P D\n
EDCS-10900349.translation: In honor of the divine house, for the god Mercury, for the safety of Sabinus, Lucius P D erected this altar in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-10900349.summary: This inscription records the erection of an altar to Mercury by Lucius P D for the safety of Sabinus, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-10900351.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio et Maiiae sic aedem cum signis Lucius Cornelius Augurinus decurio civitatis Aquensis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900351.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Cornelius Augurinus, a decurion of the city of Aquis, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury and Maia by dedicating this shrine with statues.
EDCS-10900351.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cornelius Augurinus dedicating a shrine to Mercury and Maia on behalf of the imperial family.

EDCS-10900355.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Aprilis Donati votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900355.translation: Aprilis Donati willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10900355.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter by Aprilis Donati.

EDCS-10900357.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Candidus Vintrionis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900357.translation: Candidus Vintrionis willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10900357.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter by Candidus Vintrionis.

EDCS-10900361.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Marcus Firminius Martius libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900361.translation: Marcus Firminius Martius willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-10900361.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter by Marcus Firminius Martius.

EDCS-10900363.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius A T I N I A G\n
EDCS-10900363.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius A T I N I A G.
EDCS-10900363.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter Best and Greatest by Lucius A T I N I A G.

EDCS-10900364.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo cohors I Asturum cui praeest Caius Iulius Artemo praefectus votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-10900364.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the First Cohort of Astures, commanded by Gaius Julius Artemo, prefect, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled its vow.
EDCS-10900364.summary: A military inscription recording a vow fulfilled by the First Cohort of Astures to Jupiter.

EDCS-10900365.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo cohors Asturum cui praeest Caius Iulius Artemo praefectus votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-10900365.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the Cohort of Astures, commanded by Gaius Julius Artemo, prefect, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled its vow.
EDCS-10900365.summary: A military inscription recording a vow fulfilled by the Cohort of Astures to Jupiter.

EDCS-10900366.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo cohors I Asturum equitata curam agente Diodoto\n
EDCS-10900366.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the First Cohort of Astures, equitate, under the supervision of Diodotus.
EDCS-10900366.summary: A military inscription dedicated to Jupiter by the First Cohort of Astures, equitate, during an unknown period.

EDCS-10900368.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo cohors I Asturum equitata curam agente Marco Mevio Marci filio Fabia Capriolo praefecto fecit\n
EDCS-10900368.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the First Cohort of Astures, equitate, under the supervision of Marcus Mevius, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe, Capriolus, prefect, made this.
EDCS-10900368.summary: A military inscription dedicated to Jupiter by the First Cohort of Astures, equitate, with Marcus Mevius Capriolus as prefect.

EDCS-10900369.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo cohors I Asturum equitata curam agente o praefecto\n
EDCS-10900369.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, the First Cohort of Astures, equitate, under the supervision of o, prefect.
EDCS-10900369.summary: A military inscription dedicated to Jupiter by the First Cohort of Astures, equitate, with an unnamed prefect.

EDCS-10900371.text_edition: \n Luci Septimi Severi veterani consistenses ad hiberna cohortis I Germanorum duobus Silanis consulibus\n
EDCS-10900371.translation: To Lucius Septimius Severus, the veterans residing at the winter quarters of the First Cohort of Germans, in the consulship of the two Silani.
EDCS-10900371.summary: An inscription related to veterans and the winter quarters of the First Cohort of Germans, dated to the consulship of the two Silani.

EDCS-10900373.text_edition: \n Legio XXII Primigenia pia fidelis centuria Aeli Sabini primi pili\n
EDCS-10900373.translation: The Twenty-Second Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, the century of Aelius Sabinus, first file.
EDCS-10900373.summary: An inscription identifying a century within the Twenty-Second Legion Primigenia, likely military.

EDCS-10900374.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Minervae Genio Imperatoris Commodi Augusti Pii Felicis Invicti Brittannici Quintus Villonius Verecundus miles legionis VIII Augustae piae fidelis constantis Commodae beneficiarius consularis duobus Silanis consulibus Idibus Iuliis votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900374.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, to Minerva, to the Genius of the Emperor Commodus Augustus Pius Felix Invictus Britannicus, Quintus Villonius Verecundus, soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta, pious, faithful, constant, Commodan, a consular beneficiarius, in the consulship of the two Silani, on the Ides of July, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900374.summary: A military dedication to various deities and the emperor Commodus by Quintus Villonius Verecundus, a soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta, dated to the consulship of the two Silani.

EDCS-10900375.text_edition: \n Dis deabusque omnibus sacrum Caius Sanctinius Mercator miles legionis VIII Augustae piae fidelis constantis Commodae beneficiarius consularis pro salute sua et suorum omnium posuit votum solvit laetus libens merito Idibus Ianuariis Aproniano et Bradua consulibus\n
EDCS-10900375.translation: Sacred to all the gods and goddesses. Gaius Sanctinius Mercator, soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta, pious, faithful, constant, Commodan, a consular beneficiarius, set this up for his own safety and that of all his family, and willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow on the Ides of January, in the consulship of Apronianus and Bradua.
EDCS-10900375.summary: A dedication to all gods and goddesses for safety by Gaius Sanctinius Mercator, a soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta, dated to the consulship of Apronianus and Bradua.

EDCS-10900376.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Genio loci ceterisque dis immortalibus Titus Atticius Pacatus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis votum solvit laetus libens merito Idibus Iuliis Muciano et Fabiano consulibus\n
EDCS-10900376.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, to the Genius of the place, and to all the other immortal gods, Titus Atticius Pacatus, soldier of the Twenty-Second Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, a consular beneficiarius, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow on the Ides of July, in the consulship of Mucianus and Fabianus.
EDCS-10900376.summary: A military dedication to Jupiter, the Genius loci, and other gods by Titus Atticius Pacatus, a soldier of the Twenty-Second Legion Primigenia, dated to the consulship of Mucianus and Fabianus.

EDCS-10900377.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Re<g=C>inae et Genio loci Gaius Iulius Servandus beneficiarius consularis legionis VIII Augustae posuit Idibus Iuliis Albino et Aem<i=L>liano consulibus libens merito \n
EDCS-10900377.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, and to the Genius of the place, Gaius Julius Servandus, *beneficiarius consularis* of the Eighth Augustan Legion, set this up with good will and deserving merit on the Ides of July, when Albinus and Aemilianus were consuls.
EDCS-10900377.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius Loci, set up by a *beneficiarius consularis* of the Eighth Legion during the consulship of Albinus and Aemilianus.

EDCS-10900378.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci Marcus Bellius Marcellinus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900378.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the place, Marcus Bellius Marcellinus, *beneficiarius consularis*, happily and with good will and deserving merit, paid his vow.
EDCS-10900378.summary: Marcus Bellius Marcellinus, a *beneficiarius consularis*, paid a vow to Jupiter and the Genius Loci.

EDCS-10900379.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci ceterisque diis deabusque immortalibus sacrum Marcus Aurelius Superinius lectus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900379.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the place and to all the other immortal gods and goddesses, Marcus Aurelius Superinius, *lectus* and *beneficiarius consularis*, happily and with good will and deserving merit, paid his vow.
EDCS-10900379.summary: Marcus Aurelius Superinius, a *lectus* and *beneficiarius consularis*, paid a vow to Jupiter, the Genius Loci, and all other gods and goddesses.

EDCS-10900381.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to Jupiter Dolichenus, for the safety of our lords Augusti, a detachment of the Twenty-second Primigenian Pia Fidelis Legion, serving in the lumber yard under Clodius Caerellius, centurion of the First Parthian Legion, with Maiorius Urbanus, *optio*, overseeing, during the consulship of Albinus and Aemilianus.
EDCS-10900381.summary: A detachment of legionaries from the Twenty-second Legion stationed in a lumber yard made a dedication to Jupiter and Jupiter Dolichenus for the safety of the emperors, during the consulship of Albinus and Aemilianus.

EDCS-10900382.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Here lies Honoratianus, my son, snatched away by an untimely fate, an infant who lived only ten months. He lies here, covered by the earth. His father, Flavius Florentinus, had this eternal honor inscribed for him.
EDCS-10900382.summary: This tombstone records the death of a ten-month-old infant named Honoratianus, for whom his father, Flavius Florentinus, commissioned the inscription.

EDCS-10900383.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. For Perpetuus Severus and Quintinia Secunda, mother and step-son, separated from their parents. Carinius Carantius, freedman, [beloved son, who lived] 27 years [---] of them.
EDCS-10900383.summary: This funerary inscription is for Perpetuus Severus and Quintinia Secunda, and was set up by Carinius Carantius, a freedman, for his beloved son who died at age 27.

EDCS-10900384.text_edition: \n ------ et] omnibus dibus Valens votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-10900384.translation: [---] and to all the gods, Valens happily and with good will and deserving merit, paid his vow.
EDCS-10900384.summary: This inscription records Valens paying a vow to all the gods, with the beginning of the text missing.

EDCS-10900385.text_edition: \n Matri deum Marcus Mansuetius Atrectus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900385.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, Marcus Mansuetius Atrectus paid his vow with good will, happily, and deserving merit.
EDCS-10900385.summary: Marcus Mansuetius Atrectus paid a vow to the Mother of the Gods.

EDCS-10900386.text_edition: \n Matri deum Flavia Donata Flavi I filia pro salute sua suorumque votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-10900386.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, Flavia Donata, daughter of Flavius I, paid her vow with good will, happily, and deserving merit, for her own safety and that of her family.
EDCS-10900386.summary: Flavia Donata, daughter of Flavius I, paid a vow to the Mother of the Gods for herself and her family.

EDCS-10900387.text_edition: \n Virtuti sacrum Titus Martialius Candidus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-10900387.translation: Sacred to Virtus. Titus Martialius Candidus paid his vow with good will, happily, and deserving merit.
EDCS-10900387.summary: Titus Martialius Candidus made a dedication to Virtus, likely as a vow.

EDCS-10900390.text_edition: \n Haerecurae sic Liberarinia Severa pro salute Severi fili votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-10900390.translation: Severa, a servant of the household, freely and gladly paid her vow for the health of her son Severus, as was deserved.
EDCS-10900390.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Severa for the health of her son, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10900391.text_edition: \n Fortunae sacrum Marcus Torius Victor praefectus legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-10900391.translation: Sacred to Fortuna: Marcus Torius Victor, prefect of the Twenty-second Legion Primigenia, Pious and Faithful, freely and gladly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-10900391.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Fortuna by Marcus Torius Victor, prefect of a legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900393.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae signum Mercurio et numero |(denarios) |(mille) ut bbenefficiarii legati de ussuris sic eorum omnibus nnis sportulas accipiant die Kalendis Augustis Amatorius Peregrinus veteranus utrumque donum dedit\n
EDCS-10900393.translation: In honor of the divine house, a statue to Mercury and the sum of 1000 denarii, so that the beneficiarii of the legate may receive their sportula daily from the revenues; Amatorius Peregrinus, a veteran, gave both gifts on the Kalends of August.
EDCS-10900393.summary: This inscription records a dedication of a statue and money to Mercury and the imperial household by a veteran, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900394.text_edition: \n Legio XIIII gemina Martia victrix centuria Quinti Fanestris Blandi\n
EDCS-10900394.translation: The Fourteenth Legion Gemina Martia Victrix, the century of Quintus Fanestris Blandus.
EDCS-10900394.summary: This inscription likely commemorates a military unit, the Fourteenth Legion Gemina Martia Victrix, and possibly a specific century, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900396.text_edition: \n Rufus Valerius Quinti filius Sergia Augusta miles legionis XIIII geminae annorum XXV stipendiorum II hic situs est\n
EDCS-10900396.translation: Rufus Valerius, son of Quintus, of the Sergia tribe, from Augusta, a soldier of the Fourteenth Legion Gemina, 25 years old, with 2 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-10900396.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Rufus Valerius, a soldier of the Fourteenth Legion Gemina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900399.text_edition: \n Maris Casiti filius nnrum L stipendiorum XXX ala Parthorum et Araborum turma Variagnis Masicates frater et Tigranus posierunt sic\n
EDCS-10900399.translation: Maris, son of Casitus, 50 years old, with 30 years of service, of the ala Parthorum et Araborum, the turma of Variagnis; his brother Tigranus erected this.
EDCS-10900399.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Maris, a soldier from a cavalry unit, and was erected by his brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900400.text_edition: \n Pradus Sarni filius miles ex cohorte VII Breucorum annorum XXV stipendiorum IIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-10900400.translation: Pradus, son of Sarnius, a soldier from the Seventh Cohort of Breuci, 25 years old, with 4 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-10900400.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Pradus, a soldier from the Seventh Cohort of Breuci, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900401.translation: [burial] of the Nervii, Roman citizens / [century?] of Varius Priscus / [aged?] 31 years, is buried here.
EDCS-10900401.summary: This fragmented tombstone inscription likely records the burial of a Roman citizen from the Nervii tribe, possibly dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900402.text_edition: \n Florio Albano et Statiliae Tattoni Sextus Publicius Fronto parentibus suis fecit\n
EDCS-10900402.translation: Sextus Publicius Fronto made this for his parents, Florius Albanus and Statilia Tatta.
EDCS-10900402.summary: This inscription records a dedication or tombstone made by Sextus Publicius Fronto for his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900403.text_edition: \n Gario annorum L et Sincorilla uxor annorum XXXII et \n
EDCS-10900403.translation: Garius, 50 years old, and his wife Sincorilla, 32 years old, and...
EDCS-10900403.summary: This fragmented inscription likely begins a tombstone for Garius and his wife Sincorilla, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10900404.translation: Gratus, son of Atiacus, aged 30, lies here.
EDCS-10900404.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a man named Gratus, indicating his age and that he is buried here.

EDCS-10900415.translation: Eusebia rests here in peace, who lived 6 years and 5 days.
EDCS-10900415.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for a young girl named Eusebia, stating her age at death.

EDCS-11000004.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Lucinius Victurus ex voto\n
EDCS-11000004.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Lucinius fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000004.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Lucinius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-11000005.summary: This is a dedication by Tertius, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-11000006.translation: Titus Licinius, son of DFICII BAS (illegible patronymic).
EDCS-11000006.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription mentioning Titus Licinius and his father, with an illegible patronymic.

EDCS-11000007.text_edition: \n Legitimus Cossationis Conteddius Teddilli Carantus Victoris Clementinius Carantus Paterio Atessatis Primus Legitimi Sollemnis Apagante Caius Iulius Spatalus Martius Domiti Iustinus Iuvenis Aelius Segillius Nonnus Tatae Maturus Peregrinus\n
EDCS-11000007.translation: Legitimus, Cossationis, Conteddius, Teddilli, Carantus, Victoris, Clementinius, Carantus, Paterio, Atessatis, Primus, Legitimi, Sollemnis, Apagante, Caius Iulius Spatalus, Martius, Domiti, Iustinus Iuvenis, Aelius Segillius Nonnus, Tatae, Maturus Peregrinus.
EDCS-11000007.summary: This inscription lists a very long series of names, possibly related to a dedication, inheritance, or a list of associated individuals.

EDCS-11000010.translation: To the god Medru Matutina, of Cobnertus.
EDCS-11000010.summary: This is a dedication to a local deity named Medru Matutina, possibly associated with Cobnertus.

EDCS-11000011.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Maiae Ibliomarus cissae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000011.translation: Ibliomarus gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury and Maia.
EDCS-11000011.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ibliomarus to the gods Mercury and Maia.

EDCS-11000012.text_edition: \n ------] Segillius et Mercatorius Constans Bellatoricis <f=L>i<l=I>i ex iussu posuerunt \n
EDCS-11000012.translation: Segillius and Mercatorius Constans, sons of Bellatoricus, erected this by order.
EDCS-11000012.summary: This is a dedication or monument erected by Segillius and Mercatorius Constans, sons of Bellatoricus, by order.

EDCS-11000015.text_edition: \n Deae Can--- Reginae Divixta Terentiani votum solvit\n
EDCS-11000015.translation: To the goddess Can--- Regina, Divixta Terentiani fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-11000015.summary: This is a votive inscription to a goddess, partially restored, by Divixta Terentiani.

EDCS-11000017.text_edition: \n Augustae filiae Secconis et Constans uxori posuit\n
EDCS-11000017.translation: Secconis dedicated this to his daughter Augustae.
EDCS-11000017.summary: A funerary dedication by Secconis to his daughter Augustae, likely a private monument.

EDCS-11000018.translation: Sacred to Mercury and Maia. Sennaus [son of] Le..., Gnata wife of Luteui, Ratulla and her sons Rufino and Quadrato, acting as consuls, dedicated [this].
EDCS-11000018.summary: A dedication to Mercury and Maia by Sennaus, Gnata, and their sons Rufino and Quadrato, who were consuls, likely a public or communal religious monument, dated by the consul names.

EDCS-11000019.text_edition: \n ri sacerdos et Candidius Euhodus praefectus de suo posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000019.translation: The priestess [name illegible] and Candidius Euhodus, the prefect, dedicated this at their own expense.
EDCS-11000019.summary: A dedication by a priestess and Candidius Euhodus, a prefect, at their own expense, possibly a public or religious monument.

EDCS-11000020.text_edition: \n Vosego Silvestri sacrum Adnamus Nertomari filius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000020.translation: Sacred to Vosegus Silvestris. Adnamus, son of Nertomarus, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000020.summary: A votive offering to the god Vosegus Silvestris by Adnamus, son of Nertomarus, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000021.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Iulius Coventi et Exsuperator Taluppe votum solveruntt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000021.translation: To the god Mercury, Iulius Coventi and Exsuperator Taluppe willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled their vows.
EDCS-11000021.summary: A dual votive offering to Mercury by Iulius Coventi and Exsuperator Taluppe, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000022.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Iulius Matutinus ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11000022.translation: To the god Mercury, Iulius Matutinus dedicated this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000022.summary: A votive dedication to Mercury by Iulius Matutinus, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000023.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Lucius San ex iussu posuit\n
EDCS-11000023.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Lucius San dedicated this by order.
EDCS-11000023.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Lucius San, possibly under instruction or obligation, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000024.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Lupercianus Lutulli voto fecit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000024.translation: To the god Mercury, Lupercianus Lutulli made this by vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000024.summary: A votive dedication to Mercury by Lupercianus Lutulli, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000025.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Paternianus Pacati posuit libens laetus\n
EDCS-11000025.translation: To the god Mercury, Paternianus Pacati dedicated this, willingly and joyfully.
EDCS-11000025.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Paternianus Pacati, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000026.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Pervinca, daughter of Paternus, dedicated this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000026.summary: A votive dedication to Mercury by Pervinca, daughter of Paternus, a personal religious dedication.

EDCS-11000027.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Severus Equoni, fulfilling his vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000027.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the god Mercury by Severus Equoni, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000028.summary: This incomplete inscription is a dedication to the god Mercury, mentioning a name, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000032.translation: In the consulship of Emperor Antoninus for the third time and Geta for the second time.
EDCS-11000032.summary: This is a consular dating formula, likely part of a larger inscription, referring to the year 208 AD.

EDCS-11000033.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly recording a name, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000037.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio sacrum Victorina Natalis ex voto posuit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11000037.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Victorina Natalis willingly, gladly, and deservedly set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000037.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Mercury by Victorina Natalis, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000038.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio sacrum Fortunatus pro se et suis ex iussu posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000038.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Fortunatus set this up for himself and his family by order, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000038.summary: This is a votive dedication to the god Mercury by Fortunatus for himself and his family, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000042.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio Loci Erennius Pervinci filius votum? solvit? \n
EDCS-11000042.translation: In honor of the divine house. Genio Loci. Erennius Pervinci, son, fulfilled his vow?
EDCS-11000042.summary: This inscription honors the imperial family and a local genius, with a possible votive dedication by Erennius Pervinci, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000043.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Augustius Ursulus et Tauganius \n
EDCS-11000043.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Augustius Ursulus and Tauganius...
EDCS-11000043.summary: This inscription begins a dedication to Jupiter by Augustius Ursulus and Tauganius, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000047.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio attegiam teguliciam compositam Severinius Satullinus civis Tribocus ex voto posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000047.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Severinius Satullinus, a citizen of the Triboci, willingly, gladly, and deservedly set up this tiled roof covering in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000047.summary: This is a votive dedication of a tiled roof structure to the god Mercury by Severinius Satullinus, a member of the Triboci tribe, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000050.text_edition: \n Soli et Lunae sacrum Edullius Visurionis ex iussu solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000050.translation: Sacred to Sol and Luna. Edullius Visurionis fulfilled his obligation willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000050.summary: This is a dedication to the sun and moon deities Sol and Luna, likely by Edullius Visurionis, probably from the Roman period.

EDCS-11000053.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Marti Biviis Quartus Iuvenis votum solvit libens\n
EDCS-11000053.translation: In honor of the divine house, Quartus Iuvenis willingly fulfilled his vow to the god Mars Bivius.
EDCS-11000053.summary: This is a votive inscription honoring the god Mars Bivius, dedicated by Quartus Iuvenis.

EDCS-11000056.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Aelius Super votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000056.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Aelius Super willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000056.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mercury by Aelius Super.

EDCS-11000057.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Civilis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000057.translation: To the god Mercury. Civilis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
