EDCS-11000057.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mercury by Civilis.

EDCS-11000058.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Lucius Attici ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11000058.translation: Lucius Attici erected this to the god Mercury in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000058.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mercury by Lucius Attici.

EDCS-11000059.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury by Moderatus.

EDCS-11000063.translation: To Dis Pater and Mars. Vassorix.
EDCS-11000063.summary: This inscription dedicates offerings to Dis Pater and Mars by Vassorix.

EDCS-11000064.translation: Sacred to Mars. Facundanus fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000064.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mars by Facundanus.

EDCS-11000066.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus stri linia filia annorum XL perius E\n
EDCS-11000066.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Stri Linia, daughter of Perius, aged 40.
EDCS-11000066.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Stri Linia, daughter of Perius, who died at the age of 40.

EDCS-11000067.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Celianus Pagani votum libens merito\n
EDCS-11000067.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Celianus and the villagers willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11000067.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Celianus and the villagers.

EDCS-11000068.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo in honorem domus divinae Lucius Severinius Victorinus veteranus ex signifero legionis VIII Augustae Antoninianae piae fidelis o dedicavit\n
EDCS-11000068.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, in honor of the divine house. Lucius Severinius Victorinus, a veteran former standard-bearer of the Eighth Legion Augusta Antoniniana Pia Fidelis, dedicated this.
EDCS-11000068.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the imperial family, made by Lucius Severinius Victorinus, a veteran of the Eighth Legion.

EDCS-11000069.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio sacrum Acceptinius Festinus posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000069.translation: Sacred to the god Mercury. Acceptinius Festinus set this up, willingly, joyfully, as he deserved.
EDCS-11000069.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury by Acceptinius Festinus.

EDCS-11000070.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio aedem aram Attianus Magissa et Magissius Hibernus custos armorum legionis XXII piae fidelis\n
EDCS-11000070.translation: In honor of the divine house, Attianus Magissa and Magissius Hibernus, keeper of the arms of the 22nd Legion Piae Fidelis, set up this temple and altar to the god Mercury.
EDCS-11000070.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple and altar to Mercury, honoring the imperial family, by Attianus Magissa and Magissius Hibernus, an officer of the 22nd Legion.

EDCS-11000072.text_edition: \n Vosego Maxsiiminus sic votum solvit libens laetus\n
EDCS-11000072.translation: Vosego Maxsiiminus thus fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully.
EDCS-11000072.summary: This inscription records Vosego Maxsiiminus fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-11000074.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iulius Modestus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000074.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Iulius Modestus fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully, as he deserved.
EDCS-11000074.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Iulius Modestus.

EDCS-11000075.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Respectus Iuli solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000075.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Respectus Iuli fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully, as he deserved.
EDCS-11000075.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Respectus Iuli.

EDCS-11000077.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Samm\n
EDCS-11000077.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Samm [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-11000077.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus in honor of the imperial family by Samm.

EDCS-11000078.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Mansuetus Artaci et Oclatia Secunda votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000078.translation: To the god Mercury, Mansuetus Artaci and Oclatia Secunda fulfilled their vow, willingly, joyfully, as they deserved.
EDCS-11000078.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury by Mansuetus Artaci and Oclatia Secunda.

EDCS-11000079.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Cissonio Caius Atulius Gorgias votum solvit\n
EDCS-11000079.translation: To the god Mercury, Caius Atulius Gorgias of Cissos fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000079.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury by Caius Atulius Gorgias.

EDCS-11000080.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mythrae sic vassa sic decem Tertius Rustici votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000080.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, Tertius Rustici fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully, as he deserved, with these vessels and ten [other items?].
EDCS-11000080.summary: This inscription records a votive offering of vessels and other items to the god Mithras by Tertius Rustici.

EDCS-11000081.text_edition: \n Silvano Tettoserus filius Taciti ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11000081.translation: To Silvanus, Tettoserus, son of Tacitus, set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000081.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Silvanus by Tettoserus.

EDCS-11000082.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Lucius Silvanius Probus pontes de suo donum dedit\n
EDCS-11000082.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Silvanius Probus dedicated the bridges as his gift.
EDCS-11000082.summary: This is a dedication of bridges by Lucius Silvanius Probus, likely in the imperial period due to the reference to the 'divine house'.

EDCS-11000084.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus memoriae Dalmatius Severinae carae coniugi posuit quae vixit annos XXVI et menses et dies \n
EDCS-11000084.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, Dalmatius erected this memorial to his dear wife Severina, who lived 26 years, [some days].
EDCS-11000084.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Dalmatius for his wife Severina, dating to a period when such tombstones were common, likely the 2nd-4th centuries CE.

EDCS-11000085.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Cambo Iusti votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000085.translation: To the god Mercury Cambus, Iusti fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000085.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Mercury Cambus by Iusti, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000086.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Mansuetus Natalis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000086.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Mansuetus Natalis fulfilled his vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000086.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Mansuetus Natalis, a common dedication in Roman religion, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-11000087.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Cassii Victorinus et Urbicus libentes posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000087.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, Cassii Victorinus and Urbicus joyfully erected this.
EDCS-11000087.summary: This inscription records the joint erection of a monument to Jupiter and Juno by Cassii Victorinus and Urbicus, typical of Roman religious practice.

EDCS-11000088.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Taranucno et Ravini quibus ex collata stipendia Iulius Iul Caius Copiex iussu pos(uerunt)\n
EDCS-11000088.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Taranucnus and Ravinus, Julius Caius Copiex erected this by order from the money collected from his stipend.
EDCS-11000088.summary: This inscription, honoring the imperial family and local deities, was erected by Julius Caius Copiex using funds from his military pay, suggesting a period of Roman military presence.

EDCS-11000089.text_edition: \n Deae Maiiae aedem a solo fecit Gaius Arrius Patruitus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000089.translation: Gaius Arrius Patruitus, a beneficiarius of the consular governor, built the temple to the goddess Maia from the ground up, fulfilling his vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000089.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple to the goddess Maia by Gaius Arrius Patruitus, a military official, likely in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000090.text_edition: \n Biviis Triviis Quadruviis ex voto suscepto pos<u=I>it Primius Victor votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000090.translation: At the crossroads and intersections, from a vow undertaken, Primius Victor erected this, fulfilling his vow, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000090.summary: This inscription records Primius Victor's fulfillment of a vow related to crossroads and intersections, a common practice in Roman popular religion.

EDCS-11000091.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Claudi Mascellio et Clemens merito solverunt\n
EDCS-11000091.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Claudi Mascellio and Clemens fulfilled their vow deservedly.
EDCS-11000091.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Claudi Mascellio and Clemens, typical of Roman religious practice during the imperial era.

EDCS-11000092.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Procli Pollio et Fuscus votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000092.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, Procli Pollio and Fuscus fulfilled their vows willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000092.summary: This inscription records Procli Pollio and Fuscus fulfilling vows to Jupiter and Juno, a common dedication in Roman religious contexts.

EDCS-11000093.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Nicinia SI L MAT votum solventes titulum posuerunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000093.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and Juno Regina, Nicinia SI L MAT, fulfilling their vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly erected this inscription.
EDCS-11000093.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Nicinia SI L MAT, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000094.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Veccinius Similis et Superinia Decumilla votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000094.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and Juno Regina, Veccinius Similis and Superinia Decumilla fulfilled their vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000094.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Veccinius Similis and Superinia Decumilla, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000095.translation: To the god Mercury, Acconius TAI.
EDCS-11000095.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Acconius TAI, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000096.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Flavi Ubtio Avitus Maximus votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000096.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Flavi Ubtio Avitus Maximus fulfilled their vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000096.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Flavi Ubtio Avitus Maximus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000097.text_edition: \n pro salute Messi Vitalis Rhenicus ex voto libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000097.translation: For the health of Messi Vitalis, Rhenicus, in fulfillment of a vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000097.summary: This is a votive dedication for the health of Messi Vitalis by Rhenicus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000098.translation: To the Divine Manes. Flavius Proculus, a soldier of the above-mentioned legion, a fellow tent-mate, had this made for Aurelius Vitalis, a soldier of the IV Flavia legion, who served for 7 years, lived for 25 years, while on campaign in Germania, his second heir, well-deserving.
EDCS-11000098.summary: This is a tombstone for Aurelius Vitalis, a soldier of the IV Flavia legion, set up by his fellow soldier and heir, Flavius Proculus, and likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000100.text_edition: \n D(is)? M(anibus) io decurioni civitatis Nemetum Fatalis heres f(aciendum) curavit\n
EDCS-11000100.translation: To the Divine Manes? Fatalis, heir of the decurion of the civitas of the Nemetum, had this made.
EDCS-11000100.summary: This is a tombstone, possibly for a decurion of the Nemetum, with the heir Fatalis commissioning the monument.

EDCS-11000101.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Constantio Valentino fratri et Lunae matri Consantius Maximus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000101.translation: To the Divine Manes. Consantius Maximus had this made for Constantinus Valens, his brother, and Luna, his mother.
EDCS-11000101.summary: This is a tombstone commissioned by Consantius Maximus for his brother Constantinus Valens and his mother Luna.

EDCS-11000102.text_edition: \n D(is)? M(anibus) perpetuae securitati Iustiniae Iustinae coniugi Drombinius Sacer ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000102.translation: To the Divine Manes for eternal security. Drombinius Sacer had this placed for Iustinia Iustina, his wife.
EDCS-11000102.summary: This is a tombstone commissioned by Drombinius Sacer for his wife Iustinia Iustina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000103.text_edition: \n Peregrinus Cai Iuli Nigellionis servus nnorum X hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000103.translation: Peregrinus, the slave of Caius Julius Nigellio, aged 10 years, lies here.
EDCS-11000103.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young slave named Peregrinus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000104.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus \xc2\xa0Secundino Iciae IVE et pecto filio eorum Claudius Fe soceris de suo ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000104.translation: To the Divine Manes. Claudius Fe had this set up at his own expense for his parents-in-law, Secundinus, son of Icia, and Pecto, their son.
EDCS-11000104.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Claudius Fe for his parents-in-law, indicating a familial relationship and likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000105.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus BLI C IV NL ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000105.translation: To the Divine Manes. [Name unknown] had this set up.
EDCS-11000105.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, mentioning a person who arranged for its erection.

EDCS-11000108.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Atturus Matti fillius annorum LX Titur[ius ------\n
EDCS-11000108.translation: To the Divine Manes. Atturus, son of Mattius, aged 60 years. Titurius [---]
EDCS-11000108.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Atturus, son of Mattius, providing his age and mentioning Titurius, likely indicating a family member or the person responsible for the monument, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000109.text_edition: \n Viciniae tullini et coniux donavit reficiendam INAGLO [--- D]ecio Augusto [III De]cio Caesare consulibus Iunias\n
EDCS-11000109.translation: The neighborhood association donated this for repair. In the consulship of Decius Augustus and Decius Caesar (III), Iunias [---]
EDCS-11000109.summary: This inscription records a donation for repair by a neighborhood association, dated by the consuls Decius Augustus and Decius Caesar, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000110.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae in sic domus divinae dis Cassibus Castus Taluppae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000110.translation: In honor of the divine household, Cassius Taluppae paid his vow freely, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000110.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Cassius Taluppae in honor of the imperial family, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000112.text_edition: \n Mercurio Vituo Favionis votum libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000112.translation: To Mercury Vitous, son of Favonius, he paid his vow freely, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000112.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury Vitous by an individual named Favonius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000113.text_edition: \n Deo Cissonio ex voto posuit Paternus O\n
EDCS-11000113.translation: Paternus O erected this to the god Cissionius in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000113.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Cissionius by Paternus O, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000114.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Aelius Aquinus [dedicated this].
EDCS-11000114.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Aelius Aquinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000115.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Caupillius Adiutor ex iussu posuit\n
EDCS-11000115.translation: Caupillius Adiutor erected this to the god Mercury by order.
EDCS-11000115.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Caupillius Adiutor, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000117.text_edition: \n I Ursio Capitonis filius ex voto libens laetus merito pos(uit)\n
EDCS-11000117.translation: I, Ursio, son of Capito, willingly, gladly, and deservedly set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000117.summary: This inscription records an individual named Ursio setting up a monument in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-11000119.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus nucconi Cacussonis et Primae coniugi et Pepponi fillio in agro pedes \n
EDCS-11000119.translation: To the Divine Shades: Cacussonis, his wife Prima, and their son Peppo, in a field of [x] feet.
EDCS-11000119.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Cacussonis, his wife Prima, and son Peppo, likely marking a grave plot.

EDCS-11000121.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio beneficiariorum consularis Germaniae superioris et loci Concordiae duarum stationum Caius Iulius Adventus beneficiarius consularis Imperatore C[ommo][do] Augusto III et Burro consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito templum l restituit\n
EDCS-11000121.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Julius Adventus, a beneficiarius consularis, restored this temple to the Genius of the beneficiarii of the governor of Upper Germany and to Concordia of the two stations, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilling a vow, during the consulship of Emperor Commodus Augustus for the third time and Burrus.
EDCS-11000121.summary: This inscription records Caius Julius Adventus, a military official, restoring a temple dedicated to the Genius of the beneficiarii and Concordia, under Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-11000122.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Addo ex voto posuit pro salute sua suorumque MANNOE diem CON SOLOAKTVV POSO II OMES\n
EDCS-11000122.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Addo set this up in fulfillment of a vow for his own health and that of his family; MANNOE diem CON SOLOAKTVV POSO II OMES.
EDCS-11000122.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Addo, likely concerning health and family well-being.

EDCS-11000123.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Reginius Potens votum solvit X Kalendas Octobres Gordiano Augusto et Aviola consulibus\n
EDCS-11000123.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Reginius Potens fulfilled his vow on the tenth day before the Kalends of October, during the consulship of Gordianus Augustus and Aviola.
EDCS-11000123.summary: This inscription records Reginius Potens fulfilling a vow to Jupiter and Juno on a specific date during the consulship of Gordianus Augustus and Aviola.

EDCS-11000125.text_edition: \n Marti et Nemetonae Silvini Iustus et Dubitatus votum solverunt libentes laeti posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000125.translation: Silvinius Iustus and Dubitatus willingly, gladly, and deservedly set this up for Mars and Nemetona.
EDCS-11000125.summary: This inscription records Silvinius Iustus and Dubitatus setting up a monument dedicated to the deities Mars and Nemetona.

EDCS-11000127.text_edition: \n Immunes librarii Lup Gimio Paternius Aprosus Ver Vitalis Aurelius Nobilis Septimius Secundinus Ca Si T I V \n
EDCS-11000127.translation: The tax-exempt scribes: Lup Gimio, Paternius, Aprosus, Ver, Vitalis, Aurelius Nobilis, Septimius Secundinus...
EDCS-11000127.summary: This inscription lists several individuals who were tax-exempt scribes, possibly associated with an administrative or religious body.

EDCS-11000129.text_edition: \n annorum XX Magnus Tulli pater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000129.translation: Magnus Tulli arranged for this to be made for [his son] aged 20.
EDCS-11000129.summary: This inscription records Magnus Tulli arranging for a monument or work to be made for his 20-year-old son.

EDCS-11000137.text_edition: \n Sextinus Romulus Victoriae Seiae votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-11000137.translation: Sextinus and Romulus fulfilled their vow to Seia Victoria willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000137.summary: This inscription records Sextinus and Romulus fulfilling a vow to the deity Seia Victoria.

EDCS-11000138.translation: To the Divine Shades: Atrexstus, his wife Mato, and [their family members] themselves and their own [family] arranged for this to be made (?).
EDCS-11000138.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Atrexstus and his wife Mato, potentially also for other family members, indicating they arranged for their burials.

EDCS-11000142.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus beneficiario consularis stipendiorum XVIII qui vixit annis XXXIII mensibus VIII Prudentia Favorina uxor et heres coniugi dulcissimo faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000142.translation: To the Divine Manes. Prudentia Favorina, wife and heir, had this made for her most dear husband, a beneficiarius of the consular governor, after 18 years of service, who lived 33 years and 8 months.
EDCS-11000142.summary: This is a tombstone for a deceased husband, set up by his wife and heir, who served as a beneficiarius.

EDCS-11000143.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Paternii Gratinus et Clemens ex iussu\n
EDCS-11000143.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Paternii Gratinus and Clemens, by command.
EDCS-11000143.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter, likely by Paternii Gratinus and Clemens, possibly acting under orders.

EDCS-11000144.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti et Victoriae Giamonius Statutus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000144.translation: In honor of the divine house, Giamonius Statutus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars and Victory.
EDCS-11000144.summary: This inscription records Giamonius Statutus fulfilling a vow to Mars and Victory in honor of the emperor's family.

EDCS-11000145.text_edition: \n Deo Silvano Lucios sic Cinonis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000145.translation: To the god Silvanus. Lucios son of Cinonis willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000145.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Silvanus by Lucios son of Cinonis.

EDCS-11000146.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Septumius sic Florentinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000146.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Lucius Septumius Florentinus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000146.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter by Lucius Septumius Florentinus.

EDCS-11000148.translation: To the god Mercury. Vitalius son of Peito.
EDCS-11000148.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Vitalius son of Peito.

EDCS-11000149.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Olisaius Sero et Iustius LIAENIVI MAI E coniugi\n
EDCS-11000149.translation: To the Divine Manes. Olisaius Sero and Iustius [---] for their husband/father.
EDCS-11000149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a deceased individual, dedicated by Olisaius Sero and Iustius, likely family members.

EDCS-11000150.text_edition: \n Maturio Serroni et Manatiae Victorinae filiae eorum fecerunt\n
EDCS-11000150.translation: They made [this] for Maturius Serroni and his daughter Manatia Victorina.
EDCS-11000150.summary: This inscription records Maturio Serroni and his daughter Manatia Victorina as the recipients of a monument or gift, made by an unnamed person or group.

EDCS-11000152.text_edition: \n Diss Cassibus Matuinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000152.translation: To the Divine Casses. Matuinus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000152.summary: This is a votive inscription to the Divine Casses by Matuinus.

EDCS-11000153.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caciro Tege\xc4\x91\xc4\x91i et Billiccedni patribus Magissa filius faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000153.translation: To the Divine Manes. Magissa son of Caciro Tege[---] and Billiccednus had this made for his fathers.
EDCS-11000153.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two fathers, commissioned by their son Magissa.

EDCS-11000155.text_edition: \n Mercurio ex voto Masuinnus Irduti filius custos armorum ex numero VI RGIN CVM \n
EDCS-11000155.translation: To Mercury, according to a vow, Masuinnus, son of Irdutus, keeper of arms from the Sixth Cohort, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11000155.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mercury by Masuinnus, keeper of arms from the Sixth Cohort, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000156.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Maiae Qunitus Seius Postumus votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-11000156.translation: Quintus Seius Postumus joyfully, willingly, and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury and Maia.
EDCS-11000156.summary: This is a votive inscription recording Quintus Seius Postumus fulfilling a vow to Mercury and Maia, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000157.text_edition: \n Dis Inferis Manibus Honoratio Sancto et Sollemniae Iustae Sanctius Honoratus et Sollemnia Iustina monumentum fecerunt\n
EDCS-11000157.translation: Sanctius Honoratus and Sollemnia Iustina made this monument to the Infernal Gods, the Shades, for Honoratus Sanctus and Sollemnia Iusta.
EDCS-11000157.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription commissioned by Sanctius Honoratus and Sollemnia Iustina for Honoratus Sanctus and Sollemnia Iusta, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000158.text_edition: \n Bellius Suavis filius vivus sibi et Noviae Postumi uxsori\n
EDCS-11000158.translation: Bellius Suavis, while alive, [dedicated this] for himself and for his wife, Novia Postuma.
EDCS-11000158.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bellius Suavis, set up by himself while alive for himself and his wife, Novia Postuma, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000159.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to the Shades, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000162.text_edition: \n vus Quint suis viv<u=O>s et Lupulae uxsori defunctae \n
EDCS-11000162.translation: Quintus, while alive, [dedicated this] for himself and for his deceased wife, Lupula.
EDCS-11000162.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Quintus, set up by himself while alive for himself and his deceased wife, Lupula, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000163.text_edition: \n us S T mater R Ammo\n
EDCS-11000163.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning a mother, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000180.text_edition: \n Attonia Selma Nicco Attonis filio et Quinto et Saturnina Caranti filio et filiae LIT \n
EDCS-11000180.translation: Attonia Selma for Nicco, son of Attus, and for Quinto and Saturnina, daughter of Carantius, and [daughter] LIT [---]
EDCS-11000180.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription commemorating Nicco, son of Attus, and Quinto and Saturnina, daughter of Carantius, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000182.text_edition: \n IAINONIS a et CaranOM E T I V S \xc2\xa0sibi I vivus et coniugi --- h(eres) faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000182.translation: IAINIONIS, and CaranOM E T I V S [dedicated this] for himself while alive and for his spouse. The heir took care to have it made.
EDCS-11000182.summary: This is a funerary inscription for IAINONIS and CaranOM E T I V S, set up by the survivor for themselves and their spouse, with the heir overseeing its completion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000183.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Oclatio marito defuncto Rundo filius Materna\n
EDCS-11000183.translation: To the Shades. Oclatius, her deceased husband, [dedicated this] by Rundo, son of Materna.
EDCS-11000183.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to the Shades, with Rundo, son of Materna, commemorating his deceased husband Oclatius, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000184.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sextino filio defuncto Sextus et Perpetuia\n
EDCS-11000184.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sextinus, my son, departed. Sextus and Perpetuia [made this].
EDCS-11000184.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents for their deceased son.

EDCS-11000187.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph mentioning a father and son.

EDCS-11000188.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Ndacoco filio DEIREL MI vixitL\n
EDCS-11000188.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Ndacoco, son of Dei... [lived].
EDCS-11000188.summary: A funerary epitaph for Ndacoco, son of Dei..., whose lifespan is partially recorded.

EDCS-11000190.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Axsini Ammula coniugi Mariniano de suo? \n
EDCS-11000190.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Axsini, wife of Marinianus, [dedicated] by his own [means].
EDCS-11000190.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his deceased wife, possibly paid for by the husband himself.

EDCS-11000191.summary: An incomplete inscription potentially recording the names of two individuals, possibly for funerary or dedicatory purposes.

EDCS-11000194.translation: For Pina, [his] wife, departed. Paternus [made this].
EDCS-11000194.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Paternus for his deceased wife, Pina.

EDCS-11000195.summary: An inscription recording a dedication, likely votive, from Tallon to Samios.

EDCS-11000196.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Visionio Iaso et coniugi fili eius fecerunt\n
EDCS-11000196.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Iaso and his spouse made this for Visionio, his son.
EDCS-11000196.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents, Iaso and his spouse, for their son Visionio.

EDCS-11000197.summary: An incomplete inscription indicating a self-funded funerary monument or dedication by Ustina.

EDCS-11000200.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Sextus Cottius Tasgillus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000200.translation: To the god Mercury. Sextus Cottius Tasgillus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11000200.summary: A votive inscription recording Sextus Cottius Tasgillus fulfilling a vow to the god Mercury.

EDCS-11000201.text_edition: \n Valeri Ambii et Domitianus et sibi vivi fecerunt\n
EDCS-11000201.translation: Valerius Ambius and Domitianus made this, while alive, for themselves.
EDCS-11000201.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Valerius Ambius and Domitianus for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-11000203.text_edition: \n frater et heres Tiberio Candidianio Tacito mon<u=I>mentum fecit Tiberius Candidianius Iunianus \n
EDCS-11000203.translation: His brother and heir, Tiberius Candidianius Iunianus, made this monument for Tiberius Candidianius Tacitus.
EDCS-11000203.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Tiberius Candidianius Iunianus, brother and heir, for Tiberius Candidianius Tacitus.

EDCS-11000204.text_edition: \n Catullini Iu ST Luppili fili is sanctissimi C\n
EDCS-11000204.translation: The most holy Catullinus, son of Luppilius, [---]
EDCS-11000204.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning Catullinus, son of Luppilius, possibly as the deceased or a dedicant.

EDCS-11000206.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Po et Valiae Popp Solimar\n
EDCS-11000206.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Po and Valia Poppa Solimar [---]
EDCS-11000206.summary: This inscription is dedicated to the 'Dis Manes' (spirits of the underworld) for Po and Valia Poppa Solimar.

EDCS-11000211.translation: Mercator gladly fulfilled his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11000211.summary: This inscription records Mercator fulfilling a vow willingly and deservedly.

EDCS-11000214.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that begins with the name Sextus Pus[---].

EDCS-11000215.text_edition: \n Marco Aventinio Honorato patri et Avitiae Victorinae matri et Marco Honoratio \n
EDCS-11000215.translation: For Marcus Aventinius Honoratus, father, and Avitia Victorina, mother, and Marcus Honoratus [---]
EDCS-11000215.summary: This inscription is a dedication for parents, Marcus Aventinius Honoratus and Avitia Victorina, and possibly a son named Marcus Honoratus.

EDCS-11000219.text_edition: \n Caius Baburius Festus Pomptina Arretio tribunus legionis VII geminae felicis praefectus alae Scubulorum Iovi\n
EDCS-11000219.translation: Gaius Baburius Festus of the Pomptina tribe, tribune of the Seventh Twin Legion Felix, prefect of the Scubulorum ala, [dedicated this] to Jupiter.
EDCS-11000219.summary: This inscription records Gaius Baburius Festus, a military officer, dedicating something to Jupiter.

EDCS-11000220.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Octavius Celer praefectus cohortis VII Br<e=I>ucorum et cohortis I Thracum \n
EDCS-11000220.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius Octavius Celer, prefect of the Seventh Cohort of Breuci and the First Cohort of Thracians, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11000220.summary: This inscription records Lucius Octavius Celer, a military commander of two cohorts, dedicating something to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-11000221.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Pistillus et Quintus et Maianus Bellici filii votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000221.translation: Pistillus, Quintus, and Maianus, sons of Bellicus, gladly and joyfully fulfilled their vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest, as deserved.
EDCS-11000221.summary: This inscription records Pistillus, Quintus, and Maianus, sons of Bellicus, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-11000222.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Quintus Vindillius Pervincius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000222.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Quintus Vindillius Pervincius willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000222.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Quintus Vindillius Pervincius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000223.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Intamelius Eburo et Firmia Lucia ex voto in suo posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000223.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Intamelius Eburo and Firmia Lucia placed this in their own property according to their vow.
EDCS-11000223.summary: This inscription records a joint votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Intamelius Eburo and Firmia Lucia, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000224.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Mallius Sofio libens solvit merito\n
EDCS-11000224.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Mallius Sofio willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000224.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Mallius Sofio, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000225.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Novia Prisca ex voto suscepto\n
EDCS-11000225.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Novia Prisca [fulfilled] from her undertaken vow.
EDCS-11000225.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Novia Prisca, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000226.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Victorinia Primitiva posuit\n
EDCS-11000226.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Victorinia Primitiva placed this.
EDCS-11000226.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Victorinia Primitiva to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000227.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Tiberius C\n
EDCS-11000227.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Tiberius C[---]
EDCS-11000227.summary: This is a partial inscription recording a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Tiberius C[---], likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000228.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti Loucetio sacrum Amandus Velugni filius Devas\n
EDCS-11000228.translation: Sacred to Mars Loucetius in honor of the divine house, Amandus son of Velugnus [dedicated this].
EDCS-11000228.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Mars Loucetius in honor of the imperial family, made by Amandus son of Velugnus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000230.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio et Rosmertae Lucius Servandius Quietus ex voto in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11000230.translation: To the god Mercury and to Rosmerta, Lucius Servandius Quietus placed this in his own property according to his vow.
EDCS-11000230.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Mercury and Rosmerta by Lucius Servandius Quietus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000231.text_edition: \n Deabus Parcis Caesonius Liberalis veteranus legionis VIII Augustae \n
EDCS-11000231.translation: To the Parcae goddesses, Caesonius Liberalis, a veteran of the Eighth Augustan Legion, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11000231.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Parcae goddesses by Caesonius Liberalis, a veteran of the Eighth Augustan Legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000232.text_edition: \n Deo Sucelo Silvano Tiberius G I libens posuit\n
EDCS-11000232.translation: To the god Sucellus [and] Silvanus, Tiberius G I willingly placed this.
EDCS-11000232.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the gods Sucellus and Silvanus by Tiberius G I, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000233.text_edition: \n Victoriae Lucius Romanius Respectus decurio civitatis Vangionum libens ex voto in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11000233.translation: To Victory, Lucius Romanius Respectus, decurion of the Vangiones tribe, willingly set this up as vowed.
EDCS-11000233.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Victoria by a decurion of the Vangiones tribe.

EDCS-11000234.text_edition: \n VIO IOCATVS IIES ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11000234.translation: Vio Iocatus set this up as vowed.
EDCS-11000234.summary: This is a votive dedication, likely by an individual named Vio Iocatus.

EDCS-11000235.text_edition: \n ius Quartus votum solvit libens laetus\n
EDCS-11000235.translation: Quartus willingly and happily fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000235.summary: This records the fulfillment of a vow by an individual named Quartus.

EDCS-11000238.text_edition: \n Argiotalus Smertulitani filius Namnis eques ala Indiana stipendiorum X nnrum XXX hic situs est heredes posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000238.translation: Argiotalus, son of Smertulitanus, of the Namnis, an equestrian of the ala Indiana, with 10 years of service and 30 years of age, is buried here; his heirs set this up.
EDCS-11000238.summary: This is a tombstone for Argiotalus, an auxiliary cavalryman, erected by his heirs.

EDCS-11000239.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aurelius Dizza custos armorum legionis II Parthicae centuria IIII pili posterioris vixit nnos XXXVI dies II militavit nnos XIIII Mucmiles legionis supra scriptae centuria et Aurelius Pyrrhus heredes fratri posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000239.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Dizza, armourer of the II Parthica legion, 4th century, rear cohort, lived 36 years and served 14 years. Aurelius Pyrrhus, a fellow soldier of the legion mentioned above, of the same century, set this up for his brother.
EDCS-11000239.summary: This tombstone commemorates Aurelius Dizza, an armourer in the II Parthica legion, and was erected by his fellow soldier and brother.

EDCS-11000240.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aurelio Vapino circitori Aurelius Flavinus contubernali suo pro fratre possuit\n
EDCS-11000240.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Flavinus set this up for his brother Aurelius Vapinus, a circitor, as a companion.
EDCS-11000240.summary: This tombstone records Aurelius Flavinus setting up a monument for his companion and brother, Aurelius Vapinus.

EDCS-11000241.text_edition: \n Quinto Carminio Ingenuo equiti alae I Hispanorum annorum stipendiorum XXV signifero Sacer Iulius heres ex testamento\n
EDCS-11000241.translation: To Quinto Carminio Ingenuo, an equestrian of the ala I Hispanorum, with 25 years of service and serving as a standard-bearer, his heir Sacer Iulius set this up according to his will.
EDCS-11000241.summary: This is a tombstone for Quinto Carminio Ingenuo, a standard-bearer in the ala I Hispanorum, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000242.text_edition: \n Licinus Clossi filius Helvetius nnorum XLVII eques ala I Hispanorum stipendiorum XXVI hic situs est Tiberius Iulius Capito heres p(osuit)\n
EDCS-11000242.translation: Licinus, son of Clossus, a Helvetian, aged 47, an equestrian of the ala I Hispanorum, with 26 years of service, is buried here; Tiberius Iulius Capito, his heir, set this up.
EDCS-11000242.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Licinus, an auxiliary cavalryman, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000243.text_edition: \n Partus Mutii filius eques ala Agrippiana natione Trever nnm XXXV stipendiorum XIIII hic situs est fratres posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000243.translation: Partus, son of Mutius, an equestrian of the ala Agrippiana, of the Trever tribe, aged 35, with 14 years of service, is buried here; his brothers set this up.
EDCS-11000243.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Partus, a Trever auxiliary cavalryman, erected by his brothers.

EDCS-11000244.text_edition: \n Marcus Sempronius Luci filius domo Termestinus annorum XX decurio eques alae Sebosianae hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000244.translation: Marcus Sempronius, son of Lucius, from Termestinus, aged 20, decurion and equestrian of the ala Sebosiana, is buried here.
EDCS-11000244.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Marcus Sempronius, a decurion and auxiliary cavalryman of the ala Sebosiana.

EDCS-11000245.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titio Tummoni et Albisiae coniugi Titius Restitutus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae Piae Fidelis faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000245.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Titius Restitutus, a soldier of the twenty-second legion Primigenia, Pious and Faithful, had this made for Titius Tumminus and his wife Albisia.
EDCS-11000245.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a soldier for his relatives.

EDCS-11000246.text_edition: \n Manibus dis Valerius Maxantius eques ex numeri sic katafractariorum vixit annis XXXII mensibus VI Valerius Dacus frater fecit\n
EDCS-11000246.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Valerius Maxantius, a cavalryman from the unit of cataphractarii, who lived 32 years and 6 months. His brother Valerius Dacus made this.
EDCS-11000246.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a cavalryman and was erected by his brother.

EDCS-11000248.text_edition: \n Veiagenus Sisgi filius miles ex cohorte Raetorum annorum XLVI stipendiorum XXIV natus Monte hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000248.translation: Veiagenus, son of Sisgi, a soldier from the cohort of Raetians, 46 years old with 24 years of service, born in Monte, is buried here.
EDCS-11000248.summary: This funerary inscription records a soldier of the Raetian cohort and his service years.

EDCS-11000249.text_edition: \n Caius Vibius Cai filius Voltinia Virilio eques legionis XV nnorum XLV stipendiorum XXII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000249.translation: Gaius Vibius, son of Caius, of the Voltinian tribe, a cavalryman of the fifteenth legion, 45 years old with 22 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000249.summary: This funerary inscription records a cavalryman of the fifteenth legion and his service years.

EDCS-11000251.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Candidio Martino IIIIIIviro Augustali civi Sentio Severia Severa coniux et Candidia sive Martinia Dignilla filia faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000251.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Gaius Candidius Martinus, an Augustalis and member of the IIIIvirate. His wife Severia Severa and his daughter Candidia, also called Martinia Dignilla, had this made.
EDCS-11000251.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the wife and daughter of an Augustalis and member of the IIIIvirate.

EDCS-11000252.text_edition: \n Caius Lucius Victor decurio civitatis Vangionum omnibus honeribus sic functus et Victori Florentinus et Victorinus filii ob amorem patriae et civium portam omni sumptu suo exstructam donaverunt\n
EDCS-11000252.translation: Gaius Lucius Victor, a decurion of the citizenry of the Vangiones, who had fulfilled all public offices, and his sons Victor Florentinus and Victorinus, have donated the gate, constructed at their own expense, out of love for their homeland and fellow citizens.
EDCS-11000252.summary: This inscription records a donation of a city gate by a decurion and his sons, honoring their homeland and fellow citizens.

EDCS-11000253.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Faustae iuvenis infelicis quae vixit annos XXVII et menses IIII dies XX \n
EDCS-11000253.translation: To the spirits of the departed of Faustas, an unhappy youth, who lived 27 years, 4 months, and 20 days.
EDCS-11000253.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young woman named Faustas.

EDCS-11000255.text_edition: \n Lupulio Luperco doctori artis calculaturae Novionia Motuca mater per Lupulium Lupianum filium fecit\n
EDCS-11000255.translation: Novionia Motuca, mother, had this made through her son Lupulius Lupianus for Lupulius Lupercus, teacher of the art of calculation.
EDCS-11000255.summary: This inscription records a monument made by a mother and son for the teacher of arithmetic.

EDCS-11000256.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The body of Martia Marcellina, mother, after completing 70 years of her life. [Erected by] Placidius [Valen]tianus [and Ana]tol[ius] under the consulship of [consuls' names].
EDCS-11000256.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Martia Marcellina after 70 years of life and names the consuls of that year.

EDCS-11000257.text_edition: \n Oc<t=L>aviae Amandae coniugi carissimae Lasionius Firminus faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11000257.translation: Lasionius Firminus had this made for his dearest wife Octavia Amanda.
EDCS-11000257.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-11000258.text_edition: \n DisDis Severio Lupulo iuveni qui vixit annos XXXV menses V et Severio Florentino fratere sic qui vixit annos XXII menses X negotiatori et caudiciario Licontius mater infelix quae sibi a filiis optaverat fieri contra votum filiis memoriam posuit\n
EDCS-11000258.translation: To the departed spirits. Licontius, an unhappy mother, who had wished for things from her sons contrary to her vows, placed this memorial for Severius Lupulus the younger, who lived 35 years and 5 months, and for Severius Florentinus, a merchant and ship-owner, her brother, who lived 22 years and 10 months.
EDCS-11000258.summary: An epitaph set up by an unhappy mother for her two sons, Severius Lupulus and Severius Florentinus, one a merchant and ship-owner, who died relatively young.

EDCS-11000259.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Spectatiae Peregrinae Servandius Sollemnis et Servandia Servanda fili eiius faciundum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000259.translation: To the departed spirits. Servandius Sollemnis and his children Servandia and Servanda had this made.
EDCS-11000259.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Servandius Sollemnis and his children for Servatia Peregrina.

EDCS-11000260.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Spectatiae Spectatiae coniugi carissimae Luttonius Lupulus coniunx infelicissimus cum filiabus posuit faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000260.translation: To the departed spirits. Luttonius Lupulus, a most unhappy husband, with his daughters, placed this for his dearest wife Spectatia.
EDCS-11000260.summary: An epitaph for Spectatia, erected by her deeply grieving husband Luttonius Lupulus and their daughters.

EDCS-11000264.translation: Aldvalhus rests here, whose soul rejoices in heaven.
EDCS-11000264.summary: A tombstone inscription for Aldvalh, stating that his soul is in heaven.

EDCS-11000265.translation: Ludinus rests here, who lived 30 years; his wife Duda placed the monument.
EDCS-11000265.summary: An epitaph for Ludinus, who lived 30 years, erected by his wife Duda.

EDCS-11000266.translation: Here rests in peace Pauta, aged 56 years and 15 days; Puasi, Quito, Sicco, Boddi, and Ivio placed the monument.
EDCS-11000266.summary: A tombstone inscription for Pauta, aged 56 years and 15 days, erected by five individuals: Puasi, Quito, Sicco, Boddi, and Ivio.

EDCS-11000267.summary: A tombstone inscription stating that Grutilus rests in peace.

EDCS-11000268.translation: Unfaclas rests here, who lived 5 years; his father placed the monument.
EDCS-11000268.summary: An epitaph for Unfaclas, who died at the age of 5, erected by his father.

EDCS-11000270.text_edition: \n Fortunae deae ex voto suscepto Lucius Gnatius Mascellio votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000270.translation: To the goddess Fortuna, Lucius Gnatius Mascellio gladly and deservedly paid his vow as undertaken.
EDCS-11000270.summary: A votive inscription to the goddess Fortuna, dedicated by Lucius Gnatius Mascellio.

EDCS-11000272.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Minervae Vitalinius Secundinus fullo donum dedit\n
EDCS-11000272.translation: In honor of the divine house, Vitalinius Secundinus, a fuller, gave this gift to the goddess Minerva.
EDCS-11000272.summary: A dedication to the goddess Minerva and the imperial family by Vitalinius Secundinus, a fuller.

EDCS-11000273.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deabus Nymphis vicani Altiaienses aram posuerunt cura Octoni Terti et Castoni Cassi X Kalendas Decembres Maximo et Aeliano consulibus\n
EDCS-11000273.translation: In honor of the divine house, the villagers of Altia raised this altar to the Nymphs, under the supervision of Octonius Tertius and Cassius Cassius, ten days before the Kalends of December, during the consulship of Maximus and Aelianus.
EDCS-11000273.summary: This is a votive altar dedicated to the Nymphs by the villagers of Altia, likely in the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-11000274.translation: Attonius Lucanus to the goddess Sulis.
EDCS-11000274.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Sulis by Attonius Lucanus, likely from Roman Britain.

EDCS-11000275.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio Victorius Victor\n
EDCS-11000275.translation: Victoricius Victor to Mercury, in honor of the divine house.
EDCS-11000275.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Victoricius Victor, likely honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-11000277.text_edition: \n Faustinio Faustino Sennauci Florionis filio militi cohortis I Flaviae Damascenorum pediti singulari consularis Gemmellinia Faustina mater et Faustinia Potentina soror heredes secundum volumtatem! testamenti posuerunt vixit annos XXV decidit in flore iuventae faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000277.translation: Faustina Gemellinia, mother, and Faustinia Potentina, sister, had this made in accordance with the terms of the will for Faustinius Faustinus, son of Sennaucius Florion, a soldier of the I Flavia Damascenorum cohort, an infantryman with special duties, who lived for 25 years and died in the flower of his youth. They oversaw its construction.
EDCS-11000277.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by the mother and sister for Faustinius Faustinus, a soldier, who died young, likely in the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000278.translation: Lucius Herennius Laetus, an evocatus of Augustus.
EDCS-11000278.summary: This is a dedication or identification marker for Lucius Herennius Laetus, who served as an evocatus (a recalled soldier) under Augustus.

EDCS-11000279.text_edition: \n Deo Apollini et Sironae Iulia Frontina votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11000279.translation: Iulia Frontina willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the god Apollo and Sirona.
EDCS-11000279.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulia Frontina to Apollo and Sirona, likely from the provinces where both deities were worshipped.

EDCS-11000282.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Felicio Secci votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000282.translation: Felicio Secci willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury, in honor of the divine house.
EDCS-11000282.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Felicio Secci, likely honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-11000284.text_edition: \n Silius Attonis filius eques alae Picentianae annorum XLV stipendiorum XXIV heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000284.translation: Silius, son of Atto, a cavalryman of the Ala Picentiana, aged 45 and with 24 years of service, had this made.
EDCS-11000284.summary: This is a funerary or commemorative monument for Silius, a cavalryman, paid for by himself as the heir, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000286.text_edition: \n Memoriae aeternitatis Lucaniae Victorinae coniugi pudicissimae adque sic castissimae Pervincius Romulus beneficiarius consularis maritus et Romanus filius ob inmensurabilem pietatem eius\n
EDCS-11000286.translation: For eternal memory of Lucania Victorina, his most chaste and most modest wife, Pervincius Romulus, a beneficiarius of a consular, and his son Romanus, for her immeasurable devotion.
EDCS-11000286.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a wife, Lucania Victorina, by her husband and son, highlighting her virtues, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000287.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Fabricio et Acceptio Decembri Paternia Priscilla mater filiis de suo fecit\n
EDCS-11000287.translation: Paternia Priscilla made this for her sons Fabricius and Acceptius Decembrius.
EDCS-11000287.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother, Paternia Priscilla, for her two sons, Fabricius and Acceptius Decembrius.

EDCS-11000288.summary: This inscription likely names individuals, possibly Gemelli, but the text is too fragmentary to determine the exact context or date.

EDCS-11000289.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tertiae matri Venusti et Gemelli et Serotinae Primia Ammilla posuit ex voluptate Tertini Venusti\n
EDCS-11000289.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Primia Ammilla set this up for Tertia, mother of Venustus, Gemellus, and Serotina, out of her fond regard for Tertinus Venustus.
EDCS-11000289.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Primia Ammilla for her mother Tertia, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000291.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deanae Abnobae Cassianus Casati votum solvit libens laetus merito et Attianus frater Falcone et Claro consulibus\n
EDCS-11000291.translation: In honor of the divine house, Cassianus Casati, along with his brother Attianus, gladly and deservedly fulfilled a vow to the goddess Deana Abnova, under the consulship of Falco and Clarus.
EDCS-11000291.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the goddess Deana Abnova, honoring the imperial family, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE, given the consuls.

EDCS-11000293.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Baebius Baebiique filii solverunt votum \n
EDCS-11000293.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Baebius and the sons of Baebius fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11000293.summary: This is a dedication of a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Baebius and his sons, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11000294.text_edition: \n Lucio Valerio Albino domo Hisp |(centurioni) cohortis I Trhacum sic nnorum LXV stipendiorum XXIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000294.translation: Lucius Valerius Albinus, from Hispania, a centurion of the 1st cohort of Thracians, aged 65 years and 23 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000294.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Albinus, a Roman centurion, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000300.text_edition: \n Matri Deum Caius Sempronius Saturninus |(centurio) cohortis XXVI voluntariorum civium Romanorum votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000300.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, Gaius Sempronius Saturninus, a centurion of the 26th cohort of Roman citizen volunteers, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000300.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the Mother of the Gods by Gaius Sempronius Saturninus, a centurion, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11000301.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio Quintus Caecilius Sollemnis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000301.translation: In honor of the divine house, Quintus Caecilius Sollemnis gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-11000301.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Mercury, honoring the imperial family, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11000302.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Mercatori Pruso \n
EDCS-11000302.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Mercury the Trader, Pruso [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-11000302.summary: This inscription records a vow to Mercury the Trader, honoring the imperial family, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11000303.text_edition: \n Minervae sacrum Nympheros Luci Lolli Certi praefecti cohortis V Spanorum \n
EDCS-11000303.translation: Sacred to Minerva. Nympheros, [son of] Lucius Lollius Certus, prefect of the 5th cohort of Spaniards.
EDCS-11000303.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva made by Nympheros, son of Lucius Lollius Certus, who was a prefect in the 5th cohort of Spaniards, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11000304.translation: To the divine spirits of Magia and Ianuaria, the magistra [fulfilled her vow].
EDCS-11000304.summary: This inscription records a vow made to Magia and Ianuaria by a female official (magistra), likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11000305.text_edition: \n EIXOBEIae sacrum us pro Ingenua votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000305.translation: Sacred to Eixobius. Ingenua willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-11000305.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deity Eixobius, with a vow fulfilled by Ingenua.

EDCS-11000309.text_edition: \n Marco Aurelio Antonino Caesari Imperatori destinato Imperatoris Luci Septimi Severi Pertinacis Augusti filio res publica Aquensis\n
EDCS-11000309.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, destined Emperor, son of Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax Augustus, the state of Aquensis.
EDCS-11000309.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, son of Septimius Severus, by the community of Aquensis, likely during the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000311.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate consul pater patriae\n
EDCS-11000311.translation: Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the country.
EDCS-11000311.summary: This is a titulature inscription for Emperor Severus Alexander, dating to his reign (222-235 CE).

EDCS-11000312.text_edition: \n ------ Anton]ino Augusto Rufinus tignariorum m et omnes o\n
EDCS-11000312.translation: To Antoninus Augustus. Rufinus, of the tignarii, and all...
EDCS-11000312.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicated to Antoninus Augustus, mentioning Rufinus, possibly related to construction (tignarii).

EDCS-11000313.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucius Aemilius Luci filius Claudia Crescens Ara miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis Valeri Bassi nnorum XXXIIII stipendiorum XIIII Lucius Aemilius Mansuetus et Lucius Aemilius Albanus fratres idemque heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000313.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Lucius Aemilius Crescens, son of Lucius of the Claudia tribe, an Ara soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion of Valerius Bassus, aged 34, with 14 years of service. Lucius Aemilius Mansuetus and Lucius Aemilius Albanus, brothers, and also his heirs, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11000313.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Aemilius Crescens, a soldier in the 14th Legion, set up by his brothers and heirs, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000314.text_edition: \n Lucius Reburrinius Luci filius Claudia Candidus Ara miles cohortis XXVI voluntariorum civium Romanorum Anici Victoris stipendiorum XIII heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000314.translation: Lucius Reburrinius Candidus, son of Lucius of the Claudia tribe, an Ara soldier of the 26th cohort of Roman citizen volunteers of Anicius Victor, with 13 years of service, his heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11000314.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Reburrinius Candidus, a soldier in a volunteer cohort, set up by his heir, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000318.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gabrillae Antonius Giamatus pater posuit\n
EDCS-11000318.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. Gabrillae. Antonius Giamatus, father, set this up.
EDCS-11000318.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Gabrillae, set up by her father, Antonius Giamatus.

EDCS-11000319.text_edition: \n Valerio Casto patri Valerio Augustali filio Quintus Valerius Pruso vivos sic sibi et Domesticae coniugi fecit\n
EDCS-11000319.translation: To Valerius Castus, father. To his son Valerius Augustalis. Quintus Valerius Pruso made this while alive for himself and his wife Domestica.
EDCS-11000319.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Quintus Valerius Pruso for his deceased father, Valerius Castus, and also for himself and his living wife, Domestica.

EDCS-11000320.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Honoriae Amabili annorum XXXX Honorius Primigenius ux(ori)? dul(cissimae) \n
EDCS-11000320.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. For Honoria Amabilis, aged 40. Honorius Primigenius for his dearest wife.
EDCS-11000320.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Honoria Amabilis, set up by her husband Honorius Primigenius.

EDCS-11000325.text_edition: \n Mercurio Claudius Secundinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000325.translation: To Mercury. Claudius Secundinus willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000325.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury, dedicated by Claudius Secundinus.

EDCS-11000326.text_edition: \n Flavio Mariniano militi legionis VIII Augustae diem functo expeditione Germanica stipendiorum VIII <f=E>uit NOCR Atrectinia Bra L sibi et genero faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11000326.translation: Flavius Marinianus, a soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta, having died on the German campaign after 8 years of service, his wife Atrectinia Bra erected this monument for herself and her son-in-law.
EDCS-11000326.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Marinianus, a soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta, erected by his wife.

EDCS-11000327.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tito Valerio Iustino |(centurioni) legionis VIII Augustae Iustina Felicia secunda heres <f=E>(ecit) \n
EDCS-11000327.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Iustina Felicia, his second surviving heir, erected this for Titus Valerius Iustinus, a centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta.
EDCS-11000327.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Valerius Iustinus, a centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000329.translation: To Florentina, daughter of Tiberius Carrunius.
EDCS-11000329.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Florentina, daughter of Tiberius Carrunius.

EDCS-11000331.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae sanctae Aericurae et Diti Patri Veterius Paternus et Adiecta Paterna\n
EDCS-11000331.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the holy goddess Aericura and to Father Dis. Veterius Paternus and Adiecta Paterna dedicated this.
EDCS-11000331.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Aericura and Father Dis, made by Veterius Paternus and Adiecta Paterna in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11000333.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Neptune. Cornelius Aliquandus, from his own funds, dedicated this to the association of boatmen.
EDCS-11000333.summary: This is a dedication to Neptune by Cornelius Aliquandus for the association of boatmen, made in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11000334.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Publius Veratius Florus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000334.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Publius Veratius Florus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000334.summary: This is a votive inscription from Publius Veratius Florus to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-11000335.text_edition: \n Deae Abnobae Lucilius Moderatus votum solvit merito\n
EDCS-11000335.translation: To the goddess Abnoba. Lucilius Moderatus deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000335.summary: This is a votive inscription from Lucilius Moderatus to the goddess Abnoba.

EDCS-11000336.text_edition: \n Deae Sironae Claudius Marcianus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000336.translation: To the goddess Sirona. Claudius Marcianus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000336.summary: This is a votive inscription from Claudius Marcianus to the goddess Sirona.

EDCS-11000337.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Flavio Sterioni veterano annorum C Flavius Vi<e=I>mens filius et h<e=I>(res) posuit \n
EDCS-11000337.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Flavius Vi mens, his son and heir, erected this for Flavius Sterioni, a veteran of 100 years.
EDCS-11000337.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius Sterioni, a veteran, erected by his son and heir.

EDCS-11000338.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iuvenalius Macrinus vicanus Senotensis maceriam de suo dedit\n
EDCS-11000338.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Iuvenalius Macrinus, a villager of Senotensis, built the wall at his own expense.
EDCS-11000338.summary: This is an inscription by Iuvenalius Macrinus, a villager, who built a wall to Jupiter Optimus Maximus in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11000341.summary: This is a dedication to the god Abnobis by Anulius, likely a votive inscription.

EDCS-11000342.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Nigrinius \n
EDCS-11000342.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Gaius Nigrinius [dedicates this].
EDCS-11000342.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus in honor of the imperial family, by Gaius Nigrinius.

EDCS-11000343.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Lucius Veratius Paternus miles legionis VIII Augustae solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000343.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus, Lucius Veratius Paternus, a soldier of the Legio VIII Augusta, gladly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-11000343.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Veratius Paternus, a soldier of Legio VIII Augusta, to Jupiter Dolichenus.

EDCS-11000344.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury Senotes, likely a votive inscription.

EDCS-11000346.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintus Iuli Auto filio\n
EDCS-11000346.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintus Iulius [dedicated this] for his son.
EDCS-11000346.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Iulius' son, dedicated to the Dis Manibus (Spirits of the Underworld).

EDCS-11000348.text_edition: \n Senecianiorum Sollemnis et Romuli Arruntia Victorina mater ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000348.translation: Arruntia Victorina, mother, arranged for this to be set up for Senecianiorum and Romulus.
EDCS-11000348.summary: This funerary monument was set up by Arruntia Victorina, mother, for Senecianiorum and Romulus.

EDCS-11000349.text_edition: \n Tiberius Iulius Severus decurio civitatis Aquensis aedem restituit et signum posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito Deo Mercurio\n
EDCS-11000349.translation: Tiberius Iulius Severus, decurion of the civitas Aquensis, restored the temple and set up the statue, gladly and with pleasure fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury.
EDCS-11000349.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple and the setting up of a statue to Mercury by Tiberius Iulius Severus, a decurion of the civitas Aquensis.

EDCS-11000351.text_edition: \n Mercurio Cessorinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000351.translation: To Mercury Cessorinus, he gladly and with pleasure fulfilled his vow as deserved.
EDCS-11000351.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury Cessorinus by an unnamed individual.

EDCS-11000353.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deabus Quadrubiis sic Ursinus Coccei et Cassi coniunx Ursinia Gaiani ex voto posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000353.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddesses of the crossroads. Thus Ursinus, husband of Cocceia and Cassia, and Ursinia, wife of Gaianus, set [this] up according to their vow.
EDCS-11000353.summary: This is a dedication to the deae Quadruviae (goddesses of crossroads) in honor of the imperial family, by Ursinus and Ursinia.

EDCS-11000356.text_edition: \n Minervae et Herculi Lucius Antonius Maternus |(centurio) cohortis XXIIII voluntariorum civium Romanorum\n
EDCS-11000356.translation: To Minerva and Hercules. Lucius Antonius Maternus, centurion of the 24th cohort of Roman citizen volunteers.
EDCS-11000356.summary: This is a dedication to Minerva and Hercules by Lucius Antonius Maternus, a centurion in the 24th cohort of Roman citizen volunteers.

EDCS-11000357.text_edition: \n Visucio Mercurio Senilis Massae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000357.translation: Visucio, freely and gladly, has rightly paid her vow to Mercury Senilis Massa.
EDCS-11000357.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury Senilis Massa, dedicated by Visucio.

EDCS-11000358.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury, made by Domitia Facundina.

EDCS-11000362.summary: This is an ownership or dedication inscription for Lucius Pervincius Saturninus.

EDCS-11000366.text_edition: \n Deae Fortunae Lucius Marius Victor posuit\n
EDCS-11000366.translation: Lucius Marius Victor erected this to the goddess Fortuna.
EDCS-11000366.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna, erected by Lucius Marius Victor.

EDCS-11000368.text_edition: \n Abnobae sacrum Lucius Vennonius S Me\n
EDCS-11000368.translation: Sacred to Abnobae, Lucius Vennonius, son of S[---], [paid his vow].
EDCS-11000368.summary: This is a sacred inscription to Abnobae, likely a votive offering by Lucius Vennonius.

EDCS-11000369.text_edition: \n Abnobae Quintus Antonius Silo |(centurio) legionis I adiutricis et legionis II adiutricis et legionis III Augustae et legionis IIII Flaviae felicis et legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis et legionis XXII piae fidelis Domitianae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000369.translation: Quintus Antonius Silo, a centurion of the I Adjutrix, II Adjutrix, III Augusta, IIII Flavia Felix, XI Claudia Pia Fidelis, and XXII Pia Fidelis Domitiana legions, freely and gladly has rightly paid his vow to Abnobae.
EDCS-11000369.summary: This is a lengthy votive inscription to Abnobae by Quintus Antonius Silo, detailing his extensive military service across multiple legions.

EDCS-11000370.text_edition: \n Deanae in honorem domus divinae pro iuventute civitatis Sumelocennensis Iulius Hermes faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000370.translation: Julius Hermes arranged for this to be made in honor of the divine house and for the youth of the community of Sumelocenna.
EDCS-11000370.summary: This is a public works or dedication inscription arranged by Julius Hermes, honoring the imperial family and the youth of Sumelocenna.

EDCS-11000371.text_edition: \n Otacilia Matrona Herecurae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000371.translation: Otacilia Matrona freely and gladly has rightly paid her vow to Herecura.
EDCS-11000371.summary: This is a votive inscription to Herecura, dedicated by Otacilia Matrona.

EDCS-11000374.text_edition: \n Invicto Mythrae sic Publius Aelius Vocco miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000374.translation: To the Invictus Mithras, Publius Aelius Vocco, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis legion, freely and gladly has rightly paid his vow.
EDCS-11000374.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mithras, dedicated by Publius Aelius Vocco, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia legion.

EDCS-11000375.text_edition: \n D<e=I>ae Her<e=I>cu<r=P>ae Quin<t=I>us <e=I>x vo<t=I>o votum libens laetus \n
EDCS-11000375.translation: To the goddess Herecura, Quintus [paid his] vow freely and gladly.
EDCS-11000375.summary: This is a votive inscription to the goddess Herecura, dedicated by Quintus.

EDCS-11000377.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae ex decreto ordinis saltus Sumelocennensis curam agentibus Iulio Dextro et Gaio Turranio Marciano iter(um) magistris\n
EDCS-11000377.translation: In honor of the divine house, by decree of the council of the Sumelocennensis forest, with Julius Dexter and Gaius Turranius Marcianus serving as magistrates for the second time.
EDCS-11000377.summary: This inscription records a decree by the council of the Sumelocennensis forest honoring the imperial family, with specific magistrates named.

EDCS-11000378.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marcus Messius Fortunatus IIIIIIvir Augustalis negotiator artis cretariae negotiator paenularius omni impendio suo fecit Fusco II et Dextro consulibus\n
EDCS-11000378.translation: Marcus Messius Fortunatus, a high priest of the Augustales, a merchant of the pottery trade, a seller of cloaks, made this at his own expense, with Fuscus and Dexter as consuls.
EDCS-11000378.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by Marcus Messius Fortunatus, a merchant and priest, during the consulship of Fuscus and Dexter.

EDCS-11000379.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo signum et columnam cum ara Lucius Iulius Secundinus posuit\n
EDCS-11000379.translation: Lucius Julius Secundinus erected a statue and column with an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-11000379.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue, column, and altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Julius Secundinus.

EDCS-11000380.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iuliae Severinae Decimus Iulius Severus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000380.translation: Decimus Julius Severus arranged for this to be made for the spirits of the underworld in honor of Julia Severina.
EDCS-11000380.summary: This funerary inscription records that Decimus Julius Severus arranged for a monument to be made for Julia Severina.

EDCS-11000381.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Matrona Caratulli filia cives sic Helvetica annorum XL Balbius Liber maritus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000381.translation: Matrona, daughter of Caratullus, a Helvetian citizen, aged 40, Balbius Liber, her husband, arranged for this to be made for the spirits of the underworld.
EDCS-11000381.summary: This funerary inscription records that Balbius Liber commissioned a monument for his Helvetian wife, Matrona, aged 40.

EDCS-11000382.summary: This very brief inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial, possibly naming a person and their status.

EDCS-11000383.translation: For the spirits of the underworld, of Scalla, aged...
EDCS-11000383.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary inscription, commemorating Scalla and indicating her age was recorded.

EDCS-11000384.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tessiae Iuvenili Helvetiae annorum XXXVII Silius Victor Helvetius coniugi et sibi faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000384.translation: Silius Victor, a Helvetian, arranged for this to be made for the spirits of the underworld for his wife Tessia Iuvenilis of Helvetia, aged 37, and for himself.
EDCS-11000384.summary: This funerary inscription records that Silius Victor commissioned a monument for his wife Tessia Iuvenilis, aged 37, and for himself.

EDCS-11000385.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Vitellius Martialis vixit annos testamento f(ieri)? i(ussit)\n
EDCS-11000385.translation: For the spirits of the underworld, Vitellius Martialis lived X years; he ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-11000385.summary: This funerary inscription records that Vitellius Martialis, who lived for X years, commissioned his monument by his will.

EDCS-11000387.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae sacrum Iunii Paternus et Proclus libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000387.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Iunii Paternus and Proclus, willingly, gladly, deservedly.
EDCS-11000387.summary: This inscription records a sacred dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Iunii Paternus and Proclus.

EDCS-11000392.translation: Horrius Agilis fulfilled his vow deservedly.
EDCS-11000392.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Horrius Agilis, likely related to a personal or military dedication.

EDCS-11000394.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Marcus lcius Maternus beneficiarius consularis ex iussu posuit libens laetus merito Iuliis no et consulibus\n
EDCS-11000394.translation: Marcus Iulcius Maternus, a soldier serving as a beneficiarius consularis, set this up by order, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, in the consulship of Iulius and another, whose names are lost.
EDCS-11000394.summary: This inscription records a military dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus by Marcus Iulcius Maternus, a beneficiarius consularis, during a specific consular period.

EDCS-11000395.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Visucio et sanctae Visuciae Publius Quartionius Secundinus decurio civitatis Sumalocennensis ex iussu votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000395.translation: Publius Quartionius Secundinus, a decurio of the community of Sumalocenna, fulfilled his vow to the god Mercury Visucius and the holy Visucia, by order, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000395.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Publius Quartionius Secundinus, a decurio of Sumalocenna, to the gods Mercury Visucius and Visucia.

EDCS-11000396.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Virtuti Lucius Amicius Donatus pro salute sua et suorum votum solvit libens merito Nonis Novembribus Praesente et Extricato consulibus\n
EDCS-11000396.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Amicius Donatus fulfilled his vow to the goddess Virtus for his own safety and that of his family, willingly, deservedly, on the Nones of November, in the consulship of Praesens and Extricatus.
EDCS-11000396.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lucius Amicius Donatus to the goddess Virtus for his health and that of his family, likely during the imperial period given the 'divine house' reference.

EDCS-11000398.translation: Lucius(?) Iuvencius Iustinus set this up for his own safety and that of his family.
EDCS-11000398.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Fortuna Sancta by Lucius(?) Iuvencius Iustinus for his health and that of his family.

EDCS-11000401.text_edition: \n Matronis Alhiahenabus Iulius Veranius Super pro se et suis votum solvit libens merito\n
