EDCS-11000401.translation: Iulius Veranius Super fulfilled his vow to the Matronae Alhiahenabenses for himself and his family, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000401.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Iulius Veranius Super to the Matronae Alhiahenabenses for himself and his family.

EDCS-11000403.text_edition: \n ------] vicani Nediess<e=I>s sic de suo fecerunt cura Quinti Dacci \n
EDCS-11000403.translation: The villagers of Nediessis made this from their own resources, under the supervision of Quintus Daccius.
EDCS-11000403.summary: This inscription records a communal work undertaken by the villagers of Nediessis, supervised by Quintus Daccius.

EDCS-11000404.text_edition: \n Genio Apollinis Exoratus et Secunda votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000404.translation: Exoratus and Secunda fulfilled their vow to the Genius of Apollo, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000404.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Exoratus and Secunda to the Genius of Apollo.

EDCS-11000405.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Lucius Viturius Quintus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000405.translation: Lucius Viturius Quintus fulfilled his vow to the Unconquered God, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000405.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Lucius Viturius Quintus to an Unconquered God, likely a military deity.

EDCS-11000406.text_edition: \n Deo Soli Vita<l=I>ius Severus votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000406.translation: Vita(?)lius Severus fulfilled his vow to the God Sol, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000406.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Vita(?)lius Severus to the Sun God Sol.

EDCS-11000407.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Peto Attici annorum LXXX et Meddilae coniugi annorum LX Fortio <f=I>ilius faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11000407.translation: To the departed spirits. Fortius, son of [?], took care to have this made for Peto Atticus, aged 80, and his wife Meddila, aged 60.
EDCS-11000407.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Peto Atticus and his wife Meddila, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000408.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Mogetio M<e=I>ddi filio civi Mediomatrico annorum LXX filius faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11000408.translation: To the departed spirits. A son took care to have this made for Mogetius, son of Meddius, a citizen of the Mediomatrici, aged 70.
EDCS-11000408.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mogetius, a citizen of the Mediomatrici, erected by his son, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000409.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iulius Secundus et Iulius Ianuarius fratres votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000409.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest. The brothers Julius Secundus and Julius Ianuarius gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11000409.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by two brothers, Julius Secundus and Julius Ianuarius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000410.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo sacrum Candidius Quartus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000410.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest. Candidius Quartus gladly and deservedly dedicated this sacred object, fulfilling his vow.
EDCS-11000410.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Candidius Quartus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000411.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo aram et columnam pro se et suis Caius Vereius Clemens miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000411.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest. Caius Vereius Clemens, a soldier of the Eighth Augustan Legion, a *beneficiarius consularis*, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow by dedicating an altar and column for himself and his family.
EDCS-11000411.summary: This dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, including an altar and column, was made by Caius Vereius Clemens, a soldier in the Eighth Legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000413.text_edition: \n Mercurio Cimb(rio) basem cum signo Lucius Candidius Mercator decurio civium civitatis Sueborum Nicrensium votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000413.translation: To Mercury the Cimbrian. Lucius Candidius Mercator, a *decurio* of the citizens of the Suebi Nicrenses tribe, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow by dedicating a base with an image.
EDCS-11000413.summary: This dedication to Mercury was made by Lucius Candidius Mercator, a local official of the Suebi Nicrenses, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000414.text_edition: \n Mercurio Marcus Lusius Vicarius et Messorius Perpetuus et Valerius Marus libentes posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000414.translation: To Mercury. Marcus Lusius Vicarius and Messorius Perpetuus and Valerius Marus set this up gladly.
EDCS-11000414.summary: This dedication to Mercury was set up by Marcus Lusius Vicarius, Messorius Perpetuus, and Valerius Marus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000415.summary: This is a dedication to Mercury by Timonia Vittuo, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000417.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Neptuno aedem cum signo Valerius Paternus architectus et Aelius Macer ex voto posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000417.translation: In honor of the divine house. Valerius Paternus, an architect, and Aelius Macer fulfilled their vow by dedicating a temple with an image.
EDCS-11000417.summary: This dedication to Neptune, honoring the imperial family, was made by Valerius Paternus the architect and Aelius Macer, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000418.text_edition: \n Visucio aedem cum signo Caius Candidius Calpurnianus decurio civium civitatis Sueborum Nicrensium item decurio civium civitatis Nemetum fecit\n
EDCS-11000418.translation: To Visucius. Caius Candidius Calpurnianus, a *decurio* of the citizens of the Suebi Nicrenses tribe, and also a *decurio* of the citizens of the Nemetum tribe, made this temple with an image.
EDCS-11000418.summary: This dedication to Visucius was made by Caius Candidius Calpurnianus, who held leadership positions in both the Suebi Nicrenses and Nemetum tribes, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000419.text_edition: \n Ostiarius Stellatinianus quem Quintus Vei Vetus consularis pro sua benevolentia et sullicitudine sic probavit commilitonibus Germanicianorum numeri fecit votum solvit libens laetus merito VII Kalendas Martias Fusco et Dextro consulibus\n
EDCS-11000419.translation: Stellatinianus the gatekeeper, whom Quintus Vei Vetus, a consular governor, approved because of his own goodwill and diligence, made into a fellow soldier of the Germaniciani unit; he fulfilled his vow gladly, joyfully, as was deserved, on the 21st of February during the consulship of Fuscus and Dexter.
EDCS-11000419.summary: This is a dedication by a gatekeeper approved by a consular governor, likely related to military service, dated to the consulship of Fuscus and Dexter.

EDCS-11000420.text_edition: \n Lucius Sextionius Terpnus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000420.translation: Lucius Sextionius Terpnus fulfilled his vow gladly, joyfully, as was deserved.
EDCS-11000420.summary: A personal votive inscription by Lucius Sextionius Terpnus, likely a private individual.

EDCS-11000421.text_edition: \n cohortis II Augustae C<y=I>renaicae equitatae turma Aureli Restituti voto animo libens <fec=PP>it \n
EDCS-11000421.translation: The troop of the Second Augusta Cohort of Cyrene, a mounted unit, of Aurelius Restitutus, with a vow and willing spirit, made this.
EDCS-11000421.summary: A dedication by a troop of a mounted cohort, indicating a military context.

EDCS-11000424.summary: An inscription fragment that appears to record a person's name and origin, with the purpose and date missing.

EDCS-11000425.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Volcio Mercatori annorum XXXX Luteia Caranti coniugi pientissimo posuit\n
EDCS-11000425.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Luteia Caranti placed this for her most dutiful husband, Volcius Mercator, aged 40.
EDCS-11000425.summary: A funerary inscription for Volcius Mercator, placed by his wife Luteia Caranti, dating to some point in Roman history.

EDCS-11000426.text_edition: \n ------] Mediomatrico annorum LX Paternus filius ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000426.translation: ------] aged 60. His son Paternus arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-11000426.summary: A funerary inscription fragment mentioning a person's age and that their son arranged for the monument.

EDCS-11000431.text_edition: \n Afrania Afra perpetuae Quieti ex visu monita ob sic salute sua et suorum posuit\n
EDCS-11000431.translation: Afrania Afra placed this for Perpetua Quies, warned by a vision, for her own safety and that of her family.
EDCS-11000431.summary: A votive inscription by Afrania Afra, motivated by a divine vision, for the safety of her family.

EDCS-11000434.text_edition: \n Genium donum dederunt Secundinus et Florus\n
EDCS-11000434.translation: Secundinus and Florus gave this gift to the Genii.
EDCS-11000434.summary: A dedication to the Genii by two individuals, Secundinus and Florus.

EDCS-11000435.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Quintius Ursus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000435.translation: Quintius Ursus fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest, gladly, as was deserved.
EDCS-11000435.summary: A votive inscription by Quintius Ursus to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-11000437.text_edition: \n Ursus --- c(ivitatis) U(lpiae) Sueborum Nicrensium di fasci Tiberius Se et im NeI Iulian\n
EDCS-11000437.translation: Ursus ------ of the Ulpian Civic community of the Suebi Nicrensia, Tiberius Se and im NeI Iulian ------.
EDCS-11000437.summary: An inscription fragment that mentions a person named Ursus, a civic community of Suebi, and possibly Roman officials or names.

EDCS-11000440.translation: Titus Flavius Ianuarius, the local official of the district.
EDCS-11000440.summary: This is an inscription recording Titus Flavius Ianuarius, a magister pagi, likely a local administrative official.

EDCS-11000441.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Paridi vikario sic Eutychas dispensator bene merenti faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000441.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. Eutychas, the steward, had this made for Paris, his deserving deputy.
EDCS-11000441.summary: This funerary inscription honors Paris, a deputy, with a monument erected by his steward, Eutychas.

EDCS-11000443.text_edition: \n Genio Mercuri Alauni Iulius Acconius Augustinus ex voto solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000443.translation: To the genius of Mercury of Alauni. Iulius Acconius Augustinus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000443.summary: This dedication records Iulius Acconius Augustinus fulfilling a vow to the genius of Mercury of Alauni.

EDCS-11000445.text_edition: \n Quartoniae Florentinae matri dulcissimae Urbanius Firmus filius heres ex volu<n=M>tate testamenti faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11000445.translation: For Quartonia Florentina, dearest mother. Urbanius Firmus, son and heir, had this made in fulfillment of the wish in his will.
EDCS-11000445.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Urbanius Firmus for his mother, Quartonia Florentina.

EDCS-11000446.summary: This inscription simply records the name of the craftsman, Xysticus, who likely made the object it is inscribed upon.

EDCS-11000447.text_edition: \n e m e hic interfecere latrones quem genuit Teano Sidicino sic ex Campania altera contexit tellus dedit altera nasci Perigenes habet titulum Secundus officium Publius Clodius Secundus fratri pientissimo\n
EDCS-11000447.translation: Here they killed him, robbers, who was born in Teano Sidicino. Thus another earth from Campania embraced him; the other gave birth to him. Perigenes holds the title. Secundus, his duty. Publius Clodius Secundus, for his most devoted brother.
EDCS-11000447.summary: This complex funerary inscription commemorates Perigenes, who was killed by robbers, and identifies his devoted brother, Publius Clodius Secundus, as the one responsible for the monument, possibly after his original burial in Teano Sidicino.

EDCS-11000448.text_edition: \n Biviis Triviis Quadriviis Aelius Demetrius |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000448.translation: To the deities of crossroads and intersections. Aelius Demetrius, a centurion of the XXII Primigenia legion, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000448.summary: This dedication records Aelius Demetrius, a centurion, fulfilling a vow to the deities associated with roads and intersections.

EDCS-11000449.text_edition: \n Cassibus vota fecerunt Macelus Faustinus m posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000449.translation: They made vows to Cassibus. Macelus and Faustinus erected [it].
EDCS-11000449.summary: This inscription records Macelus and Faustinus making and fulfilling vows, likely related to a deity named Cassibus.

EDCS-11000450.text_edition: \n Numini Augusti Deo Invicto Caetius Maior ex voto suscepto votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000450.translation: To the numen of the August, the Unconquered God. Caetius Maior gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow from a vow undertaken.
EDCS-11000450.summary: This dedication records Caetius Maior fulfilling a vow to the emperor's numen and the Unconquered God.

EDCS-11000451.text_edition: \n Numini Augusti Deo Invicto Lucius Trougilli ex voto suscepto solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000451.translation: To the numen of the August, the Unconquered God. Lucius Trougilli gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow from a vow undertaken.
EDCS-11000451.summary: This dedication records Lucius Trougilli fulfilling a vow to the emperor's numen and the Unconquered God.

EDCS-11000452.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio vici v v Lucius Martialinius Messor et Titus Euemius <C=G>upitus donum dederunt \n
EDCS-11000452.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Martialinius Messor and Titus Evantius Cupitus gave this offering to the Genius of the district.
EDCS-11000452.summary: This is a dedication to the Genius of a district by two individuals, likely made in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000454.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Seniliae Restitutae coniugi pientissimae Marcus Surianius Fidelis et sibi vivus fecit is facti curriculis sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-11000454.translation: To the Divine Manes of Senilia Restituta, a most dutiful wife, Marcus Surianius Fidelis made this for himself and her, while alive; may the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-11000454.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, with a reciprocal provision for himself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000455.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintio Liberali qui vixit annis LI et Proximoniae Sanctae coniugi eiius vivae sibi fili eorum Liberalini Iuvenis et Iuventina et Maternus et Faustus et Tibernalis fili eorum patri incomparabili faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000455.translation: To the Divine Manes of Quintius Liberalis, who lived 51 years, and Proximonia Sancta, his wife, while alive, their children Liberalinus Iuvenis, Iuventina, Maternus, Faustus, and Tibernalis, their children, had this made for their incomparable father.
EDCS-11000455.summary: A funerary monument erected by children for their parents, one of whom had already died, with a specific mention of the father's 'incomparable' status.

EDCS-11000457.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Biviis Triviis Quadriviis Sattonius Iuvenilis beneficiarius consularis pro salute sua et suorum posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito Idibus Decembribus Grato et Seleuco consulibus\n
EDCS-11000457.translation: In honor of the divine house, Sattonius Iuvenilis, a beneficiarius consularis, set this up at the crossroads for his own well-being and that of his family, and gladly paid his vow willingly, happily, deservedly, on the Ides of December in the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus.
EDCS-11000457.summary: A dedication to various deities and aspects of the divine house by a military official seeking good fortune for himself and his family, dated by consuls to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000458.text_edition: \n Herecurae Cottus Galli ex voto suscepto posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000458.translation: Cottus, son of Gallus, erected this image to Hercules in fulfillment of a vow and gladly paid his vow willingly, happily, deservedly.
EDCS-11000458.summary: A votive offering to Hercules by an individual named Cottus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000459.text_edition: \n Herecurae signum Valerius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000459.translation: Valerius erected this image to Hercules, and gladly paid his vow willingly, happily, deservedly.
EDCS-11000459.summary: A votive dedication of an image to Hercules by Valerius, typical of Roman Imperial private religious practice.

EDCS-11000460.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo <M=VI>(aximo) et Iunoni Reginae Genio loci et dis deabusque omnibus Publius Sedulius Iulianus miles le<g=S>(ionis) VIII Augustae Antoninianae beneficiarius consularis pro salute sua et suorum statione iterat<a=O> posuit Imperatore domino <n=IVI>(ostro) Antonin<o=I> Augusto PETVR et consulibus \n
EDCS-11000460.translation: In honor of the divine house, Publius Sedulius Iulianus, a beneficiarius consularis of the legion VIII Augusta Antoniniana, set this up at his post, which he repeated, for his own well-being and that of his family, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, the Genius of the place, and all the gods and goddesses, during the reign of our lord Emperor Antoninus Augustus, and in the consulship of PETVR and his colleague.
EDCS-11000460.summary: A dedication by a military officer to various deities and the imperial family, including a specific legion and mention of his post, dated to the reign of Antoninus.

EDCS-11000461.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi et Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci ETGERIONIS S<e=R>verus miles legionis XXII Antoni<ni>anae beneficiarius consularis pro <sal>(ute) sua et suorum domino <n=IV>(ostro) Antonino Augusto II et Sacerdote II consulibus \n
EDCS-11000461.translation: In honor of the divine house, Severus, a soldier of the legion XXII Antoniniana, a beneficiarius consularis, set this up for his own well-being and that of his family, to Jupiter, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, during the reign of our lord Antoninus Augustus II and Sacerdos II, consuls.
EDCS-11000461.summary: A dedication by a military officer of legion XXII to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius loci, likely from the mid-3rd century CE based on the consul names.

EDCS-11000462.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Genio loci et Fortunae dis deabusque Emeritius Sextus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Severianae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito Maximo et Aeliano consulibus Idibus Ianuariis\n
EDCS-11000462.translation: In honor of the divine house, Emeritius Sextus, a soldier of the legion XXII Primigenia, pious, faithful, Severiana, a beneficiarius consularis, set this up for himself and his family, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the Genius of the place, and Fortune, and to all the gods and goddesses, and gladly paid his vow willingly, happily, deservedly, on the Ides of January in the consulship of Maximinus and Aelianus.
EDCS-11000462.summary: A votive dedication by a soldier of legion XXII to multiple deities and the imperial house, dated to January in the consulship of Maximinus and Aelianus.

EDCS-11000465.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Viducius Geminianus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000465.translation: In honor of the divine house, Viducius Geminianus paid his vow willingly, happily, deservedly.
EDCS-11000465.summary: A short votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the divine house by Viducius Geminianus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000466.translation: Clodius made this for his wife.
EDCS-11000466.summary: A funerary inscription recording that Clodius dedicated this monument to his wife.

EDCS-11000470.text_edition: \n Campestribus sacrum Publius Quintius Luci filius Quirina Terminus domo Sicca Veneria tribunus cohortis XXIIII voluntariorum civium Romanorum\n
EDCS-11000470.translation: Sacred to the Campestres. Publius Quintius, son of Lucius, of the Quirina tribe, from Sicca Veneria, tribune of the 24th cohort of Roman volunteers.
EDCS-11000470.summary: An inscription dedicating a sacred object or place to the Campestres, identifying the dedicator and his military rank and origin.

EDCS-11000471.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Genio nautarum Gaius Iulius Urbicus donum dedit votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000471.translation: For the safety of the Emperor. Gaius Julius Urbicus, a sailor, gave this gift, fulfilling his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000471.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the Genius of the sailors for the Emperor's safety, by Gaius Julius Urbicus, a sailor.

EDCS-11000472.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio peregrinorum Severus Meliddati de suo dono dedit\n
EDCS-11000472.translation: In honor of the divine house, Severus of Melidda gave this gift to the Genius of the foreigners from his own funds.
EDCS-11000472.summary: An inscription honoring the imperial family and dedicated to the Genius of foreigners, by Severus of Melidda.

EDCS-11000474.text_edition: \n Victoriam cum base Domitius Condollus coll<e=I>(gio) peregrinorum votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000474.translation: For Victory, with a base. Domitius Condollus of the collegium of foreigners fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000474.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Victory, by Domitius Condollus, a member of the collegium of foreigners.

EDCS-11000476.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Marti Cnabetio simullac<r=L>um Cartsrcon votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000476.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Mars Cnabetius. For an image of Cartsrcon. He fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000476.summary: An inscription honoring the imperial family and dedicating an image of Cartsrcon to the god Mars Cnabetius.

EDCS-11000477.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae pro salute Luci Dubitati Peregrini veterani ex |(centurione) voluntariorum et suorum omnium voto suscepit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000477.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, for the safety of Lucius Dubitatus Peregrinus, a veteran ex-centurion of the volunteers, and all his family. He undertook the vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000477.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter and Juno for the safety of Lucius Dubitatus Peregrinus, a veteran, and his family.

EDCS-11000479.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Apollini et Sironae aedem cum signis Caius Longinius Speratus veteranus legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis et Iunia Deva coniunx et Longinii Pacatus Martinula Hilaritas Speratianus filii in suo posuerunt votum solverunt libentes laeti merito Muciano et Fabiano consulibus\n
EDCS-11000479.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Apollo and Sirona, with images. Gaius Longinius Speratus, veteran of the 22nd legion Primigenia, the pious and faithful, and his wife Iunia Deva, and their sons Longinii Pacatus, Martinula, Hilaritas, and Speratianus, placed this temple with statues in their own property and fulfilled their vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, under the consulship of Mucianus and Fabius.
EDCS-11000479.summary: A dedication of a temple with statues to Apollo and Sirona, by Gaius Longinius Speratus, his wife Iunia Deva, and their sons, honoring the imperial family and dated by the consuls Mucianus and Fabius.

EDCS-11000480.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico Britannico Germanico pontifici maximo et Iuliae Augustae matri castroruum ob victoriam Germanicam\n
EDCS-11000480.translation: For the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of Parthia, Britain, and Germany, Pontifex Maximus, and for Iulia Augusta, mother of the camps, for the victory in Germany.
EDCS-11000480.summary: An inscription honoring Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Empress Julia Domna for military victories in Germany.

EDCS-11000481.text_edition: \n Iummae Exobni filio cive sic Mediomatrico nnm C Atuns Bunnae filiae coniugi eius nnm LXXX Dometius Iustus filius et heres parentibus fecit\n
EDCS-11000481.translation: To Iumma, son of Exobnus, a citizen of Mediomatrici, 80 nummi. And to Atuns Bunna, his wife, 80 nummi. Dometius Iustus, son and heir, made this for his parents.
EDCS-11000481.summary: A funerary monument erected by Dometius Iustus for his parents, Iumma and Atuns Bunna, indicating a payment of 80 nummi for each.

EDCS-11000482.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely dedicatory, mentioning personal names, with the beginning lost.

EDCS-11000483.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Apollini Granno Lucius Iulius Victorinus decurio civitatis A G pater pro filio L(ucio) Iulio Lepido votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000483.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Julius Victorinus, a decurion of the civitas of A[...], willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled a vow to Apollo Grannus on behalf of his son Lucius Julius Lepidus.
EDCS-11000483.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Apollo Grannus by Lucius Julius Victorinus for his son, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE given the names and titles.

EDCS-11000484.translation: Marcus Victorius Ambaxius, minister of Apollo.
EDCS-11000484.summary: This is a brief inscription recording the service of Marcus Victorius Ambaxius as a minister of Apollo, possibly dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000485.text_edition: \n Genio Martis Ursus Condolli votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000485.translation: Ursus Condolli willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled a vow to the Genius of Mars.
EDCS-11000485.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ursus Condolli to the Genius of Mars, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000487.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Severi Augusti nostri filio P T V S ATREC\n
EDCS-11000487.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of Severus Augustus our lord. P T V S ATREC.
EDCS-11000487.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus (Caracalla), likely from the early 3rd century CE, with a partially preserved acclamation or dedication.

EDCS-11000488.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinaci Augusto Ar[abico ------\n
EDCS-11000488.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, the Arabicus [and...]
EDCS-11000488.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription honoring Emperor Septimius Severus, likely from the early 3rd century CE, with a large lacuna.

EDCS-11000489.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Augusto Luci Septimi Severi Augusti nostri filio statuam ob honorem decurionatus et flaminatus \n
EDCS-11000489.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, son of Lucius Septimius Severus Augustus our lord, a statue for the honor of the office of decurion and the priesthood.
EDCS-11000489.summary: This is an inscription dedicating a statue to Emperor Caracalla, son of Septimius Severus, likely from the early 3rd century CE, related to civic honors.

EDCS-11000491.text_edition: \n Apollini Pythio sacrum Nasellius Proclianus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae Torquato et Iuliano consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000491.translation: Sacred to Pythian Apollo. Nasellius Proclianus, centurion of the Legio VIII Augusta, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled a vow during the consulship of Torquatus and Julianus.
EDCS-11000491.summary: This is a votive inscription by Nasellius Proclianus, a centurion of Legio VIII Augusta, to Apollo Pythius, dated to the consulship of Torquatus and Julianus, likely in the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000492.text_edition: \n Campestribus ex voto Caius Sanctinius Gai filius Quirina Aeternus praefectus\n
EDCS-11000492.translation: For the safety of comrades, Caius Sanctinius Aeternus, son of Gaius, of the tribe Quirina, prefect, by vow.
EDCS-11000492.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Sanctinius Aeternus, a prefect, made for the safety of his comrades, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000493.text_edition: \n Pro salute commilitonum Fortunae sacrum Cassius Troianus |(centurio) Brittonum Murrensium votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000493.translation: Sacred to Fortuna, for the safety of comrades. Cassius Troianus, centurion of the Murrensian Britons, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled a vow.
EDCS-11000493.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Fortuna by Cassius Troianus, a centurion of the Murrensian Britons, for the safety of his comrades, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000494.text_edition: \n Fortunae Respicienti sacrum Nasellius Proclianus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae praepositus cohortis I Helvetiorum Torquato et Iuliano consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000494.translation: Sacred to Fortuna Respiciens. Nasellius Proclianus, centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta, prefect of the First Cohort of Helvetii, discharged his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, during the consulship of Torquatus and Julianus.
EDCS-11000494.summary: This is a votive dedication to Fortuna Respiciens by Nasellius Proclianus, a military officer, dated by consuls to the period when he was prefect of the First Cohort of Helvetii.

EDCS-11000495.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iulius Victor |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae\n
EDCS-11000495.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Iulius Victor, centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta.
EDCS-11000495.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Best and Greatest by Iulius Victor, a centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta.

EDCS-11000496.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Marti Caturigi Genio loci Caius Iulius Quietus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000496.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to Mars Caturigus, and to the Genius of the place. Caius Iulius Quietus, a beneficiary of the consular governor, discharged his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000496.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter, Mars Caturigus, and the Genius Loci by Caius Iulius Quietus, a military official.

EDCS-11000497.text_edition: \n SENO Matronis cohors I Helvetiorum cui praeest Valerius ctus |(enturio) legionis VIII Augustae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11000497.translation: To the Old Mothers. The First Cohort of Helvetii, commanded by Valerius ctus, centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta, pious and faithful, discharged its vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000497.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Matres by the First Cohort of Helvetii, led by Valerius ctus, a centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta.

EDCS-11000498.text_edition: \n Deo Mercuri<o=D> Cultori Ripanus ex iussu eius libens laetus merito reddidit \n
EDCS-11000498.translation: To the god Mercurius Cultor. Ripanus restored this willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, by his order.
EDCS-11000498.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercurius Cultor by Ripanus, who restored something on the god's command.

EDCS-11000499.text_edition: \n Soli Invicto Mithrae sacrum Publius Nasellius Proclianus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000499.translation: Sacred to Sol Invictus Mithras. Publius Nasellius Proclianus, centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta, discharged his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000499.summary: This is a votive dedication to Sol Invictus Mithras by Publius Nasellius Proclianus, a centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta.

EDCS-11000500.text_edition: \n Deo Taranucno Veratius Primus ex iussu\n
EDCS-11000500.translation: To the god Taranucnus. Veratius Primus, by his order.
EDCS-11000500.summary: This is an inscription to the god Taranucnus by Veratius Primus, indicating a divine command.

EDCS-11000502.text_edition: \n Deanae Attonius Senecianus libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000502.translation: To the goddess Deana. Attonius Senecianus discharged his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000502.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Deana by Attonius Senecianus.

EDCS-11000503.text_edition: \n Dianae aedem cum sigillo Lucius Memmius Maternus votum solvit\n
EDCS-11000503.translation: To Diana, a temple with a statue. Lucius Memmius Maternus discharged his vow.
EDCS-11000503.summary: This is a dedication of a temple with a statue to Diana by Lucius Memmius Maternus.

EDCS-11000504.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae genium civitatis Alisinensium Lucius Aventinius Maternus decurio civitatis S T donavit\n
EDCS-11000504.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Aventinius Maternus, decurion of the Alisinensium community, donated the Genius of the community.
EDCS-11000504.summary: This inscription records the donation of the Genius Civitatis by Lucius Aventinius Maternus, a decurion, in honor of the imperial family and the local community.

EDCS-11000505.text_edition: \n Mercurio aram ex voto suscepto Iulianus fieri mandavit\n
EDCS-11000505.translation: Iulianus commanded that an altar be made for Mercury, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000505.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000506.text_edition: \n Deae Fortunae OGL sunt aquibus percultae Durinius Ursus Camigenius Antoninus Ioincius Lupio Secundinius Divixtus Senecionius Ursinus Senonius Verecundus Servatius Servandio Entionius Vittio Moderatius Aprianus nnius Augustus Sennonius Perpetuus Censorinius Ursulus Primanius Potens nnius Cara Augustanius Apis Sennonius Severus Ursinius Catius Victorius Niarius\n
EDCS-11000506.translation: The Goddess Fortuna: Durinius Ursus Camigenius Antoninus Ioincius Lupio Secundinius Divixtus Senecionius Ursinus Senonius Verecundus, and many others, have erected this.
EDCS-11000506.summary: This is a dedication to the Goddess Fortuna by a group of individuals, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000508.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Caius Fabius Germanus beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000508.translation: Gaius Fabius Germanus, a *beneficiarius consularis*, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, for himself and his family.
EDCS-11000508.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and Juno by a *beneficiarius consularis*, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000509.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio Martialis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000509.translation: In honor of the divine house, Martialis fulfilled his vow to Mercury, gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000509.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury, made in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000510.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Viroddi Avita Maximini votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11000510.translation: In honor of the divine house, Avita, wife of Maximinius, gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the goddess Viroddis.
EDCS-11000510.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Viroddis, made in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000511.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio Martis Gnaeus Vindonius Messor votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000511.translation: In honor of the divine house, Gnaeus Vindonius Messor gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Genius of Mars.
EDCS-11000511.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Genius of Mars, made in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000512.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio aedem signum agrum |(centuriarum) IIII Lucius Bellonius Marcus a Mercurio iussus fecit et consacravit\n
EDCS-11000512.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Bellonius Marcus, ordered by Mercury, made and consecrated this temple, image, and land of four centuriae.
EDCS-11000512.summary: This is a dedication of a temple, image, and land to Mercury, made in honor of the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000514.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Tito Aelio Hadriano Antonino Augusto Pio pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli IIII patri patriae numerus Brittonum Elantiensium\n
EDCS-11000514.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power, consul for the fourth time, Father of the Fatherland, the contingent of Britons from Elatia...
EDCS-11000514.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely set up by a military unit, possibly from the mid-2nd century AD.

EDCS-11000520.text_edition: \n AIIRIIORII SEoLensis obiit morte procul? a? patria sua Cappadocia Nannorum XXXV et Nerto \n
EDCS-11000520.translation: SEoLensis... died, perhaps far from his homeland, in Cappadocia, at the age of 35, and Nerto.
EDCS-11000520.summary: This is a funerary inscription for an individual identified as SEoLensis, who died at the age of 35 in Cappadocia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000526.text_edition: \n Fortunae sacrum Brittones Triputienses qui sunt sub cura Titi Mani Titi fili Pollia Magni Senope sic |(centurionis) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis ob \n
EDCS-11000526.translation: Sacred to Fortuna, the Britons of Triputienses who are under the command of Titus Manius Pollia, son of Titus, son of Magnus Senope, a centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, on account of...
EDCS-11000526.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna by a group of Britons serving under a centurion of the 22nd Legion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11000528.text_edition: \n Publius Aelius Silvanus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis legionis V Macedonicae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000528.translation: Publius Aelius Silvanus, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis and of the 5th Legion Macedonica, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000528.summary: This is a dedication by a centurion of two legions, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000529.summary: A fragment of an inscription, too damaged to provide further information.

EDCS-11000533.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo vexillatio cohortis I Sequanorum et Rauricorum equitatae sub cura Antoni Natalis |(centurionis) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis ob burgum explicitum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000533.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, a detachment of the 1st Cohort of Sequani and Raurici (cavalry), under the supervision of Antonius Natalis, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis, paid their vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly for the completion of a fort.
EDCS-11000533.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by a vexillation of a cohort for the completion of a fort, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000538.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Hadriani filio Tito Aelio Hadriano Antonino Augusto Pio pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VIII consuli patri patriae Brittones Triputienses Claro II et Severo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000538.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 8th time, consul, father of the fatherland, the Brittones Triputienses, during the consulship ofrespectively Claro II and Severus.
EDCS-11000538.summary: This inscription records the titles and consulship of Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely dating to 145 CE.

EDCS-11000539.text_edition: \n Marcus Marcellus opus fecid sic su\n
EDCS-11000539.translation: Marcus Marcellus made the work as...
EDCS-11000539.summary: A very fragmentary inscription recording a construction or artwork by Marcus Marcellus.

EDCS-11000540.text_edition: \n Fortunae Lucius Favonius Seccianus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae\n
EDCS-11000540.translation: To Fortune, Lucius Favonius Seccianus, centurion of the 8th Legion Augusta.
EDCS-11000540.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna by a centurion of the 8th Legion Augusta.

EDCS-11000546.text_edition: \n Dianae votum Vitalis pro se et suuos votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000546.translation: To Diana, Vitalis paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly for himself and his family.
EDCS-11000546.summary: This is a dedication to Diana by Vitalis for himself and his family.

EDCS-11000547.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead, of Lucius Sextius Valens [...]
EDCS-11000547.summary: This is a funerary inscription to Lucius Sextius Valens, the rest of which is illegible.

EDCS-11000548.translation: Sacred to Fortune, Lucius Curiatius Ursinus.
EDCS-11000548.summary: This is a dedication to Fortune by Lucius Curiatius Ursinus.

EDCS-11000552.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo pro salute dominorum Imperatorum Marcus Octavius Severus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae praepositus Brittonum et exploratorum\n
EDCS-11000552.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, for the safety of the Lords Emperors, Marcus Octavius Severus, centurion of the 8th Legion Augusta, prefect of the Brittones and scouts.
EDCS-11000552.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Marcus Octavius Severus, a centurion and prefect, for the emperors' safety.

EDCS-11000557.text_edition: \n Soli Invicto Mithrae Sextus Iulius Decimi filius Horatia Florus Victorinus tribunus cohortis XXIIII voluntariorum civium Romanorum templo a solo restituto votum pro se ac suis solvit\n
EDCS-11000557.translation: To Sol Invictus Mithras. Sextus Julius Florus Victorinus, son of Decimus, of the Horatia tribe, tribune of the 24th cohort of Roman citizen volunteers, having restored the temple from its foundations, paid his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-11000557.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Sol Invictus Mithras by a military tribune who restored a temple, likely dating to the late 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000558.text_edition: \n Iuliae Augustae matri indulgentissimi principis Marci Aureli Antonini Pii Augusti matri senatus matri castrorum matri patriae cohors XXIIII voluntariorum Antoniniana civium Romanorum devota numini eius\n
EDCS-11000558.translation: To Julia Augusta, mother of the most indulgent emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Augustus, mother of the senate, mother of the camp, mother of the fatherland, the 24th Antoninian cohort of Roman citizen volunteers is devoted to her divine spirit.
EDCS-11000558.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the 24th cohort of Roman volunteers to Julia Augusta, likely Julia Domna, mother of Caracalla, during the reign of Marcus Aurelius or later in the Severan period.

EDCS-11000559.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Severo [Alexandro] Pio Felici Augusto cohors XXIIII voluntariorum Severiana civium Romanorum devotissima numini eiius\n
EDCS-11000559.translation: To the emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, the 24th Severan cohort of Roman citizen volunteers is most devoted to his divine spirit.
EDCS-11000559.summary: This is an acclamation of loyalty from the 24th cohort of Roman volunteers to Emperor Severus Alexander, dating to his reign (222-235 CE).

EDCS-11000560.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Assonius Iustus miles cohortis XXIIII voluntariorum vixit annos XL Cintusmus s<e=I>cundus heres sua voluntate fecit \n
EDCS-11000560.translation: To the departed spirits. Assonius Iustus, a soldier in the 24th cohort of volunteers, lived 40 years. Cintusmus Secundus, his heir, erected this by his own will.
EDCS-11000560.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Assonius Iustus, a soldier in the 24th cohort of volunteers, who died at age 40, with his heir erecting the monument.

EDCS-11000561.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Meddillio Caranto patri et Victorinae matri Carantia Aelia filia dulcissima heres ex testamento posuit\n
EDCS-11000561.translation: To the departed spirits. Carantia Aelia, daughter and dearest heir, erected this monument to her father Meddillius Carantus and her mother Victorina, as prescribed by the will.
EDCS-11000561.summary: This funerary inscription records Carantia Aelia erecting a monument to her parents, Meddillius Carantus and Victorina, as her inheritance.

EDCS-11000565.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Maximo Dasantis mensori cohortis I Asturum centuria Coeuni Quintini stipendiorum XVIII annorum XXXVIII civis Dalmata ex municipio Magab et Batoni Beusantis optioni cohortis supra scriptae centuria eadem stipendiorum XVIII annorum XL ex municipio Salvio Apies \n
EDCS-11000565.translation: To the departed spirits. Maximo Dasantis, a surveyor in the 1st cohort of Asturians, in the century of Coeunius Quintinus, with 18 years of service, aged 38, a citizen of Magab, and Batunus Beusantis, an optio in the aforementioned cohort, in the same century, with 18 years of service, aged 40, from the municipality of Salvium. Apies [erected this].
EDCS-11000565.summary: This funerary inscription honors two individuals, Maximo Dasantis and Batunus Beusantis, both serving in the 1st cohort of Asturians with specific ranks, years of service, and ages, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000566.text_edition: \n Adnamatius Victorinus et Adnamatia Sperata filii faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000566.translation: Adnamatius Victorinus and Adnamatia Sperata, children, saw to the construction of this.
EDCS-11000566.summary: This is a simple dedication by two children, Adnamatius Victorinus and Adnamatia Sperata, to construct a monument, likely funerary, for their family.

EDCS-11000568.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae vicanis Aurelianensibus signum Minervae suo impendio restituit Faustius Faventinus quaestor Lupo et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000568.translation: In honor of the divine house, Faustius Faventinus, quaestor, restored the statue of Minerva at his own expense for the villagers of Aurelianis, during the consulship of Lupo and Maximo.
EDCS-11000568.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a statue of Minerva by Faustius Faventinus, a quaestor, for the villagers of Aurelianis, during a specific consular period likely in the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-11000569.text_edition: \n liberorumque et totius domus divinae eius Nemesi Publio Cornelio Anullino legato Augusti pro praetore cohors I Helvetiorum et Brittones Aurelianenses sub cura Cai Valeri Titi |(centurionis) legionis ex corniculario co(n)s(ularis)\n
EDCS-11000569.translation: and of their children and the entire divine house. To Nemesis. Publius Cornelius Anullinus, legate of the emperor with praetorian power, the 1st cohort of Helvetians and the Aurelianenses Brittones, under the supervision of Caius Valerius Titus, a centurion of a legion, from the office of a consular staff officer.
EDCS-11000569.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the goddess Nemesis by the 1st Helvetian cohort and the Aurelianenses Brittones, under the command of Publius Cornelius Anullinus, a legate, and overseen by a centurion.

EDCS-11000571.text_edition: \n nus NI rnus Te\xc4\x91\xc4\x91 Tacitus Pedu MED Ianuarinius Atticus Maximinus Dutti Senecianus Senecio Cupitus Celsi votum solverunt libentes laeti merito de sua pecunia Kalendis Septembribus Prisco et Apollinare consulibus\n
EDCS-11000571.translation: and... Tacitus Pedu, ... Ianuarinius Atticus, Maximinus Dutti, Senecianus, Senecio, Cupitus, Celsus paid their vow willingly, gladly, deservedly, from their own funds, on the Kalends of September, during the consulship of Priscus and Apollinaris.
EDCS-11000571.summary: This inscription records a group of individuals, likely soldiers or members of a collegium, paying a vow from their own funds on a specific date, during the consulship of Priscus and Apollinaris.

EDCS-11000575.text_edition: \n Pedatura |(centuriae) Iuli Silvani sub cura Vaterculi Proculi |(centurionis) legio VIII Augusta opus perfecit\n
EDCS-11000575.translation: The works of Pedatura (of the century) of Iulius Silvanus were completed under the supervision of Vaterculus Proculus, centurion of the Eighth Legion Augusta.
EDCS-11000575.summary: This is a building inscription recording the completion of works by a centurion's century under a supervisor.

EDCS-11000579.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deae Fortunae sanctae balineari reduci Valerius Valerianus tribunus cohortis I <G=C>ermanorum Philippianae votum posuit Impperatoribus ddominis nnostris Philippis Auggustis III et iterum consulibus libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000579.translation: In honor of the divine house, Valerius Valerianus, tribune of the First Cohort of Germans Philippiana, dedicated this votive offering to the sacred Goddess Fortuna, who was restored to the baths, freely, gladly, and deservedly, during the consulship of our Lords the Emperors Philippus Augustus for the third time and again.
EDCS-11000579.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna for restoring the baths by a tribune of the First Cohort of Germans Philippiana during the reign of the Philippi.

EDCS-11000581.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Atusonius Victorinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000581.translation: Atusonius Victorinus freely, gladly, and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-11000581.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Atusonius Victorinus.

EDCS-11000582.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Lucius Petronius Tertius |(centurio) cohortis I Germanorum ex voto suscepto pro se et suis posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000582.translation: Lucius Petronius Tertius, centurion of the First Cohort of Germans, set this up in fulfillment of his vow for himself and his family to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, freely, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000582.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by a centurion of the First Cohort of Germans for himself and his family.

EDCS-11000583.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Genio loci Lucius Flavius Paternus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito P consulibus III Idus Martias\n
EDCS-11000583.translation: Lucius Flavius Paternus, an auxiliary soldier under the legate, paid his vow freely, gladly, and deservedly to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, on the 13th day before the Ides of March, during the consulship of P for the third time.
EDCS-11000583.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, and the Genius loci by an auxiliary soldier under the legate, dated to March 13th.

EDCS-11000584.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Lucius Pompeius Gratinus miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis Imperatore Commodo II et Vero II consulibus\n
EDCS-11000584.translation: Lucius Pompeius Gratinus, a soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta and an auxiliary soldier under the legate, set this up for himself and his family to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, and the Genius of the place, during the consulship of Emperor Commodus for the second time and Verus for the second time.
EDCS-11000584.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, and the Genius loci by a soldier of the Eighth Legion Augusta during the consulship of Commodus and Verus.

EDCS-11000585.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et His Sed Titus Flavius Vitalis Aelia Augusta miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis stipendiorum XXVI pro salute sua et sui sic omnium votum solvit libens laetus merito Imperatore Commodo Pio Felici V et Glabrione consulibus\n
EDCS-11000585.translation: Titus Flavius Vitalis, a soldier of the Twenty-second Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, an auxiliary soldier under the legate with 26 years of service, paid his vow for his own health and that of his family, and indeed all, freely, gladly, and deservedly, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, and His Sed, during the consulship of Emperor Commodus Pius Felix Invictus for the fifth time and Glabrio.
EDCS-11000585.summary: This is a votive dedication for health by a soldier of the Twenty-second Legion Primigenia, specifying 26 years of service, during the consulship of Commodus and Glabrio.

EDCS-11000586.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Marti et Herculi diis sic patriis dis deabusque omnibus Iunius Iuvenis signifer in suo votum solvit libens laetus merito Grato et Seleuco consulibus\n
EDCS-11000586.translation: Iunius Iuvenis, a standard-bearer, paid his vow freely, gladly, and deservedly to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, Mars, and Hercules, and indeed all the ancestral gods and goddesses, in his own place, during the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus.
EDCS-11000586.summary: This is a votive dedication by a standard-bearer to various deities, including household gods, during the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus.

EDCS-11000587.translation: …tor, an auxiliary soldier under the legate, paid his vow.
EDCS-11000587.summary: This is a fragmented votive dedication by an auxiliary soldier under a legate.

EDCS-11000589.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus et Marcus Iulius Philippus nobilissimus Caesar balineum cohortis I Germanorum Philippianae vetustate conlabsum sic restituerunt curante Quinto Caecilio Pudente viro clarissimo legato Auggustorum pro praetore insistente Quinto Mamilio Honorato tribuno cohortis supra scriptae\n
EDCS-11000589.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Iulius Philippus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Marcus Iulius Philippus nobilissimus Caesar restored the baths of the First Cohort of Germans Philippiana, which had collapsed from age, under the supervision of Quintus Caecilius Pudens, a most distinguished man, imperial legate with praetorian power, with Quintus Mamilius Honoratus, tribune of the aforementioned cohort, overseeing.
EDCS-11000589.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the baths of the First Cohort of Germans Philippiana by the emperors Philippus and his son, under the supervision of the legate and tribune.

EDCS-11000597.text_edition: \n Genio turmae Iusti Attiani Iustius Attianus decurio de suo posuit \n
EDCS-11000597.translation: To the Genius of the troop of Iustius Attianus, Iustius Attianus, decurion, dedicated from his own funds.
EDCS-11000597.summary: This is a dedication by a decurion to the Genius of his troop, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000598.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci Calvinius Titus beneficiarius consularis \n
EDCS-11000598.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the place, Calvinius Titus, a beneficiarius consularis, dedicated this.
EDCS-11000598.summary: This inscription records a dedication by a beneficiarius consularis to Jupiter and the Genius loci, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000599.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Iulius Agricola veteranus ex |(centurione) et Repenia Augusta pro Digniano filio \n
EDCS-11000599.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, Julius Agricola, a veteran and former centurion, and Repenia Augusta, dedicated this for their son Dignanus.
EDCS-11000599.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter and Juno, honoring the imperial family, made by a veteran centurion and his wife for their son, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000600.text_edition: \n Paterio cornicen Marti Cnabetio votum reddidit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000600.translation: To Paterius, a cornicen, Marti Cnabetio, willingly and gladly paid his vow, as was deserved.
EDCS-11000600.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Marti Cnabetio by Paterius, a cornicen, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000602.text_edition: \n Deo Marti militari Piru Mestui filius legionis X \n
EDCS-11000602.translation: To the military god Mars, Piru son of Mestus, of the Tenth Legion.
EDCS-11000602.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Mars by a soldier of the Tenth Legion, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000603.text_edition: \n Minervae Titus Attonius Fortio |(centurio) ex corniculario et Placidius Placidinus |(centurio) po(suerunt)\n
EDCS-11000603.translation: To Minerva, Titus Attonius Fortis, a centurion and former cornicularius, and Placidius Placidinus, a centurion, dedicated this.
EDCS-11000603.summary: This dedication to Minerva was made by two centurions, one of whom was a former cornicularius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000604.text_edition: \n Deo Soli invicto Mithrae Mercatorius Castrensis in suo constituit\n
EDCS-11000604.translation: To the unconquered god Sol Mithras, Mercatorius Castrensis erected this on his own land.
EDCS-11000604.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument to the god Sol Invictus Mithras by Mercatorius Castrensis, probably during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000605.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Victoriae Verinus VCAL equitum cohortis III Aquitanorum ex voto posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000605.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Victoria, Verinus, of the equites of the Third Aquitanian Cohort, dedicated this from his vow, willingly, gladly, as was deserved.
EDCS-11000605.summary: This inscription is a votive dedication to the goddess Victoria by a soldier of the Third Aquitanian Cohort, honoring the imperial family, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000613.translation: The Twenty-Second Legion, the century of Primus Montanus.
EDCS-11000613.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a legion and a century, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000617.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a century, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11000618.summary: This inscription likely records a military unit or division, possibly related to land ownership or administration, identified by the name Messoris Sacirus.

EDCS-11000619.summary: This inscription is a possessive statement, indicating ownership or dedication by Titus Quartus Agraptus.

EDCS-11000626.text_edition: \n Deae Fortunae sanctae balineum vetustate conlapsum exploratores Sturi et Brittones gentiles et officiales Brit dediticiorum Alexandrianorum de suo restituerunt curam agente Tito Flavio Romano |(centurione) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Idibus Augustis Lupo et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000626.translation: Explorers, Sturi and Brittones, native and official troops of the surrendered Alexandrians, restored to the holy goddess Fortuna a bathhouse that had collapsed from age, at their own expense, with Titus Flavius Romanus, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, overseeing the work, on the Ides of August in the consulship of Lupus and Maximus.
EDCS-11000626.summary: This is a dedication by auxiliary troops of various origins to the goddess Fortuna, who restored a public bathhouse, dated to August in the consulship of Lupus and Maximus (likely 212 CE or later).

EDCS-11000627.text_edition: \n Pro salute Auggustorum Marti et Victoriae aram posuit Caius Cominius\n
EDCS-11000627.translation: For the safety of the Augusti, Gaius Cominius erected an altar to Mars and Victoria.
EDCS-11000627.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to Mars and Victoria for the well-being of the reigning emperors, made by Gaius Cominius.

EDCS-11000631.text_edition: \n Deae Fortunae sacrum Sempronius Martialis praefectus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000631.translation: To the goddess Fortuna, Sempronius Martialis, prefect, freely, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000631.summary: This is a votive dedication to the goddess Fortuna by Sempronius Martialis, a prefect, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-11000632.text_edition: \n Fortunae sacrum Caius Valerius Quirina Titus |(centurio) legionis ex corniculario consularis\n
EDCS-11000632.translation: Sacred to Fortuna, Gaius Valerius Titus, centurion of the legion, formerly an official from the consular staff.
EDCS-11000632.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna by Gaius Valerius Titus, a centurion of a legion, who previously served as an administrative official.

EDCS-11000633.text_edition: \n Genio exploratorum Triputiensium Marcus Aelius Titus librarius posuit\n
EDCS-11000633.translation: Marcus Aelius Titus, a scribe, set up this for the genius of the Triputiensian scouts.
EDCS-11000633.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to the genius of the Triputiensian scouts by Marcus Aelius Titus, a scribe.

EDCS-11000634.text_edition: \n Genio numeri Seiopensium Titus Valerius Carantinus |(centurio) ex voto suscepto libens posuit\n
EDCS-11000634.translation: To the genius of the Seiopensian cohort, Titus Valerius Carantinus, centurion, set this up from a vowed offering, freely.
EDCS-11000634.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of the Seiopensian cohort by Titus Valerius Carantinus, a centurion, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-11000635.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio sacrum Gabinius Nativus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000635.translation: In honor of the divine house, Gabinius Nativus dedicated this to Mercury, fulfilling his vow freely, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000635.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Mercury in honor of the imperial family, made by Gabinius Nativus who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-11000636.translation: To Mercury, Libo, gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000636.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Libo, who willingly fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-11000637.text_edition: \n Mercurio Arvernorigi Cossillus donavi sic es sic visu laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-11000637.translation: To Mercury Arvernorigus, Cossillus gave this, as it was, as it seemed right, gladly, willingly, deservedly.
EDCS-11000637.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury Arvernorigus by Cossillus, likely a local deity, with the donor expressing gratitude.

EDCS-11000640.text_edition: \n Nymphis numerus Brittonum Triputiensium sub cura Marci Ulpi Malchi |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis\n
EDCS-11000640.translation: To the Nymphs, a contingent of the Triputian Britons, under the supervision of Marcus Ulpius Malchus, centurion of the 22nd Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful.
EDCS-11000640.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Nymphs by a detachment of Britons serving in the Roman army, supervised by a centurion.

EDCS-11000641.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Santio Genio |(centuriae) Luci[li ------\n
EDCS-11000641.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Santus, Genius of the century of Lucilius [and others ---].
EDCS-11000641.summary: This is an incomplete inscription honoring the imperial family and a deity named Santus, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-11000644.summary: This is a very short inscription, possibly a territorial marker or a tribal designation.

EDCS-11000645.summary: This inscription appears to identify an individual named Secuens who held the rank of standard-bearer.

EDCS-11000652.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Silvano Conservatori Dianae Augustae v<e=I>xillatio legionis XXII Antoninianae Primigeniae piae fidelis agentium lignariis sub cura Mamertini Iusti optionis dedicavit II Aspris consulibus \n
EDCS-11000652.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Silvanus the Preserver, to Augusta Diana, a detachment of the 22nd Antoniniana Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful, working as woodcutters, under the supervision of Mamertinus Justus, optio, dedicated this, with Aspris as consuls.
EDCS-11000652.summary: This is a military dedication to several deities by a detachment of the 22nd legion involved in logging, dated by the consulship of Aspris.

EDCS-11000654.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius Petronius Florentinus, from the town of Saldas, prefect of the 4th Cohort of Aquitanians, equipped with cavalry, Roman citizens, paid his vow willingly, gladly, deservedly.
EDCS-11000654.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Lucius Petronius Florentinus, a prefect of an auxiliary cohort, to Jupiter.

EDCS-11000655.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Apollini et Aesculapio Saluti Fortunae sacrum pro salute Luci Petroni <F=E>lorentini praefecti cohortis IIII Aquitanorum equitatae civium Romanorum Marcus Rubrius Zosimus medicus cohortis supra scriptae domu Ostia votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000655.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Apollo and Aesculapius, Health, and Fortune, for the well-being of Lucius Petronius Florentinus, prefect of the 4th Cohort of Aquitanians, equipped with cavalry, Roman citizens. Marcus Rubrius Zosimus, a doctor of the cohort mentioned above, from Ostia, paid his vow willingly, gladly, deservedly.
EDCS-11000655.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by a military doctor for the health of his cohort prefect and other deities.

EDCS-11000656.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Ati Utilis cornucularius sic Brittonum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000656.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Atius Utilis, a cornicularius [a type of soldier], thus of the Britons, paid his vow willingly, gladly, deservedly.
EDCS-11000656.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Gaius Atius Utilis, a soldier likely of British origin, to Jupiter.

EDCS-11000657.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno sacrum vexillatio legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis agentium in lignariis sub principe Publio Volusinio Sabino et Tito Honoratio Dentiliano optione Apro et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000657.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus, sacred. A detachment of the 22nd Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful, working in the logging operations, under the princeps Publius Volusinius Sabinus and the optio Titus Honoratius Dentilianus, with Apro and Maximus as consuls.
EDCS-11000657.summary: This is a military dedication to Jupiter Dolichenus and the imperial family by a detachment of the 22nd legion working in forestry, dated by the consulship of Apro and Maximus.

EDCS-11000660.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Girisoni Cubi filio et Bibul<l=i>iae Verecundi filiae coniugibus Gi<r=B>iso Trihyadeia Caeda memoriam pietate \n
EDCS-11000660.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Giriso, son of Cubus, and Bibullia Verecunda, wife, in memory of their marriage, dedicated by Giriso Trihyadeia Caeda out of dutiful affection.
EDCS-11000660.summary: A funerary epitaph for a married couple, dedicated by a relative, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000662.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci Caius Iulius Bellinus et Caius Iul(ius) Montanus beneficiarii consulares pro se et suis Imperatore Commodo Augusto III et Burro consulibus\n
EDCS-11000662.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to the Genius of the place. Caius Julius Bellinus and Caius Julius Montanus, officers serving under the consular legates, for themselves and their families, during the consulship of Emperor Commodus Augustus for the third time and Burrus.
EDCS-11000662.summary: A dedication to Jupiter and the Genius of the place by two officers, mentioning a specific consulship during the reign of Commodus (175-192 CE).

EDCS-11000663.text_edition: \n Apollini et Dianae numerus Brittonum et exploratores Nemaningenses curam agente Tito Aurelio Firmino |(centurione) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solverunt libentes laeti merito Idibus Augustis Orfito et Rufo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000663.translation: To Apollo and Diana, the unit of Britons and the scouts of Nemaninga, under the supervision of Titus Aurelius Firminus, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, fulfilled their vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, on the Ides of August, during the consulship of Orfitus and Rufus.
EDCS-11000663.summary: A votive inscription by a military unit and scouts dedicated to Apollo and Diana, mentioning a specific consulship and a centurion of Legio XXII (likely late 2nd or early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-11000664.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Apollini et Dianae dis deabusque omnibus Titus Aurelius Firminus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis et Aelius Maior optio eius cum suis votum solverunt libentes laeti merito Idibus Augustis Orfito Rufo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000664.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Apollo and Diana, and to all the gods and goddesses. Titus Aurelius Firminus, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, and his optio Aelius Maior, with their families, fulfilled their vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, on the Ides of August, during the consulship of Orfitus and Rufus.
EDCS-11000664.summary: A votive inscription by a centurion and his optio from Legio XXII and their families, dedicated to Jupiter, Apollo, Diana, and other deities, referencing a specific consulship (likely late 2nd or early 3rd century CE).

EDCS-11000666.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae dis deabusque omnibus et Genio loci Aelius Heraclida beneficiarius consularis libens merito\n
EDCS-11000666.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, and to all the gods and goddesses, and to the Genius of the place. Aelius Heraclida, an officer serving under the consular legates, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000666.summary: A votive dedication to Jupiter, Juno, all gods, and the Genius loci by a military officer, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000668.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Mercurio et Genio loci Lucius Flavius Paternus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Imperatore Vero III et Quadrato consulibus\n
EDCS-11000668.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, to Mercury, and to the Genius of the place. Lucius Flavius Paternus, an officer serving under the consular legates, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, during the consulship of Verus for the third time and Quadratus.
EDCS-11000668.summary: A votive inscription by a military officer dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, Mercury, and the Genius loci, mentioning a specific consulship (178 CE).

EDCS-11000669.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Caius Iulius Peregrinus beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito Mamertino et Rufo consulibus VII Kalendas Augustas\n
EDCS-11000669.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, and to the Genius of the place. Caius Julius Peregrinus, an officer serving under the consular legates, for himself and his family, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, during the consulship of Mamertinus and Rufus, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August.
EDCS-11000669.summary: A votive inscription by a military officer and his family dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius loci, mentioning a specific consulship and date (July 26, 175 CE).

EDCS-11000670.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Caius Iulius Petunnatius beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Imperatore Vero III et Quadrato consulibus\n
EDCS-11000670.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno Regina, and to the Genius of the place. Caius Julius Petunnatius, an officer serving under the consular legates, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, during the consulship of Verus for the third time and Quadratus.
EDCS-11000670.summary: A votive inscription by a military officer dedicated to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius loci, mentioning a specific consulship (178 CE).

EDCS-11000672.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Isis Sarapis Conservattori ceteris diis deabusque et Genio Iuni Victorini consularis Caius Secionius Senilis beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000672.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Isis Sarapis the Preserver, and to all other gods and goddesses, and to the Genius of Iunius Victorinus. Caius Secionius Senilis, an officer serving under the consular legates, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000672.summary: A votive inscription by a military officer dedicated to Jupiter, Isis Sarapis, other deities, and the Genius of a specific individual, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000673.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, and to the Genius of the place, for himself and his family. Valerius Maximus, an officer serving under the consular legates, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000673.summary: A partial votive inscription by a military officer and his family dedicated to Jupiter and the Genius loci, likely from the late 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000679.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Titus Aurelius Firminus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000679.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Titus Aurelius Firminus, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000679.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Jupiter.

EDCS-11000680.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Titus Aurelius Firminus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000680.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Titus Aurelius Firminus, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000680.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Jupiter.

EDCS-11000681.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno in honorem domus divinae Publius Ferrasius Claudia Avitus Savaria |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae piae fidelis Constantis Commodae ex aquilifero legionis I adiutricis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito Aproniano et Bradua consulibus\n
EDCS-11000681.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, and to Jupiter Dolichenus, in honor of the divine house, Publius Ferrasius Claudia Avitus of Savaria, centurion of the 8th Legion Augusta, pious, faithful, of Constans, Commodus, formerly an aquilifer of the 1st Legion Adiutrix, for himself and his family, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow, when Apronianus and Bradua were consuls.
EDCS-11000681.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Jupiter and Jupiter Dolichenus, likely during the early 3rd century CE, given the consular names.

EDCS-11000683.text_edition: \n Mercurio Caius Iulius Iustinus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000683.translation: To Mercury, Caius Iulius Iustinus, a beneficiarius consularis, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000683.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Mercury.

EDCS-11000684.text_edition: \n Mercurio Titus Flavius Avitus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000684.translation: To Mercury, Titus Flavius Avitus, a beneficiarius consularis, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000684.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Mercury.

EDCS-11000685.text_edition: \n Nymfae Apollinares renovatae meritoque aris dedicandae quod utrumque a se factum gaudet pro se et suis Lucius Memmius Iuvenis beneficiarius consularis Pudente et Pollione consulibus\n
EDCS-11000685.translation: To the Nymphs Apollinares, renovated and deservedly for the altars to be dedicated, which he is glad he has done for himself and his family, Lucius Memmius Iuvenis, a beneficiarius consularis, when Pudens and Pollio were consuls.
EDCS-11000685.summary: This inscription records the renovation of altars dedicated to the Nymphs Apollinares, with the dedication made by a soldier during the consulship of Pudens and Pollio.

EDCS-11000691.text_edition: \n Diomedes miles cohortis II Hispanorum natione Isaurus stipendiorum VI Fronton et Marcus vexillarii curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000691.translation: Diomedes, a soldier of the 2nd Cohort of Spaniards, of Isaurian nationality, with six years of service, Fronton and Marcus, vexillarii, arranged for this.
EDCS-11000691.summary: This inscription records a dedication arranged by two vexillarii for a soldier named Diomedes.

EDCS-11000700.text_edition: \n Dianae Augustae pro salute dominorum nostrorum Severi et Antonini Augustorum et Getae Caesaris totiusque dis deabusque Lucius Gellius Luci filius Flavia Celerianus Nemes |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis aram et tabulam pro se et suis posuit Cilone et Libone consulibus\n
EDCS-11000700.translation: To Diana Augusta, for the health of our lords Severus and Antoninus Augusti and Geta Caesar, and for the entire household of gods and goddesses, Lucius Gellius, son of Lucius, Flavia Celerianus Nemes, centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, set up this altar and tablet for himself and his family, when Cilo and Libo were consuls.
EDCS-11000700.summary: This inscription records a soldier's dedication to Diana Augusta for the imperial family's health, dating to the period of Severus, Antoninus, and Geta.

EDCS-11000701.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci dis deabusque Lucius Bel\n
EDCS-11000701.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, and to the Genius of the place, and to the gods and goddesses, Lucius Bel...
EDCS-11000701.summary: This is an incomplete inscription recording a dedication to Jupiter, the Genius loci, and other deities by Lucius Bel.

EDCS-11000703.text_edition: \n Apollini sacrum Caius Iulius Sabinus I \n
EDCS-11000703.translation: Sacred to Apollo, Caius Iulius Sabinus I...
EDCS-11000703.summary: This is an incomplete inscription recording a dedication to Apollo by Caius Iulius Sabinus.

EDCS-11000704.text_edition: \n Apollini Lucius Sertorius Ianuarius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000704.translation: To Apollo, Lucius Sertorius Ianuarius willingly fulfilled his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11000704.summary: A private vow fulfillment to the god Apollo by Lucius Sertorius Ianuarius.

EDCS-11000705.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Attini Victorius Salutaris libertus \n
EDCS-11000705.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Attis, Victorius Salutaris, freedman.
