EDCS-11000705.summary: An inscription honoring the imperial family and the god Attis, dedicated by Victorius Salutaris, a freedman.

EDCS-11000706.text_edition: \n Deabus Aufaniabus et Tutelae loci pro salute et incolumitate sua suorumque omnium Lucius Maiorius Cogitatus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Idibus Iuliis Gentiano et Basso consulibus\n
EDCS-11000706.translation: To the goddesses of the Aufanian region and to Tutela of the place, for his own health and the safety of all his kin, Lucius Maiorius Cogitatus, a beneficiarius consularis, willingly, gladly, and as deserved fulfilled his vow on the Ides of July in the consulship of Gentianus and Bassus.
EDCS-11000706.summary: A vow fulfillment to local goddesses and Tutela for health and safety, dedicated by Lucius Maiorius Cogitatus, a beneficiarius consularis, during the consulship of Gentianus and Bassus.

EDCS-11000707.text_edition: \n Bellonae Terentia Martia votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000707.translation: To Bellona, Terentia Martia willingly fulfilled her vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11000707.summary: A private vow fulfillment to the goddess Bellona by Terentia Martia.

EDCS-11000708.text_edition: \n Bibis sic Tribis sic Quadruviis Iulius Bellicus veteranus legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000708.translation: To the four roads, Tribus, and Bibis, Iulius Bellicus, a veteran of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, willingly, gladly, and as deserved fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000708.summary: A vow fulfillment by Iulius Bellicus, a veteran of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, to roadside deities.

EDCS-11000709.text_edition: \n Bonis Cassubus sic vexillarii legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis q(uorum) curam e<g=C>it Cornelius Marcellus <c=S>enturio legionis eiusdem votum solvit libens laetus S merito \n
EDCS-11000709.translation: To the good Cassubian deities, the standard-bearers of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, whose care was undertaken by Cornelius Marcellus, a centurion of the same legion, willingly, gladly, and with good merit fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11000709.summary: A vow fulfillment by standard-bearers and a centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia to local deities.

EDCS-11000710.text_edition: \n Bonum sic Eventum sic eeqquitum legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Albanius Agricola et Macrinius Iulianus qquaestores cives Sumelocennenses Pompeiano et Paeligniano consulibus\n
EDCS-11000710.translation: To Good Fortune, the equestrians of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, Albanius Agricola and Macrinius Iulianus, quaestors and citizens of Sumelocenna, during the consulship of Pompeianus and Paelignianus.
EDCS-11000710.summary: An inscription related to the equestrians of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, mentioning their quaestors, Albanius Agricola and Macrinius Iulianus, during the consulship of Pompeianus and Paelignianus.

EDCS-11000711.text_edition: \n Pro salute ddominorum nnostrorum sanctissimorum Impperatorum Bono Eventu sic militum exercitus Germaniae superioris Maternius Perpetuus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis strator consularis curam agente to PO\n
EDCS-11000711.translation: For the health of our most sacred masters the Emperors, and for Good Fortune, and for the soldiers of the army of Upper Germany, Maternius Perpetuus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, a strator consularis, while the cura was being handled by...
EDCS-11000711.summary: An inscription for the health of the Emperors and the army of Upper Germany, dedicated by Maternius Perpetuus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia.

EDCS-11000713.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deae Dianae Caius Lucilius Messor miles legionis XXII Primigeniae fidelis custos basilicae Dextro et Prisco consulibus\n
EDCS-11000713.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Diana, Caius Lucilius Messor, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, faithful, guardian of the basilica, during the consulship of Dextrus and Priscus.
EDCS-11000713.summary: An inscription honoring the imperial house and the goddess Diana, dedicated by Caius Lucilius Messor, a soldier and basilica guardian of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, during the consulship of Dextrus and Priscus.

EDCS-11000715.text_edition: \n Deae Fortunae Placidius Curio votum solvit libens merito in suo\n
EDCS-11000715.translation: To the goddess Fortuna, Placidius Curio willingly fulfilled his vow, as deserved, on his own property.
EDCS-11000715.summary: A private vow fulfillment to the goddess Fortuna by Placidius Curio.

EDCS-11000716.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna.

EDCS-11000717.text_edition: \n Fortunae Augustae sacrum Caius Nemonius Senecio curator vici et Titus Tertius Felix quaestor et Caius Atius Verecundus actor de suo posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000717.translation: Sacred to Imperial Fortuna Augusta. Gaius Nemonius Senecio, curator of the district, Titus Tertius Felix, quaestor, and Gaius Atius Verecundus, administrator, set this up at their own expense.
EDCS-11000717.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna Augusta by local officials, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000718.text_edition: \n Pro salute Imperatoris Marci Aureli Commod[i] Antonini Pii Felicis Fortunae Reduci legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Caius Gentilius Victor veteranus legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis missus honesta missione negotiator gladiarius testamento suo fieri iussit ad HS nummum VIII milia\n
EDCS-11000718.translation: For the health of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Pius Felix, to Fortuna Redux, Gaius Gentilius Victor, a veteran of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, piously and faithfully, honorably discharged, a merchant dealing in gladiators, ordered this to be made by his will for 8,000 sesterces.
EDCS-11000718.summary: This is a dedication to Fortuna Redux and for the emperor's health by a veteran of the 22nd Legion, likely from the period of Commodus (177-192 CE).

EDCS-11000720.text_edition: \n Deae Fortunae Salutari lius Lucianus tribunus pro filio libens vovit P tia Maximina uxor? p(osuit)\n
EDCS-11000720.translation: To the goddess Fortuna Salutaris.lius Lucianus, tribune, vowed willingly for his son. P(t)ia Maximina, his wife(?), set this up.
EDCS-11000720.summary: This is a votive offering to Fortuna Salutaris by a tribune for his son, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000721.text_edition: \n Fortunam superam Honori aquilae legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Marcus Minicius Marci filius Quirina Lindo Marcellinus primus pilus legionis eiusdem \n
EDCS-11000721.translation: To Fortunata, the superior, and to the honor of the eagle of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, piously and faithfully, Marcus Minicius Marcellinus, son of Marcus, of the Quirina tribe, primus pilus of the same legion, set this up.
EDCS-11000721.summary: This is a dedication to Fortunata and the eagle standard of the 22nd Legion by its primus pilus, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000722.text_edition: \n Genio |(centuriae) Nigidi Censorini Aelius Verinus architectus Geminius Primus custos armorum ex voto suscepto posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000722.translation: To the genius of the century of Nigidius Censorinus, Aelius Verinus, architect, and Geminius Primus, armour-bearer, set this up in fulfillment of a vowed offering.
EDCS-11000722.summary: This records a dedication to the genius of a military century by two soldiers, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000723.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio |(centuriae) II |(pili posterioris) Atrectius Atilianus tesserarius stipendiorum XVIII pro se et contironibus suos sic cum tabula posuit Augustius Finio Crescentius Liberalis Cobnertius Speratus Publius Publianus Sextius Secundinus Victorius Equester llius Augustus Perpetuius Patruinus Rufius Carinus Hilarius Sequens Agrius Largus dedicata VI Idus Maias Clementino et Agricola consulibus votum\n
EDCS-11000723.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the genius of the century of the II double-pili posterioris, Atrectius Atilianus, tesserarius with 18 years of service, set this up for himself and his comrades, along with this tablet. Augustius Finio Crescentius, Liberalis Cobnertius, Speratus Publianus, Sextus Secundinus, Victorius Equester, llius Augustus, Perpetuius Patruinus, Rufius Carinus, Hilarius Sequens, Agrius Largus. Dedicated on the sixth day before the Ides of May, in the consulship of Clementinus and Agricola.
EDCS-11000723.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of a military century and the imperial house by a group of soldiers, dated by consuls to 201 CE.

EDCS-11000724.text_edition: \n Genio |(centuriae) Caius Mellonius Severus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000724.translation: To the genius of the century, Gaius Mellonius Severus, centurion of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, deservedly.
EDCS-11000724.summary: This records a centurion of the 22nd Legion fulfilling a vow to his century's genius, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000725.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio |(centuriae) II Titus Quiaetius sic Perpetuus custos armorum votum solvit libens laetus merito probatus Maximo et Urbano consulibus\n
EDCS-11000725.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the genius of the II century, Titus Quiaetius Perpetuus, armour-bearer, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, deservedly, approved. In the consulship of Maximus and Urbanus.
EDCS-11000725.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of a military century and the imperial house by an armour-bearer, dated by consuls to 217 CE.

EDCS-11000726.text_edition: \n Genium SI[] III[] SV[] VV[] VILII donum dedit Titius Saturio custos armorum de suo restituit\n
EDCS-11000726.translation: To the genius S.I. III S.V.V.V. VILII, Titus Saturio, armour-bearer, gave a gift from his own resources and restored it.
EDCS-11000726.summary: This records an armour-bearer's gift and restoration to a genius, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000727.text_edition: \n Genio centuriae Valerius Martius et Secundius Mansuetus votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000727.translation: To the genius of the century, Valerius Martius and Secundius Mansuetus gladly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11000727.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Valerius Martius and Secundius Mansuetus to the genius of their century.

EDCS-11000728.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio |(centuriae) Volusi Veri Honoratius Clemens miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laetus merito Cilone et Libone consulibus\n
EDCS-11000728.translation: In honor of the divine house, Honoratius Clemens, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the genius of Volusius Verus's century, under the consulship of Cilo and Libo.
EDCS-11000728.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by a soldier of the 22nd Legion to the genius of a century, likely dedicated in honor of the imperial family, dated by consuls.

EDCS-11000730.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio cohortis I Septimiae Belgarum [Alexandrianae] pecunia sua posuerunt Claudius Valerius Gentilius Augustus Similius Paternus Senecionius Priminus Hibernius Agilis Iunianius Rogatus SINs Restitutius Patruinus Gentius Verinus Sr Maternus Publius Aelius Moderatus Aquinius Mnus Aelius Lupionius Decemius Florinus V \n
EDCS-11000730.translation: In honor of the divine house, Claudius Valerius Gentilius, Augustus Similius Paternus, Senecionius Priminus, Hibernius Agilis, Iunianius Rogatus, Sins Restitutius, Patruinus Gentius, Verinus, Sr Maternus, Publius Aelius Moderatus, Aquinius Mnus, Aelius Lupionius, Decemius Florinus, and V [---] erected this at their own expense to the genius of the 1st Septimia Belgarum cohort [Alexandrianae].
EDCS-11000730.summary: This inscription records a dedication by multiple individuals to the genius of the 1st Septimia Belgarum cohort, likely in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11000731.text_edition: \n In <h=M>(onorem) domus divinae Genio collegii iuventutis vici Apollinensis Acutius Ursus et Acutia Ursa donum dederunt Imperatore [] []IMP[] [] et Comazonte consulibus \n
EDCS-11000731.translation: In honor of the divine house, Acutius Ursus and Acutia Ursa gave this gift to the genius of the association of youth of the district of Apollo, under the consulship of Emperor [---] [IMP] [---] and Comazo.
EDCS-11000731.summary: This inscription records a gift by Acutius Ursus and Acutia Ursa to the genius of a youth association, dedicated in honor of the imperial family and dated by consuls.

EDCS-11000732.text_edition: \n et Genio Iuventutis Vobergensis Titus Genialinius Crescens votum solvit libens laetus merito Anullino II et Frontone consulibus\n
EDCS-11000732.translation: And to the genius of the Voberg youth, Titus Genialinius Crescens gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow, under the consulship of Anullinus II and Fronto.
EDCS-11000732.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Titus Genialinius Crescens to the genius of the Voberg youth, dated by consuls.

EDCS-11000733.text_edition: \n Genium legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Honori aquilae legionis supra scriptae Aurelius \n
EDCS-11000733.translation: To the genius of the 22nd Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful, [---] Aurelius [---] for the honor of the legion's eagle mentioned above.
EDCS-11000733.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Aurelius to the genius and the eagle of the 22nd Primigenia legion.

EDCS-11000736.text_edition: \n Herculi sacrum Valeria Sperata Lucio Magalio Victore Caio Valerio Senecione Lucio Valerio Secundo Publio Valerio Pacato filiis votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11000736.translation: Sacred to Hercules, Valeria Sperata fulfilled her vow gladly and deservedly for her sons Lucius Magalio Victor, Gaius Valerius Senecio, Lucius Valerius Secundus, and Publius Valerius Pacatus.
EDCS-11000736.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Hercules by Valeria Sperata on behalf of her sons.

EDCS-11000737.text_edition: \n Deo Herculi Victoria Martia votum solvit libens laeta merito pro se et Ingena\n
EDCS-11000737.translation: To the god Hercules, Victoria Martia gladly and deservedly fulfilled her vow for herself and Ingena.
EDCS-11000737.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Hercules by Victoria Martia for herself and Ingena.

EDCS-11000740.text_edition: \n Iunoni Reginae et Genio loci Lucius Crescentinius Gratinus beneficiarius legati votum solvit libens laetus merito dedicatum X Kalendas Augustas Imperatore domino nostro Antonino consule\n
EDCS-11000740.translation: To Juno Regina and the genius of the place, Lucius Crescentinius Gratinus, a beneficiary of the legate, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow, dedicated on the 10th day before the Kalends of August, in the consulship of our lord Emperor Antoninus.
EDCS-11000740.summary: This inscription records a votive offering by Lucius Crescentinius Gratinus, a military official, to Juno Regina and the genius loci, dated by a consul.

EDCS-11000744.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunius Valens medicus legionis IIII Macedonicae\n
EDCS-11000744.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Iunius Valens, physician of the 4th Macedonian legion.
EDCS-11000744.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Iunius Valens, a physician in the 4th Macedonian legion.

EDCS-11000745.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo pro salute Imperatoris Luci Aeli Aureli Commodi Augusti Pii Felicis patri patriae et I \n
EDCS-11000745.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, for the safety of the Emperor Lucius Aelius Aurelius Commodus Augustus Pius Felix, father of the fatherland, and I...
EDCS-11000745.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter for the safety of Emperor Commodus, likely from the late 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000746.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Marcus P P votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000746.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Marcus, pater patriae, fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000746.summary: This is a votive inscription by Marcus, likely a high-ranking official, to Jupiter, dated possibly to the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000747.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Zosimus Papiri centurionis lib(ertus) pro patrono sua pecunia\n
EDCS-11000747.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Zosimus, freedman of Papirius the centurion, [dedicated this] for his patron with his own money.
EDCS-11000747.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by a freedman for his patron, a centurion, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000749.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Conservatori arcum et porticus quos Dativius Victor decurio civitatis Taunensium sacerdotalis Mogontiacensibus promisit Victorii Ursus frumentarius et Lupus filii et heredes consummaverunt\n
EDCS-11000749.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, the Preserver: the arch and porticoes, which Dativius Victor, decurion of the civitas Taunensium and priest, had promised to the people of Mogontiacum, were completed by Victorii Ursus the grain supplier and Lupus, his sons and heirs.
EDCS-11000749.summary: This inscription records the completion of an arch and porticoes dedicated to Jupiter, honoring the imperial family and completed by sons and heirs, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000750.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Conservatori Caius Memmius Martialis |(centurio) legionis XI votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000750.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, the Preserver, Caius Memmius Martialis, centurion of the XI legion, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000750.summary: This is a votive inscription by a centurion of the XI legion to Jupiter the Preserver, likely from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000751.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Sintillius Ursulus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000751.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus, Sintillius Ursulus fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000751.summary: This is a votive inscription by Sintillius Ursulus to Jupiter Dolichenus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000752.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Sabasio Conservatori Honori aquilae legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Alexandrianae Marcus Aurelius Germanus domo Emona \n
EDCS-11000752.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest Sabasius, the Preserver, and to the honor of the eagle of the XXII Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis Alexandriana, Marcus Aurelius Germanus, from Emona, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11000752.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Jupiter Sabasius the Preserver and the eagle standard of the XXII Legion by a soldier from Emona, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000753.text_edition: \n Numinibus Augustorum Iovi Optimo Maximo Fortunae Vestae D Laribus Penatibus Lucius Sallustius Sedatus hospes votum solvit libens merito Vestae Laribus Penatibus Lucius Sallustius Sedatus hospes votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11000753.translation: To the divine powers of the Augusti, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Fortune, to Vesta, to the household gods and penates, Lucius Sallustius Sedatus, a guest, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly. [Dedicated to] Vesta, household gods and penates, Lucius Sallustius Sedatus, a guest, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000753.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the imperial deities, Jupiter, Fortune, Vesta, and household gods by a guest, Lucius Sallustius Sedatus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000754.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio |(centuriae) Valeri Alexandri Titus Devillius Titi immunis filius Aurelia Victorinus custos armorum legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis de <suo> posuit Imperatore Antonino II et Geta Caesare consulibus\n
EDCS-11000754.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the century of Valerius Alexander, Titus Devillius, son of Titus, an immunis and keeper of the arms of the XXII Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis, placed this from his own funds, when Emperor Antoninus II and Caesar Geta were consuls.
EDCS-11000754.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and the Genius of a century by a soldier of the XXII Legion, dating to the consulship of Antoninus II and Geta (likely 205 CE).

EDCS-11000755.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio bene merenti |(centuriae) Nammi Rufi Aeli(us) Atessas miles posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito Mamertino et Rufo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000755.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the deserving Genius of the century of Nammius Rufus, Aelius Atessas, a soldier, placed this and fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly, when Mamertinus and Rufus were consuls.
EDCS-11000755.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and the Genius of a century by a soldier, Aelius Atessas, dating to the consulship of Mamertinus and Rufus (likely 210 CE).

EDCS-11000756.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci Lucius Septimius Bellus signifer legionis XXII Primigeniae optio navaliorum votum solvit laetus libens merito Saturnino et Gallo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000756.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the place, Lucius Septimius Bellus, standard-bearer of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, an optio navaliorum, happily, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow, Saturninus and Gallus being consuls.
EDCS-11000756.summary: This inscription records a soldier's fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter and the Genius of the place, dated by the consulship of Saturninus and Gallus.

EDCS-11000758.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Titus Albanius Primanus signifer legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis optio navaliorum pro se et suis votum solvit laetus libens merito Materno et Bradua consulibus\n
EDCS-11000758.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Titus Albanius Primanus, standard-bearer of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, an optio navaliorum, for himself and his family, happily, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow, Maternos and Bradua being consuls.
EDCS-11000758.summary: This inscription records a soldier's fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter and Juno Regina, including his family, dated by the consulship of Maternos and Bradua.

EDCS-11000759.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae -- Marcus As A in suo\n
EDCS-11000759.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina -- Marcus -- in his own property.
EDCS-11000759.summary: This fragmentary inscription records an offering to Jupiter and Juno Regina by Marcus.

EDCS-11000760.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Aulus Mucatralis beneficiarius legati legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Alexandri[anae] votum solvit libens laetus merito X Kalendas Decembres Albino et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-11000760.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Aulus Mucatralis, a beneficiarius of the legate of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, Alexandriana, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, on the 10th day before the Kalends of December, Albinus and Maximus being consuls.
EDCS-11000760.summary: This inscription records a soldier's vow fulfillment to Jupiter and Juno Regina, dated by the consulship of Albinus and Maximus.

EDCS-11000761.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Aurelius Hermes NEG C- tia ana Apollinari filii votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11000761.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Aurelius Hermes and his sons, Negotia and Apollinaris, willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11000761.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter and Juno Regina by Aurelius Hermes and his sons.

EDCS-11000762.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Claudius Quartinus <c=S>ives Aeduus ex voto in suo posuit Praesente et Extricato consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11000762.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Claudius Quartinus, an Aeduan citizen, set this up according to his vow on his own property, Praesens and Extricatus being consuls; he fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000762.summary: This inscription records a citizen's erection of a monument to Jupiter and Juno Regina, dated by the consulship of Praesens and Extricatus.

EDCS-11000763.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Marcus G F in suo sua pecunia posuit\n
EDCS-11000763.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Marcus, son of G., set this up with his own money on his own property.
EDCS-11000763.summary: This inscription records Marcus, son of G., setting up a monument at his own expense to Jupiter and Juno Regina.

EDCS-11000764.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Quintus Pompeius Valens |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae pro se et suis libens merito\n
EDCS-11000764.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Quintus Pompeius Valens, a centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, for himself and his family, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11000764.summary: This inscription records a centurion of the 22nd Legion Primigenia making an offering to Jupiter and Juno Regina for himself and his family.

EDCS-11000765.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Caius Sallustius Taurus <s=E>peculator legionis V<I=L>II Augustae basim et columnam cum statua fecit \n
EDCS-11000765.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Caius Sallustius Taurus, a special agent (speculator) of the 22nd Legion Augustae, made the base, column, and statue.
EDCS-11000765.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the 22nd Legion Augustae commissioning a statue and its base and column dedicated to Jupiter and Juno Regina.

EDCS-11000768.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Gaius Vitalinius Florentinus et Luciliania Honorata coniux fecerunt\n
EDCS-11000768.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, Gaius Vitalinius Florentinus and his wife Luciliania Honorata made this.
EDCS-11000768.summary: This inscription records Gaius Vitalinius Florentinus and his wife Luciliania Honorata dedicating a monument to Jupiter and Juno Regina.

EDCS-11000774.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo M(aximo) et Matribus Perpertua posuit votum solvit libens laeta dedit\n
EDCS-11000774.translation: Perpetua placed this offering to Jupiter Best and Greatest and the Mothers, gladly and joyfully fulfilling her vow.
EDCS-11000774.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter and the Mothers, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-11000775.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Sucaelo et Genio loci pro salute Cai Calpurni Seppiani primi pili legionis XXII Primigeniae piae Trophimus actor et canabarii ex voto\n
EDCS-11000775.translation: Trophimus, an actor, and the stallkeepers, for the health of Caius Calpurnius Seppianus, a chief centurion of the XXII Primigenia Pious and Loyal legion, set this up in fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Sucaelus, and to the Genius of the place.
EDCS-11000775.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter, Sucaelus, and the Genius Loci by soldiers and stallkeepers for the well-being of a high-ranking centurion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000776.text_edition: \n Laribus Competalibus sive Quadriviis Titus Flavius Castus beneficiarius consularis cum vilico posuit\n
EDCS-11000776.translation: Titus Flavius Castus, a beneficiary of the consular governor, set this up with the overseer for the Lares of the crossroads.
EDCS-11000776.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a shrine to the Lares Compitales (gods of crossroads) by a military official and an overseer, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000777.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Laribus stratorum consularis legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis veterani missi honesta missione Menenius Adiutor Caius Appuleius Saturninus BIIIVS ND \n
EDCS-11000777.translation: In honor of the divine house, the veterans Menenius Adiutor and Caius Appuleius Saturninus, honorably discharged from the XXII Primigenia Pious and Loyal legion, set this up for the household gods of the consular general.
EDCS-11000777.summary: This inscription honors the imperial family and records the dedication of a shrine by veterans of the XXII Primigenia legion, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000778.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Lunae Marcellinius Placidinus decurio civium Romanorum Mogontiaci et Martinia Martina mater eius ex voto posuerunt libentes laeti Tacito et Aemiliano consulibus Kalendis Iuniis\n
EDCS-11000778.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcellinius Placidinus, a decurion of Roman citizens in Mogontiacum, and his mother Martinia Martina, set this up for the goddess Luna in fulfillment of a vow, gladly and joyfully, on the Kalends of June during the consulship of Tacitus and Aemilianus.
EDCS-11000778.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the goddess Luna by a Roman decurion and his mother, dedicated in Mogontiacum (modern Mainz) in 273 CE.

EDCS-11000780.text_edition: \n Deo Marti Emeritius Ursinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000780.translation: Emeritius Ursinus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow to the god Mars.
EDCS-11000780.summary: This is a personal votive inscription to the god Mars, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000781.translation: In honor of the divine house / To the god Mars / Flavia Aenia
EDCS-11000781.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Mars and the imperial family by Flavia Aenia, probably from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000782.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti Surius Felix votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000782.translation: In honor of the divine house, Surius Felix gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow to the god Mars.
EDCS-11000782.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars and the imperial family by Surius Felix, likely from the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000783.text_edition: \n Deo Marti aram Iulius Emeritus miles legionis VIII Augustae Severianae Alexandrian[ae] exactus consularis dedicatam XIII Kalendas Maias Maximo et Aeliano consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000783.translation: Iulius Emeritus, a soldier of the VIII Augusta Severiana Alexandriana legion, a former consular exactor, dedicated this altar to the god Mars, dedicated on the 13th day before the Kalends of May during the consulship of Maximinus and Aelianus, and gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000783.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to Mars by a soldier and former tax collector of the VIII Augusta legion, dated to 219 CE.

EDCS-11000784.text_edition: \n RE VLII Sollius Gallicanus miles legionis I adiutricis centuria Valeri Frontonis optio custodiarum dedit dedicavit\n
EDCS-11000784.translation: The soldier Sollius Gallicanus of the I Adiutrix legion, opti of the guard detailed to the century of Valerius Fronto, gave and dedicated this.
EDCS-11000784.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument by a soldier and an optio (officer) from the I Adiutrix legion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000785.text_edition: \n Deo Marti Noadato Flavius Mucatralis veteranus legionis XXII ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11000785.translation: To the god Mars Noadatus, Flavius Mucatralis, a veteran of the 22nd legion, dedicated this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000785.summary: This inscription records a veteran of the 22nd legion dedicating an offering to the god Mars Noadatus.

EDCS-11000787.text_edition: \n Marti Victoriae Fortunae Tertinius Senecio miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis beneficiarius consularis Imperatore Severo II et Albino Caesare II consulibus\n
EDCS-11000787.translation: To Mars, Victory, and Fortune, Tertinius Senecio, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis legion, a beneficiarius consularis, dedicated this during the consulship of Emperor Severus II and Albinus Caesar II.
EDCS-11000787.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the 22nd legion dedicating an offering to Mars, Victory, and Fortune during the consulship of Severus II and Albinus II.

EDCS-11000788.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Tiberius Iustinius Aelia Augusta Titianus beneficiarius legati legionis XXII et Servandia Augusta eius votum solverunt Faustino et Rufino consulibus\n
EDCS-11000788.translation: To the god Mercury, Tiberius Iustinius, Aelia Augusta Titianus, a beneficiarius of the legate of the 22nd legion, and his wife Servandia Augusta, fulfilled their vow during the consulship of Faustinus and Rufinus.
EDCS-11000788.summary: This inscription records a beneficiarius of the legate of the 22nd legion and his wife dedicating an offering to Mercury.

EDCS-11000789.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcellinius Marcianus, a cornicen of the 4th Cohort of Aquitanians, set up the temple with a statue and an altar, fulfilling his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, during the consulship of Faustinus and Rufinus.
EDCS-11000789.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the 4th Cohort of Aquitanians dedicating a temple, statue, and altar to the god Mercury.

EDCS-11000792.text_edition: \n Minervae Flavius Sextinus strator legati votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000792.translation: To Minerva, Flavius Sextinus, strator to the legate, fulfilled his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000792.summary: This inscription records Flavius Sextinus, a strator to a legate, dedicating an offering to Minerva.

EDCS-11000793.translation: To the goddess Pallas, Gaius Aurelius Festinus, a centurion of the stratores of the legate Cl. Egnatianus, built a suspended archive room from the ground up, with the assistance of Cossius Martinus, during the consulship of Praesens and Extricatus.
EDCS-11000793.summary: This inscription records a centurion of the stratores dedicating a suspended archive room to the goddess Pallas.

EDCS-11000795.translation: To the Water Mensor Numina, [name illegible] fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000795.summary: This inscription records an offering to the god Numina associated with water.

EDCS-11000797.translation: Quintus Atilius fulfilled his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-11000797.summary: This inscription records Quintus Atilius dedicating an offering to the Nymphs.

EDCS-11000799.text_edition: \n Pietati legionis XXII Primigeniae [Alexandrianae] piae fidelis et Honori aquilae Lucius Domitius Iulianus iunior Domiti Iuliani quondam prrimi pili filius donum dedit ob merita dedicante Maximio Attiano clarissimo viro legato Augusti pro praetore Germaniae superioris V Kalendas Apriles domino nostro Alexandro Augusto III et Dione consulibus\n
EDCS-11000799.translation: Lucius Domitius Iulianus the younger, son of the late Lucius Domitius Iulianus, primipilus, dedicated a gift to the Pietas of the 22nd Primigenia Alexandriana Pia Fidelis legion and to the Honor of the aquila, because of his merits, during the dedication by Maximus Attianus, a most distinguished man, legate of the emperor with praetorian power in Upper Germany, four days before the Kalends of April, to our lord Alexander Augustus (in his third consulship) and Dion.
EDCS-11000799.summary: This inscription records Lucius Domitius Iulianus dedicating a gift to the Pietas of the 22nd legion and the Honor of the aquila, under the governorship of Maximus Attianus and during the consulship of Alexander Augustus III and Dion.

EDCS-11000803.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Catianusnustum ex iussu? s(olvit) libens laetus m(erito)\n
EDCS-11000803.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, Catianusnustum fulfilled his vow, possibly by order, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000803.summary: This inscription records Catianusnustum dedicating an offering to the god Mithras.

EDCS-11000804.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae <q=O>ui vovit <s>o<lv=IN>it libens laetus m(erito) \n
EDCS-11000804.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, who vowed, gladly and with reason fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000804.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Mithras, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000808.text_edition: \n Virodacti sive Lucenae Augustius Iustus ex voto numinibus sanctissimis \n
EDCS-11000808.translation: Virodactus or Lucenus, Iustus, fulfilling his vow to the most holy divine powers.
EDCS-11000808.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to divine powers, possibly of local significance, by Iustus.

EDCS-11000812.text_edition: \n Aram Tiberius Adnamius Sequens pro salute sua et Seniliae cetae coniugis filiorum et Titus Saturninius Aurelius pro salute sua et Iuniae Lucillae coniugis et Titi Aureli Apollinaris filii haruspicibus collegiis dederunt dedicaverunt\n
EDCS-11000812.translation: Tiberius Adnamius Sequens, for the health of himself and his wife Senilia Ceta, and their sons, and Titus Saturninius Aurelius, for the health of himself and his wife Iunia Lucilla, and his son Titus Aurelius Apollinaris, gave and dedicated this altar to the haruspices and colleges.
EDCS-11000812.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar by Tiberius Adnamius Sequens and Titus Saturninius Aurelius for the health of their families, possibly around the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000813.text_edition: \n onius Adoratus amma coniunx in suo posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000813.translation: [...]onius Adoratus and [his wife?] amma placed [this] in their own [property].
EDCS-11000813.summary: This inscription records a private dedication by Adonius Adoratus and his wife Amma, likely a funerary or religious marker.

EDCS-11000814.text_edition: \n Genio IIE ICIST ammius Saturninus votum solvit libens laetus merito IMPVM\n
EDCS-11000814.translation: To the Genius of this place, Ammius Saturninus gladly and with reason fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000814.summary: This inscription records a fulfilled vow to the Genius Loci by Ammius Saturninus, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000815.text_edition: \n Titus Florius Saturninus veteranus ex signifero legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Alexandrianae missus honesta missione allectus in ordinem civium Romanorum Alexandrianorum Mogontiaci ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11000815.translation: Titus Florius Saturninus, a veteran, former standard-bearer of the XXII Legion Primigenia, loyal and faithful, Alexandrian, discharged with honorable dismissal, appointed to the order of Roman citizens of Alexandria, at Mogontiacum, placed this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11000815.summary: This inscription records a veteran, Titus Florius Saturninus, fulfilling a vow by dedicating a monument in Mogontiacum (modern Mainz, Germany), probably in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000816.text_edition: \n Deo Mithrae Quietius Amandus D votum quod voverat solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000816.translation: To the god Mithras, Quietius Amandus D., gladly and with reason fulfilled the vow which he had made.
EDCS-11000816.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Mithras by Quietius Amandus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000817.text_edition: \n Mammilianius Victorinus ex voto suscepto votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11000817.translation: Mammilianius Victorinus fulfilled his vow, gladly and with reason, according to his undertaken vow.
EDCS-11000817.summary: This inscription records a fulfilled vow by Mammilianius Victorinus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000818.text_edition: \n Messoria Placida pro salute Augustaliniorum Inpetrati et Augustinae filiorum suorum votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11000818.translation: Messoria Placida, for the health of Augustal Iuventius and her sons Augustina, gladly and with reason fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-11000818.summary: This inscription records a fulfilled vow by Messoria Placida for the health of her family, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11000819.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming a woman, [3]celima, and her father, Solimutus, possibly funerary.

EDCS-11000821.text_edition: \n AIRIV MARORVM Valerius Faustus LAMBRE Modestus estor Valerius Albanus actor posuerunt de suo\n
EDCS-11000821.translation: Valerius Faustus, the actor Lambre Modestus, and Valerius Albanus, the actor, set this up at their own expense.
EDCS-11000821.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument by two actors, Valerius Faustus and Valerius Albanus, at their own expense.

EDCS-11000822.text_edition: \n Marcus Valerius Pudens Lucius Antonius Placidus Marcus Biracius Indutius Caius Silvius Senecio platiodanni vici novi sub cura sua de suo\n
EDCS-11000822.translation: Marcus Valerius Pudens, Lucius Antonius Placidus, Marcus Biracius Indutius, and Caius Silvius Senecio, platodanni of the new village, set this up at their own expense under their own supervision.
EDCS-11000822.summary: This inscription records a public work or monument funded by four individuals identified as platodanni of a new village, set up under their supervision.

EDCS-11000823.text_edition: \n S Victorinus beneficiarius legati votum solvit libens laetus merito Laeto iterum et Ceriale consulibus\n
EDCS-11000823.translation: S. Victorinus, a subordinate of the legate, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow, with Laetus and Cerialis as consuls.
EDCS-11000823.summary: This is a votive inscription by S. Victorinus, a subordinate of a legate, who fulfilled his vow during the consulship of Laetus and Cerialis.

EDCS-11000824.text_edition: \n voto suscepto Lucius Vireius Dexter seplasiarius in legione I adiutrice votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-11000824.translation: Lucius Vireius Dexter, a seller of the 'seplasium' drug in the First Adjutant Legion, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11000824.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Vireius Dexter, a soldier in the Legio I Adjutrix, who fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-11000829.text_edition: \n Lugenus veteteranus? legionis VIII Augustae Lugena eius\n
EDCS-11000829.translation: Lugenus, a veteran of the Eighth Augustan Legion, and his wife Lugena.
EDCS-11000829.summary: This inscription records Lugenus, a veteran of the Eighth Augustan Legion, and his wife Lugena.

EDCS-11000833.translation: The freedman Iulius Maior fulfilled his vow gladly, joyfully, and deservedly, dedicated [date missing] under consuls [names missing].
EDCS-11000833.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulius Maior, likely a freedman, with missing details about the dedication date and consuls.

EDCS-11000838.translation: Secundinus(?) [name or title missing], son of [name missing], fulfilled his vow gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11000838.summary: This is a fragmentary votive inscription by Secundinus(?), who fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-11000843.translation: To Felicitas, daughter of Tiberius; Victoria, daughter of Augustus Aurelius.
EDCS-11000843.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or commemoration to two female individuals, Felicitas and Victoria.

EDCS-11000844.text_edition: \n Tiberio Claudio Caesari Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate III imperatori IIII patri patriae consuli III cives Romani manticularii negotiatores Caio Vibio Rufino legato pro praetore\n
EDCS-11000844.translation: The Roman citizens, the bag makers and merchants, to Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 3rd time, hailed as Imperator for the 4th time, father of the country, consul for the 3rd time, with Gaius Vibius Rufus as legate pro praetore.
EDCS-11000844.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Roman bag makers and merchants to Emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, honoring him during his consulship and tribunician power, with Gaius Vibius Rufus as legate.

EDCS-11000848.text_edition: \n In honorem Luci Septimi Severi Pii Pertinacis Augusti invicti Imperatoris et Marci Aureli Antonini Caesaris legioni XXII Primigeniae piae fideli honoris virtutisque causa civitas Treverorum in obsidione ab ea defensa\n
EDCS-11000848.translation: In honor of Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax Augustus, the unconquered Emperor, and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Caesar, the city of the Treveri, for defending it in siege, dedicates this to the Twenty-second Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, for honor and valor.
EDCS-11000848.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the civitas Treverorum to the Legio XXII Primigenia in honor of its defense of the city during a siege, also honoring Emperors Septimius Severus and Caracalla.

EDCS-11000855.text_edition: \n ------ legatus] Augusti pro praetore provinciarum Thraciae Moesiae superioris Raetiae Germaniae superioris et Brittanniae et Modestiana eius et Caerellii Marcianus et Germanilla filii\n
EDCS-11000855.translation: legatus Augusti pro praetore of the provinces of Thracia, Moesia Superior, Raetia, Germania Superior, and Britannia, and Modestiana his wife, and their children Caerellii Marcianus and Germanilla.
EDCS-11000855.summary: This inscription likely commemorates a legate of the emperor serving in multiple provinces, along with his family.

EDCS-11000856.text_edition: \n Claudio Aelio Pollioni legato Augusti pro praetore Germaniae superioris praesidi integerrimo bbenefficiarii consularis Germaniae superioris\n
EDCS-11000856.translation: To Claudius Aelius Pollio, imperial legate pro praetore of Germania Superior, most upright governor, from the beneficiarii consularis of Germania Superior.
EDCS-11000856.summary: This is a dedication by the beneficiarii consularis to their governor, Claudius Aelius Pollio, of Germania Superior.

EDCS-11000857.inscription_type: carmina, tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-11000857.text_edition: \n Aram dis Manibus et innocentiae Hipponici servi Dignillae Iuni Pastoris legati legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Hedyepes et Genesia parentes ut primum adolevit pollens viribus decora facie Cupidinis os habitumque gerens nec metuam dicere Apollineus huic expletis ter centum ter denisque diebus invisae Parcae sollemnem celebrare diem iamque ut esset gratus amicis invidia superum cessavit amari\n
EDCS-11000857.translation: To the Shades of the Underworld and to the innocence of Hipponicus, slave of Dignilla, wife of Iunius Pastor, legate of the XXII Primigenia Pious Faithful Legion. Hedyepes and Genesia, his parents, lament that as soon as he grew up, a strong man with a handsome face, bearing the appearance and countenance of Cupid, and not fearing to call him Apollonian, the hateful Fates, after completing three hundred and thirty days, celebrated their solemn day, and already, so that he would be pleasing to his friends, envy of the gods ceased to be loved.
EDCS-11000857.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to the deceased Hipponicus by his parents, lamenting his premature death and praising his youthful beauty and character.

EDCS-11000858.text_edition: \n Lucius Otacilius Fabricius Xvir stlitibus iudicandis tribunus militum legionis X--- quaestor --- tribunus plebis praetor legatus Caesaris\n
EDCS-11000858.translation: Lucius Otacilius Fabricius, decemvir for judging lawsuits, military tribune of the X Legion [---], quaestor [---], tribune of the plebs, praetor, legate of Caesar.
EDCS-11000858.summary: This is a career summary of Lucius Otacilius Fabricius, detailing his progression through various Roman magistracies and military positions.

EDCS-11000860.text_edition: \n Ulpiae Lucillae incomparabilis pietatis matri Adiutorius Lucilianus filius eques Romanus\n
EDCS-11000860.translation: To Ulpia Lucilla, mother of incomparable piety, from her son Adiutorius Lucilianus, an equestrian.
EDCS-11000860.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a son to his devoted mother, Ulpia Lucilla.

EDCS-11000861.translation: To the Shades of the Underworld. For Gaius Antestius Severus, son of Gaius, of the Veturia tribe, prefect of smiths, prefect of the II Cohort of Bituriges, prefect of the I Cohort of Cyrenaica, military tribune of the IV Macedonian Legion. He lived for 46 years. Antestii Fortunatus and Cecilius had this made.
EDCS-11000861.summary: This tombstone records the career of Gaius Antestius Severus, who held several prefectural and tribuneship posts, and was made by his relatives.

EDCS-11000862.translation: To the Shades of the Underworld. For Genialine Grata, his most devoted wife, who lived 35 years and 4 months. Lucius Baebius, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia Pious Faithful Legion, had this made.
EDCS-11000862.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Genialine Grata, the devoted wife of Lucius Baebius, a soldier.

EDCS-11000863.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titi Flavi Salviani ex praefecto exploratorum Divitiensium militiae quartae equiti Romano Baebius Isidorus |(centurio) legionis amico faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000863.translation: To the Shades of the Underworld. For Titus Flavius Salvianus, former prefect of scouts of the Divitiensian Fourth Cohort, a Roman equestrian. Baebius Isidorus, a centurion of the legion, had this made for his friend.
EDCS-11000863.summary: This funerary inscription is for Titus Flavius Salvianus, a former prefect of scouts and an equestrian, commissioned by his friend and fellow soldier.

EDCS-11000864.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Marcus Vinius Pudens Salinianus, who held the rank of prefect.

EDCS-11000865.text_edition: \n Cnaeus Petronius Cnaei filius Pomptina Asellio tribunus militum praefectus equitum praefectus fabrum Tiberii Caesaris\n
EDCS-11000865.translation: Gnaeus Petronius Asellio, son of Gnaeus, of the Pomptina tribe, military tribune, cavalry prefect, prefect of the smiths of Tiberius Caesar.
EDCS-11000865.summary: This inscription lists the military and administrative career of Gnaeus Petronius Asellio, serving under Tiberius Caesar.

EDCS-11000866.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Statilius Taurus, prefect of the engineers (!), prefect of the I Augusta Praetoria Cohort of Ituraeans and the VI Thracian Cohort, military tribune of the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, lived 36 years. Statilius Fortunatus, his freedman, saw to its construction.
EDCS-11000866.summary: A funerary inscription for Titus Statilius Taurus, a military officer, detailing his career and mentioning his freedman who erected the monument.

EDCS-11000867.translation: [...] of Caius Vin[3]nius, the principal [...], at the expense of [...], prefect of the camp (?).
EDCS-11000867.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly recording the career of a military officer named Caius Vin[3]nius, serving as a camp prefect.

EDCS-11000868.text_edition: \n legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis L fili-- Hippi Cadyanda A Cybira sic \n
EDCS-11000868.translation: of the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, son L, Hippi [from] Cadyanda, from Cybira, thus.
EDCS-11000868.summary: A very fragmentary inscription possibly related to a soldier from the XXII Legion Primigenia, with possible geographical references.

EDCS-11000869.text_edition: \n pro salute Neronis Claudi Caesaris Augusti Germanici Imperatoris Lucio Antistio Vetere legato Augusti pro praetore Quinto Volusio Saturnino Publio Cornelio Scipione consulibus ala Gallorum Petriana per Caium Iulium Augurinum praefectum\n
EDCS-11000869.translation: For the health of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus Imperator, during the consulship of Lucius Antistius Vetus, imperial legate with praetorian power, and Quintus Volusius Saturninus and Publius Cornelius Scipio, the ala Gallorum Petriana, under Caius Julius Augurinus, prefect.
EDCS-11000869.summary: An inscription recording a dedication made by the ala Gallorum Petriana, under its prefect Caius Julius Augurinus, for the health of Emperor Nero.

EDCS-11000872.translation: To the departed spirits and good memory. Why do you stand and [---]. He served 24 years, approved here in the VII Claudia Legion, chosen in the praetorium, made a cavalryman, promoted (centurion) from the staff of prefects. Born in the province of Upper Moesia, in the region of Scupi [ni]a(?), Dardania. [---] gave birth to me, (my) colonist from Germany. Caius O[3] Sergia Valens, first heir and cousin, [---]
EDCS-11000872.summary: A funerary inscription for a soldier named Caius Valens, who served 24 years in the VII Claudia Legion and was promoted through the ranks, with details about his origins and family.

EDCS-11000874.text_edition: \n Marcus Aemilius Marci filius Claudia Fuscus Savaria miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XXV stipendiorum VIII hic situs est frater pro pietate posuit\n
EDCS-11000874.translation: Marcus Aemilius Fuscus, son of Marcus, of the Claudia tribe, from Savaria, a soldier of the I Adiutrix Legion, aged 25, with 8 years of service, is buried here. His brother placed this out of duty.
EDCS-11000874.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Aemilius Fuscus, a soldier in the I Adiutrix Legion, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11000875.text_edition: \n Caius Antonius Cai filius Claudia Rufus Apro miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XX stipendiorum XVII hic situs est heres ex testamento faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000875.translation: Caius Antonius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Claudia tribe, from Apro, a soldier of the I Adiutrix Legion, aged 20, with 17 years of service, is buried here. The heir had this constructed by will.
EDCS-11000875.summary: A funerary inscription for Caius Antonius Rufus, a soldier in the I Adiutrix Legion, whose heir commissioned the monument according to his will.

EDCS-11000876.text_edition: \n Lucius Appuleius Luci filius Sergia Iadestinus Iader miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XXV stipendiorum VI hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000876.translation: Lucius Appuleius Iadestinus, son of Lucius, of the Sergia tribe, from Iader, a soldier of the I Adiutrix Legion, aged 25, with 6 years of service, is buried here. The heir had this constructed.
EDCS-11000876.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Appuleius Iadestinus, a soldier in the I Adiutrix Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000877.text_edition: \n Quintus Attius Quinti filius Tromentina Rufus Aequo miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XXX stipendiorum IX hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000877.translation: Quintus Attius Rufus, son of Quintus, of the Tromentina tribe, from Aequo, a soldier of the I Adiutrix Legion, aged 30, with 9 years of service, is buried here. The heir had this constructed.
EDCS-11000877.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Attius Rufus, a soldier in the I Adiutrix Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000878.text_edition: \n Caius Cassius Cai filius Claudia Longinus Savaria miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XXX stipendiorum X hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000878.translation: Caius Cassius Longinus, son of Caius, of the Claudia tribe, from Savaria, a soldier of the I Adiutrix Legion, aged 30, with 10 years of service, is buried here. The heir had this constructed.
EDCS-11000878.summary: A funerary inscription for Caius Cassius Longinus, a soldier in the I Adiutrix Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000879.translation: Didius Clemens (of the tribe Tromentina), a soldier of the legion I Adiutrix, aged 30 years with 30 years of service, is buried here; he ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-11000879.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Didius Clemens, a soldier of the legion I Adiutrix, who died after 30 years of service.

EDCS-11000880.translation: Marcus Marius Vegetus, son of Marcus, of the tribe Tromentina, a soldier of the legion I Adiutricis, aged 35 years with 15 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-11000880.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Marius Vegetus, a soldier of the legion I Adiutricis, who died after 15 years of service, dating to the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11000881.text_edition: \n Titus Valerius Claudia Montanus Savaria miles legionis I adiutricis nnorum XXXIIII stipendiorum XI hic conditus est\n
EDCS-11000881.translation: Titus Valerius Montanus, of the Claudia tribe, from Savaria, a soldier of the legion I adiutricis, aged 34 years with 11 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000881.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Titus Valerius Montanus, a soldier of the legion I Adiutricis, who died after 11 years of service.

EDCS-11000882.translation: Gaius Vibius Severus, son of Caius, of the tribe Tromentina, a soldier of the legion I Adiutricis, aged 35 years with 16 years of service, [is buried here].
EDCS-11000882.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Vibius Severus, a soldier of the legion I Adiutricis, who died after 16 years of service.

EDCS-11000884.text_edition: \n Publilia Firmus Verona miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XXIstipendiorum II \n
EDCS-11000884.translation: Publilia Firmus, from Verona, a soldier of the legion I adiutricis, aged 21 years with 2 years of service.
EDCS-11000884.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publilia Firmus, a soldier of the legion I Adiutricis, who died after 2 years of service.

EDCS-11000886.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Cai Porci Valentis\n
EDCS-11000886.translation: The legion I adiutrix, the century of Caius Porcius Valens.
EDCS-11000886.summary: This inscription records the century of Caius Porcius Valens within the legion I adiutrix, likely indicating a building or dedication by that unit.

EDCS-11000887.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Claudi Bucculi\n
EDCS-11000887.translation: The legion I adiutrix, the century of Claudius Bucculus.
EDCS-11000887.summary: This inscription records the century of Claudius Bucculus within the legion I adiutrix, likely indicating a building or dedication by that unit.

EDCS-11000888.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Luci Domiti Prisci\n
EDCS-11000888.translation: The legion I adiutrix, the century of Lucius Domitius Priscus.
EDCS-11000888.summary: This inscription records the century of Lucius Domitius Priscus within the legion I adiutrix, likely indicating a building or dedication by that unit.

EDCS-11000889.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Luci Flavi Pudentis\n
EDCS-11000889.translation: The legion I adiutrix, the century of Lucius Flavius Pudentis.
EDCS-11000889.summary: This inscription records the century of Lucius Flavius Pudentis within the legion I adiutrix, likely indicating a building or dedication by that unit.

EDCS-11000890.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Decimi Iuni Verecundi\n
EDCS-11000890.translation: The legion I adiutrix, the century of Decimus Iunius Verecundus.
EDCS-11000890.summary: This inscription records the century of Decimus Iunius Verecundus within the legion I adiutrix, likely indicating a building or dedication by that unit.

EDCS-11000891.translation: Legio I Adiutrix, century of Seionius Verecundus.
EDCS-11000891.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a century of the Legio I Adiutrix.

EDCS-11000892.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Marci Sili Ianuari\n
EDCS-11000892.translation: Legio I Adiutrix, century of Marcus Silius Ianvarius.
EDCS-11000892.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a century of the Legio I Adiutrix.

EDCS-11000893.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Luci Valeri Modesti\n
EDCS-11000893.translation: Legio I Adiutrix, century of Lucius Valerius Modestus.
EDCS-11000893.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a century of the Legio I Adiutrix.

EDCS-11000894.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Vari Ten\n
EDCS-11000894.translation: Legio I Adiutrix, century of Varius Ten(tius?).
EDCS-11000894.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a century of the Legio I Adiutrix.

EDCS-11000895.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria Cai Vetti Paulli\n
EDCS-11000895.translation: Legio I Adiutrix, century of Caius Vettius Paulus.
EDCS-11000895.summary: This is a military inscription identifying a century of the Legio I Adiutrix.

EDCS-11000903.text_edition: \n Memoria Flavi Pusinnionis optionis legionis II Pannonicae qui vixit annos XXXX stupendia sic XVIII Iustinus heres sic pro pietate posuit MIINAM\n
EDCS-11000903.translation: In memory of Flavius Pusinnio, optio of Legio II Pannonica, who lived 40 years, with 18 years of service. Iustinus, his heir, set this up with devotion.
EDCS-11000903.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Pusinnio, an optio in Legio II Pannonica, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11000904.translation: Gaius Valerius Pudens Sava[ri]us, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, soldier of Legio I Adiu[tricis], aged 25 years, 6 years of service, lies here. His heir had this made. Sacred to the departed gods.
EDCS-11000904.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Valerius Pudens Sava[ri]us, a soldier of Legio I Adiu[tricis], dated to the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11000905.translation: To the departed gods. Tiberius Ulpius Iulianus, a merchant in iron (?), from the province of Pontus Bithynia, from Tio (?). His freedman Chrysogonus had this made. Lived 35 years.
EDCS-11000905.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tiberius Ulpius Iulianus, a merchant from Pontus Bithynia, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11000907.translation: Lucius Attius Nepos, son of Lucius, of the Galeria tribe, from Nertobriga, soldier of Legio IIII Macedonica, aged 34 years, 18 years of service, lies here. By his will, his fellow townsmen and freedmen had this made.
EDCS-11000907.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Attius Nepos, a soldier of Legio IIII Macedonica, dated to the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11000908.text_edition: \n Quintus Atius Quinti filius Galeria Quietus domo Nertobriga miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XLV stipendiorum XXV hic situs est heres exs sic testamento faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000908.translation: Quintus Atius Quietus, son of Quintus, of the Galeria tribe, from Nertobriga, soldier of Legio IIII Macedonica, aged 45 years, 25 years of service, lies here. His heir had this made according to his will.
EDCS-11000908.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Atius Quietus, a soldier of Legio IIII Macedonica, dated to the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11000909.text_edition: \n Marcus Aurelius Marci filius Camilia Metellus Alba miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXX stipendiorum X hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000909.translation: Marcus Aurelius Metellus Alba, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, aged 30 and with 10 years of service, is buried here. His heir had this made.
EDCS-11000909.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Aurelius Metellus Alba, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000910.translation: Quintus Bruttius Crescens, son of Quintus, of the Sergia tribe, from Tucci, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, aged 44 and with 22 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000910.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Bruttius Crescens, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, indicating his origin and service length.

EDCS-11000911.text_edition: \n Have Caecili Caius Caecilius Cai filius Pupinia Parra domo Baeterris miles legionis IIII Macedonicae centuria Quinti Aemili annorum XIIX stipendiorum II hic situs est Marcus Antonius Flaccus de suo dedit\n
EDCS-11000911.translation: Hail! Caecilius Parra, son of Caius, of the Pupinia tribe, from Baeterris, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion in the centuria of Quintus Aemilius, aged 18 and with 2 years of service, is buried here. Marcus Antonius Flaccus dedicated this at his own expense.
EDCS-11000911.summary: A tombstone for Caecilius Parra, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, with a dedication by Marcus Antonius Flaccus.

EDCS-11000912.text_edition: \n Titus Caecilius Titi filius Galeria Ausone miles legionis IIII Macedonicae centuria Munati annorum XXXVII aerorum XVII hic situs est Lucius Sempronius Ausone optio |(centuriae) Iuli Martialis exs sic testamento fecit vivite felices quibus est data vita fruendi nam mihi non fato datum est felice morari hic ego nunc iaceo fatis compostus iniquis crudeles superi ni me fortuna iniqua tulisset et mea iam V APM DA \n
EDCS-11000912.translation: Titus Caecilius Ausone, son of Titus, of the Galeria tribe, from Ausone, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion in the centuria of Munatius, aged 37 and with 17 years of service, is buried here. Lucius Sempronius Ausone, optio of the 1st centuria of Julius Martialis, made this according to his will. Live happily, you who have been granted life to enjoy it, for it was not granted to me to die happily. Here I lie now, laid to rest by cruel fate. If only unfair fortune had not taken me, and my...
EDCS-11000912.summary: A tombstone for Titus Caecilius Ausone, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, whose optio, Lucius Sempronius Ausone, fulfilled his will, reflecting on an unhappy fate.

EDCS-11000913.text_edition: \n Quintus Castricius Quinti filius Papiria Severus Ticini miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXX stipendiorum XI hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000913.translation: Quintus Castricius Severus, son of Quintus, of the Papiria tribe, from Ticini, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, aged 30 and with 11 years of service, is buried here. His heir had this made.
EDCS-11000913.summary: A tombstone for Quintus Castricius Severus, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000914.text_edition: \n Lucius Cattonius Luci filius Secundus Claudia Viruno miles legionis IIII annorum XXIV stipendiorum IIII hic situs est heredes Cottii faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000914.translation: Lucius Cattonius Secundus, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, from Viruno, a soldier of the 4th Legion, aged 24 and with 4 years of service, is buried here. The heirs of Cottius had this made.
EDCS-11000914.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Cattonius Secundus, a soldier of the 4th Legion, erected by the heirs of Cottius.

EDCS-11000916.text_edition: \n Titus Clodius Titi filius Stellatina Optatus Augusta Taurinorum miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXV stipendiorum V hic situs est Titus N C heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000916.translation: Titus Clodius Optatus, son of Titus, of the Stellatina tribe, from Augusta Taurinorum, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, aged 25 and with 5 years of service, is buried here. Titus N C, his heir, had this made.
EDCS-11000916.summary: A tombstone for Titus Clodius Optatus, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, erected by his heir, Titus N C.

EDCS-11000917.text_edition: \n Cnaeus Coelius Cnaei filius Papiria Marullinus domo Narbone miles legionis IIIII Macedonicae annorum XXXV stipendiorum XIIII hic situs est heres ex testamento faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000917.translation: Cnaeus Coelius Marullinus, son of Cnaeus, of the Papiria tribe, from Narbo, a soldier of the 5th Macedonian Legion, aged 35 and with 14 years of service, is buried here. His heir had this made according to the will.
EDCS-11000917.summary: A tombstone for Cnaeus Coelius Marullinus, a soldier of the 5th Macedonian Legion, erected by his heir as per his will.

EDCS-11000918.translation: Lucius Giamillius Cerialis, son of Lucius, of the Claudia tribe, from Viruno, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, aged 25 and with 5 years of service, is buried here. His heir had this made.
EDCS-11000918.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Giamillius Cerialis, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11000919.translation: Titus Iulius Macer, son of Lucius, of the Galeria tribe, from Nertobriga, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, aged 45 and with 17 years of service, is buried here. His brother had this made.
EDCS-11000919.summary: A tombstone for Titus Iulius Macer, a soldier of the 4th Macedonian Legion, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11000920.text_edition: \n Marcus Iulius Marci filius Aniensis Foro Iuli Macrinus miles legionis IIII Macedonicae nnorum XXVI stipendiorum VI hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000920.translation: Marcus Iulius Macrinus, son of Marcus, of the Aniensis tribe, from Forum Iuli, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 26, with 6 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000920.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Iulius Macrinus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at the age of 26.

EDCS-11000921.text_edition: \n Gaius Iulius Gai filius Voltinia Priscus Tolosa miles sic legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXX stipendiorum X hic situs est tesamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000921.translation: Gaius Iulius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Tolosa, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 30, with 10 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made according to his will.
EDCS-11000921.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Iulius Priscus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, whose heir commissioned the monument after his death at age 30.

EDCS-11000922.text_edition: \n Lucius Lictavius Luci filius Aniensis Verus Foro Iuli miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXVI stipendiorum VIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000922.translation: Lucius Lictavius Verus, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Forum Iuli, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 26, with 8 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000922.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Lictavius Verus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at the age of 26.

EDCS-11000925.text_edition: \n Marcus Lutatius Marci filius Sergia Albanus domo Corfinio miles legionis IIII Macedonicae nnum XL stipendiorum XX Ventilator heres fecit\n
EDCS-11000925.translation: Marcus Lutatius Albanus, son of Marcus, of the Sergia tribe, from Corfinium, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 40, with 20 years of service. Ventilator. His heir had this made.
EDCS-11000925.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Lutatius Albanus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at age 40.

EDCS-11000926.text_edition: \n Gaius Minicius Gai filius Stellatina Asper Augu<s>ta Taurinorum miles legionis IIII Ma<c=G>(edonicae) nnorum VL stipendiorum XXV hic situs est frater de suo \n
EDCS-11000926.translation: Gaius Minicius Asper, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe, from Augusta Taurinorum, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 45, with 25 years of service, is buried here. His brother made this at his own expense.
EDCS-11000926.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Minicius Asper, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at age 45, commissioned by his brother.

EDCS-11000927.translation: Marcus Petronius Mansuetus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Viana, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 30, with 9 years of service, is buried here; he ordered this to be made by his will, and his heir had it made.
EDCS-11000927.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Petronius Mansuetus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at age 30, commissioned by his heir as per his will.

EDCS-11000928.text_edition: \n Marcus Sullius Marci filius Voltinia Viana Campanus miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXV stipendiorum VI hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000928.translation: Marcus Sullius Campanus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Viana, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 25, with 6 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000928.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Sullius Campanus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at the age of 25.

EDCS-11000929.translation: Sextus Valerius Mansuetus, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vienna, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 25, with 4 years of service, is buried here; his heirs had it made.
EDCS-11000929.summary: This is a tombstone for Sextus Valerius Mansuetus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at age 25, commissioned by his heirs.

EDCS-11000930.text_edition: \n Gaius Valerius Gai filius Papiria Narbo Taurus miles legionis IIII Macedonicae nnrum XXX stipendiorum X ex testamento\n
EDCS-11000930.translation: Gaius Valerius Taurus, son of Gaius, of the Papiria tribe, from Narbo, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 30, with 10 years of service, according to his will.
EDCS-11000930.summary: This inscription records the posthumous arrangement for Gaius Valerius Taurus, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, based on his will, who died at age 30.

EDCS-11000931.text_edition: \n Caius Valerius Luci filius Pollia Tertius Hasta miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXX stipendiorum X hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000931.translation: Caius Valerius Tertius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, from Hasta, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, aged 30, with 10 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-11000931.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Valerius Tertius, a soldier of the IV Macedonica legion, who died at age 30, commissioned by his heir.

EDCS-11000932.text_edition: \n Lucius Vinicius Luci filius Galeria domo Modestus Luguduno miles legionis IIII Macedonicae nnum XXXV stipendiorum XII heres pro pietate\n
EDCS-11000932.translation: Lucius Vinicius Modestus, son of Lucius, of the Galerian tribe, from Lugudunum, a soldier of Legio IV Macedonica, aged 35, with 12 years of service, erected this as heir out of duty.
EDCS-11000932.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vinicius Modestus, a soldier of Legio IV Macedonica.

EDCS-11000933.translation: Valentia, of the Pollian tribe, a soldier of Legio IV Macedonica, aged 25, with 8 years of service, lies here. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11000933.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Valentia, a soldier of Legio IV Macedonica.

EDCS-11000935.translation: Legio IIII [?], century of Rufinus [?], [?], of Servilius Severus.
EDCS-11000935.summary: This inscription appears to be a military dedication or record, possibly related to Legio IIII and centurions.

EDCS-11000936.translation: Victorinus Clementinus and Victorinus Senecionius Iulianus, his sons, had this made for their most dutiful father, Victorio Cassianus, a veteran of Legio VII, who lived 55 years, through their freedman Victorius Hermetes.
EDCS-11000936.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by sons for their father, Victorio Cassianus, a veteran of Legio VII.

EDCS-11000937.translation: Titus Agileius Carus, son of Titus, of the Voltinian tribe, a veteran from Legio VIII Augusta.
EDCS-11000937.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Agileius Carus, a veteran of Legio VIII Augusta.

EDCS-11000938.text_edition: \n legionis VIII Augustae item legionis II Tr<a=O>ianae Titus Flavius Aeternus et Titus Flavius Albinus et Titus Flavius Verecundus LVIITIIFPOVFS \n
EDCS-11000938.translation: Titus Flavius Aeternus, Titus Flavius Albinus, and Titus Flavius Verecundus, of Legio VIII Augusta, and also of Legio II Traiana.
EDCS-11000938.summary: This inscription likely records the service or memorial of soldiers from Legio VIII Augusta and Legio II Traiana.

EDCS-11000939.text_edition: \n Publius Urvinus Publi filius Pollia Foro Fulvi speculator legionis XIII stipendiorum XIIX annorum XXXV hic situs est Marcus Aruntius consobrinus curam egit\n
EDCS-11000939.translation: Publius Urvinus, son of Publius, of the Pollian tribe, from Foro Fulvi, a speculator (scout) of Legio XIII, with 12 years of service, aged 35, lies here; Marcus Aruntius, his cousin, saw to the care.
EDCS-11000939.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Urvinus, a speculator of Legio XIII.

EDCS-11000940.text_edition: \n Primus Aebutius Luci filius Veturia Placentia veteranus exs sic legione XIIII nnrum LV aerorum XXII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000940.translation: Primus Aebutius, son of Lucius, of the Veturian tribe, from Placentia, a veteran of this legion [Legio XIIII], aged 55, with 22 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11000940.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Primus Aebutius, a veteran of Legio XIIII.

EDCS-11000941.text_edition: \n Caius Allius Cai filius Aniensis Cremona miles legionis XIIII geminae nnum XXX stipendiorum XV hic situs est frater ob pietatem\n
EDCS-11000941.translation: Gaius Allius, son of Gaius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Cremona, a soldier of Legio XIIII Gemina, aged 30, with 15 years of service, lies here; his brother [erected this] out of duty.
EDCS-11000941.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Allius, a soldier of Legio XIIII Gemina, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11000942.text_edition: \n Marcus Braetius Marci Stellatina Taurinis miles legionis XIIII geminae annorum XXXV stipendiorum XIIII hic situs est ex testamento\n
EDCS-11000942.translation: Marcus Braetius, son of Marcus, of the Stellatina tribe, from Taurinis, a soldier of Legio XIIII Gemina, aged 35, with 14 years of service, lies here, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-11000942.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Braetius, a soldier of Legio XIIII Gemina, erected according to his will.

EDCS-11000943.text_edition: \n Priscus servus Publi Cassi aquiliferi legionis XIIII geminae nnorum XVII dominus pro beneficiis posuit hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000943.translation: Priscus, slave of Publius Cassius, aquilifer of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 17, erected this for his master because of his kindness; he lies here.
EDCS-11000943.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a slave for his master, a standard-bearer in the 14th Legion, dated to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000944.text_edition: \n Quintus Clodius Quinti filius Aniensis Vercellis miles legionis XIIII geminae an(norum) -XXV \n
EDCS-11000944.translation: Quintus Clodius, son of Quintus, of the Aniensis tribe from Vercellae, soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 25.
EDCS-11000944.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Clodius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000945.translation: Gaius Cornelius, son of Gaius, of the Pollia tribe from Ast(a), soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 40, with 23 years of service. Three freedmen saw to the making of this monument according to his will; he lies here.
EDCS-11000945.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Cornelius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, whose freedmen fulfilled his burial arrangements, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000946.translation: Gaius Dannius Secundus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe from Vianna, soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 30, with 12 years of service. He ordered by his will that this be done, his heir took care of the making of it; he lies here.
EDCS-11000946.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Dannius Secundus, a soldier of the 14th Legion, whose will stipulated his burial, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000947.text_edition: \n Caius Donius Suavis Claudia Viruno vixit annos XL miles legionis XIIII geminae stipendiorum XV Lucius Donius Albanus frater faciundum curavit hic intus situs <e=T>(st) \n
