EDCS-11000947.translation: Gaius Donius Suavis and Claudia of Virunum lived 40 years; he was a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion with 15 years of service. Lucius Donius Albanus, his brother, saw to the making of this; he lies within.
EDCS-11000947.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Donius Suavis, a soldier of the 14th Legion, and his wife Claudia, set up by his brother, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000948.text_edition: \n Quintus Gavius Marci filius Arniensis Histonio miles legionis XIIII geminae nnrum XIIX stipendii I hic situs est frater pro pietate de suo\n
EDCS-11000948.translation: Quintus Gavius, son of Marcus, of the Arnien(sis) tribe from Histonium, soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 18, with 1 year of service; he lies here. His brother set this up out of dutiful affection.
EDCS-11000948.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Gavius, a young soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his brother out of affection, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000949.text_edition: \n Marcus Gellius Marci filius Claudia Secundus Ara miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XXIV stipendiorum IIII hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000949.translation: Marcus Gellius, son of Marcus, of the Claudia tribe from Secundus Ara, soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 24, with 4 years of service; he lies here. His heir saw to the making of this.
EDCS-11000949.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Gellius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his heir, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000950.translation: Gaius Iulius Marinus of Ara, a soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion in the armamentarii, aged 30, with 12 years of service. His heir made this according to the will, and acted as supervisor.
EDCS-11000950.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Iulius Marinus, a specialist soldier (armamentarius) in the 14th Legion, whose heir fulfilled his burial wishes, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000951.text_edition: \n Titus Iulius Titi filius Sabatina Secundus Firmo miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XXXV stipendiorum IX hic situs est testamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000951.translation: Titus Iulius Secundus of Firmo, son of Titus, of the Sabatina tribe, soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 35, with 9 years of service; he lies here. He ordered by his will that this be done, his heir took care of the making of it.
EDCS-11000951.summary: A funerary inscription for Titus Iulius Secundus, a soldier of the 14th Legion, whose burial was arranged by his heir according to his will, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000952.text_edition: \n Quintus Lollius Marci filius Voltinia miles legionis XIIII geminae nnorum XXXX stipendiorum XVIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000952.translation: Quintus Lollius, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 40, with 18 years of service; he lies here.
EDCS-11000952.summary: A funerary inscription for Quintus Lollius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000953.text_edition: \n Quintus Luccius Quinti filius Pollia Faustus Pollentia miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XXXV stipendiorum XVII hic situs est heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000953.translation: Quintus Luccius Faustus, son of Quintus, of the Pollia tribe, a soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 35 and with 17 years of service, is buried here. His heirs arranged for this monument to be made.
EDCS-11000953.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Luccius Faustus, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his heirs.

EDCS-11000954.text_edition: \n Secundus Metilius Marci filius Stellatina Taurinis miles legionis XIV geminae nnrum XXX stipendiorum VII hic situs est aemici posuerunt\n
EDCS-11000954.translation: Secundus Metilius, son of Marcus, of the Stellatina tribe from Taurinis, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 30 and with 7 years of service, is buried here. His friends erected this.
EDCS-11000954.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Secundus Metilius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his friends.

EDCS-11000955.text_edition: \n Quintus Mettius Cai filius Ste<L=i>(latina) Foro Vibi miles legionis XIIII geminae nnorum XXX stipendiorum VII hic situs est fratres pro pietate dederunt de suo \n
EDCS-11000955.translation: Quintus Mettius, son of Caius, of the Stellatina tribe from Forum Vibii, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 30 and with 7 years of service, is buried here. His brothers dedicated this from their own means out of piety.
EDCS-11000955.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Mettius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his brothers.

EDCS-11000956.text_edition: \n Cnaeus Musius Titi filius Galeria Veleias annorum XXXII stipendiorum XV aquilifer legionis XIIII geminae Marcus Musius |(centurio) frater posuit\n
EDCS-11000956.translation: Gnaeus Musius, son of Titus, of the Galeria tribe from Veleia, aged 32 and with 15 years of service, aquilifer of the 14th Gemina legion. Marcus Musius, his brother and a centurion, erected this.
EDCS-11000956.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gnaeus Musius, an aquilifer in the 14th Legion, erected by his brother, Marcus Musius, a centurion.

EDCS-11000957.text_edition: \n Lucius Naevius Publi filius Stellatina Taurinis miles legionis XIIII geminae nnum XLV stipendiorum XXIII hic situs est frater posuit\n
EDCS-11000957.translation: Lucius Naevius, son of Publius, of the Stellatina tribe from Taurinis, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 45 and with 23 years of service, is buried here. His brother erected this.
EDCS-11000957.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Naevius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11000958.text_edition: \n Sextus Naevius Sexti filius Tromentina Aquis miles legionis XIIII geminae nnorum XXXV stipendia XI hic situs est Titus Licinius exs sic testamenti formula posuit\n
EDCS-11000958.translation: Sextus Naevius, son of Sextus, of the Tromentina tribe from Aquae, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 35 and with 11 years of service, is buried here. Titus Licinius erected this according to the terms of the will.
EDCS-11000958.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextus Naevius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected according to his will by Titus Licinius.

EDCS-11000959.text_edition: \n Quintus Octavius Quinti filius Voltinia Tolosa eques legionis XIIII geminae annorum XXXV stipendiorum XII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000959.translation: Quintus Octavius, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe from Tolosa, an *eques* (cavalryman) of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 35 and with 12 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000959.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Octavius, a cavalryman in the 14th Legion.

EDCS-11000960.text_edition: \n Quintus Pompeiius sic Quinti filius Publilia Severus Verona miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum XL stipendiorum XIX hic situs est testamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11000960.translation: Quintus Pompeius Severus, son of Quintus, of the Publilia tribe from Verona, a soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 40 and with 19 years of service, is buried here. He ordered this to be made in his will, and his heirs arranged for it to be done.
EDCS-11000960.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Pompeius Severus, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected posthumously as per his will.

EDCS-11000961.text_edition: \n Titus Quintius Titi filius Pollia Vardagate miles legionis XIIII <g=C>eminae nnrum XXXXIIII stipendiorum XXIII hic situs est frater posuit titulum ex testamento pro pietate \n
EDCS-11000961.translation: Titus Quintius, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe from Vardagate, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 44 and with 23 years of service, is buried here. His brother erected this monument from his own funds according to his will, out of piety.
EDCS-11000961.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Quintius, a soldier of the 14th Legion, erected by his brother as per his will.

EDCS-11000962.text_edition: \n Marcus Servilius Marci filius Fabia Seneca domo Brixia nnorum XXXX miles legionis XIIII geminae centuria Quinti Helvi Bucconis stipendiorum XIX hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000962.translation: Marcus Servilius, son of Marcus, of the Fabia tribe from Seneca (born in Brixia), aged 40, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, in the century of Quintus Helvius Bucconis, with 19 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000962.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Servilius, a soldier in the 14th Legion, noting his unit and place of origin.

EDCS-11000963.text_edition: \n Lucius Statius Luci filius Pollia Pollentia miles legionis XIIII geminae nnrum XXXIIX stipendiorum XIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000963.translation: Lucius Statius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, from Pollentia, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 38, with 13 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000963.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Statius, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE based on the legion's history.

EDCS-11000964.text_edition: \n Titus Tertius Titi filius Voltinia Vianna miles legionis XIIII geminae annorum XXV stipendiorum IIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000964.translation: Titus Tertius, son of Titus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vianna, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 25, with 4 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000964.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Tertius, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000965.text_edition: \n Marcus Valerius Luci filius Publilia Verona miles legionis XIIII geminae annorum XXXV stipendiorum XVI hic situs est fratres posuerunt ave vale\n
EDCS-11000965.translation: Marcus Valerius, son of Lucius, of the Publilia tribe, from Verona, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 35, with 16 years of service, is buried here. His brothers erected this. Hail and farewell.
EDCS-11000965.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Valerius, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, erected by his brothers, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000967.translation: Lucius Valerius Verecundus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vienna, a veteran of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 50, is buried here. He ordered this to be made in his will; his heir took care of its construction.
EDCS-11000967.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Valerius Verecundus, a veteran of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, indicating provision for burial in his will, likely dating to the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000968.translation: Quintus Vettius Reis, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 27, with 7 years of service, is buried here. His heir, Iulius, placed this according to his will.
EDCS-11000968.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Vettius Reis, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, whose burial was arranged by his heir Iulius, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000969.text_edition: \n ? Virius Macconis filius Pollia Eporedia miles legionis XIIII geminae nnorum XXIIX stipendiorum VII hic situs est curavit Firmus ValPS \n
EDCS-11000969.translation: ? Virius, son of Macco, of the Pollia tribe, from Eporedia, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 28, with 7 years of service, is buried here. Firmus administered its construction.
EDCS-11000969.summary: This is a tombstone for ? Virius, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, with administration by Firmus, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000970.text_edition: \n i filius Papiria Rufus veteranus ex legione XIIII gemina Martia victrice nnorum XLV hic situs est heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11000970.translation: Rufus, son of ?, of the Papiria tribe, a veteran from the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged 45, is buried here. His heirs arranged for its construction.
EDCS-11000970.summary: This is a tombstone for Rufus, a veteran of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, with construction arranged by his heirs, likely dating to the late 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000971.translation: ..., son of Lucius (?), of the Velina tribe, from Ag[...], a cavalryman of the 14th Gemina legion, is buried here.
EDCS-11000971.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for an unnamed cavalryman of the 14th Gemina legion, with tribal affiliation and origin partially preserved, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000974.text_edition: \n legionis XIV geminae stipendiorum IIX hic situs est Gaius Ennius municeps donavit\n
EDCS-11000974.translation: Gaius Ennius, a citizen, donated [this monument] for a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion with 8 years of service, who is buried here.
EDCS-11000974.summary: This inscription records a donation by Gaius Ennius for a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000975.text_edition: \n Firmo miles legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis annorum stipendiorum \n
EDCS-11000975.translation: Firmo, a soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, aged [---], with [---] years of service, [is buried here].
EDCS-11000975.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Firmo, a soldier of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, with missing age and service years, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11000981.translation: Legio XIIII [gemina Martia victrix], [centuria] C(ai) Ap[...].
EDCS-11000981.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely from a military context, mentioning the 14th Legion and a centuria.

EDCS-11000983.text_edition: \n Legio XIIII gemina Martia victrix centuria Publi Helvi Terti\n
EDCS-11000983.translation: Legio XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, centuria of Publius Helvius Tertius.
EDCS-11000983.summary: This inscription records a centuria of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion.

EDCS-11000984.text_edition: \n Cohors II legionis XIIII <g=C>(eminae) Martiae victricis centuria Fuli Sedati \n
EDCS-11000984.translation: The second cohort of the 14th Gemina Martiae Victricis legion, centuria of Fulvius Sedatus.
EDCS-11000984.summary: This inscription identifies a centuria within the second cohort of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion.

EDCS-11000986.translation: Legio XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, cohort I, centuria of Publius Murrasius.
EDCS-11000986.summary: This inscription records a centuria of the first cohort of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion.

EDCS-11000987.summary: This fragmentary inscription indicates a centuria of the 10th Legion.

EDCS-11000988.translation: Legio XIIII, centuria of Lucius Rufus.
EDCS-11000988.summary: This inscription records a centuria of the 14th Legion.

EDCS-11000989.text_edition: \n Legio XIIII gemina Martia victrix centuria Cai Senti\n
EDCS-11000989.translation: Legio XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, centuria of Caius Senti[us].
EDCS-11000989.summary: This inscription records a centuria of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion.

EDCS-11000990.text_edition: \n <L=I>egio XIIII gemina Martia victrix centuria Cai Ve<l=I>si Secundi \n
EDCS-11000990.translation: Legio XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, centuria of Caius Velsius Secundus.
EDCS-11000990.summary: This inscription records a centuria of the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion, likely dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-11000991.translation: Legio XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, centuria of Caecilius V(---) Sabinei; centuria of Caecilius V(---) Musentius, assistant; centuria of Caecilius V(---) Meto.
EDCS-11000991.summary: This inscription lists three centuriae, all possibly belonging to Caecilius V(---), within the 14th Gemina Martia Victrix legion.

EDCS-11000992.text_edition: \n Lucius Antestius Cai filius Veturia Placentia miles legionis XVI annorum XXVI stipendiorum II hic situs est Titus Antestius frater posuit\n
EDCS-11000992.translation: Lucius Antestius, son of Caius, of the Veturia tribe, from Placentia, a soldier of the 16th Legion, 26 years old, with 2 years of service, lies here. Titus Antestius, his brother, set this up.
EDCS-11000992.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Antestius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, erected by his brother, likely dating to the early imperial period.

EDCS-11000993.text_edition: \n Lucius Cassius Luci filius Ouffentina sic miles legionis XVI annorum XXXV stipendiorum XII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000993.translation: Lucius Cassius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 16th Legion, aged 35, with 12 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000993.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Cassius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, indicating his age and years of service.

EDCS-11000994.text_edition: \n Quintus Cornelius Quinti filius Voltinia miles legionis XVI \n
EDCS-11000994.translation: Quintus Cornelius, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 16th Legion.
EDCS-11000994.summary: This inscription records Quintus Cornelius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, likely part of a funerary monument.

EDCS-11000995.translation: Tertius Exsomnus, son of Tertius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Vercelli, a soldier of the 16th Legion, aged 40, with 16 years of service, is buried here. Aurelius erected this at his own expense.
EDCS-11000995.summary: This is a tombstone for Tertius Exsomnus, a soldier of the 16th Legion, with a dedication possibly by Aurelius.

EDCS-11000996.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai filius Voltinia Andiccus miles legionis XVI nnrum XLV stipendiorum XXI hic situs est heres posuit\n
EDCS-11000996.translation: Caius Iulius Andiccus, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 16th Legion, aged 45, with 21 years of service, is buried here. His heir erected this.
EDCS-11000996.summary: This tombstone commemorates Caius Iulius Andiccus, a soldier of the 16th Legion, with his age, service, and the fact his heir erected it.

EDCS-11000997.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai filius Galeria Luguduno Optatus miles legionis XVI centuria Sei annorum XXXV stipendiorum XVI quod heredes posuere hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000997.translation: Caius Iulius Optatus, son of Caius, of the Galeria tribe, from Lugudunum, a soldier of the 16th Legion, in the century of Seius, aged 35, with 16 years of service, is buried here. His heirs erected this.
EDCS-11000997.summary: This inscription is for Caius Iulius Optatus, a soldier of the 16th Legion, buried here, with his heirs noted as the erectors.

EDCS-11000998.text_edition: \n Miles legionis XVI centuria Viatoris Sextus Lartidius Sexti filius Velina Pistoriis nnrum XXVI stipendiorum IV hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000998.translation: Sextus Lartidius, son of Sextus, of the Velina tribe, from Pistoria, a soldier of the 16th Legion, in the century of Viator, aged 26, with 4 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000998.summary: This tombstone records Sextus Lartidius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, detailing his age and service.

EDCS-11000999.text_edition: \n Lucius Novellius Titi filius Pollia Hispello miles legionis XVI annorum XXXXV stipendiorum XVII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11000999.translation: Lucius Novellius, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, from Hispellum, a soldier of the 16th Legion, aged 45, with 17 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11000999.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Novellius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, indicating his age and years of service.

EDCS-11001000.text_edition: \n Titus Pompeius Titi filius Voltinia Viana miles legionis XVI annorum XXXX stipendiorum XIX hic situs est heres posuit municeps\n
EDCS-11001000.translation: Titus Pompeius, son of Titus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Viana, a soldier of the 16th Legion, aged 40, with 19 years of service, is buried here. His heir erected this as a municipal official.
EDCS-11001000.summary: This tombstone honors Titus Pompeius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, erected by his heir who was also a municipal official.

EDCS-11001001.text_edition: \n Caius Satrius Cai filius Voltinia Caballione sic miles legionis XVI nnorum XLV stipendiorum XX hic situs est heredes ex testamento posuerunt\n
EDCS-11001001.translation: Caius Satrius, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Caballio, a soldier of the 16th Legion, aged 45, with 20 years of service, is buried here. His heirs erected this according to his will.
EDCS-11001001.summary: This inscription records the burial of Caius Satrius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, with his heirs erecting it as per his will.

EDCS-11001002.text_edition: \n Titus Viccius Titi filius Voturia Placentia miles ex legione XVI annorum L stipendiorum XXIIII hic situs est heres ex testamento posuit\n
EDCS-11001002.translation: Titus Viccius, son of Titus, of the Voturia tribe, from Placentia, a soldier from the 16th Legion, aged 50, with 24 years of service, is buried here. His heir erected this according to his will.
EDCS-11001002.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Viccius, a soldier of the 16th Legion, with his heir erecting it according to his will.

EDCS-11001003.translation: Luso, aged [3?] years, a soldier of the 16th Legion, lies here; he had a tombstone erected for himself at his own expense.
EDCS-11001003.summary: This is a tombstone for Luso, a soldier of the 16th Legion, who paid for his own monument.

EDCS-11001005.text_edition: \n Lucius Marius Luci filius Pupinea sic Baeterris miles legionis XXI stipendiorum XVI nnrum XXXX hic situs est frater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001005.translation: Lucius Marius, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe, a soldier of the 21st Legion, with 16 years of service and 40 years of age, lies here; his brother arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11001005.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Marius, a soldier of the 21st Legion, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11001006.translation: Marcus Valerius Matto, son of Marcus, of the Lemonia tribe, a soldier of the 21st Rapax Legion, in the century of Lucius Faltonius Firmus, aged 40 years and with 19 years of service, lies here; he ordered by his will to have this done, and his heir arranged for it to be made.
EDCS-11001006.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Valerius Matto, a soldier of the 21st Legion, who was 40 years old with 19 years of service and whose heir fulfilled his testamentary wishes.

EDCS-11001007.text_edition: \n Bononia miles legionis XXI rapacis annorum XXXV stipendiorum XIV hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001007.translation: Bononia, a soldier of the 21st Rapax Legion, aged 35 years and with 14 years of service, lies here; his heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11001007.summary: This is a tombstone for Bononia, a soldier of the 21st Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001008.text_edition: \n Quintus Marcius Balbus missicius legionis XXI et Celer filius eius hic siti sunt\n
EDCS-11001008.translation: Quintus Marcius Balbus, honorably discharged soldier of the 21st Legion, and his son Celer, lie here.
EDCS-11001008.summary: This is a tombstone for Quintus Marcius Balbus, a discharged soldier of the 21st Legion, and his son Celer.

EDCS-11001011.text_edition: \n Caius Annius Cai filius Aniensi Salutus Vercellis miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXXIII stipendiorum XI hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001011.translation: Caius Annius Salutus, son of Caius, of the Aniensis tribe, from Vercelli, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 33 years and with 11 years of service, lies here; his heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11001011.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Annius Salutus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001012.text_edition: \n Romanus Titi Avidi Cordi equitis legionis XXII Primigeniae servus annorum XXVII meritis eius positum hic intus situs est sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-11001012.translation: Romanus, slave of Titus Avidus Cordus, a cavalryman of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 27 years, has been placed here in consideration of his services; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11001012.summary: This is a tombstone for Romanus, a slave of a cavalryman of the 22nd Legion, who died at age 27.

EDCS-11001013.translation: [...], a standard-bearer of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, a citizen of Traian[a?], aged [30s?], with 15 years of service, lies here; his heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11001013.summary: This is a tombstone for Aurotrae Biti, a standard-bearer of the 22nd Legion, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001014.translation: Maternia Materna, his wife, and his heir, Lucanius Maternus, his father-in-law, arranged for this to be made for Aurelius Alexander, a soldier of the 22nd Legion.
EDCS-11001014.summary: This is a tombstone for Aurelius Alexander, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, erected by his wife and father-in-law.

EDCS-11001015.translation: Aulus Baebius Clemens, son of Caius, of the Scaptia tribe, from Faesulae, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, aged 41 years and with 24 years of service, lies here; Crescens, son of Lucius, arranged for this.
EDCS-11001015.summary: This is a tombstone for Aulus Baebius Clemens, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, erected by Crescens.

EDCS-11001016.text_edition: \n Sextus Careius Sexti filius Voltinia Florus Foro Augusti miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXIX stipendiorum IX hic situs est heres ex testamento\n
EDCS-11001016.translation: Sextus Careius Florus, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 29, with 9 years of service, is buried here; his heir arranged for this monument according to his will.
EDCS-11001016.summary: A tombstone for Sextus Careius Florus, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, stating his age, service years, and that his heir arranged it via his will.

EDCS-11001017.text_edition: \n Marcus Cornelius Marci filius Voltinia Optatus Aquis Sextiis miles legionis XXII Primigeniae centuria Quinti Stati Proxumi aerorum XI testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-11001017.translation: Marcus Cornelius Optatus, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion in the century of Quintus Statius Proximus, with 11 years of service, ordered this monument to be made by his will.
EDCS-11001017.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Cornelius Optatus, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, stating his service years and that he ordered it made by his will.

EDCS-11001018.text_edition: \n Caius Faltonius Cai filius Pomptina Secundus Dertona miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XLVI stipendiorum XXI hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001018.translation: Caius Faltonius Secundus, son of Caius, of the Pomptina tribe, from Dertona, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 46, with 21 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11001018.summary: A tombstone for Caius Faltonius Secundus, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, stating his age and service years.

EDCS-11001019.translation: Titus Iavennius Proculus, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, from Faventia, a centurion of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 45, with [years] of service [...]
EDCS-11001019.summary: A tombstone fragment for Titus Iavennius Proculus, likely a centurion of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, indicating his age and partial service years.

EDCS-11001020.translation: To Gaius Julius Flavius, a cornicularius (clerk) to the legate of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, with 17 years of service, who lived 35 years, 11 months, and 25 days; Cocceia Chrysis erected this monument for her incomparable and dutiful wife.
EDCS-11001020.summary: A dedication by Cocceia Chrysis to her deceased husband, Gaius Julius Flavius, a soldier in the 22nd Primigenia Legion, detailing his service, age, and her affection.

EDCS-11001021.translation: Tiberius Julius Rufinus, son of Tiberius, of the Claudia tribe, a cavalryman from Virunum, of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, with 26 years of service, ordered this monument to be made by his will; his heirs arranged for it to be erected.
EDCS-11001021.summary: A tombstone for Tiberius Julius Rufinus, a cavalryman in the 22nd Primigenia Legion, stating his service years and that his heirs arranged it by his will.

EDCS-11001022.text_edition: \n Caius Matteius Cai filius Lemonia Priscus Bononia miles legionis XXII Primigeniae nnorum XXXIII stipendiorum XIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001022.translation: Caius Matteius Priscus, son of Caius, of the Lemonia tribe, from Bononia, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 33, with 13 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11001022.summary: A tombstone for Caius Matteius Priscus, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, stating his age and service years.

EDCS-11001023.translation: Publius Metellus, son of Lucius, [---]VS, [---] of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, [---]III years of service [...]
EDCS-11001023.summary: A fragmentary inscription for Publius Metellus, likely a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, with illegible details about his rank and service years.

EDCS-11001024.translation: Marcus Mucius Pudens, son of Marcus, of the Publilia tribe, from Albenga, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, aged 30, with 9 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11001024.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Mucius Pudens, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, stating his age and service years.

EDCS-11001025.text_edition: \n Marcus Novellius Marci filius Oufentina Romanus Mediolani miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXXIII stipendiorum XIII hic situs est ex testamento titulum fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001025.translation: Marcus Novellius Romanus, son of Marcus, of the Oufentina tribe, from Milan, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 33, with 13 years of service, is buried here; he ordered the monument to be made by his will, and his heir arranged for it to be erected.
EDCS-11001025.summary: A tombstone for Marcus Novellius Romanus, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, stating his age, service years, and that his heir arranged it via his will.

EDCS-11001026.translation: To the departed spirits and eternal memory of Perpetua Severa, a citizen of Cologne, an exceptionally dutiful mother, who lived 71 years. Pervincius Ursinus, soldier, armourer of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, and his daughter-in-law Vitalinia Servanda had this made.
EDCS-11001026.summary: This funerary epitaph was set up for Perpetua Severa by her son Pervincius Ursinus and daughter-in-law Vitalinia Servanda, mentioning her age and his military service in the 22nd Legion.

EDCS-11001027.text_edition: \n Caius Rittius Cai filius Voltinia Paullus Vienna miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXXVIII stipendiorum XVIII hic situs est et ave et vale\n
EDCS-11001027.translation: Gaius Rittius Paullus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Vienna, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, 38 years old, with 18 years of service, lies here. Hail and farewell.
EDCS-11001027.summary: This is the epitaph of Gaius Rittius Paullus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, recording his age and service length.

EDCS-11001029.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Claudinae coniugi carissimae et reverentissimae Sammonius Paterculus custos armorum legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis et Marcellinus et Marcus parbuli sic faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001029.translation: To the departed spirits. For Claudina, my most beloved and reverent wife, Sammonius Paterculus, armourer of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, and his sons Marcellinus and Marcus, had this made.
EDCS-11001029.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated by Sammonius Paterculus, an armourer of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, to his wife Claudina, with his sons Marcellinus and Marcus also involved.

EDCS-11001030.text_edition: \n Lucius Sergius Luci filius Sabatina Valentinus legionis XXII nnorum XXVII stipendiorum VII\n
EDCS-11001030.translation: Lucius Sergius Valentinus, son of Lucius, of the Sabatina tribe, of the 22nd Legion, 27 years old, with 7 years of service.
EDCS-11001030.summary: This is a tombstone fragment for Lucius Sergius Valentinus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, noting his age and service length.

EDCS-11001031.text_edition: \n Publius Solius Publi filius Voltinia Suavis Viana miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXXXVII stipendiorum \n
EDCS-11001031.translation: Publius Solius Suavis, son of Publius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Viana, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, 47 years old, with [number illegible] years of service.
EDCS-11001031.summary: This epitaph records Publius Solius Suavis, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, noting his age and service length.

EDCS-11001032.text_edition: \n Marcus Sulpicius Marci filius Sabatina Valens Mantua miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum L stipendiorum XXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001032.translation: Marcus Sulpicius Valens, son of Marcus, of the Sabatina tribe, from Mantua, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, 50 years old, with 25 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001032.summary: This epitaph records Marcus Sulpicius Valens, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, noting his age, service length, and place of origin.

EDCS-11001033.translation: Marcus Terentius Tertius, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia(?) tribe, [soldier?] of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, 33 years old, with 13 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001033.summary: This funerary epitaph records Marcus Terentius Tertius, likely a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, noting his age and service length.

EDCS-11001034.text_edition: \n Quintus Valerius Quinti filius Oufentina Virilio Mediolano miles legionis XXII Primigeniae centuria Bargoni annorum XXIII stipendiorum III testamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001034.translation: Quintus Valerius Virilio, son of Quintus, of the Oufentina tribe, from Milan, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, in the centuria of Bargus, 23 years old, with 3 years of service. He ordered this to be made in his will; his heir had this made.
EDCS-11001034.summary: This epitaph for Quintus Valerius Virilio, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, notes his age, service length, unit, and that it was commissioned in his will.

EDCS-11001035.translation: Valerius Sabinus, son of Lucius, of the Papiria tribe, from Narbonne, soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia.
EDCS-11001035.summary: This is a fragment of an epitaph for Valerius Sabinus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, noting his origin.

EDCS-11001036.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caius Valerius Secundus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis stipendiorum XXV Valerius Veranius fratri faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001036.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Valerius Secundus, soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, pious and faithful, with 25 years of service. Valerius Veranius had this made for his brother.
EDCS-11001036.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Valerius Veranius for his brother Gaius Valerius Secundus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, recording his service length.

EDCS-11001037.text_edition: \n Sextus Valerius Sexti filius Voltinia Severus Luco Augusti miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XL stipendiorum XIX hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001037.translation: Sextus Valerius Severus, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 40, with 19 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-11001037.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Sextus Valerius Severus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001038.text_edition: \n Lucius Valerius Luci filius Pupinia Tertullus Laude miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXVI stipendiorum VI hic situs est heredes et secundus heres posuerunt\n
EDCS-11001038.translation: Lucius Valerius Tertullus, son of Lucius, of the Pupinia tribe, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 26, with 6 years of service, is buried here; his heirs and his secondary heir set this up.
EDCS-11001038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Tertullus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001039.translation: To the departed gods. Julius had this made for Lucius Valerius Victor, a soldier of the 22nd Legion.
EDCS-11001039.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Victor, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, with the dedicator identified as Julius.

EDCS-11001040.text_edition: \n Titus Vibius Titi filius Pollia Optatus Eporedia miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXXI stipendiorum XI hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001040.translation: Titus Vibius Optatus, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, from Eporedia, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 31, with 11 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-11001040.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Vibius Optatus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001041.text_edition: \n Caius Vibulius Cai filius Oufentina Valentinus Mediolano miles legionis XXII annorum XXXVIII stipendiorum XVIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001041.translation: Gaius Vibulius Valentinus, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe, from Mediolanum, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, aged 38, with 18 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11001041.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vibulius Valentinus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001042.text_edition: \n Vitalinio Salutari equiti legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Quintia Quintina uxor et Salutarii Victorina Victorinus Victor filii faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001042.translation: Quintia Quintina his wife and his children Salutarii, Victorina, Victorinus, and Victor had this made for Vitalinius Salutarius, an equestrian soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Pious Faithful Legion.
EDCS-11001042.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vitalinius Salutarius, an equestrian soldier of the 22nd Legion, commissioned by his wife and children.

EDCS-11001043.text_edition: \n Catulus Viruno miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum LV stipendiorum XXX hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001043.translation: Catulus from Virunum, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, aged 55, with 30 years of service, is buried here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-11001043.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Catulus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001044.translation: Favor (?), a veteran, duplarius of the 22nd Primigenia Pious Faithful Legion, who lived 67 years, a citizen of Taunum (?), his wife and Potentinius Victor, an optio of the 22nd Primigenia Pious Faithful Legion, and their mother (as heirs) had this made.
EDCS-11001044.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Favor, a veteran duplarius of the 22nd Legion, and mentions his wife, son, and mother as heirs, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001045.text_edition: \n Titi filius Pap(iria) Nigrinus Narbone miles legionis XXII \n
EDCS-11001045.translation: Nigrinus, son of Titus, of the Papiria tribe, from Narbonne, a soldier of the 22nd Legion.
EDCS-11001045.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph fragment for Nigrinus, a soldier of the 22nd Legion.

EDCS-11001053.text_edition: \n Legio XXII Primigenia pia fidelis centuria Atti Atrecti\n
EDCS-11001053.translation: The 22nd Primigenia Pious Faithful Legion, the century of Attius Atreclus.
EDCS-11001053.summary: This inscription records a military unit, the 22nd Primigenia Legion, specifically mentioning the century of Attius Atreclus.

EDCS-11001058.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely referring to a military unit, specifically the century of Vetus.

EDCS-11001059.translation: Maternius Pardus, a soldier of the 22nd legion, had this made for his wife Candidia Urbana.
EDCS-11001059.summary: A tombstone erected by a soldier of the 22nd legion for his wife, indicating a dedication and the relationship between the individuals.

EDCS-11001060.text_edition: \n Licinio Liciniano beneficiario consularis Saecularia Severina coniunx faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001060.translation: Saecularia Severina, his wife, had this made for Licinius Licinianus, a beneficiarius consularis.
EDCS-11001060.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a wife for her husband, who held the position of beneficiarius consularis.

EDCS-11001061.text_edition: \n --- b(ene)f(iciarius) consularis qui vixit annos XXI menses V dies XXVI Restionius Restutus frater \n
EDCS-11001061.translation: Restionius Restutus, his brother, erected this for the beneficiarius consularis who lived 21 years, 5 months, and 26 days.
EDCS-11001061.summary: A tombstone erected by a brother for a deceased beneficiarius consularis, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-11001062.text_edition: \n lle S cum bis duodenos aetas NO tum rapuit fatis mors inimica suis ut rescit mater planxit flevere sodales flevisset genitor occidit ipse prior cognati proprii longa regione relicti hi pompam ornassent funeris usque mei qui posuit Proculus titulum nomenque sodalis inscripsit maerens hic pietatis honos sis felix valeas et te tua servet origo et dicas claro sit tibi terra levis Lucius Valerius Proculus commanipularis de sua pecunia curavit\n
EDCS-11001062.translation: Harsh fate snatched him away in his twelfth year. Death, an enemy to his own, mourned him; his mother wept, his comrades lamented, and his father would have lamented if he had died before him. His own kinsmen, left far behind, would have adorned his funeral procession. Proculus, a fellow soldier, placed this tombstone and inscribed his comrade's name, grieving, 'May earthly soil be light upon you; be happy, farewell, and may your lineage preserve you, and may you say 'may the earth be light for you'. Lucius Valerius Proculus, a fellow soldier, arranged for this from his own funds.
EDCS-11001062.summary: A detailed epitaph for Lucius Valerius Proculus, a young boy and fellow soldier, who died prematurely, with a poignant poem and his comrade's inscription.

EDCS-11001063.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Paulinae filiae nnrum XII aetatis infelicissimae Quietius Secundus librarius legati et Secundinia Paula patres faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001063.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Paulina, our daughter, 12 years of age, most unfortunate. Quietius Secundus, scribe of the legate, and Secundinia Paula, her parents, had this made.
EDCS-11001063.summary: A funerary inscription for an unfortunate 12-year-old girl, erected by her parents who both served in administrative roles connected to a legate.

EDCS-11001064.text_edition: \n D(is) M(anibus) Secundiniae Paulae coniugi incomparabili et pientissimae marito obsequentissimae Quietius Secundus beneficiarius legati\n
EDCS-11001064.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Secundinia Paula, an incomparable and most devoted wife, and a most obedient wife to her husband. Quietius Secundus, beneficiarius of the legate.
EDCS-11001064.summary: A tombstone dedicated to an exemplary wife by her husband, who was a beneficiarius of a legate.

EDCS-11001065.translation: From the scribes of the legate, with an honorable discharge. Zmaragdus, freedman and heir, had this made.
EDCS-11001065.summary: An inscription indicating a dedication from a freedman and heir who had previously served as a scribe for a legate and received an honorable discharge.

EDCS-11001066.text_edition: \n Fideliae Verulae Prudentius Reverens obtio sic signiferorum coniugi incomparabili ac dulcissimae quae vixit annis XXXI mensibus III diebus XIII faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001066.translation: For Fidelia Verula, his incomparable and dearest wife, who lived 31 years, 3 months, and 13 days. Prudentius Reverens, an obtio and signifer, had this made.
EDCS-11001066.summary: A tombstone erected by a soldier holding the rank of obtio and signifer for his wife, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-11001067.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Priminiae Comitillae quae vixit annis XX cives sic Mediomatrica Maternius Nemausus strator consularis et Lucius Lucinus mensor frumenti numeri \n
EDCS-11001067.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. For Priminia Comitilla, who lived 20 years. As citizens of Mediomatrica, Maternius Nemausus, strator of the consul, and Lucius Lucinus, grain measurer of the numerical unit, [had this made].
EDCS-11001067.summary: A funerary inscription for Priminia Comitilla, aged 20, erected by two officials with civic and military roles: a strator consularis and a grain measurer.

EDCS-11001068.text_edition: \n Caius Cassius Cai filius Claudia Valens Varvaria \n
EDCS-11001068.translation: Gaius Cassius Valens Varvaria, son of Caius, of the Claudia tribe.
EDCS-11001068.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Gaius Cassius Valens Varvaria.

EDCS-11001071.text_edition: \n Lucius Livius Marci filius Camilia Atria miles legionis X \n
EDCS-11001071.translation: Lucius Livius, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, a soldier of the Tenth Legion.
EDCS-11001071.summary: This inscription records the name and military affiliation of Lucius Livius.

EDCS-11001072.text_edition: \n Lucius Valerius Luci filius Voltinia Gratus Barnaeus Luco Augusti annorum XIIX hic situs est sit tibi terra levis amici ob meritis S\n
EDCS-11001072.translation: Lucius Valerius Gratus Barnaeus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, servant of Augustus, aged 18, is buried here. May the earth lie lightly upon you. His friends [placed this] for his merits.
EDCS-11001072.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Gratus Barnaeus, a young servant of Augustus, placed by his friends, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-11001073.text_edition: \n Caius Vet stipendiorum hic est s(itus)? --- ---E \n
EDCS-11001073.translation: Gaius Vet is here, [buried?] of military pay [---] [---].
EDCS-11001073.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vet, mentioning his military pay, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001074.text_edition: \n Caius Vibius Cai filius Voltinia Luco annorum XXVI stipendiorum III hic situs est fratres posuerunt\n
EDCS-11001074.translation: Gaius Vibius Luco, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, aged 26, with 3 years of service, is buried here. His brothers placed [this].
EDCS-11001074.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Vibius Luco, who served for three years and died at the age of 26, erected by his brothers, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001075.text_edition: \n Marcus Vinicius Marci filius Voltinia Mesor Aquis Sextiis miles \n
EDCS-11001075.translation: Marcus Vinicius Mesor, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of Aquae Sextiae.
EDCS-11001075.summary: This inscription records the name and military posting of Marcus Vinicius Mesor, a soldier from Aquae Sextiae.

EDCS-11001076.text_edition: \n AR E IICIII centuria Claudi Secundi annorum stipendiorum III hic situs est heredes fecerunt et viator dic sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-11001076.translation: AR E IICIII, century of Claudius Secundus, aged [---], with 3 years of service, is buried here. The heirs had [it] made and the courier [said]: May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11001076.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a soldier from the century of Claudius Secundus, mentioning his short service, erected by his heirs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001082.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Asper.

EDCS-11001084.text_edition: \n Andes Sexti filius cives sic Raetinio eques ala Claudia annorum XXX stipendiorum V hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001084.translation: Andes, son of Sextus, citizen, of the Raetini, an equestrian of the Claudia ala, aged 30, with 5 years of service, is buried here. The heir took care to have [it] made.
EDCS-11001084.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Andes, an equestrian soldier serving in the Claudia ala, who died at age 30 after 5 years of service, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001085.text_edition: \n Iulius Ingen<u=I>us Massae filius cives sic Helvetius missicius ex ala <I=T> Flaviae hic situs est heres faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11001085.translation: Iulius Ingenuus, son of Massa, citizen, of the Helvetii, a recalled soldier from the I Flaviae ala, is buried here. The heir took care to have [it] made.
EDCS-11001085.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulius Ingenuus, a soldier recalled from the I Flaviae ala, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001086.text_edition: \n Annauso Sedavonis filius cives sic Betasius eques alae II Flaviae \n
EDCS-11001086.translation: Annaus, son of Sedavonis, a citizen, also called Betasius, an equestrian of the II Flaviae ala.
EDCS-11001086.summary: This is an epitaph for a Roman equestrian soldier named Annaus Betasius, serving in the II Flaviae ala, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11001087.text_edition: \n Rufus Coutusvati filius natione Helvetius eques alae Hispanae stipendiorum XIIX annorum XXXVI heres posuit hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001087.translation: Rufus, son of Coutusvatus, a Helvetian by nation, an equestrian of the Hispana ala, with 18 years of service and 36 years of age, his heir placed this; he rests here.
EDCS-11001087.summary: This funerary inscription records Rufus, a Helvetian equestrian in the Hispana ala, who died at age 36 after 18 years of service; his heir erected the monument.

EDCS-11001089.text_edition: \n Sequentiae Faustinae coniugi sanctissimae et dulcissimae quae vixit annos XXXVII menses IIII sarcophagum iussu ipseius sic Flavius Flavianus Aventinus decurio alae Indianae coniugi incomparabili faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001089.translation: Flavius Flavianus Aventinus, a decurion of the Indiana ala, had this sarcophagus made by order of his most holy and sweetest wife, who lived 37 years and 4 months, for his incomparable wife.
EDCS-11001089.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Flavius Flavianus Aventinus for his wife, who died at the age of 37 years and 4 months, and ordered the sarcophagus before her death.

EDCS-11001090.text_edition: \n Caius Romanius eques alae Noricorum Claudia Capito Celeia annorum XL stipendiorum XIX hic situs est heres ex testamento faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001090.translation: Caius Romanius, an equestrian of the Noricorum ala, Claudia Capito Celeia, aged 40, with 19 years of service, rests here; his heir had this made according to the will.
EDCS-11001090.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Romanius, an equestrian of the Noricorum ala, who died at age 40 after 19 years of service; his heir fulfilled his testament.

EDCS-11001092.text_edition: \n Adbogius Coinagi filius natione Petrucorius eques alae Rusonis annorum XXIIX stipendiorum X hic situs est ex testamento libertus fecit\n
EDCS-11001092.translation: Adbogius, son of Coinagus, a Petrucorian by nation, an equestrian of the Rusonis ala, aged 28, with 10 years of service, rests here; his freedman made this according to the will.
EDCS-11001092.summary: This funerary inscription records Adbogius, a Petrucorian equestrian in the Rusonis ala, who died at age 28 after 10 years of service; his freedman erected the monument as per his will.

EDCS-11001093.text_edition: \n Iuliae Privatae sive Florentiae coniugi inconparabili sic Ianuarius Potens decurio alae I Scubulorum signifer consularis dulcissimae ob merita eius faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001093.translation: Ianuarius Potens, a decurion of the I Scubulorum ala and a signifer consularis, had this made for his incomparable and sweetest wife, Iulia Privata, also called Florentia, because of her merits.
EDCS-11001093.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Ianuarius Potens, a decurion and signifer, for his wife Iulia Privata, also known as Florentia, in recognition of her virtues.

EDCS-11001094.translation: Cantaber, son of Virotus, of the TR [tribe].
EDCS-11001094.summary: This is a fragmented inscription identifying Cantaber, son of Virotus, and noting his tribal affiliation as TR.

EDCS-11001095.translation: Togitius, son of Solimarus, from Lingauster.
EDCS-11001095.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Togitius, son of Solimarus, and his place of origin or ethnicity as Lingauster.

EDCS-11001097.text_edition: \n Freioverus Veransati filius cives sic Tunger eques ex cohorte I Asturum annorum XL stipendiorum XXII hic situs est testamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001097.translation: Freioverus, son of Veransatus, a citizen, also called Tunger, an equestrian of the I Asturum cohort, aged 40, with 22 years of service, rests here; he ordered this made by his will and his heir had it made.
EDCS-11001097.summary: This funerary inscription records Freioverus, a Tungrian equestrian in the I Asturum cohort, who died at age 40 after 22 years of service; he dictated his will for the monument, and his heir executed it.

EDCS-11001098.text_edition: \n Ogrigenus Pintili filius ex cohorte Aesturerum sic et Callaecorum annorum XXIX stipendiorum IX heres posuit\n
EDCS-11001098.translation: Ogrigenus, son of Pintilus, from the Aesturerum and Callaecorum cohort, aged 29, with 9 years of service, his heir placed this.
EDCS-11001098.summary: This funerary inscription records Ogrigenus, son of Pintilus, who served in the Aesturerum and Callaecorum cohort, dying at age 29 after 9 years of service; his heir erected the monument.

EDCS-11001099.text_edition: \n Aprilis Soli filius |(centurio) cohortis <I> Belgicae natione Lingauster nnorum XXII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001099.translation: Aprilis, son of Solius, a centurion of the 1st Cohort of Belgae, of Lingauster nationality, 22 years old, lies here.
EDCS-11001099.summary: This is a tombstone for Aprilis, a centurion of the 1st Cohort of Belgae, dated by the style of the inscription.

EDCS-11001100.text_edition: \n Talanio Plassi filius Docleas sic miles ex cohorte V Dalmatarum centuria Capitonis nnrum XXXV stipendiorum VI hic situs est Ziraeus posuit sic municeps suo\n
EDCS-11001100.translation: Docleas, son of Talanio Plassius, a soldier from the 5th Cohort of Dalmatae, in the century of Capito, 35 years old, 6 years of service, lies here. Ziraeus, a fellow townsman, erected this.
EDCS-11001100.summary: This tombstone records the death of Docleas, a soldier of the 5th Cohort of Dalmatae, erected by his fellow townsman Ziraeus.

EDCS-11001101.text_edition: \n Caeus Haneli filius mhiles ex cohorte I Itura<e=I>orum annorum L stipendiorum XIX hic situs est Iamlicus frater fecit \n
EDCS-11001101.translation: Caeus, son of Hanelius, a soldier from the 1st Cohort of Ituraeans, 50 years old, 19 years of service, lies here. His brother Iamlicus made this.
EDCS-11001101.summary: This tombstone records the death of Caeus, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Ituraeans, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11001102.text_edition: \n Monimus Ierombali filius miles cohortis I Ituraeorum nnorum L stipendiorum XXI hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001102.translation: Monimus, son of Ierombalus, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Ituraeans, 50 years old, 21 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001102.summary: This tombstone records the death of Monimus, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Ituraeans.

EDCS-11001103.text_edition: \n Sibbaeus Eronis filius tubicen ex cohorte I Ituraeorum miles nnorum XXIV stipendiorum VIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001103.translation: Sibbaeus, son of Eronis, a trumpeter and soldier from the 1st Cohort of Ituraeans, 24 years old, 8 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001103.summary: This tombstone records the death of Sibbaeus, a trumpeter and soldier of the 1st Cohort of Ituraeans.

EDCS-11001104.text_edition: \n Caius Vinicarius Luci filius cohortis I Yturaiorum sic nnum XXXVII stipendiorum IIII Lucius Vinicarius frater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001104.translation: Caius Vinicarius, son of Lucius, of the 1st Cohort of Yturai, 37 years old, 4 years of service. Lucius Vinicarius, his brother, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11001104.summary: This tombstone records the death of Caius Vinicarius, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Yturai, arranged by his brother.

EDCS-11001106.text_edition: \n Reburrus Coroturetis filius miles cohortis I Lucensium Hispanorum annorum <L=I>III stipendiorum XXIIII hic situs est heres ex testamento faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11001106.translation: Reburrus, son of Coroturetis, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Lucenses Hispani, 63 years old, 24 years of service, lies here. The heir arranged for this to be made according to the will.
EDCS-11001106.summary: This tombstone records the death of Reburrus, a soldier of the 1st Cohort of Lucenses Hispani, with the monument erected by the heir as stipulated in the will.

EDCS-11001108.text_edition: \n Attio Lani filius Montanus nnum XLV miles cohortis Ra<e=I>torum stipendiorum XIX hic situs est \n
EDCS-11001108.translation: Montanus, son of Attius Lani, 45 years old, a soldier of the Raetorian Cohort, 19 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001108.summary: This tombstone records the death of Montanus, a soldier of the Raetorian Cohort.

EDCS-11001109.text_edition: \n Cuses Sugentis filius Reguscus ex cohorte Raetorum et Vindelicorum nnum XL stipendiorum XX hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001109.translation: Reguscus, son of Cuses Sugentis, from the Cohort of Raetorum et Vindelicorum, 40 years old, 20 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001109.summary: This tombstone records the death of Reguscus, a soldier from the Cohort of Raetorum et Vindelicorum.

EDCS-11001110.text_edition: \n sese Lenulae filius Dansala miles ex cohorte IIII Thracum nnorum XXXI stipendiorum XII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001110.translation: Dansala, son of sese Lenulae, a soldier from the 4th Cohort of Thracians, 31 years old, 12 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001110.summary: This tombstone records the death of Dansala, a soldier of the 4th Cohort of Thracians.

EDCS-11001111.text_edition: \n Caius Tutius Mani filius Dansala eques ex cohorte IIII T<hr=RH>acum annorum XXXV stipendiorum X hic situs est posuit Bitus Staci filius ex testamento \n
EDCS-11001111.translation: Gaius Tutius Dansala, son of Mani, an equestrian soldier from the 4th Cohort of Thracians, aged 35, with 10 years of service, lies here; his heir Bitus, son of Staci, had this set up according to the will.
EDCS-11001111.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Tutius Dansala, an equestrian soldier, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001113.text_edition: \n Petronius Disacentus Dentubrisae filius eques turma Longini ex cohorte VI Thracum nnorum XX stipendiorum V hic situs est heres posuit\n
EDCS-11001113.translation: Petronius Disacentus, son of Dentubrisae, an equestrian soldier of the troop of Longinus from the 6th Cohort of Thracians, aged 20, with 5 years of service, lies here; his heir had this set up.
EDCS-11001113.summary: This is a tombstone for Petronius Disacentus, an equestrian soldier, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001115.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Togio Statuto militi numeri exploratorum Divitiensium Antoninianorum stipendiorum XVIIII Togia Faventina soror et heres fratri carissimo faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001115.translation: To the departed spirits. Togia Faventina, his sister and heir, took care to have this made for her dearest brother, Togius Statutus, a soldier of the numerical scouts of the Divitienses Antoniniani, with 19 years of service.
EDCS-11001115.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Togius Statutus, a soldier, commissioned by his sister and heir.

EDCS-11001116.text_edition: \n Norbania Saturnina Norbani Abroni veterani liberta annorum XL hic sita est Flaccilla filia in statum impendio? suo restituit\n
EDCS-11001116.translation: Norbania Saturnina, freedwoman of Norbanus Abronius, a veteran, aged 40, lies here; Flaccilla, her daughter, restored this in its former state at her own expense.
EDCS-11001116.summary: This is a tombstone for Norbania Saturnina, a freedwoman, restored by her daughter.

EDCS-11001117.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Titus Aurelius Auli filius Secundus missus honesta missione ex custode armorum vixit \n
EDCS-11001117.translation: To the departed spirits. Titus Aurelius Secundus, son of Aulus, who was honorably discharged from the post of armor keeper, lived [here].
EDCS-11001117.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Titus Aurelius Secundus, who received an honorable discharge as armor keeper.

EDCS-11001121.translation: The century of Sabinus Fers Octiumei.
EDCS-11001121.summary: This inscription likely refers to a military unit or a land division.

EDCS-11001122.translation: The century of Lucius Semtius Prionimus.
EDCS-11001122.summary: This inscription likely refers to a military unit or a land division.

EDCS-11001123.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Simplicio IIIIIIviro Augustali civitatis Ulpiae Mattiacorum pragmatico Crescentinia Regina ob merita eius faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001123.translation: Crescentinia Regina had this made for Gaius Julius Simplicio, a magistrate of the highest rank in the community of Ulpia Mattiacorum and an official administrator, because of his merits.
EDCS-11001123.summary: This is a dedication honoring Gaius Julius Simplicio, a prominent official, likely by a woman named Crescentinia Regina.

EDCS-11001124.text_edition: \n decurio civitatis Mattiacorum Iulio Amatori filio infanti dulcissimo qui vixit annum sic aetatis VIII dies XIIII faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001124.translation: The decurion of the community of Mattiacorum had this made for his sweetest infant son, Julius Amator, who lived for 8 years and 14 days.
EDCS-11001124.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a child, Julius Amator, commissioned by his father who was a decurion.

EDCS-11001125.text_edition: \n Bononiae quae vixit annis II mensibus II dies XVI Novellius Festus decurio civitatis Mattiacorum faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001125.translation: Novellius Festus, a decurion of the community of Mattiacorum, had this made for Bononia, who lived for 2 years, 2 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-11001125.summary: This is a funerary dedication for a child, Bononia, commissioned by her father who was a decurion.

EDCS-11001126.text_edition: \n Lucio Sextio Pervvinco decurioni civitatis Auderiensium causidico Acceptia Aerepta sic coniugi sanctissimo faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001126.translation: To Lucius Sextius Pervincus, councilor of the Auderensian tribe, advocate, Acceptia Aerepta had this made for her most devoted husband.
EDCS-11001126.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a wife for her husband, who was a councilor and advocate, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-11001127.text_edition: \n Cai Paterni Postumini decurionis civitatis Taunensium viri sacerdotal<l=S>is pragmatici Paternia Honorata fili<a=E> et heres per suos parentes faciendum curavit \n
EDCS-11001127.translation: Paterniana Honorata, daughter and heir of the councilor of the Taunensian tribe, Caius Paternus Postuminus, a man of priestly rank and a legal expert, had this made for her parents.
EDCS-11001127.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a daughter and heir for her parents, one of whom was a councilor and priest, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001128.text_edition: \n Pervincius Stabilis collegio fabrorum donum dedit decuria secunda\n
EDCS-11001128.translation: Pervincius Stabilis gave this gift to the guild of artisans, from the second turma.
EDCS-11001128.summary: This inscription records a dedication by an individual, Pervincius Stabilis, to a guild of artisans, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001129.translation: Lucius Quinctius had this made for his brother, [Caec]ilius(?) Metellus Baiulus.
EDCS-11001129.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a brother for his sibling, with a partial restoration of names, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001130.text_edition: \n Blussus Atusiri filius nauta annorum LXXV hic situs est Menimane Brigionis filia annorum uxsor! viva sibi fecit Satto verna annorum hic situs est Primus filius parentibus pro pietate posuit Blussus Atusiri filius nauta annorum LXXV hic situs est Menimane Brigionis filia annorum uxsor sic viva sibi fecit Primus filius parentibus pro pietate posuit\n
EDCS-11001130.translation: Blussus, son of Atusir, a sailor, aged 75, is buried here. Menimane, daughter of Brigio, his wife, aged [?], had this made for herself while alive. Satto, a slave, aged [?], is buried here. Primus, his son, erected this for his parents out of dutifulness. Blussus, son of Atusir, a sailor, aged 75, is buried here. Menimane, daughter of Brigio, his wife, had this made for herself while alive. Primus, his son, erected this for his parents out of dutifulness.
EDCS-11001130.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription for multiple individuals, including a sailor, his wife, a slave, and a son who erected a monument for his parents, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001133.text_edition: \n Iucundus Marci Terenti libertus pecuarius praeteriens quicumque legis consiste viator et vide quam indigne raptus inane querar vivere non potui plures XXX per annos nam erupuit sic servos sic mihi vitam et ipse praecipitem sesse sic deiecit in amnem apstulit sic huic Moenus quod domino eripuit patronus de suo posuit\n
EDCS-11001133.translation: Iucundus, freedman of Marcus Terentius, a cattle dealer, passes by. Whoever you are, traveler, stop and see how unjustly I was snatched away. Alas, I could not live more than 30 years, for like a slave, life itself threw me headlong into the river. Moenus took what belonged to his master and erected this from his own means. Thus, the patron placed [this] for the one who took from his master.
EDCS-11001133.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman, Iucundus, who died tragically, with a complex narrative involving a patron and a slave, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001134.text_edition: \n R tabulario da coniux Aureliae et Procla filiae et heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001134.translation: R. The husband, for Aurelia and Procla, his daughters and heirs, had this made.
EDCS-11001134.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a husband for his daughters and heirs, with a partially restored inscription, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001135.translation: Veratius(?) the Young / Superstius Secundus Primanius / Primitivus Sabinius Desideratus Saplutius E[---] / [---]as Vinnonia / Iattusa Livia Altusilla Pollionia / Ursula Placidia / Lucilla Sennau[---] / Matt[---]
EDCS-11001135.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several names, likely representing individuals honored or buried together, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001136.translation: [---]NVII[---] / S[---]PFV[---]IVSI / VMEI(?) I() L[---] Senuri(?) / L[---]RNTO Crescent() C[---] / S[---]CVA(?) Gemello V[---] / P[---]NTOIN[---]SI DDA[---]X BE[---] / CER ECTV [---] Secundi PI[---] / Secundin(i?) Calatori M[---] / CVIVDI(?) Saturnin[---] / [---]ETV[---]ONIV[---] / [---]TV[---]
EDCS-11001136.summary: This is a highly fragmentary inscription containing what appear to be names and possibly phrases, making its purpose and date difficult to determine without further context.

EDCS-11001137.summary: This is a very brief inscription containing a personal name, possibly an epitaph or a dedication, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001138.text_edition: \n Aquilinius sor et ia Ammosa patri carissimo et fratri faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001138.translation: Aquilinius and his sister Ammosa had this made for their dearest father and brother.
EDCS-11001138.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Aquilinius and his sister Ammosa for their father and brother.

EDCS-11001139.text_edition: \n Attianiae Ursae Domitius Salvianus coniunx et Domitii Ursus et Salvia filii faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001139.translation: Domitius Salvianus, her husband, and their children Domitius Ursus and Salvia had this made for Attianiae Ursa.
EDCS-11001139.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Domitius Salvianus and his children for Attianiae Ursa.

EDCS-11001140.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Attilliae Runae matri Respectius Servandus miles pecuarius le<g=C>(ionis) XXII et Respectius RE Respectinus filius et Servandia Maximina et Servandius Severinus nepotes faciendum curaverunt \n
EDCS-11001140.translation: For Attillia Runa, mother. Respectius Servandus, a soldier in the 22nd pecuary unit, and his son Respectius RE Respectinus, and his grandchildren Servandia Maximina and Servandius Severinus had this made.
EDCS-11001140.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Respectius Servandus and his descendants for Attillia Runa.

EDCS-11001141.text_edition: \n Aureliae Constantinae sive Palladiae infanti innocentissimae quae vixit annis XII mensibus XI\n
EDCS-11001141.translation: For Aurelia Constantina, also known as Palladia, a most innocent infant who lived 12 years and 11 months.
EDCS-11001141.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Aurelia Constantina (or Palladia), who died at the age of 12 years and 11 months.

EDCS-11001142.text_edition: \n assia coniugi sanctissimo et sibi vivi fecerunt\n
EDCS-11001142.translation: For Assia, my most virtuous wife, and for myself, made while alive.
EDCS-11001142.summary: This funerary monument was jointly commissioned by Assia and her husband for themselves during their lifetime.

EDCS-11001145.text_edition: \n Lucius Canuleius Luci filius Successus annorum V mensium III dierum XXIII Lucius Canuleius Primigenius filio et sibi vivos sic fecit\n
EDCS-11001145.translation: Lucius Canuleius Successus, son of Lucius, aged 5 years, 3 months, and 23 days. Lucius Canuleius Primigenius made this for his son and himself while alive.
EDCS-11001145.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Lucius Canuleius Primigenius for his young son Lucius Canuleius Successus and himself.

EDCS-11001146.text_edition: \n Digni Ursi et Gratiae Hibernalis Hegont filiae et Ursio sic Hibernalis et Ursiae Urssulae ffiliorum eorum Sedatius Gratus parentibus pientissimis faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001146.translation: For the worthy children of Ursius and Gratia Hibernalis, Hegont daughter, and Ursio Hibernalis and Ursia Urssula. Sedatius Gratus had this made for his most devoted parents.
EDCS-11001146.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Sedatius Gratus for his parents, Ursius and Gratia Hibernalis, and their children.

EDCS-11001147.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gai natione Rhodii Athenodorus pater fecit Legio XX\n
EDCS-11001147.translation: To the Divine Manes. Athenodorus, father, from Rhodes by nation, made [this] for Legio XX.
EDCS-11001147.summary: This monument was dedicated by Athenodorus, likely a soldier or official associated with Legio XX, to the Divine Manes.

EDCS-11001148.text_edition: \n Caius Gavius Cai libertus Celer nnorum XXI hic situs est fidus vixsisti sic sine crimine Gavi hoc tibi pro meritis sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-11001148.translation: Caius Gavius Celer, freedman of Caius, aged 21 years, is buried here. You lived faithfully, without fault. May the earth be light upon you, Gavi, in return for your merits.
EDCS-11001148.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Caius Gavius Celer, a freedman, praising his virtuous life and wishing him a light earth.

EDCS-11001149.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Gamuxpero Andangi Titus filius faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001149.translation: To the Divine Manes. Titus, son of Andangus, had this made for Gamuxper.
EDCS-11001149.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Titus for Gamuxper.

EDCS-11001150.translation: To the departed spirits. Herennianus saw to the making [of this monument] for Honorata, wife of Vetus, a most dutiful woman.
EDCS-11001150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Honorata, commissioned by Herennianus, likely a relative.

EDCS-11001151.text_edition: \n Cirrata Iulia Annai sic filia natione Nervia annorum XXVIII inmunis sic beneficio Aproni hic sita est Rufus Iulius pro pietate posuit\n
EDCS-11001151.translation: Cirrata Iulia, daughter of Annaius, of the Nervian tribe, aged 28, free from duties, rests here by the favor of Apronius. Rufus Iulius erected [this] for her out of filial devotion.
EDCS-11001151.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cirrata Iulia, a 28-year-old Nervian woman, erected by Rufus Iulius.

EDCS-11001152.text_edition: \n Lychnis Quinti Epidi ancilla annucula sic et menses IIII hic sita est Felixs sic posuit\n
EDCS-11001152.translation: Lychnis, a young slave girl of Quintus Epidius, aged one year and four months, rests here. Felix erected [this].
EDCS-11001152.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lychnis, a young slave girl of Quintus Epidius, erected by Felix.

EDCS-11001153.text_edition: \n Messiae Maximae iuveni infelicissimae inmatura morte praereptae quae quae vixit annos XXVI Primitivius Senilianus filius et Messius Maxumus sic frater faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001153.translation: For Messia Maxima, a very unhappy young woman, snatched away by an untimely death, who lived 26 years. Her son Primitivius Senilianus and her brother Messius Maxumus saw to the making [of this monument].
EDCS-11001153.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Messia Maxima, who died at age 26, commissioned by her son and brother.

EDCS-11001155.text_edition: \n Mogetiae Quintinae matronae sanctissimae Quintinius Fruendus libertus et heres patronae optimae in se pietatis et reverentiae faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001155.translation: Quintinius Fruendus, freedman and heir, saw to the making [of this monument] for Mogetia Quintina, a most holy matron, his most excellent patroness, out of devotion and reverence towards her.
EDCS-11001155.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mogetia Quintina, a matron, commissioned by her freedman and heir, Quintinius Fruendus.

EDCS-11001156.text_edition: \n nia Nigrina mater filiae karissimae faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001156.translation: For his dearest daughter, [his wife] Nia Nigrina saw to the making [of this monument].
EDCS-11001156.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed daughter, commissioned by her mother Nia Nigrina.

EDCS-11001157.text_edition: \n Peregrinio Heliodoro consummatae peritiae medico et mirae pietatis iuveni Cominia Faustina mater infelicissima faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001157.translation: Cominia Faustina, a most unhappy mother, saw to the making [of this monument] for Peregrinius Heliodorus, a physician of consummate skill and a remarkably devoted young man.
EDCS-11001157.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Peregrinius Heliodorus, a skilled physician, commissioned by his grieving mother, Cominia Faustina.

EDCS-11001158.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucio Peregrinio Iustino filio Soliti\n
EDCS-11001158.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Peregrinius Iustinus, [her] son. Solitus [erected this].
EDCS-11001158.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Peregrinius Iustinus, erected by his mother Solitus.

EDCS-11001159.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae Pescennia Roma quae vixit mensibus VII Marcus Antonius \n
EDCS-11001159.translation: To a good memory. Pescennia Roma, who lived 7 months. Marcus Antonius [erected this].
EDCS-11001159.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pescennia Roma, who lived only 7 months, erected by Marcus Antonius.

EDCS-11001160.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Placidius aius SAR cent(urio legionis decimae Mes fecit et filiI \n
EDCS-11001160.translation: To the departed spirits. Placidius, centurion of the tenth legion, made [this] for himself and his sons.
EDCS-11001160.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Placidius, a centurion of the tenth legion, and his sons.

EDCS-11001161.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Poppius Afro...
EDCS-11001161.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Poppius Afro.

EDCS-11001163.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a person named Primitiva, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-11001164.text_edition: \n Pusa Trougilli filius annorum CXX hic situs est Prisca Pusae filia annorum XXX hic sita est Vinda Ateegniomari filia hic sita futura est annorum LXXX\n
EDCS-11001164.translation: Pusa, son of Trougillus, 120 years old, is buried here. Prisca, daughter of Pusa, 30 years old, is buried here. Vinda, daughter of Ateegniomarus, 80 years old, will be buried here.
EDCS-11001164.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial of Pusa and Prisca, with a future burial planned for Vinda, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001165.text_edition: \n Memoriae aeternitatis Quintiae Quintinae Festii Victor et Quintinus filii matri dulcissimae faciundum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001165.translation: For eternal memory. Quintius Festius Victor and Quintinus, sons, had this made for their dearest mother.
EDCS-11001165.summary: This funerary inscription records that sons Quintius Festius Victor and Quintinus commissioned a monument for their mother, Quintia Quintina.

EDCS-11001166.translation: Saturninus... parents(?) most unfortunate had this made.
EDCS-11001166.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription where unfortunate parents commissioned a monument, possibly for their child.

EDCS-11001167.text_edition: \n Caius Seccius Cai libertus Corinthus nnorum XXX hic intus situs est patronus posuit\n
EDCS-11001167.translation: Gaius Seccius Corinthus, freedman of Gaius, 30 years old, is buried inside here. His patron erected this.
EDCS-11001167.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Gaius Seccius Corinthus, a freedman, and states that his patron erected the monument.

EDCS-11001168.text_edition: \n Caius Seccius Cai libertus Lesbius annorum XX hic situs est cum mihi prima novos spargebat flore iuventus heu miser aetatis praemia nulla <t=I>uli bis denis mihi mors annis accessit iniqua ingemit et damno Seccius ille gravi di meliora precor pro nostro munera casu sentiat et plures possit habere suos hic tumulum titulumque mihi donavit honori et proprium nomen d<e=I>stinat in lacr<i=V>mas bene merenti \n
EDCS-11001168.translation: Gaius Seccius Lesbius, freedman of Gaius, 20 years old, is buried here. When my youth was just beginning to flourish, alas, death came to me at the age of 20, with no rewards. May that unfortunate Seccius lament with such grief; may the gods grant better things. May he experience rewards for our fate and be able to have more of his own. He gave this tomb and inscription to me in honor and destined my own name for the tears of one who deserved well.
EDCS-11001168.summary: This is a poetic funerary inscription for Gaius Seccius Lesbius, a freedman, who died at the age of 20, lamenting his short life and the patron's grief and memorialization.

EDCS-11001169.text_edition: \n Caius Seccius Cai libertus Verecundus nnorum XXV hic situs est patronus pro meritis posuit Romanus Cai Secci servus nnrum XII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001169.translation: Gaius Seccius Verecundus, freedman of Gaius, 25 years old, is buried here. His patron erected this for his merits. Romanus, slave of Gaius Seccius, 12 years old, is buried here.
EDCS-11001169.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of two individuals, Gaius Seccius Verecundus and Romanus, a slave, with their patron or owner indicated.

EDCS-11001170.translation: ...dinia, for daughter Secundi... and heirs(?) according to the will
EDCS-11001170.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription indicating a bequest or memorial for a daughter named Secundina, to be carried out by heirs according to a will.

EDCS-11001171.translation: ... for dearest mother. Laurentia(?) and Felicianus, her sons, had this made.
