EDCS-11001171.summary: This funerary inscription records that Laurentia(?) and Felicianus had a monument made for their dearest mother, Sentiia Laurea.

EDCS-11001172.translation: Publius Sepetumius Fronto, son of Lucius, aged 25. [---] DCT[
EDCS-11001172.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Publius Sepetumius Fronto, who died at the age of 25, with the surviving text indicating his name and age.

EDCS-11001173.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that begins with the name Publius Septimius, likely for a funerary monument.

EDCS-11001174.translation: To the departed spirits. Severus [---] Fabriceius [
EDCS-11001174.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription that invokes the 'Dis Manibus' (departed spirits) and mentions the names Severus and Fabriceius.

EDCS-11001175.translation: Speratius Hermodorus and Iuliana, parents of the boy Lucius Speratus Desideratus, whose outstanding hope and incomparable devotion they judged wrongly because of the Fates, placed this [monument] while surviving him.
EDCS-11001175.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by parents for their deceased son, Lucius Speratus Desideratus, lamenting his premature death due to fate.

EDCS-11001176.translation: To the departed spirits. It is necessary for Telesphora and her husband, her parents, to grieve for their dearest daughter, that you would not have been [born] if the Fates had returned you so pleasingly from where you were given to us. She lived for half a year and eight days. She bloomed like a rose at once and immediately perished.
EDCS-11001176.summary: This is a touching funerary inscription from parents to their infant daughter Telesphora, lamenting her short life of only six months and eight days.

EDCS-11001177.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Telesphoris et maritus eius parentes filiae dulcissimae\n
EDCS-11001177.translation: To the departed spirits. Telesphora and her husband, her parents.
EDCS-11001177.summary: This is a funerary inscription that begins with the invocation 'Dis Manibus' and identifies the dedicants as parents mourning their daughter Telesphora.

EDCS-11001178.translation: To the departed spirits. Tertinius Suitulus and Avvia [
EDCS-11001178.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription that begins with the invocation 'Dis Manibus' and names Tertinius Suitulus and Avvia.

EDCS-11001179.translation: [---]MAC[---]. His mother Ammia [---] and his father Titinius Castus.
EDCS-11001179.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription where the mother, Titinia Ammia, and father, Titinius Castus, are named as dedicants.

EDCS-11001180.translation: Turrania Suadulla, freedwoman of Titus, aged 25. Urbana, aged 20. They lie here. Lucilius [erected this] for his sisters (?).
EDCS-11001180.summary: This inscription records the burial of two women, Turrania Suadulla and Urbana, with Lucilius as the likely dedicator for his sisters.

EDCS-11001181.translation: [To the departed spirits?] Valentinia Avita, a praiseworthy matron and citizen of Trier. Vera and Honorata, daughters and heirs, took care to have this made for their most dutiful mother.
EDCS-11001181.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Valentinia Avita, a respected woman of Trier, by her daughters and heirs, Vera and Honorata.

EDCS-11001182.translation: Servandus, freedman of Lucius, Caius, and Sextius Valerius, aged 20, is buried here; his patrons placed him here for his merits. "Slavery, you were never unkind to me; death took away my freedom, unjust."
EDCS-11001182.summary: This is a tombstone for a freedman named Servandus, erected by his patrons.

EDCS-11001183.translation: To Veterius, son of Lucius, Sammonius, [---]. His sister (?) and heir Lamma (?) placed this.
EDCS-11001183.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely for Veterius, with a dedication from his sister and heir, possibly dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001184.translation: Vettia Tyrannis lived 26 years and 9 months.
EDCS-11001184.summary: This is a tombstone for Vettia Tyrannis, recording her age at death.

EDCS-11001185.translation: To the departed spirits. To Vitalinius Gromatius, most sweet infant, who lived 10 years and 3 months. His mother Dignia Legitima had this made.
EDCS-11001185.summary: This is a tombstone for a child named Vitalinius Gromatius, erected by his mother.

EDCS-11001186.text_edition: \n Quintus Voltius Quinti filius Viator annorum XVI hic situs est mater et pater pro pietate posuere\n
EDCS-11001186.translation: Quintus Voltius Viator, son of Quintus, aged 16, is buried here; his mother and father placed this out of devotion.
EDCS-11001186.summary: This is a tombstone for a young boy named Quintus Voltius Viator, erected by his parents.

EDCS-11001187.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to mention at least one soldier and possibly family members, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001188.translation: [---]O[---], Secundus (?) and [---] Maturus, [---]amarina, [---]ia Macrina, [---] to [his/her] spouse and [---].
EDCS-11001188.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record names of individuals and a dedication to a spouse, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001189.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records the name and age of a deceased person, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001194.translation: [---] is buried here. Atticus (?) his/her husband paid for this from his own funds for [merits/his/her] merits [---].
EDCS-11001194.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone where the deceased is identified by Atticus as her husband, who paid for the monument.

EDCS-11001207.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that lists several names, likely funerary or dedicatory, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001231.summary: This inscription, likely from a tombstone, records the age of Eunus, dating from the late Roman period.

EDCS-11001241.translation: Repentinus saw to it that [this was made] as [fitting] as possible.
EDCS-11001241.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication for a monument, possibly a tomb, with Repentinus as the likely dedicator.

EDCS-11001260.summary: This very fragmentary inscription seems to refer to a centuria, possibly related to a military or land division.

EDCS-11001289.translation: In this tomb rests well-remembered Adalhari, who lived in peace for [?] years.
EDCS-11001289.summary: This epitaph records the death and peaceful life of Adalhari, likely from the post-Roman period.

EDCS-11001290.translation: On this inscription rests Audolendis, who lived in peace for 3 years, happily.
EDCS-11001290.summary: This epitaph records the short but happy life of Audolendis, who lived for 3 years in peace.

EDCS-11001291.translation: On this inscription rests Bertisindis, of good memory, who lived for 20 years. Randoaldus, who lived for thirty years, happily.
EDCS-11001291.summary: This epitaph records the lives of two individuals, Bertisindis and Randoaldus, likely from the post-Roman period.

EDCS-11001292.translation: [...] Dructacharius rests, who lived in peace for 21 years. This tomb was founded; the bones of the sepulchre rest here, and there lies buried his own citadel. It came to pass from tearful parents, their hearts of the miserable.
EDCS-11001292.summary: This funerary inscription, possibly from the post-Roman period, details the death of Dructacharius and includes a poetic and emotional dedication from his parents.

EDCS-11001293.translation: On this inscription rests Radelindis, of good memory, who lived in peace for 25 years.
EDCS-11001293.summary: This epitaph records the death of Radelindis, who lived in peace for 25 years, likely from the post-Roman period.

EDCS-11001296.translation: Here lies Florentius(?), soldier, who lived for twenty years and 6 months and 3 months.
EDCS-11001296.summary: This epitaph records the death of Florentius, identified as a soldier, and specifies his age at death.

EDCS-11001297.translation: Here rests in peace the infant Paulinus, who lived one year and 4 months minus 1 day. His father and mother placed the inscription.
EDCS-11001297.summary: This epitaph records the death of the infant Paulinus, specifying his age and noting that it was placed by his parents.

EDCS-11001298.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Nymphis Caius Spurius Lucius Novirius Camerinus optio legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis votum solvit libens laetus merito Orfito et Rufo consulibus\n
EDCS-11001298.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Nymphs, Caius Spurius Lucius Novirius Camerinus, optio of the 22nd Primigenia, pious and faithful legion, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, when Orfitus and Rufus were consuls.
EDCS-11001298.summary: A vow to Jupiter and Nymphs by a military officer of the 22nd Legion, dated to the consulship of Orfitus and Rufus.

EDCS-11001301.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Mercury, Bytytralis son of Bitu(s), a veteran of the 21st [Legion?], paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001301.summary: A dedication to Mercury by a veteran of the 21st Legion, likely honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-11001302.summary: A dedication to Mercury by an individual named Caecilius, with a partially restored name.

EDCS-11001303.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Donatus publici XX libertatis servus vilicus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001303.translation: Sacred to Mercury, Donatus, a slave from the public XXth district of liberty, the steward, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001303.summary: A vow to Mercury by a freedman steward from a public district, indicating his status and role.

EDCS-11001304.translation: To Mercury, Titus Flavius I [paid his vow].
EDCS-11001304.summary: An incomplete dedication to Mercury by Titus Flavius I.

EDCS-11001305.translation: Sacred to Mercury, Marcus Iulius Crescens, a veteran of the 22nd Primigenia, pious and faithful legion, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001305.summary: A vow to Mercury by Marcus Iulius Crescens, a veteran of the 22nd Primigenia Legion.

EDCS-11001306.translation: To Mercury, who deserved well, Titus Iulius Ingenus, a veteran of the [22nd Primigenia, Pious and Faithful] Legion, [paid his vow] willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001306.summary: A vow to Mercury by Titus Iulius Ingenus, a veteran of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, acknowledging the god's merit.

EDCS-11001307.translation: To Mercury, Lucius Iullonius Iullinus. In honor of the divine house, to Mercury, Lucius Iullonius Iullinus paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001307.summary: A bilingual dedication to Mercury, with the second part also honoring the imperial family, by Lucius Iullonius Iullinus.

EDCS-11001309.translation: To Mercury, [S]aturninus, possibly a slave of Domitianus, paid his vow.
EDCS-11001309.summary: A vow to Mercury by Saturninus, possibly a slave, with a partially restored name and affiliation.

EDCS-11001310.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the god Mercury, Lucius Senilius Decmanus, quaestor, curator of Roman citizens who manage goods for merchants of Mogontiacum, a citizen of Taunus, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly, when Saturninus and Gallus were consuls.
EDCS-11001310.summary: A dedication to Mercury and the imperial family by Lucius Senilius Decmanus, a prominent merchant and official from Taunus, dated to the consulship of Saturninus and Gallus.

EDCS-11001320.translation: Lucius Antestius Tertius Cremona, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, soldier of the legion, aged 50 years, [with 28] years of service.
EDCS-11001320.summary: A tombstone for Lucius Antestius Tertius Cremona, a soldier, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001322.translation: Gaius Julius Niger, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Carcassonne, soldier of the Second Legion, aged 45 years, 17 years of service, lies here. Stranger, approach, and with a few verses understand his eternal destiny. His home will be here; within this tomb he will be enclosed. Here Julius himself, here his ashes, made from flesh and bone. When life flourished pleasantly for me, the final limit came from fate. The 45th year was when the bitter day arrived for me. Here I am now forced to cross the Stygian marshes; my fate holds me in eternal abodes. I remember being born in Gaul, with dear parents, and as a soldier I bravely bore arms. Cruel Gaul granted me funeral rites and fire, and my limbs are pressed down by earth and ash. [He was born?] son, soldier of the Second Legion [---]. He is the heir.
EDCS-11001322.summary: An epitaph for Gaius Julius Niger, a soldier of the Second Legion, who died at the age of 45, including a lengthy poetic lament for his death and a mention of his heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001323.translation: Gaius Iunius Concordia, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe.
EDCS-11001323.summary: An incomplete funerary inscription naming Gaius Iunius Concordia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001324.translation: Marcus Petronius Acele, son of Gaius, of the Claudia tribe, soldier of the Fourteenth Gemina Legion, aged 20 years, 5 years of service, lies here. Gaius Petronius, his brother, piously had this made.
EDCS-11001324.summary: A tombstone erected by Gaius Petronius for his brother Marcus Petronius Acele, a soldier of the Fourteenth Gemina Legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001326.translation: Titus Ennius Amantius, freedman of Titus, aged 70 years, and Ennius, son of Titus, aged 35 years, lie here.
EDCS-11001326.summary: A tombstone recording the burial of two individuals, Titus Ennius Amantius and Ennius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001327.translation: Marcus Maximus Victor, junior, most sweet infant, who lived 1 year, 2 months, and 17 days. His father and mother had this made.
EDCS-11001327.summary: A tombstone for an infant named Marcus Maximus Victor, erected by his parents, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001329.text_edition: \n Curtilia Prepusa Marti Loucetio votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11001329.translation: Curtilia Prepusa willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Mars Loucetius.
EDCS-11001329.summary: A votive inscription recording Curtilia Prepusa fulfilling a vow to the god Mars Loucetius, likely from a provincial Roman context.

EDCS-11001330.text_edition: \n Marti Leucetio Titus Satrius Censorinus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001330.translation: Titus Satrius Censorinus willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Leucetius.
EDCS-11001330.summary: A votive inscription recording Titus Satrius Censorinus fulfilling a vow to the god Mars Leucetius, likely from a provincial Roman context.

EDCS-11001331.translation: In honor of the Divine House, Lucius Indutius Victor willingly, happily, and deservedly dedicated a temple to the god Mercury in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11001331.summary: A dedication of a temple to Mercury by Lucius Indutius Victor, honoring the imperial family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001332.translation: Atinius, son of Septimius, of the Romilia tribe, from Ateste, soldier of the Second Legion [Primigenia?], aged 35 years, [with X] years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001332.summary: A tombstone for Atinius, a soldier of the Second Legion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001334.translation: Capito, son of Augur, a veteran from the II Cohort of Raeti, aged 52. His heir arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11001334.summary: A funerary epitaph for Capito, a veteran of the II Cohort of Raeti, arranged by his heir.

EDCS-11001335.translation: Capito, freedman of Arrius, an Argentinian (money-changer) from Pannonia, aged 35. He lies here. Diomedes, slave of Arrius, erected this.
EDCS-11001335.summary: A funerary epitaph for Capito, a freedman and money-changer from Pannonia, erected by a slave.

EDCS-11001336.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo ceterisque dis deabusque Securius Carantus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis II in suo posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001336.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to all the gods and goddesses. Securius Carantus, a soldier of the XXII Legion Primigenia, pious and loyal, erected this in his own plot, willingly, gladly, deservedly.
EDCS-11001336.summary: A dedication to Jupiter and other deities by Securius Carantus, a soldier of the XXII Legion Primigenia.

EDCS-11001337.text_edition: \n Marti et Victoriae in honorem domus divinae Lucius Bittius Paulinus anularius voto suscepto posuit\n
EDCS-11001337.translation: To Mars and Victory, in honor of the divine house. Lucius Bittius Paulinus, a ring-maker, erected this in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11001337.summary: A dedication to Mars and Victory by Lucius Bittius Paulinus, a ring-maker, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-11001339.text_edition: \n vicanis? et? hastiferis castelli Mattiacorum Aurelius Candidus cornicularius Mattiac(o)rum Gordianorum allectus inter ipsos\n
EDCS-11001339.translation: To the villagers (?) and standard-bearers (?) of the fort of Mattiaci. Aurelius Candidus, a cornicularius of the Mattiaci Gordiani, elected among them.
EDCS-11001339.summary: An inscription possibly recording the election of Aurelius Candidus among the villagers and standard-bearers of the fort of Mattiaci.

EDCS-11001342.text_edition: \n Aulus Didius Gallus Fabricius Veiento consul III XVvir sacris faciendis sodalis Augustalis sodalis Flavialis sodalis Titialis et Attica eius Nemetonae votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-11001342.translation: Aulus Didius Gallus Fabricius Veiento, consul for the third time, quindecimvir for sacred rites, member of the Augustales, member of the Flavianals, member of the Titials, and his wife Attica Nemetona, fulfilled their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001342.summary: A record of a vow fulfilled by the distinguished Roman official Aulus Didius Gallus Fabricius Veiento and his wife.

EDCS-11001343.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly naming two individuals.

EDCS-11001344.text_edition: \n Publius Flavoleius Publi filius Pollia Mutina Cordus miles legionis XIIII geminae hic situs est nnorum XLIII stipendiorum XXIII Caius Vibennius Luci filius ex testamento fecit\n
EDCS-11001344.translation: Publius Flavoleius Cordus, son of Publius, of the Pollia tribe, from Mutina. A soldier of the XIIII Gemina Legion, aged 43, with 23 years of service. Caius Vibennius, son of Lucius, made this according to the will.
EDCS-11001344.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Flavoleius Cordus, a soldier of the XIIII Gemina Legion, commissioned by Caius Vibennius in his will.

EDCS-11001345.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Primanius Primulus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis Augustaliniae Afrae coniugi dulcissimae quae vixit annos XXI menses IIII dies XXVIII et Lucania Summula mater filiae et Augustalinius Afer frater et Primania Primula filia faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001345.translation: To the Spirits of the Dead. Primanius Primulus, a centurion of the XXII Legion Primigenia, pious and loyal, arranged for this to be made for his most sweet wife Afra, who lived 21 years, 4 months, and 28 days, and for Lucania Summula, his daughter's mother, and for Augustalinius Afer, her brother, and for Primania Primula, his daughter.
EDCS-11001345.summary: A funerary monument for the wife of Primanius Primulus, a centurion, and other family members.

EDCS-11001346.text_edition: \n Marcelliniae Marcellae coniugi dilectissimae et dulcissimae sarcofagum sic iussu eius Iulius Paterninus decurio alae Indianae coniugi incomparabili faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001346.translation: For Marcellinia Marcella, his most beloved and sweetest wife, a sarcophagus, as she commanded. Iulius Paterninus, a decurion of the ala Indiana, arranged for this to be made for his incomparable wife.
EDCS-11001346.summary: A sarcophagus commissioned by Iulius Paterninus, a decurion, for his wife Marcellinia Marcella, according to her instructions.

EDCS-11001349.translation: To Lindis, daughter of Velandus and Thudelindis, who lived for 12 years in peace.
EDCS-11001349.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young girl named Lindis, who died at the age of 12.

EDCS-11001350.translation: In honor of the divine house. To the Genius of the street beyond the praetorian gate, Lucius L. Victor, a veteran of the XXII Legion, dedicated this gift, when Laetus and Cerialis were consuls.
EDCS-11001350.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a gift to the Genius of a street by a veteran of the XXII Legion during the consulship of Laetus and Cerialis.

EDCS-11001351.translation: To Hercules, Marcus Seppius Creon dedicated this gift.
EDCS-11001351.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a gift to the god Hercules by Marcus Seppius Creon.

EDCS-11001352.translation: To Juno Regina of the street to the right as one goes towards Nidum, Titus Veterius Atessas and Sextus Mascius Concessus made [this].
EDCS-11001352.summary: This inscription records the making of something by Titus Veterius Atessas and Sextus Mascius Concessus for Juno Regina of a street leading to Nidum.

EDCS-11001353.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus of the street to the right as one goes towards Nidum, the soldiers Adiutorius Sextus, Liberalius Speratus, Ammonius Secundanus, made [this] at their own expense.
EDCS-11001353.summary: This inscription records soldiers making something at their own expense for Jupiter Optimus Maximus of a street leading to Nidum.

EDCS-11001354.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Conservatori Cintugnatius Publius IIvir civitatis Taunensium in suo ut haberet restituit Attico et Praetextato consulibus\n
EDCS-11001354.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus the Preserver, Cintugnatius Publius, duovir of the community of the Taunenses, restored [this] on his own land so that he might have it, when Atticus and Praetextatus were consuls.
EDCS-11001354.summary: This is a dedication recording the restoration of something on private land to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Cintugnatius Publius, a duovir of the Taunenses, during the consulship of Atticus and Praetextatus.

EDCS-11001355.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Aquilinius Paternus decurio civitatis Mattiacorum ex voto posuit libens laetus merito dedicata Kalendis Octobribus ter et bis consulibus\n
EDCS-11001355.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Aquilinius Paternus, a decurion of the community of the Mattiaci, set this up in fulfillment of a vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly, dedicated on the Kalends of October, when three and two were consuls.
EDCS-11001355.summary: This votive inscription records the erection of a monument to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Aquilinius Paternus, a decurion of the Mattiaci, on October 1st.

EDCS-11001356.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Dubitatius Primitius ex voto in suo posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001356.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Dubitatius Primitius set this up on his own land in fulfillment of a vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001356.summary: This votive inscription records Dubitatius Primitius setting up a monument on his own land for Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina.

EDCS-11001357.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Finitius Fidelis miles numeri Ca<tth=DD>arensium in suo posuit Fusco et Dextro consulibus \n
EDCS-11001357.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Finitius Fidelis, a soldier of the cohort of the Cattharenses, set this up on his own land, when Fuscus and Dexter were consuls.
EDCS-11001357.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the Cattharenses cohort setting up a monument on his own land for Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina during the consulship of Fuscus and Dexter.

EDCS-11001358.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Caius Iustinius Favor veteranus et Desideratia Desiderata stolata femina in suo posuerunt L llibentes llaeti merito\n
EDCS-11001358.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Gaius Iustinius Favor, a veteran, and Desideratia Desiderata, a robed woman, set this up on their own land, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001358.summary: This inscription records a veteran and his wife setting up a monument on their own land for Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina.

EDCS-11001359.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Melonii Carantus et Iucundus de suo donum dederunt vico novo Meloniorum Cethego et Claro consulibus\n
EDCS-11001359.translation: In honor of the divine house, Melonii Carantus and Iucundus gave a gift of their own to Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, with Melonii Cethegus and Claritas as consuls in the new vicus of the Melonii.
EDCS-11001359.summary: This inscription records a private dedication to Jupiter and Juno by two individuals, likely local officials or patrons, for the imperial cult in the new vicus of the Melonii, dated by the consuls to the early imperial period.

EDCS-11001360.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Lucius Secundinius Favoralis IIIIIIvir Augustalis civitatis Mattiacorum in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11001360.translation: Lucius Secundinius Favoralis, one of the six priests of the Augustan cult of the Mattiaci community, set this up on his own property in honor of Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina.
EDCS-11001360.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by a local Augustalis priest of the Mattiaci, likely for the imperial cult, on his own property.

EDCS-11001361.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae X Kalendas Ianuarias Praesente et Albino consulibus Serotinius Cupitus et Cupitius Providens filius in suo fecerunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11001361.translation: Serotinius Cupitus and his son Cupitius Providens made this willingly, happily, and deservedly on their own property on the 23rd of December, with Praesens and Albinus as consuls.
EDCS-11001361.summary: This inscription records a private dedication made by two individuals on their own property, dated by the consuls to the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11001364.translation: Marcus Seppius Creon erected this by order, willingly and happily.
EDCS-11001364.summary: This inscription records a votive dedication to Mercury by Marcus Seppius Creon, who acted on orders.

EDCS-11001365.text_edition: \n Mercurium sic Domesticum sic Caius Iulius Satto -\n
EDCS-11001365.translation: Caius Julius Satto, for Mercury the Domestic god...
EDCS-11001365.summary: This very fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication to Mercury as a household god by Caius Julius Satto.

EDCS-11001366.text_edition: \n Mercurio Paternius Sanctinus immunis consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Imperatore Commodo IIII et Victorino II consulibus\n
EDCS-11001366.translation: Paternus Sanctinus, immune official of the consular province, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, with Emperor Commodus as consul for the fourth time and Victorinus as consul for the second time.
EDCS-11001366.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Mercury by Paternus Sanctinus, an immune official, dated by the consuls to 178 AD.

EDCS-11001367.translation: In honor of the divine house, Antiocus Apollinaris [dedicated] to the goddesses Nymphs...
EDCS-11001367.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication in honor of the imperial house to the Nymphs by Antiocus Apollinaris.

EDCS-11001368.translation: In honor of the divine house, Gaius Carantinius Maternus, prefect of the Aquenses, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly, [dedicating] statues and an altar to the goddesses Nymphs.
EDCS-11001368.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the Nymphs by Gaius Carantinius Maternus, prefect of the Aquenses, in honor of the imperial house, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001369.translation: Ollogabius Messor [dedicated] to the Aetui gods...
EDCS-11001369.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a dedication to the Aetui gods by Ollogabius Messor.

EDCS-11001370.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Virtuti Bellonae montem Vaticanum vetustate conlabsum sic restituerunt hastiferi civitatis Mattiacorum X Kalendas Septembres Imperatore domino nostro Maximino Au[gusto] et Africano consulibus hi quorum nomina infra scripta sunt Gaius Meddignatius Severus curator bis Lucius Levinius Quietus Titus Vitalinius Peregrinus Constantius Marcianus Crixsius sic Adnamatus Giamillius Crescens Titius Belatullus Iulius Severus Icnius Constans Statius Victor Tertinius Abrosus Marcrinius Perpetuus Atregtius sic Cupitianus Perrius Iustinus praeopt Attonius Asclepius Ursius Maturus Statutius Secundinus Servandius Senurus\n
EDCS-11001370.translation: In honor of the divine house, the hastiferi (sword-bearers) of the Mattiaci community restored the Vatican mountain, which had collapsed from age, to the goddess Virtue and Bellona. On August 23rd, with our lord Emperor Maximinus Augustus and Africanus as consuls. These are their names listed below: Gaius Meddignatius Severus, twice curator; Lucius Levinius Quietus; Titus Vitalinius Peregrinus; Constantius Marcianus; Crixsius Adnamatus; Giamillius Crescens; Titius Belatullus; Iulius Severus; Icnius Constans; Statius Victor; Tertinius Abrosus; Marcrinius Perpetuus; Atregtius Cupitianus; Perrius Iustinus, senior prefect; Attonius Asclepius; Ursius Maturus; Statutius Secundinus; Servandius Senurus.
EDCS-11001370.summary: This lengthy inscription records the restoration of a collapsed structure on Vatican mountain to the goddesses Virtue and Bellona by the hastiferi of the Mattiaci community, dated by the consuls to 236 AD and listing numerous individuals involved.

EDCS-11001371.translation: In the consulship of Lateranus and Rufinus.
EDCS-11001371.summary: This inscription records the consulship of Lateranus and Rufinus, likely marking a specific year.

EDCS-11001377.text_edition: \n Lucius Ci Luci filius Claudia Viruni Tertius |(centurio) legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis hic situs est Cornelia Musa uxor heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001377.translation: Lucius Ci, son of Lucius, from the Claudia tribe, Virunus Tertius, a centurion of the 11th Claudian legion, pious and faithful, lies here. Cornelia Musa, his wife and heir, had this made.
EDCS-11001377.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Ci, a centurion of the 11th Claudian legion, erected by his wife and heir, Cornelia Musa, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11001378.translation: Secundus Metius, son of Caius, of the Stellatina tribe, from Foro Vibi, a soldier of the 14th legion, [aged]...
EDCS-11001378.summary: This incomplete inscription is a tombstone for Secundus Metius, a soldier of the 14th legion, noting his origin and tribe, but the age and full details are missing.

EDCS-11001380.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Aurunculeio Iuliano equiti Romano Herennius Victorinus veteranus legionis XXII stipendiorum VIII posuit\n
EDCS-11001380.translation: To the Divine Shades. Herennius Victorinus, a veteran of the 22nd legion, with eight years of service, erected this for Marcus Aurunculeius Iulianus, an equestrian of Rome.
EDCS-11001380.summary: This funerary inscription records that Herennius Victorinus, a veteran, dedicated a tomb for Marcus Aurunculeius Iulianus, a Roman equestrian, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001381.text_edition: \n Flavio Iulio Materno veterano legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis missus honesta missione ex duplicario Flavius Sabinius Attillus veteranus et Flavius Iulius Reginus miles legionis XXII fratres et heredes et sibi vivi\n
EDCS-11001381.translation: To Flavius Iulius Maternus, veteran of the 22nd Primigenian legion, pious and faithful, honorably discharged as a duplicarius. Flavius Sabinius Attillus, veteran, and Flavius Iulius Reginus, soldier of the 22nd legion, his brothers and heirs, erected this for themselves while living.
EDCS-11001381.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavius Iulius Maternus, a veteran of the 22nd legion, who was honorably discharged, with the monument erected by his brothers and heirs.

EDCS-11001382.translation: Aulu[p]or, son of Aulusa[n]us, soldier of the 22nd Primigenian legion, pious and faithful, who lived 33 years and served 14 years, a citizen of the tribe Anche[alo]. Diatr[us]an[o]nus and Mucapor, son of Mucatralis, soldiers of the [above-mentioned] legion, his brothers and tent-mates, made this out of devotion.
EDCS-11001382.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Aulupor and two other soldiers of the 22nd Primigenian legion, erected by his fellow soldiers and tent-mates, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001383.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Caius Iullinius(?) Decimus, a tessera­rius of the 22nd Primigenian legion, pious and faithful, 37 years of age, with 18 years of service. Reginius E[...], an equestrian, Ant[...], a custos armorum, X[...].
EDCS-11001383.summary: This is a partial funerary inscription for Caius Iullinius(?) Decimus, a tessera­rius of the 22nd Primigenian legion, who died after 18 years of service, with other individuals also mentioned.

EDCS-11001384.translation: For the security of Vind[...]. [...].ius Pri[...]. [from the] XXII Pr[imigenian legion], pious and faithful, a beneficiary of the tribune. [...].scinus, his brother, [and others], his heirs, had this made.
EDCS-11001384.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription records the erection of a monument for an individual serving in the 22nd Primigenian legion, with his brother and other heirs involved.

EDCS-11001386.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Cai filio Voltinia s decurioni alae Picentinae annorum XXXXVIII F heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001386.translation: To Caius Iulius, son of Caius, of the Voltinia tribe, a decurion of the Ala Picentina, 48 years old. F[...], his heir, had this made.
EDCS-11001386.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Caius Iulius, a decurion of the Ala Picentina cavalry unit, erected by his heir, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001387.translation: [...], son of Caius Iulius Aqui[t]us, of Pictavus origin, an equestrian of the 13th legion [...]
EDCS-11001387.summary: This incomplete inscription mentions a soldier of the 13th legion, of Pictavus origin and an equestrian, but the full details and purpose are missing.

EDCS-11001388.translation: To Quiet and perpetual security, to Servandia Barbara, who lived 30 years, 4 months, and 9 days, Silvestris Servandus, orderly of the cohort of Cattharens, and Servandi Aeternus and Severina Barbara, to their most devoted and unique wife and most devoted mother, together with their father, erected this.
EDCS-11001388.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Servandia Barbara by her husband and children, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001389.text_edition: \n ------ ex numero] peditum singularium Victoria Perpetua filia et heres et Lucilia Prisca coniux et Victorinia et Gabrilla et Iulia sorores faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001389.translation: Victoria Perpetua, daughter and heir, and her wife Lucilia Prisca, and her sisters Victorinia, Gabrilla, and Iulia, saw to its construction, at the expense of the single infantrymen.
EDCS-11001389.summary: A funerary monument constructed by Victoria Perpetua and her relatives for deceased single infantrymen, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001392.translation: Pervincius Pa..., Martius Sev..., ...nnonius ..., Amabilius(?)..., ...TVLI..., ...M..., ...tonius Gal..., Amabilius Aq..., ...Augustio Magis..., Mascellio Touton..., Sextius Victor, Restutius Cupitus, Vitalinius Perpetuus, Messorius Senecianus, Carantius Statianus..., ...inus, ...atus, ...us, ...aternus..., E..., Iu..., E..., and Ursinius, actor of Secundus, at their own expense.
EDCS-11001392.summary: A list of names, likely part of a funerary monument or record of individuals contributing to one, with many lacunae, possibly from the 2nd-4th century CE.

EDCS-11001393.text_edition: \n s s Quintus Gaius Titus Gaius B Caius SaI Mar Imperatore domino nostro AL[exandro ]\n
EDCS-11001393.translation: Under the Emperor our lord Alexander, the gods approve. Quintus Gaius, Titus Gaius, B. Caius, SaI. Mar.
EDCS-11001393.summary: A dedication or record under the reign of Emperor Alexander (222-235 CE), with several names of individuals.

EDCS-11001394.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Claudiae Primigeniae coniugi karissimae quae vixit annos XXVIII menses IIII Zosimus infelicissimus faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001394.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Claudia Primigenia, most beloved wife, who lived 28 years and 4 months. Zosimus, most unhappy, saw to its construction.
EDCS-11001394.summary: A funerary monument for Claudia Primigenia, dedicated by her grieving husband Zosimus, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001395.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tiberio Claudio Decimi liberto T\n
EDCS-11001395.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Tiberius Claudius, freedman of Decimus T.
EDCS-11001395.summary: A funerary inscription for Tiberius Claudius, a freedman, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001396.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tito Flavio Crescenti marito Aurelia Samis coniunx merenti faciendum curavit vixit nnos XXXXVII\n
EDCS-11001396.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Titus Flavius Crescenti, a deserving husband, who lived 47 years. His wife Aurelia Samis saw to its construction.
EDCS-11001396.summary: A funerary monument for Titus Flavius Crescenti, dedicated by his wife Aurelia Samis, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001397.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Oclatia Masvoni, most devoted mother. Oclatius Ancario(?), freedman, made this for himself while alive and at his own expense.
EDCS-11001397.summary: A funerary monument for Oclatia Masvoni, likely dedicated by her freedman Oclatius Ancario, who also prepared a place for himself, possibly dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001398.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum IO ationis escenti Lucilius Lucilianus pater filio pientissimo MOER\n
EDCS-11001398.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld. Lucilius Lucilianus, father, for his most devoted son.
EDCS-11001398.summary: A funerary inscription for a devoted son, dedicated by his father Lucilius Lucilianus, with incomplete text, possibly from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001400.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucio Plautiano Plautii liberto Alexander sic Thral Plauti servus E P L bene merenti p f\n
EDCS-11001400.translation: To the spirits of the underworld, sacred. Alexander, slave of Thral, for Lucius Plautianus, freedman of Plautius, well deserving.
EDCS-11001400.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Plautianus, a freedman, dedicated by his master's slave, likely dating to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001401.translation: Rufus's slave made this for himself and Sab[---].
EDCS-11001401.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument made by a slave for himself and possibly others.

EDCS-11001402.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Serenus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001405.translation: Lucius Licinius Sacerdos, son of Quintus, of the Fabia tribe, lived 5 years, is buried here.
EDCS-11001405.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Licinius Sacerdos, who died at the age of five.

EDCS-11001409.text_edition: \n Legio I adiutrix centuria numeri Noni Apollinaris\n
EDCS-11001409.translation: Legio I adiutrix, the century of the unit of Nonius Apollinaris.
EDCS-11001409.summary: This inscription likely marks a position or property belonging to a specific century within the Legio I adiutrix.

EDCS-11001410.text_edition: \n Fortunae Lucius Cornelius Arator |(centurio) legionis XIIII geminae Martiae victricis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001410.translation: Lucius Cornelius Arator, centurion of the Legio XIIII Gemina Martia Victrix, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Fortuna.
EDCS-11001410.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Cornelius Arator, a centurion of Legio XIIII Gemina, to the goddess Fortuna.

EDCS-11001411.text_edition: \n M D V IS in suo posuit libens laetus merito Iuliano et Crispino consulibus\n
EDCS-11001411.translation: MDV IS placed this in his property, willingly, happily, and deservedly, when Iulianus and Crispinus were consuls.
EDCS-11001411.summary: This inscription records the placement of a monument or object by MDV IS, dated by the consulship of Iulianus and Crispinus.

EDCS-11001412.summary: This inscription marks the property or command of the century led by Caius Rufus.

EDCS-11001413.translation: In this tomb rests, in good memory, Roteldis, daughter of Rodobert, who lived in peace for 15 years.
EDCS-11001413.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Roteldis, daughter of Rodobert, indicating her peaceful life and death.

EDCS-11001414.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Caius Iunius Secundus decurio civitatis Itiu\n
EDCS-11001414.translation: Gaius Iunius Secundus, decurion of the civitas Itiu, [dedicated this] to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina.
EDCS-11001414.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Gaius Iunius Secundus, a decurion from the civitas Itiu.

EDCS-11001416.text_edition: \n Memoriae Biribam Absei decurionis alae firmae cata<f=E>ractariae bello desiderati oriundo sic ex provincia Moesopotamiae sic domo RaC \n
EDCS-11001416.translation: To the memory of Biribamus, son of Abseius, decurion of the ala firma catafractaria, missed in battle, originally from the province of Mesopotamia, from the town of RaC.
EDCS-11001416.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Biribamus, a decurion of an armored cavalry unit, who died in battle and originated from Mesopotamia.

EDCS-11001420.text_edition: \n Vegisonio Primo et Meloniae Iuniae coniugi frater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001420.translation: His brother had this made for Vegisonius Primus and his wife, Junia.
EDCS-11001420.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vegisonius Primus and his wife, commissioned by his brother.

EDCS-11001422.text_edition: \n Deo Casio Ovinius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001422.translation: Ovinius paid his vow to the god Cassius, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001422.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to the god Cassius by Ovinius.

EDCS-11001423.text_edition: \n DIvabus sic sacrum Solimarus miles cohortis IIII Vindelicorum votum solvit libens laetus merito s(olvit)\n
EDCS-11001423.translation: Sacred to the goddesses. Solimarus, a soldier of the Fourth Cohort of Vindelici, paid his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001423.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to goddesses by Solimarus, a soldier of the Fourth Cohort of Vindelici.

EDCS-11001425.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deae Fortunae Aelius Aeliodorus et Aelia Maura ex voto posuerunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11001425.translation: In honor of the divine house, Aelius Aeliodorus and Aelia Maura set this up to the goddess Fortuna, willingly, happily, and deservedly, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11001425.summary: A dedication to Fortuna in honor of the imperial family by Aelius Aeliodorus and Aelia Maura.

EDCS-11001426.text_edition: \n Fortunae Claudia Primilla votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11001426.translation: Claudia Primilla paid her vow to Fortuna, willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001426.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Fortuna by Claudia Primilla.

EDCS-11001427.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genium plateae Novi vici cum aedicula et ara Titi Flavii Sanctinus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae Alexandrianae piae fidelis immunis consularis et Perpetuus et Felix fratres cives Romani et Taunenses ex origine patris Titi Flavi Materni veterani cohortis III praetoriae piae vindicis et Aurelia Ammias mater eorum civis Romana donum dederunt Agricola et Clementino consulibus\n
EDCS-11001427.translation: In honor of the divine house, Titi Flavii Sanctinus, a soldier of the Twenty-Second Legion Primigenia Alexandriana, pious, loyal, exempt, and a consular official, and his brothers Perpetuus and Felix, Roman citizens and from Taunus, and their mother Aurelia Ammias, a Roman citizen, from the heritage of their father Titi Flavii Materni, a veteran of the Third Praetorian Cohort, pious and victorious, gave this gift, with Agricola and Clementinus as consuls.
EDCS-11001427.summary: A substantial dedication to the Genius of the Novi vicus in honor of the imperial house, made by a soldier, his brothers, and their mother, with consuls and date specified (likely 2nd century AD).

EDCS-11001428.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio plat<e=I>ae novi vici Aemilius Baricio Taunensis v<ot=DI>um solvit libens <l=E>(aetus) merito \n
EDCS-11001428.translation: In honor of the divine house, Aemilius Baricio of Taunus paid his vow to the Genius of the Novi vicus, willingly and happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001428.summary: A votive inscription to the Genius of the Novi vicus by Aemilius Baricio of Taunus, honoring the imperial house.

EDCS-11001429.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae plateae praetoriae aram qui et genium Sattonius Gratus donum dedit Imperatore Alexandro Augusto III et Dione consulibus\n
EDCS-11001429.translation: In honor of the divine house, Sattonius Gratus dedicated this altar, which is also the Genius of the Praetorian street, during the consulship of Emperor Alexander Augustus (for the third time) and Dion.
EDCS-11001429.summary: A dedication of an altar, identified as the Genius of the Praetorian street, by Sattonius Gratus, honoring the imperial house and dated by consuls (likely early 3rd century AD).

EDCS-11001430.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio sancto Marcus Aurelius Claudia Pompeianus miles legionis VIII Antoninianae Augustae beneficiarius consularis Idibus Ianuariis Imperatore domino nostro Antonino IIII et Balbino II consulibus\n
EDCS-11001430.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcus Aurelius Claudia Pompeianus, a soldier of the Eighth Antonine Legion Augusta, a beneficiarius consularis, on the Ides of January, during the consulship of our lord Emperor Antoninus (for the fourth time) and Balbinus (for the second time), dedicated this to the holy Genius.
EDCS-11001430.summary: A dedication to the holy Genius of the street in honor of the imperial house by Marcus Aurelius Claudia Pompeianus, a soldier, dated by consuls (likely mid-3rd century AD).

EDCS-11001432.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Iulius MrNIus voto\n
EDCS-11001432.translation: Caius Iulius MrNIus [made a] vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-11001432.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Caius Iulius MrNIus.

EDCS-11001433.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Gaius Victorius Ianuarius ex voto in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11001433.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Victorius Ianuarius set this up in his own place in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11001433.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Best and Greatest by Gaius Victorius Ianuarius.

EDCS-11001434.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Antonius Proclus centuria Germani votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001434.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus, Antonius Proclus of the centuria of Germanus paid his vow willingly, happily, as was deserved.
EDCS-11001434.summary: This inscription records a soldier, Antonius Proclus, fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Dolichenus.

EDCS-11001435.text_edition: \n Deo Dolicheno Atilius Tertius ex cohorte II Augusta Qurenaica sic votum solvit libens laetus posuit\n
EDCS-11001435.translation: To Deus Dolichenus, Atilius Tertius from the II Augusta Quirenaica cohort set this up, having willingly, happily paid his vow.
EDCS-11001435.summary: This inscription records a soldier, Atilius Tertius, fulfilling a vow to Deus Dolichenus.

EDCS-11001436.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Domitius Germanus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001436.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus, Domitius Germanus paid his vow willingly, happily, as was deserved.
EDCS-11001436.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter Dolichenus by Domitius Germanus, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-11001437.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno ubi ferrum nascitur Flavius Fidelis et Quintus Iulius Posstimus ex imperio ipsius pro se et suos sic\n
EDCS-11001437.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus, where iron is born, Flavius Fidelis and Quintus Iulius Posstimus, by his command, thus [fulfilled their vow] for themselves and their families.
EDCS-11001437.summary: This inscription records Flavius Fidelis and Quintus Iulius Posstimus fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Dolichenus, possibly related to mining.

EDCS-11001438.text_edition: \n Iovi Dolicheno Gaius Iulius Marinus |(centurio) Brittonum Gurvedensium donum dedit\n
EDCS-11001438.translation: To Jupiter Dolichenus, Gaius Iulius Marinus, a centurion of the Gurvedensian Britons, gave this offering.
EDCS-11001438.summary: This inscription records a gift to Jupiter Dolichenus by Gaius Iulius Marinus, a centurion of the Britons.

EDCS-11001439.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Masiacius Sequens ex iussu solvit\n
EDCS-11001439.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest Dolichenus, Masiacius Sequens paid [his vow] by order.
EDCS-11001439.summary: This inscription records Masiacius Sequens fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Dolichenus by divine command.

EDCS-11001442.text_edition: \n Iovi Olbio Seleucus Hermocratus qui et Diogenes donum dedit\n
EDCS-11001442.translation: To Jupiter Olbius, Seleucus Hermocratus, who is also called Diogenes, gave this offering.
EDCS-11001442.summary: This inscription records a gift to Jupiter Olbius by Seleucus Hermocratus.

EDCS-11001443.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Aelius Chresimus Sedatia Bassina votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11001443.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, Aelius Chresimus and Sedatia Bassina paid their vows willingly, happily, as was deserved.
EDCS-11001443.summary: This inscription records a joint vow fulfillment to Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina by Aelius Chresimus and Sedatia Bassina.

EDCS-11001444.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni S<a>mmo Conteddi votum libens merito\n
EDCS-11001444.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Summa, Conteddi willingly paid [his vow] as was deserved.
EDCS-11001444.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfillment to Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Summa by Conteddi.

EDCS-11001445.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Cingetius posuit\n
EDCS-11001445.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, Cingetius erected this.
EDCS-11001445.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Cingetius.

EDCS-11001446.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Iulius Maximinus V \n
EDCS-11001446.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, Iulius Maximinus erected this.
EDCS-11001446.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Iulius Maximinus.

EDCS-11001447.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Lucius Valens votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001447.translation: Lucius Valens willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno.
EDCS-11001447.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter and Juno by Lucius Valens.

EDCS-11001448.text_edition: \n Crescentina Maximus Maximinus Festa Maximina Honorata Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Caius Sedatius Stephanus decurio civitatis Taunensium et Caturigia Crescentina eius cum Stephaniis Maximo decurioni civitatis supra scriptae et Festa Maximino Maximina Honorata filiis in suo restituerunt III Idus Martias Sabino II et Venusto consulibus In suo ex voto renovavit\n
EDCS-11001448.translation: Crescentina, Maximus, Maximinus, Festa, Maximina, Honorata, and Caius Sedatius Stephanus, decurion of the civitas Taunensium, and his wife Caturigia Crescentina, with their children Stephani, Maximus, and Festa, restored this in their own property on the third day before the Ides of March, when Sabinus and Venustus were consuls. He renewed it in his own property according to his vow.
EDCS-11001448.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a monument by Caius Sedatius Stephanus, his family, and others, likely dedicated to Jupiter and Juno, during the consulship of Sabinus and Venustus.

EDCS-11001452.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Libero Patri Caius Secundius Saecularis ex monitu dei libens laetus posuit\n
EDCS-11001452.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Secundius Saecularis willingly and happily dedicated this to Liber Pater, at the god's suggestion.
EDCS-11001452.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Liber Pater by Caius Secundius Saecularis in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11001453.translation: C. Firmus, decurion, made this in his own property to the Matres.
EDCS-11001453.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the Matres by the decurion C. Firmus.

EDCS-11001454.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio Iulia Secundina ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11001454.translation: In honor of the divine house, Iulia Secundina dedicated this to Mercury in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11001454.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by Iulia Secundina in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11001455.translation: Lutevius Victorinus dedicated this altar to Cissonius Mercury.
EDCS-11001455.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to Mercury Cissonius by Lutevius Victorinus.

EDCS-11001457.text_edition: \n Invicto Mithrae Iulius Iuvenalis votum s(olvit)\n
EDCS-11001457.translation: Iulius Iuvenalis fulfilled his vow to the Unconquered Mithras.
EDCS-11001457.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to the god Mithras by Iulius Iuvenalis.

EDCS-11001458.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Caius Lollius Crispus |(centurio) cohortis XXXII voluntariorum\n
EDCS-11001458.translation: To the Unconquered God, Caius Lollius Crispus, centurion of the 32nd cohort of volunteers.
EDCS-11001458.summary: This inscription records a dedication to an Unconquered God by Caius Lollius Crispus, a centurion.

EDCS-11001459.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Marcus Terentius Senecio pecunia sua posuit\n
EDCS-11001459.translation: Marcus Terentius Senecio dedicated this to the Unconquered god Mithras at his own expense.
EDCS-11001459.summary: A private dedication to the god Mithras by Marcus Terentius Senecio.

EDCS-11001461.text_edition: \n Fortunae sacrum Tacitus eques alae I Flaviae turma Claudi Attici votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001461.translation: Tacitus, a cavalryman of the First Flavian Wing, deployed from the troop of Claudius Atticus, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Fortuna.
EDCS-11001461.summary: A cavalryman named Tacitus fulfilled a vow to Fortuna, possibly dedicating a monument.

EDCS-11001463.text_edition: \n Caute Lucius Domitius Agis libens merito\n
EDCS-11001463.translation: Lucius Domitius Agis willingly and deservedly [dedicated this] to Caute.
EDCS-11001463.summary: A dedication by Lucius Domitius Agis to the deity Caute.

EDCS-11001464.text_edition: \n Caute -- Lucius Domitius ? Agis libens merito\n
EDCS-11001464.translation: Lucius Domitius Agis willingly and deservedly [dedicated this] to Caute, [a god?].
EDCS-11001464.summary: A damaged dedication by Lucius Domitius Agis to the deity Caute.

EDCS-11001465.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae petram genetricem Senilius Carantinus civis Mediomatricus votum solvit libens laetus merito sive Cracissius Caute caelum Cautopate oceanum\n
EDCS-11001465.translation: Senilius Carantinus, a citizen of the Mediomatrici, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Unconquered god Mithras, the Mother Stone, or perhaps Cracissius Caute, the Sky, and Cautopates, the Ocean.
EDCS-11001465.summary: A complex dedication involving Senilius Carantinus, the god Mithras, and other deities or concepts, likely fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-11001466.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mithrae Murius Victor aedilis civitatis Taunensium ex voto posuit dedicavitque domino nostro Philippo et Titiano consulibus\n
EDCS-11001466.translation: In honor of the divine house, Murius Victor, aedile of the civitas of the Taunenses, set this up and dedicated it in fulfillment of a vow to the Unconquered god Mithras, to our lord Philippus and Titianus, consuls.
EDCS-11001466.summary: An official dedication by Murius Victor, an aedile, to the Unconquered god Mithras in honor of the imperial family, dated by the consulship of Philippus and Titianus.

EDCS-11001467.text_edition: \n In h(onorem)? d(omus)? d(ivinae) Genio collegii fabrorum tignariorum Ialius tatus de suo it\n
EDCS-11001467.translation: In honor of the divine house, Ialius tatus from his own resources [set this up?] for the Genius of the guild of carpenters.
EDCS-11001467.summary: A dedication from Ialius tatus for the Genius of the guild of carpenters, possibly in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11001469.text_edition: \n IIonius Florentinus aram in suo posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001469.translation: IIonius Florentinus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly set up an altar on his property.
EDCS-11001469.summary: A private dedication of an altar by IIonius Florentinus on his own land.

EDCS-11001474.translation: Lucius Valentius, a coppersmith, set up a sistrum.
EDCS-11001474.summary: A dedication by Lucius Valentius, a coppersmith, possibly for a deity or as a votive offering.

EDCS-11001477.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quinto Favonio Varo filio Quintus Favonius Varus cohorte XXXII voluntariorum pater et Terentia \n
EDCS-11001477.translation: To the spirits of the dead: Quintus Favonius Varus and Terentia [set this up] for their son Quintus Favonius Varus, [a soldier?] of the 32nd cohort of volunteers, father.
EDCS-11001477.summary: A funerary inscription set up by parents for their son, Quintus Favonius Varus, who served in the 32nd cohort of volunteers.

EDCS-11001478.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Philadelphus Philandri Cappadox miles cohortis XXXII voluntariorum centuria Ianuari annorum L stipendiorum XXX\n
EDCS-11001478.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Philadelphus, son of Philander, a Cappadocian, a soldier of the 32nd cohort of volunteers, century of Ianvarius, aged 50, with 30 years of service.
EDCS-11001478.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Philadelphus, a soldier in the 32nd cohort of volunteers, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001479.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus Lucius Valerius Felix Galeria Luguduno miles cohortis XXXII voluntariorum centuria Nerati Cleomenii annorum XXXX aerorum sic XXI curam egit heres\n
EDCS-11001479.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Lucius Valerius Felix of the Galerian tribe from Lugudunum, a soldier of the 32nd cohort of volunteers, century of Neratius Cleomenes, aged 40, with 21 years of service. His heir took care of this.
EDCS-11001479.summary: This tombstone inscription records Lucius Valerius Felix, a soldier in the 32nd cohort of volunteers, and was set up by his heir, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001482.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name on a monument or grave, of Marcus Honoratius Tertius, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001487.summary: This short inscription indicates that Pervincus commissioned or created this monument, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001489.text_edition: \n Herculi Tert<i>nius Catullinus decurio civitatis in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11001489.translation: Tertinius Catullinus, a decurion of the citizenry, placed this in his own ground.
EDCS-11001489.summary: This inscription records Tertinius Catullinus, a local official, dedicating a monument on his own property, likely in a Roman town or colony.

EDCS-11001491.text_edition: \n Marti et Victoriae Soemus Severus cornicularius cohortis <I=T> Flaviae Damascenorum |(milliariae) equitatae sagittariorum votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11001491.translation: To Mars and Victory, Soemus Severus, a cornicularius of the 1st Flavian cohort of Damascenes (milliaria, equitate), of the sagittarii, fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001491.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Mars and Victory by Soemus Severus, a soldier holding a specific rank in an auxiliary cohort, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001492.text_edition: \n Matronis Caius Iulius Crescenis pro Respecto votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001492.translation: To the Matrons, Caius Iulius Crescenis fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly for Respectus.
EDCS-11001492.summary: This votive inscription records Caius Iulius Crescenis dedicating something to the Matrons, likely local deities or spirits, for Respectus, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001494.text_edition: \n Deabus Quadrubiis sic Marcus Campanius Pervincus in suo posuit\n
EDCS-11001494.translation: To the Deae Quadrubiae, Marcus Campanius Pervincus placed this in his own ground.
EDCS-11001494.summary: This inscription records Marcus Campanius Pervincus dedicating a monument to the Deae Quadrubiae (goddesses of crossroads), likely in a Roman settlement.

EDCS-11001495.text_edition: \n Sol<i=F> Invicto Imperatori Caius Paulinius Ius<t=I>us beneficiarius consularis \n
EDCS-11001495.translation: To Sol Invictus, the Emperor, Caius Paulinius Iustus, a beneficiarius consularis, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11001495.summary: This is a dedication to the Unconquered Sun god by Caius Paulinius Iustus, who held a staff position under a consular governor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001496.text_edition: \n Victoriae Marcus Iunius Iovinianus miles cohortis I Aquitanorum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001496.translation: To Victory, Marcus Iunius Iovinianus, a soldier of the 1st Aquitanian cohort, fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001496.summary: This votive inscription records Marcus Iunius Iovinianus, a soldier in an auxiliary cohort, dedicating something to the goddess Victory, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001497.text_edition: \n Virtuti Invicti Imperatoris Caius Paulinius Iustus beneficiarius consularis\n
EDCS-11001497.translation: To the unconquered martial virtue of the Emperor, Gaius Paulinius Iustus, as a special subordinate of the consular legate.
EDCS-11001497.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Paulinius Iustus to the emperor's martial virtue, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001498.translation: From the century of Celsus, Flavius Verecundus.
EDCS-11001498.summary: This inscription records a dedication related to a military unit, the century of Celsus, by Flavius Verecundus.

EDCS-11001499.translation: From the century of Claudius's Ana, son of Iulius Tertius.
EDCS-11001499.summary: This inscription records a dedication related to a military unit, the century of Ana belonging to Claudius, by the son of Iulius Tertius.

EDCS-11001500.translation: From the century of Rufus Sennantis.
EDCS-11001500.summary: This inscription records a dedication related to a military unit, the century of Sennantis belonging to Rufus.

EDCS-11001501.text_edition: \n Legionis XXI Rapacis centuria Sosi Severi Sulli Noti\n
EDCS-11001501.translation: From the century of Sosis Severus Sullus Notus of the 21st Legion Rapax.
EDCS-11001501.summary: This inscription records a dedication related to a military unit, specifically the century of Sosis Severus Sullus Notus of the 21st Legion Rapax.

EDCS-11001506.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Fortionius Dubitatus pro se et suis posuit duobus Aspris consulibus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001506.translation: In honor of the divine house, Fortionius Dubitatus dedicated this to Jupiter Best and Greatest, for himself and his family, and paid his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly when the consuls were Asper and another.
EDCS-11001506.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Jupiter by Fortionius Dubitatus in honor of the imperial family, likely from the late 2nd or early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001509.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti Leucetio et Victoriae Marcus A(urelius) Severinus pro suis filiis Sperato et Pupo civibus Treveris \n
EDCS-11001509.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcus Aurelius Severinus dedicated this to Mars Leucetius and Victoria, for his sons, Speratus and Pupus, citizens of Trier.
EDCS-11001509.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mars and Victoria by Marcus Aurelius Severinus for his sons, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001510.text_edition: \n M(ercurio) Tiberius Iucundius Victorinus libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001510.translation: To Mercury, Tiberius Iucundius Victorinus willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001510.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by Tiberius Iucundius Victorinus, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001511.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Minicius Fatalis\n
EDCS-11001511.translation: In honor of the divine house, Minicius Fatalis dedicated this to the god Mercury.
EDCS-11001511.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by Minicius Fatalis in honor of the imperial family, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001513.text_edition: \n Deo Soli Invicto Mythrae sic Iulius Macrinus immunis legionis VIII Augustae ex voto suscepto solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001513.translation: To the unconquered god Sol Mithras, Iulius Macrinus, an immunis of the 8th Augustan Legion, paid his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001513.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Sol Invictus Mithras by Iulius Macrinus, a soldier of the 8th Augustan Legion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001514.text_edition: \n Pro salute et Victoria et reditu Imppperatorum Caesssarum Luci Septimi Severi Pertinacis et Marci Aureli Antonini et Publi Septimi G[etae] Piorum Auggustorum et Iuliae Domnae Augustae matris Auggustorum et castrorum Quintus Aiacius Modestus Crescentianus legatus Germaniae superioris numini devotus \n
EDCS-11001514.translation: For the safety and victory and return of the Emperors Caesar Lucius Septimius Severus Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus and Publius Septimius Geta Pius Augusti and Julia Domna Augusta, mother of the Augusti and of the camps, Quintus Aiacius Modestus Crescentianus, devoted to the divine will, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11001514.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Quintus Aiacius Modestus Crescentianus, a governor of Germania Superior, for the well-being and return of the imperial family, likely dating to the period of Septimius Severus' reign (193-211 AD).

EDCS-11001516.translation: Speratus of the 4th cohort of the Vindelici.
EDCS-11001516.summary: This is a dedication by Speratus, a soldier from the 4th cohort of the Vindelici, likely a military inscription.

EDCS-11001522.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio collegii iuventutis CONS Attico et Praetextato consulibus\n
EDCS-11001522.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Genius of the college of youth, Atticus and Praetextatus being consuls.
EDCS-11001522.summary: This inscription honors the imperial family and the Genius of a youth college, dated by the consulship of Atticus and Praetextatus, likely in the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001523.text_edition: \n Viri?tuti Vib<I=L>(us Leccus l donum dedit \n
EDCS-11001523.translation: Viritus? Vibius Leccus gave [this] as a gift.
EDCS-11001523.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Vibius Leccus, with a possible uncertainty about the reading of the first name or a dedication to Virtus.

EDCS-11001525.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Valentinius Domesticus, likely a soldier or official of some rank.

EDCS-11001530.translation: To the divine Quadrubis, Secundus fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001530.summary: This inscription records Secundus fulfilling a vow to the divine Quadrubis, likely a local or household deity.

EDCS-11001533.translation: Under Emperor Commodus Augustus, [from the] turma of Placidus Firmus of the ala of the Moesians, X.
EDCS-11001533.summary: This inscription appears to be a military record indicating a unit or individual associated with the ala of the Moesians under Emperor Commodus (177-192 AD).

EDCS-11001534.summary: This inscription likely marks a military unit or property related to the century of Titus Ianuarius Cosi.

EDCS-11001536.translation: Under Emperor Commodus Augustus, [from the] centuria of Primitivus [of the] cohort I of the Bituriges, Masclonius Primus.
EDCS-11001536.summary: This inscription records Masclonius Primus, likely a soldier, associated with the first cohort of the Bituriges under Emperor Commodus (177-192 AD).

EDCS-11001539.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio Veredariorum numeri Nidensium tionius Remus \n
EDCS-11001539.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Genius of the Veredarii (courier-riders) of the Nidensium unit, Tionius Remus [dedicated this].
EDCS-11001539.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the imperial family and the Genius of the Veredarii (courier-riders) of the Nidensium unit, by Tionius Remus.

EDCS-11001541.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus Lucio Septimio Severo Pio Pertinace et Marco Aurelio Antonino Auggustis et Publio Septimio [Geta] Caesare horreum numeri Nidensium quram sic agente Aiacio Modesto legato\n
EDCS-11001541.translation: Under the emperors Lucius Septimius Severus Pius Pertinax and Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus and Publius Septimius Geta Caesar, the granary of the Nidensian cohort, under the administration of the legate Aiacius Modestus.
EDCS-11001541.summary: This inscription records the construction of a granary for the Nidensian cohort during the reign of Severus, Caracalla, and Geta, during the legateship of Aiacius Modestus.

EDCS-11001544.summary: This is a personal name inscription, possibly a tombstone or dedication, belonging to Pacatus Saturio.

EDCS-11001548.translation: To Fortuna. Caius Mogillonius Priscianus, prefect of the II Raetorum cohort of Roman citizens, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001548.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Fortuna by Gaius Mogillonius Priscianus, prefect of the II Raetorum cohort, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001550.translation: To the genius of the century. Iallius Pacatus, standard-bearer?
EDCS-11001550.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the genius of a century by Iallius Pacatus, possibly a standard-bearer, dated to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001551.translation: To the genius of the century of Claudius Celer.
EDCS-11001551.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the genius of a century belonging to Claudius Celer, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001552.translation: In honor of the divine house. Satonius Aeneas, centurion, placed [this to the genius] of the century. Primius Auso, opto, placed [this to the genius] of the century of Caius Sosius Cupitus.
EDCS-11001552.summary: This inscription records two dedications to the genius of centuries, honoring the imperial family, and was set up by a centurion and an opto, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001553.translation: To the genius of the century of Silvinus Atti.
EDCS-11001553.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the genius of a century named after Silvinus Atti, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001554.translation: To the genius of the century. [In honor of the divine house, to the genius] of the century of Alinius Atte[lius?], [he] set up [this] at his own expense... during the consulship of our lord Emperor Antoninus.
EDCS-11001554.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the genius of a century, possibly by Alinius Atellius, funded privately and dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-11001560.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, in honor of the divine house, for the welfare of the Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, father of the country. Antonius Emilianus, centurion of the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis legion, built the temple and willingly fulfilled his vow for himself and his family.
EDCS-11001560.summary: This is a dedication to the Mother of the Gods by Antonius Emilianus, a centurion, to honor the Emperor Antoninus Pius and the imperial family, likely in the mid-2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001561.translation: To Mercury. [An]tonius Iulius gave and dedicated this altar.
EDCS-11001561.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to Mercury by Antonius Julius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-11001562.translation: To Numisius, this sacred offering. Cohors II Raetorum Civium Romanorum, commanded by the prefect Sextius Victor, has paid its vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001562.summary: A military dedication by Cohors II Raetorum Civium Romanorum to a deity named Numisius, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001563.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Condollius Marus paid his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001563.summary: A votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by an individual named Condollius Marus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001567.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Hadrian, grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the deified Nerva, Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the second time, consul for the second time, designated consul for the third time. Cohors II Raetorum Civium Romanorum.
EDCS-11001567.summary: An inscription honouring Emperor Antoninus Pius, likely marking the completion of a public work or a military dedication by Cohors II Raetorum Civium Romanorum, dating to his second tribunician power (c. 139 AD).

EDCS-11001569.summary: A fragmentary inscription honouring Emperor Lucius Septimius Severus Pius, likely a dedication or honorary text.

EDCS-11001570.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, supreme pontiff, conqueror of Britain, conqueror of Parthia, with tribunician power for the fifteenth time, consul for the third time, father of the country, proconsul. Cohors II Raetorum Antoniniana Civium Romanorum, devoted to his divine power.
EDCS-11001570.summary: A dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, honouring his titles and military successes, made by Cohors II Raetorum Antoniniana Civium Romanorum, dating to his 15th tribunician power (c. 272 AD).

EDCS-11001601.translation: To Julia Mamaea Augusta, mother of our Emperor Severus Alexander Augustus, Caesar, the camp, the Senate, and the fatherland, the explorers of Halicarnassus Alexandriana, devoted to her divine power.
EDCS-11001601.summary: A dedication by the Halicarnassian explorers to Julia Mamaea, mother of Emperor Severus Alexander, expressing devotion to her divine authority, likely dating to the reign of Severus Alexander (222-235 AD).

EDCS-11001610.translation: Lucius Antonius, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, Senilis, of the Legion XIIII Gemina.
EDCS-11001610.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription or dedication mentioning Lucius Antonius Senilis, a soldier of the Legion XIIII Gemina.

EDCS-11001612.translation: Rarissima, Septiminius Vittus and Upulalus, his parents.
EDCS-11001612.summary: A funerary inscription mentioning Septiminius Vittus and his parents, Rarissima and Upulalus.

EDCS-11001613.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-11001613.translation: In honour of the divine house. To Jupiter Optimus Maximus Pattonius. Patrinus placed this altar at his own expense in his own place, willingly, gladly, and deservedly. Under our lord Emperor Severus Alexander, consul for the third time, and Dion, as consuls.
EDCS-11001613.summary: A private dedication of an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Pattonius at his own expense, during the consulship of Severus Alexander and Dion (c. 224 AD).

EDCS-11001615.translation: To the goddesses Suleviae. Gaius Hostilius Saturninus and Hostilia Alpina, brother and sister.
EDCS-11001615.summary: A dedication to the goddesses Suleviae by the siblings Gaius Hostilius Saturninus and Hostilia Alpina, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001616.text_edition: \n Primia Accepta et Privatii Secundinus et Tertinus et Confinis fratres ex voto Privati Tertini supra scripti votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11001616.translation: Primia Accepta and Privatus Secundinus and Tertinus and Confinis, brothers, above mentioned, gladly and joyfully fulfilled their vow, as they ought, in accordance with the vow of Privatus Tertinus.
EDCS-11001616.summary: This inscription records a votive offering fulfilled by siblings, likely related to a family member's vow, probably dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11001617.text_edition: \n Lucius Fabius Luci filius Galeria Fabius Nertobriga miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XL stipendiorum XXI Anicius Modestus heres c faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001617.translation: Lucius Fabius, son of Lucius, of the Galerian tribe, a soldier of the Fourth Macedonian Legion, aged 40, with 21 years of service, was set up by his heir, Anicius Modestus.
EDCS-11001617.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Fabius, a soldier in the Fourth Macedonian Legion, erected by his heir, and dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001618.translation: Annaius Pravai, son of Pravus, from Daverzus, a soldier from the Fourth Cohort of Dalmatians, aged 36, with 15 years of service, lies here; his heir erected (this).
EDCS-11001618.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Annaius Pravai, a soldier of the Fourth Cohort of Dalmatians, erected by his heir and likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001619.translation: Bato Dasantis, son of Dasantis, a Dalmatian by birth, a soldier from the Fourth Cohort of Dalmatians, aged 35, with 15 years of service, lies here; his heir erected (this).
EDCS-11001619.summary: This tombstone inscription records Bato Dasantis, a soldier from the Fourth Cohort of Dalmatians, erected by his heir, and likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001620.translation: Beusas Sutti, son of Suttius, a Dalmatian, a soldier of the Fourth Cohort of Dalmatians, aged 26, with 7 years of service, his heir erected (this); he lies here.
EDCS-11001620.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Beusas Sutti, a soldier of the Fourth Cohort of Dalmatians, erected by his heir, and likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.
