EDCS-11001621.translation: [B]reucus, son of Blaedar[i], a soldier from the First Cohort of Pannonians, a Breucian by birth, aged 36, with 16 years of service, lies here; his heir erected (this).
EDCS-11001621.summary: This tombstone inscription records Breucus, a soldier of the First Cohort of Pannonians, erected by his heir, and likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001622.translation: Soenus Assenionis, son of Assenion, a soldier from the First Cohort of Pannonians, aged 35, with 17 years of service; his heir erected (this); he lies here.
EDCS-11001622.summary: This tombstone inscription for Soenus Assenionis, a soldier of the First Cohort of Pannonians, erected by his heir, likely dates to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001623.translation: Biddu[---], son of Astor[is], a Tripolitan, a soldier of the First Cohort of Archers, aged 27, with 15 years of service, lies here; Asipa [---].
EDCS-11001623.summary: This fragmented tombstone inscription records Biddu[---], a soldier of the First Cohort of Archers, and was likely erected by Asipa [---], dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001624.translation: Hyperanor, son of Hyperanor, a Cretan, of Lappa, a soldier of the First Cohort of Archers, aged 60, with 18 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11001624.summary: This tombstone inscription commemorates Hyperanor, a soldier of the First Cohort of Archers, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001625.text_edition: \n centuria Leubacciorum Germanicorum pedatura pedum LXXII sub cura Crescentini Respecti |(centurionis) legionis VIII Augustae\n
EDCS-11001625.translation: A unit of the German Leubaccii, seventy-two pedes (in length), under the supervision of Crescentinus Respectus, centurion of the Eighth Augustan Legion.
EDCS-11001625.summary: This inscription records the dimensions and supervision of a unit of German soldiers (Leubaccii) under a centurion of the Eighth Augustan Legion, likely related to construction or fortification.

EDCS-11001626.translation: Tiberius Iulius Abdes Pantera, a Sidonian, aged 62, with 40 years of service, a soldier from the I Cohort of Archers, is buried here.
EDCS-11001626.summary: This is a soldier's tombstone for Tiberius Iulius Abdes Pantera, a veteran archer from Sidon, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001627.translation: Caius Iulius Hastaius, a superannuated soldier of the cohort of archers. Amoena, his freedwoman, are buried here.
EDCS-11001627.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Iulius Hastaius, a retired archer, and his freedwoman Amoena, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001629.text_edition: \n Aiia sic Deccavi filia Cossillo filius Pusinna filia Sextio filius Caius Coiedius Trever coniux ob pietate posuit\n
EDCS-11001629.translation: Aiia, daughter of Deccavius, Cossillus, son of Pusinnus, and Sextius, son of Caius Coiedius, a Trever, set this up in his honour out of piety.
EDCS-11001629.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by family members for Caius Coiedius and his relatives, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001630.translation: Lucius Cominius Pollentinus, son of Quintus, is buried here, and also Cominia Secunda, daughter of Spurius.
EDCS-11001630.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Cominius Pollentinus and Cominia Secunda, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001631.translation: Macrina, daughter of Aulus Cornelius Protus, is buried here.
EDCS-11001631.summary: This is a tombstone for Macrina, daughter of Aulus Cornelius Protus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001632.translation: To the departed spirits. Solutoria Bodicca?, mother, set up this monument during her lifetime at her own expense for Focuronia Patta, daughter of [---], and for Firminius Sesinthus, her son-in-law.
EDCS-11001632.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Solutoria Bodicca for her daughter Focuronia Patta and son-in-law Firminius Sesinthus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001633.translation: Iulia Quintia, aged 40, and Tiberius Iulius Severus, aged 25, are buried here. Tiberius Iulius Eunus set this up for his wife and son.
EDCS-11001633.summary: This is a tombstone for Iulia Quintia and Tiberius Iulius Severus, erected by Tiberius Iulius Eunus, their husband and father, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001634.translation: Caius Vescius Primus, freedman of Caius, a butcher, is buried here. Caius Vescius Severus, son of Caius, and Peregrina, daughter of Caius Vescius, made this through their legal representative, Caius Vescius Varro, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-11001634.summary: This is a tombstone for Caius Vescius Primus, a butcher, erected by his son and daughter, who acted through a legal guardian, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001635.translation: [---], aged 40, is buried here. Fausta arranged for this to be made for her fellow freedman [---].
EDCS-11001635.summary: This is a tombstone for an unnamed individual, arranged for by Fausta, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11001636.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to provide specific details but appears to be a funerary monument.

EDCS-11001637.summary: This is a funerary inscription likely dedicated to a woman named Trausu[---] by her husband, whose name is partially lost.

EDCS-11001638.translation: In this tomb rests in peace the girl named Aiberga, who lived for 32 years, 5 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-11001638.summary: This is a tombstone inscription recording the death of a young girl named Aiberga.

EDCS-11001640.translation: Paulinus IIB(?)[---] noble of life [---] had wished to give a kiss [---] commending [---] to SECV[---]NTONI[---] what [---] sinus MAII[---] whom his own SV[---]MVS with D[---] RIRRANVCE[---] he said SARV[---]inus this ie[---] Paulina PI[---] [l]V(?) audand[---] A[---].
EDCS-11001640.summary: This inscription is a fragmented funerary text mentioning Paulinus, and possibly Paulina, with a complex and damaged narrative about affection and commendation.

EDCS-11001644.text_edition: \n Matri deum Calvisia Secundina votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-11001644.translation: Calvisia Secundina gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled her vow to the Mother of the Gods.
EDCS-11001644.summary: This is a votive inscription by Calvisia Secundina to the Mother of the Gods.

EDCS-11001645.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio et Maiiae caducium et aram Masclius Satto faber ex voto votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001645.translation: In honor of the divine house, Masclius Satto, a craftsman, dedicated the caduceus and altar to Mercury and Maia, fulfilling his vow gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001645.summary: This is a votive inscription by the craftsman Masclius Satto to Mercury and Maia, honoring the imperial family.

EDCS-11001647.text_edition: \n Marcus Cirrius Fronto Sextus Cirrius Secundio donum dederunt\n
EDCS-11001647.translation: Marcus Cirrius Fronto and Sextus Cirrius Secundio gave this gift.
EDCS-11001647.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription by Marcus Cirrius Fronto and Sextus Cirrius Secundio, likely a donation or memorial.

EDCS-11001648.text_edition: \n Tiberius Iulius Damo votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001648.translation: Tiberius Iulius Damo gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001648.summary: This is a votive inscription by Tiberius Iulius Damo.

EDCS-11001649.text_edition: \n Claudiae Acceptae socrae Iulius Spectatus eques legionis XXII protector pro pietate sua et Sollemnia Severa filia hic corpus condiderunt\n
EDCS-11001649.translation: For Claudia Accepta, his mother-in-law, Iulius Spectatus, an equestrian of the XXII Legion Protectress, and his daughter Sollemnia Severa, founded this burial place out of their piety.
EDCS-11001649.summary: This is a funerary inscription establishing a burial for Claudia Accepta, dedicated by her son-in-law Iulius Spectatus and his daughter Sollemnia Severa.

EDCS-11001650.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely commemorating Marcus Adiutorinius Adve[---]ntus.

EDCS-11001651.text_edition: \n Dis inferis Manibus Saceroniae Sacerillae Luculla fecit\n
EDCS-11001651.translation: Saceroniae Sacerillae Luculla made this for the underworld gods and the spirits of the dead.
EDCS-11001651.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Luculla dedicated to Saceroniae Sacerillae for the underworld deities and ancestral spirits.

EDCS-11001652.summary: This inscription fragment appears to contain a personal name and a family name, but is too incomplete to determine its purpose.

EDCS-11001665.text_edition: \n Nomina data delata legata ad inferos ut illos per vim co<r=N>ripiant Siloniam Surum Caenum Secundum ille te sponsus procat illum amo \n
EDCS-11001665.translation: The names are given, delivered, and bequeathed to the underworld, so that they may snatch Silonia, Surus, Caenu, Secundus by force; he, your betrothed, seeks him with love.
EDCS-11001665.summary: This is a curse inscription where the dedicator lists names of people to be harmed by the underworld gods, possibly related to a dispute over a betrothal.

EDCS-11001667.text_edition: \n Inimici et inimici sic Caranitani Abilius Iuvenis Sabinus apparitor Arria Dardisa Optatus Silonis Privatus Severi Cossus Maesi Marcus aerarius Atta Marci uxsor sic Camula uxsor sic Gamati Ambiti Val Ciri Atticinus Ammonis Terentius Attiso Iulia Attisonis Narcissus Caliphontis Caliphontis et Pudentis et Pudens ssia us Albus Vicinus NINTII Sic te morbo addicant dii Manes dii inferi sunt\n
EDCS-11001667.translation: Enemies and enemies, thus Caranitani, Abilius Iuvenis, Sabinus apparitor, Arria Dardisa, Optatus son of Silon, Privatus son of Severus, Cossus, Marcus aerarius, Atta wife of Marcus, thus Camula wife, thus of Gamatus Ambitus, Valerius son of Cirrus, Atticinus son of Ammon, Terentius son of Atissus, Julia daughter of Attisonis, Narcissus son of Caliphontis, Caliphontis and Pudentis and Pudens, Albus Vicinus of Nintius. Thus may the gods of the underworld, the gods below, condemn you with sickness.
EDCS-11001667.summary: This is a curse inscription listing the names of numerous individuals identified as enemies, with the intention of having them condemned by the underworld gods.

EDCS-11001668.text_edition: \n Severinus et Sanctius defero inferis nomina SEREA ut sic mihi non respondat non respondat Severinus IA in sunt\n
EDCS-11001668.translation: Severinus and Sanctius, I deliver the names of SEREA to the underworld, so that Severinus may not answer me, may not answer.
EDCS-11001668.summary: This curse inscription records Severinus and Sanctius delivering the name SEREA to the underworld, likely to prevent her from responding or acting against them.

EDCS-11001669.text_edition: \n Inimicorum nomina ad inferos ICLVM Inimicorum nomina ad inferos Optatus Silonis Faustus Ornatus Terentius Atisso Atticinus Ammonis Latinus Valeri Adiutor Iuli Tertius Domiti Mansuetus Senopatium sic Montanus materiarius Aninius Victor Quartio Severi Sinto Valentis Lutumarus lanius Similis Crescentis Lucanus Silonis Communis Mercatoris Publius offector Aemilius Silvanus Cossus Matuini\n
EDCS-11001669.translation: Names of enemies to the underworld: Optatus son of Silon, Faustus, Ornatus, Terentius son of Atissus, Atticinus son of Ammon, Latinus son of Valerius, Adiutor son of Iulius, Tertius son of Domitius, Mansuetus, sic Montanus the builder, Aninius Victor, Quartio son of Severus, Sinto son of Valentis, Lutumarus the butcher, Similis son of Crescens, Lucanus son of Silon, Communis the merchant, Publius, offector, Aemilius Silvanus, Cossus son of Matuinus.
EDCS-11001669.summary: This inscription is a list of names of enemies being 'delivered' to the underworld, functioning as a form of curse or malediction.

EDCS-11001670.text_edition: \n Valentis sic Sinto sive alii inimici Valentinus sic Sinto inimicus sic <qu=C>omod<o=I> plumbum subsid<i=E>t sic Sintonem et Martialem Sintonis et Adiutorium Sintonis et quisquis contra Rubrium fratrem et me Quartionem si quis contravenerit Sintonem et Adiutorium eius Sintonis defero ad inferos sic nusquam contra nos invenisse responsionis cum loquantur inimici sic desumat non parentem tanquam sic inferos \n
EDCS-11001670.translation: Valentis, thus Sinto, or other enemies, Valentinus, thus Sinto, enemy, thus may lead him to lead down lead; thus Sinto and Martialis, son of Sinto, and Adiutorium, son of Sinto, and whoever against Rubrius, my brother, and me Quartio, if anyone opposes, Sintonem and his Adiutorium, sons of Sintonis, I deliver to the underworld; thus nowhere may they have found a response against us when the enemies speak; thus may he choose not the parent as if the underworld.
EDCS-11001670.summary: This curse inscription details the ritual delivery of several individuals, identified as enemies of the dedicator Quartio and his brother Rubrius, to the underworld.

EDCS-11001671.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a name, possibly referring to a person or a property, but too short for further interpretation.

EDCS-11001672.text_edition: \n Fructus sic Gracilis sic et Aureum Adiutorium defero inferis Sic non possit respondere quaestionibus\n
EDCS-11001672.translation: Fructus, thus Gracilis, thus and Aureum Adiutorium, I deliver to the underworld. Thus may he not be able to answer questions.
EDCS-11001672.summary: This inscription is a curse invoking the underworld to prevent Fructus, Gracilis, and Aureum Adiutorium from answering questions, possibly in a legal or spiritual context.

EDCS-11001673.text_edition: \n Data nomina ad inferas larvas Dis Manibus hos voveo Lucium Caelium Caium Haeb et si quos alios hostes habeo neca illa nomina\n
EDCS-11001673.translation: Names given to the infernal spirits. To the departed spirits, I vow Lucius Caelis, Gaius Haebius, and if I have any other enemies, may they be killed.
EDCS-11001673.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Manes (departed spirits) combined with a curse, naming specific individuals and wishing death upon any enemies.

EDCS-11001676.translation: Here shall rest in peace / Armentarius, inno/cent servant of God, who / lived for 4 years and / 9 months, died on the / eighth day before the Kalends of October. Berencius / and Euharia, parents, / erected this monument.
EDCS-11001676.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the death of Armentarius, a young child, and mentioning his parents Berencius and Euharia, with the date of death provided.

EDCS-11001677.translation: Here rests in peace Chrodebertus, lived [X] years.
EDCS-11001677.summary: This inscription records the burial of Chrodebertus, a Christian burial inscription with an incomplete age at death.

EDCS-11001678.translation: Here rests in peace Bilefridus, lived nineteen years.
EDCS-11001678.summary: This inscription records the burial of Bilefridus, a Christian burial inscription indicating his age at death.

EDCS-11001679.translation: Here rests in peace Nonnus the presbyter, died on the fifth day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-11001679.summary: This inscription records the death of Nonnus, a presbyter, and specifies the date of his passing.

EDCS-11001684.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Apollini Toutiorigi Lucius Marinius Marinianus |(centurio) legionis VII geminae Alexandrianae voti compos\n
EDCS-11001684.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Marinius Marinianus, centurion of the Seventh Gemina Alexandriana legion, fulfilled his vow to Apollo Toutiorigus.
EDCS-11001684.summary: This inscription records a centurion's fulfillment of a vow to Apollo Toutiorigus in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11001685.text_edition: \n Antonia Postuma Titi Porci Rufiani legati legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis pro salute Porciae Rufianae filiae suae Dianae Mattiacae ex voto signum posuit\n
EDCS-11001685.translation: Antonia Postuma, wife of Titus Porcius Rufianus, legate of the Twenty-second Primigenia, pious and faithful legion, set up this statue to Diana Mattiacae for the health of her daughter Porcia Rufiana, in accordance with her vow.
EDCS-11001685.summary: This inscription records Antonia Postuma dedicating a statue to Diana Mattiacae for her daughter's health, mentioning her husband's military rank.

EDCS-11001688.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae templum Iovi Dolicheno vicani Aquenses vetustate dilabsum sic de suo restituerunt sub cura Carei Saturnini et Pinari Veri Imperatore Severo et Albino consulibus\n
EDCS-11001688.translation: In honor of the divine house, the villagers of Aquae restored this temple to Jupiter Dolichenus, which had fallen into ruin through age, at their own expense, under the supervision of Careius Saturninus and Pinarius Verus, when Severus and Albinus were consuls.
EDCS-11001688.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a temple to Jupiter Dolichenus by the villagers of Aquae during the consulship of Severus and Albinus.

EDCS-11001689.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Eugenius Macrinus pro salute Primitivae coniugis et suorum o \n
EDCS-11001689.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Eugenius Macrinus for the health of Primitiva his wife and his family.
EDCS-11001689.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Eugenius Macrinus for the well-being of his family.

EDCS-11001692.text_edition: \n Sironae Caius Iulius Restitutus curator templi de suo posuit\n
EDCS-11001692.translation: To Sirona, Caius Julius Restitutus, curator of the temple, set up at his own expense.
EDCS-11001692.summary: This inscription records Caius Julius Restitutus, the temple curator, dedicating a monument to Sirona at his own expense.

EDCS-11001693.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mithrae Caius Varonius Lupulus in suo\n
EDCS-11001693.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Varonius Lupulus to the Unconquered God Mithras, on his own land.
EDCS-11001693.summary: This inscription records Caius Varonius Lupulus dedicating a monument to Mithras on his property in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11001694.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Soli Invicto Caius Silvinius Materninus et Lucius Adiutorius Attillus et Caius Vettinius Paternus veterani legionis XXII votum solverunt libentes merito permittente Varonio Lupulo in suo\n
EDCS-11001694.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Silvinius Materninus, Lucius Adiutorius Attillus, and Caius Vettinius Paternus, veterans of the Twenty-second legion, paid their vow willingly and deservedly to the Unconquered God Sol, with the permission of Varonius Lupulus, on their own land.
EDCS-11001694.summary: This inscription records veterans of the Twenty-second legion fulfilling a vow to Sol Invictus on land belonging to Varonius Lupulus.

EDCS-11001695.text_edition: \n et Advento consulibus permittente Varonio Lupulo in suo in suo\n
EDCS-11001695.translation: With Adventus as consul, with the permission of Varonius Lupulus, on his own land.
EDCS-11001695.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a land grant or permission, dated by consuls to the time of Varonius Lupulus.

EDCS-11001699.text_edition: \n Firmius Firminus et Romula uxor ex voto\n
EDCS-11001699.translation: Firmius Firminus and his wife Romula, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11001699.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by Firmius Firminus and his wife Romula.

EDCS-11001701.text_edition: \n Caius Valerius Cai filius Berta Menenia Crispus miles legionis VIII Augustae annorum XL stipendiorum XXI frater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001701.translation: Gaius Valerius Crispus, son of Gaius, of the Menenia tribe, a soldier in the 8th Legion Augusta, aged 40, with 21 years of service, erected this as a brother.
EDCS-11001701.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a soldier of the 8th Legion Augusta for his brother.

EDCS-11001702.translation: Lucius Veturius Primus, son of Spurius, of the Voturia tribe, a veteran of the 14th Gemina Legion, lies here.
EDCS-11001702.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Veturius Primus, a veteran of the 14th Gemina Legion.

EDCS-11001704.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Tito Flavio Germano veterano legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis natione Batavus annorum L Ulpius Arvatius heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001704.translation: To the Divine Shades. Ulpius Arvatius, his heir, erected this for Titus Flavius Germanus, a veteran of the 22nd Primigenia Legion, pious and loyal, of Batavian origin, aged 50.
EDCS-11001704.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Flavius Germanus, a Batavian veteran of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001705.text_edition: \n Lucius Valerius Luci filius Fabia Secundus Brixia miles legionis \n
EDCS-11001705.translation: Lucius Valerius Secundus, son of Lucius, of the Fabia tribe, from Brixia, a soldier in the legion...
EDCS-11001705.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Lucius Valerius Secundus, a soldier from Brixia serving in a legion.

EDCS-11001706.text_edition: \n Muranus eques alae I Flaviae Androuri filius civis Secuanus sic stipendiorum XXI N\n
EDCS-11001706.translation: Muranus, son of Androuros, a Roman knight from the 1st Flavian Ala, of Secuan (Gaulish) citizen origin, with 21 years of service...
EDCS-11001706.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording details about Muranus, a Roman knight serving in the 1st Flavian Ala.

EDCS-11001707.text_edition: \n Titus Flavius Celsus veteranus ex ala Scubulorum cives sic Sappaus nnorum L hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001707.translation: Titus Flavius Celsus, a veteran from the Scubulorum Ala, of Sappaus (Thracian) citizen origin, aged 50, lies here; his heir erected this.
EDCS-11001707.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Flavius Celsus, a veteran of the Scubulorum Ala of Sappaus origin, erected by his heir.

EDCS-11001708.text_edition: \n Dassius Daetoris filius Maeseius miles cohortis V Delmatarum annorum XXXV stipendiorum XVI hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001708.translation: Dassius, son of Daetor, lies here, a soldier in the 5th Cohort of Dalmatae, aged 35, with 16 years of service.
EDCS-11001708.summary: This is a tombstone for Dassius, son of Daetor, a soldier in the 5th Cohort of Dalmatae.

EDCS-11001709.text_edition: \n Licaius Seri filius miles ex cohorte I Pannoniorum annorum XXX stipendiorum XVI hic situs est frater op sic pietatem fecit\n
EDCS-11001709.translation: Licaius, son of Seri, a soldier from the 1st Cohort of Pannonians, aged 30, with 16 years of service, lies here; his brother, out of piety, made this.
EDCS-11001709.summary: This is a tombstone for Licaius, son of Seri, a soldier in the 1st Cohort of Pannonians, erected by his brother.

EDCS-11001710.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai filius Clemens Foro Iuli veteranus annorum LX Caius Iulius Sabinus filius |(centurio) cohortis II Raetorum civium Romanorum annorum XXV hic siti sunt testamento fieri iusserunt heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001710.translation: Gaius Julius Clemens, son of Gaius Julius, a veteran from Forum Iuli, aged 60, and Gaius Julius Sabinus, son of Caius, a centurion of the II Cohort of Raetians, Roman citizens, aged 25, are buried here; they ordered this to be made by their will, and their heirs saw to its construction.
EDCS-11001710.summary: This epitaph records the burial of a veteran and a centurion, who ordered their tombs to be erected by their heirs.

EDCS-11001711.text_edition: \n Quintus Vibius Augustus Raetus miles cohortis II Raetorum annorum XXX stipendiorum XIII heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001711.translation: Quintus Vibius Augustus Raetus, a soldier of the II Cohort of Raetians, aged 30, with 13 years of service, his heir saw to its construction.
EDCS-11001711.summary: This is an epitaph for Quintus Vibius Augustus Raetus, a soldier of the II Cohort of Raetians, commissioned by his heir.

EDCS-11001712.text_edition: \n Dolanus Esbeni filius Bessus eques ex cohorte IIII Thracum nnrum XXXXVI stipendiorum XXIIII hic situs est\n
EDCS-11001712.translation: Dolanus, son of Esbenus, a Bessian, an equestrian soldier from the IV Cohort of Thracians, aged 46, with 24 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-11001712.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Dolanus, an equestrian soldier of the IV Cohort of Thracians.

EDCS-11001713.text_edition: \n BlananIiti f(ilius) civisu miles cohortis II- stipendiorum XXXIV heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001713.translation: Blananitus, son of Blananitus, a soldier of the II Cohort, with 34 years of service, his heir saw to its construction.
EDCS-11001713.summary: This epitaph records a soldier of the II Cohort who served for 34 years, with his heir commissioning the monument.

EDCS-11001716.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus memoriae Secundi Agricolae negotiatoris artis cretariae Agricolia Agrippina filia patri pientissimo faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001716.translation: To the divine spirits, in memory of Secundus Agricola, a merchant in the red-pottery trade. Agricolia Agrippina, his daughter, had this made for her most devoted father.
EDCS-11001716.summary: This funerary dedication honors Secundus Agricola, a merchant of pottery, by his devoted daughter.

EDCS-11001718.text_edition: \n Iustus Primus Atil urnius Vitalis ius Verecundus ius Perrus rius Diadumenus us Martialis us Fuscus ius Fortis ius Restitutus Iatius Secundus tus atius Magius cri Gaius Marcus ErO Lucius Licinius Lucius Valerius Lucius VaEL Sextius Marcus Va Titus TerE Amb Lucius Bla Tiberius Claudius Sextius Lucius \n
EDCS-11001718.translation: Iustus, Primus, Atilurnius Vitalis, Ius Verecundus, Ius Perrus, rius Diadumenus, us Martialis, us Fuscus, ius Fortis, ius Restitutus, Iatius Secundus, tus Atius Magius, cri Gaius Marcus, ErO Lucius Licinius, Lucius Valerius, Lucius VaEL, Sextius Marcus, Va Titus TerE, Amb Lucius Bla, Tiberius Claudius, Sextius Lucius.
EDCS-11001718.summary: This inscription lists the names of multiple individuals, likely associated with a collegium or group, without further context.

EDCS-11001720.text_edition: \n III us avunculusI suae posuit viator vale\n
EDCS-11001720.translation: To his uncle. A traveler, farewell.
EDCS-11001720.summary: This brief funerary inscription is a dedication to an uncle by a traveler.

EDCS-11001726.translation: Here lies in peace Eppo, who lived [---].
EDCS-11001726.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Eppo, indicating he lies in peace.

EDCS-11001727.summary: This is a simple epitaph for Ingildus, stating he rests in peace.

EDCS-11001728.translation: Here rests in peace Municerna, who lived 50 years.
EDCS-11001728.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Municerna, who lived for 50 years.

EDCS-11001729.translation: Qalaqit rests here in peace, who lived 10 years.
EDCS-11001729.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Qalaqit at the age of 10, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-11001730.translation: Votirilo rests here in peace, aged 50.
EDCS-11001730.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Votirilo at the age of 50, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-11001731.translation: Runa rests here in peace, who lived...
EDCS-11001731.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription recording the death of Runa, likely from the later Roman Empire.

EDCS-11001734.text_edition: \n Marti Leucetio pro salute Imperatoris domini nostri Augusti Pii Quintus Voconius Vitulus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigemiae piae fidelis ponendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001734.translation: Quintus Voconius Vitulus, a centurion of the 22nd Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful, arranged for this to be set up in honor of Mars Leucetius for the safety of our lord Emperor Augustus Pius.
EDCS-11001734.summary: An inscription dedicated to Mars Leucetius by a centurion of the 22nd legion for the emperor's safety, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11001735.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Viccius Seneca eques legionis XXII Primigeniae Antoninianae piae fidelis ex voto in suo posuit Grato et Seleugo sic consulibus pridie Kalendas Martias\n
EDCS-11001735.translation: Viccius Seneca, an equestrian of the 22nd Antoninian Primigenia legion, loyal and faithful, set this up in fulfillment of a vow on his own property, with Gratus and Seleucus as consuls, the day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-11001735.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by an equestrian of the 22nd legion, fulfilling a vow, with a precise date in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001736.translation: Publius Licinius of the Palatina tribe, a centurion of the 4th Macedonian legion, set this up for Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Serapis Caelestis, Fortuna, and the Genius of the place, for himself and his family, having vowed, willingly and gladly consecrated it.
EDCS-11001736.summary: A dedication to multiple deities by a centurion of the 4th legion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001738.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio |(centuriae) Aviti Gentiano et Basso consulibus\n
EDCS-11001738.translation: In honor of the divine house, for the Genius of the century of Avitus, with Gentianus and Bassus as consuls.
EDCS-11001738.summary: An inscription honoring the imperial family and the Genius of a century, dated by its consuls to the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001741.text_edition: \n Pedatura Treverorum pedum LXXXXVI sub cura agente Crescentin<i>o Respecto |(centurione) legionis VIII Augustae\n
EDCS-11001741.translation: A boundary of the Treveri with a length of 96 feet, under the supervision of Crescentinus Respectus, a centurion of the 8th Augusta legion.
EDCS-11001741.summary: A boundary marker for the territory of the Treveri, commissioned by a centurion of the 8th legion, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-11001743.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a tombstone or ownership mark, identified by two personal names.

EDCS-11001744.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Marti cohors II Treverorum signum Martis de suo instauraverunt libentes laeti merito instante Flav(io) Paterno |(centurione) legionis XXII\n
EDCS-11001744.translation: In honor of the divine house, the 2nd cohort of the Treveri restored the statue of Mars at their own expense, willingly, gladly, and deservedly, under the supervision of Flavius Paternnus, a centurion of the 22nd legion.
EDCS-11001744.summary: An inscription recording the restoration of a statue of Mars by the 2nd cohort of the Treveri, likely from the 3rd century AD.

EDCS-11001751.text_edition: \n Quadriviis circumsaeptum et portam ex voto suscepto Caius Crispinius Cladaeus publicanus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001751.translation: Gaius Crispinius Cladaeus, a tax collector, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow for the crossroads surrounded by a precinct and the gate.
EDCS-11001751.summary: This inscription records a private vow fulfilled by a publican, likely dedicated to a deity.

EDCS-11001752.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deae Titacae RATI NA VS\n
EDCS-11001752.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Titaca, Rati Na [---].
EDCS-11001752.summary: This dedication honors the imperial family and the goddess Titaca, possibly set up by an individual or group.

EDCS-11001754.text_edition: \n Capusoni Quartissionis filio et Danae coniugi \n
EDCS-11001754.translation: To Capusonius, son of Quartissio, and to Danae, his wife.
EDCS-11001754.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Capusonius and his wife Danae.

EDCS-11001756.translation: Publius Cornelius Domatus made this for his mother Sempronia Domata, who lived 47 years, 9 months, and 20 days, and for his well-deserving wife Attilia Regallia, aged 28, and for himself and his descendants, aged 31.
EDCS-11001756.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a son for his mother and wife, also including himself and his descendants.

EDCS-11001757.translation: Fuscus, a citizen of the Cananefates.
EDCS-11001757.summary: This inscription identifies Fuscus as a citizen of the Cananefates tribe.

EDCS-11001758.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iulio VaL Atiliae I et fratri Marco Iulio et Lucio Iulio I \n
EDCS-11001758.translation: To the departed spirits, for Iulius Va, Atilia, and her brother Marcus Iulius, and Lucius Iulius.
EDCS-11001758.summary: This is a funerary dedication to several individuals, including members of the Iulius family.

EDCS-11001759.text_edition: \n Luci-- Ru et Marc-- A ET \n
EDCS-11001759.translation: Lucius [---] Ru [---] and Marcus [---] A and [---].
EDCS-11001759.summary: This inscription is too fragmentary to determine its purpose or content.

EDCS-11001765.translation: Here rests Leupardus, a beloved lector, faithful and approved in his service, who lived 19 years, whose father Leuninus [---].
EDCS-11001765.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Leupardus, a lector who died at age 19, set up by his father.

EDCS-11001767.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus onio no defuncto oniae Se Iuniania APra et Iuniania Procella filiae eorum faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001767.translation: For Onio, who has died, and Onia Se [---]. Iuniania Pra and Iuniania Procella, their daughters, had this made.
EDCS-11001767.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by two daughters for their deceased parents.

EDCS-11001768.summary: This fragmented inscription likely records the lifespan of an individual named Desiderius.

EDCS-11001769.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae dis deabusque omnibus et Genio Lugnessium Aelius Iucundus actor <k=R>ratera cum cum ara impendio suo fecit \n
EDCS-11001769.translation: In honor of the divine house, of all the gods and goddesses, and of the Genius of Lugnessium, Aelius Iucundus, manager of the estate, with his wife, made this altar at his own expense.
EDCS-11001769.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to the imperial family and local deities by a provincial manager, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001771.translation: Indeed, the condition of parents is broken by the death of their little ones, snatched away with rapid speed, yet eternal hope offers solace for grief, for paradise has tender ages. Buried in this tomb, Desiderate, after six months added to nine years, you lie.
EDCS-11001771.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young child named Desiderate, lamenting their death but finding solace in the belief of an eternal afterlife, probably from the 4th-6th century CE given the language.

EDCS-11001772.translation: I, Faustic[---], while alive, dedicated this tombstone [---] years old [---] I left behind [---] children. Alefius [---] Ruf[---]
EDCS-11001772.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for a person named Faustic[---], who dedicated their own tombstone while alive and had children, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001774.translation: Montana, his wife, made this tombstone for Mauritius, who lived with him twelve years. She lived forty years and died on the 8th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-11001774.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by a wife, Montana, for her deceased husband, Mauritius, recording their years together and her own lifespan and date of death, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001782.translation: In this tomb rests the most blessed man, Deodatus the deacon, who lived in the world for 31 years. His burial was on the 16th day before the Kalends of July, in peace.
EDCS-11001782.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a deacon named Deodatus, recording his age at death and date of burial, likely from the 4th-6th century CE.

EDCS-11001785.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae oredo vetia Atticina mi filia his porticibus Terentius tus\n
EDCS-11001785.translation: In honor of the divine house, Credo vetia Atticina, my daughter, Terentius [dedicated?] these porticoes.
EDCS-11001785.summary: This inscription records the dedication of porticoes in honor of the imperial house and likely by a father, Terentius, for his daughter Atticina, possibly from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001786.text_edition: \n Petroniae Honestae Avitia Pacata neptis aviae sanctissimae ob eiius sic erga se merita \n
EDCS-11001786.translation: To Petronia Honesta, Avitia Pacata, her granddaughter, [erected this monument] for her most holy grandmother, on account of her merits towards her.
EDCS-11001786.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by a granddaughter, Avitia Pacata, to her grandmother, Petronia Honesta, in gratitude for her grandmother's merits, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001787.text_edition: \n Lucius Saurius Saturninus statuam testamento poni iussit Titus Flavius Mandatus Sauri filius donavit Veturia et Sauria Avia soror et Lucius Carantius Atticus arcum dederunt\n
EDCS-11001787.translation: Lucius Saurius Saturninus ordered the statue to be erected by his will. Titus Flavius Mandatus, son of Saurius, dedicated it. Veturia and Sauria Avia, his sister, and Lucius Carantius Atticus gave the arch.
EDCS-11001787.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a statue by a son, Titus Flavius Mandatus, as willed by his father Lucius Saurius Saturninus, with an arch also being donated by other family members, likely from the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001788.translation: Here the body is laid to rest in this tomb. The remains of Rigina(?), wife of Rasnehild, who lived in the world for 20 years and 6 months, were placed here. She died in peace on the Kalends of June. And her husband placed this tombstone for his wife [may she rest] in peace.
EDCS-11001788.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman named Rigina(?), wife of Rasnehild, recording her age at death and the date of her passing, and stating her husband erected the tombstone, likely from the 5th-7th century CE given the names and language.

EDCS-11001789.translation: Tychicus, having been saved from terrible pains of illness by divine love of Mars, made this small offering for the great [favor received] after having prayed to Lenus [Mars] to escape dire suffering of diseases with the labors of the body and the pains of the soul, wandering near the very thresholds of death.
EDCS-11001789.summary: This is a bilingual (Greek and Latin) votive inscription by Tychicus, dedicating an offering to the god Lenus Mars after surviving a serious illness, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001792.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus duci filius et Toccia Cripponis filia uxor vivi sibi Carantius Gracilis Iustus filii de suo faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-11001792.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Toccia Cripponis, daughter, and wife, and Carantius Gracilis Iustus, sons, saw to it that this was made for themselves while alive.
EDCS-11001792.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by sons for their deceased parents.

EDCS-11001793.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iedurcio Iuniano Montania Censorina mater heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11001793.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Montania Censorina, mother and heir, saw to it that this was made for Iedurcius Iunianus.
EDCS-11001793.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a mother and heir for her deceased son.

EDCS-11001794.text_edition: \n Deae Vercane et Medune Lucius T Acceptus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001794.translation: To the goddess Vercana and Meduna, Lucius T. Acceptus willingly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-11001794.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to two goddesses by a man named Lucius T. Acceptus.

EDCS-11001798.translation: The tomb and burial place of Ansericus and his, which was made [on the] 14th day before the Kalends of September. He lived in the world for 35 years.
EDCS-11001798.summary: This inscription records the burial of a person named Ansericus, who lived for 35 years and died in September.

EDCS-11001799.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Liberius Victor ex iusso sic posuit\n
EDCS-11001799.translation: Liberius Victor erected this by order to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-11001799.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, set up by Liberius Victor by order.

EDCS-11001800.translation: Marcus Alaius [---]tus, standard-bearer, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly for his brother Surius Quintus.
EDCS-11001800.summary: This is a funerary or votive inscription by a standard-bearer for his deceased brother.

EDCS-11001803.text_edition: \n MCius Iucundus Bi-Oiae Restitutae uxori pientissimae et filio\n
EDCS-11001803.translation: Iucundus set this up for his wife Biuia Restituta, most dutiful, and his son.
EDCS-11001803.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Iucundus to his wife and son.

EDCS-11001805.translation: For Gaius Attius Carus and his wife Iulia Suausia, and their children Attius Paternus and Attia Aviana.
EDCS-11001805.summary: This funerary inscription is for the family of Gaius Attius Carus and Iulia Suausia, including their children.

EDCS-11001806.translation: Marcus Firmius Speratus to the goddess Fortuna.
EDCS-11001806.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Fortuna by Marcus Firmius Speratus.

EDCS-11001808.translation: Similio, soldier from the German fleet, willingly, gladly, and deservedly paid his vow to his most pious and faithful Matres Domitiana, from the store of Cresimus.
EDCS-11001808.summary: This is a votive inscription by a soldier to the Matres, likely for a successful campaign or safe return.

EDCS-11001809.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio Lucius Karonius Vitalis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001809.translation: To the honor of the divine house, Lucius Karonius Vitalis willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-11001809.summary: A private individual dedicates an offering to Mercury, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001810.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Mercurio Rosmertae aedem cum signis duobus Flavia Pri votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001810.translation: To the honor of the divine house, Flavia Pri willingly and deservedly paid her vow to Mercury and Rosmerta, dedicating a temple with two statues.
EDCS-11001810.summary: A woman dedicates a temple with statues to Mercury and Rosmerta, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001812.text_edition: \n Firmus Ecconis filius miles ex cohorte Raetorum natione Montanus nnorum XXXVI stipendiorum XVII heres ex testamento posuit Fuscus servus \n
EDCS-11001812.translation: Fuscus, a slave, erected this monument according to the will of Firmus, son of Ecconis, a soldier of the cohort of Raeti, of Montanus nationality, aged 36, with 17 years of service.
EDCS-11001812.summary: A tombstone erected by a slave for his deceased master, a soldier of Raetian origin, dated to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001813.text_edition: \n Quinto Cellio Firmo et Iuliae uxori Victor filius fecit\n
EDCS-11001813.translation: Victor erected this for Quintus Celius Firmus and his wife Iulia Victor.
EDCS-11001813.summary: A funerary monument erected by a son for his parents, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001814.translation: To the Divine Shades, Valentinus for Claudia Valentina.
EDCS-11001814.summary: A funerary dedication to the Divine Shades, dated to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001815.text_edition: \n icio uco ania et fili-- tina \n
EDCS-11001815.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001819.translation: For Jupiter Best and Greatest, and Apollo and the Nymphs, Cassius Graccilis, a veteran, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11001819.summary: A veteran dedicates an offering to Jupiter, Apollo, and the Nymphs, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001822.translation: Sacred to Hercules the Bearded. Marcus Hellius Secundus, a trumpeter of the 10th Legion Gemina Pia Fidelis, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11001822.summary: A trumpeter of the 10th Legion dedicates an offering to Hercules, likely in the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001823.translation: Sacred to Hercules the Unconquered. Gaius Terentius Bassus, a centurion of the 6th Legion Victrix, and the standard-bearers of the same legion.
EDCS-11001823.summary: A centurion and standard-bearers of the 6th Legion dedicate an offering to Hercules, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001824.translation: Sacred to Hercules the Unconquered. Gaius Terentius Bassus, a centurion of the 6th Legion Victrix, and the standard-bearers of the same legion.
EDCS-11001824.summary: A centurion and standard-bearers of the 6th Legion dedicate an offering to Hercules, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001826.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, Coelius Marcellus, centurion of the X Gemina Legion, and his fellow soldiers, have paid their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001826.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and fellow soldiers of the X Gemina Legion, dated to the period when this legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 80-103 AD).

EDCS-11001827.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, Quintus Manlius Priscus, centurion of the X Gemina Legion, and his fellow soldiers, have paid their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001827.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and fellow soldiers of the X Gemina Legion, dated to the period when this legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 80-103 AD).

EDCS-11001828.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, Gaius Mettius Seneca, centurion of the XV Legion, and the standard-bearers of the same legion, have paid their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001828.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and standard-bearers of the XV Legion, dated to the period when this legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 103-114 AD).

EDCS-11001829.translation: The XV Legion, by Marcus Statilius [---], centurion, willingly and deservedly set this up.
EDCS-11001829.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a monument to Saxanus by the XV Legion and its centurion, Marcus Statilius, dated to the period when the legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 103-114 AD).

EDCS-11001830.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, Lucius Licinius Festus, centurion of the XXI Rapax Legion, and the soldiers of the same legion, have paid their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001830.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and soldiers of the XXI Rapax Legion, dated to the period when this legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 90-105 AD).

EDCS-11001831.translation: Sacred to Hercules Saxanus. The detachment of the XXII Primigenia Legion serving under the command of Centurion K() Aprili has paid [its vow] willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001831.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a detachment of the XXII Primigenia Legion under the command of Centurion K() Aprili, dated to the period when the legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 103-114 AD).

EDCS-11001832.translation: Sacred to Hercules Saxanus. Gaius Sulpicius Maturus, centurion of the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, and the fellow soldiers of the same legion who are under him, have paid their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11001832.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and fellow soldiers of the XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, dated to the period when the legion was stationed in Pannonia (c. 103-114 AD).

EDCS-11001833.translation: To Hercules Saxanus, Gemellus, standard-bearer of the II Cohort Asturum Pia Fidelis Domitiana, and the detachment of the same cohort, have paid their vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11001833.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by a standard-bearer and a detachment of the II Cohort Asturum, dated to the period when the cohort was stationed in Pannonia (c. 114-138 AD).

EDCS-11001835.translation: Sacred to Hercules Saxanus. Iulius Verecundus, centurion of the II Cohort Varcians, has [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-11001835.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by Iulius Verecundus, a centurion of the II Cohort Varcians, dated to the period when the cohort was stationed in Pannonia (c. 114-138 AD).

EDCS-11001837.text_edition: \n Herculi Saxsano sic sacrum Iulius Victor |(centurio) pro se et commilitones singulares pedites Acili Strabonis legati Augusti votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-11001837.translation: Sacred to Hercules Saxanus. Iulius Victor, centurion, has paid his vow willingly and deservedly for himself and his select foot-soldiers under the legate of Augustus, Acilius Strabo.
EDCS-11001837.summary: This is a dedication to Hercules Saxanus by Iulius Victor, a centurion, and his select soldiers, mentioning Legate Acilius Strabo, likely dating to the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-11001839.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Nerva Traiano Augusto Germanico III Sexto Iulio Frontino III consulibus Herculi Saxano tubicines sub H \n
EDCS-11001839.translation: Under the consulship of Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus for the third time and Sextus Julius Frontinus for the third time, the trumpeters under [someone] dedicated to Hercules Saxanus.
EDCS-11001839.summary: A dedication to Hercules Saxanus made by trumpeters during the consulship of Nerva and Trajan, likely in the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001841.translation: To the Genius of the place and the Boundaries and to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Titus Flavius Verecundus and Marcus Domitius Atto, soldiers [of a legion?], dedicated [this].
EDCS-11001841.summary: A dedication to local deities and Jupiter Optimus Maximus by two soldiers, likely from the late 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001842.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Lucius Papius Fortunatus, centurion of the 21st Rapax Legion, and the standard-bearers of the same legion, dedicated [this].
EDCS-11001842.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by a centurion and standard-bearers of the 21st Rapax Legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001843.text_edition: \n AK LK Iovi Optimo Maximo et Herculi Sax(ano) legio VI victrix pia fidelis legio X gemina pia fidelis legio XXII Primigenia pia fidelis et alae cohortes classis quae sub Quinto Acutio sunt cura Marci Iuli Cossuti |(centurionis) legionis VI victricis piae fidelis\n
EDCS-11001843.translation: Legio VI Victrix Pia Fidelis, Legio X Gemina Pia Fidelis, Legio XXII Primigenia Pia Fidelis, and the auxiliary units, cohorts, and fleet which are under Quintus Acutius, by the care of Marcus Julius Cossutius, centurion of Legio VI Victrix Pia Fidelis, dedicated [this] to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus.
EDCS-11001843.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus made by several legions and auxiliary units under the command of Quintus Acutius, overseen by a centurion of Legio VI Victrix, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001844.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aprillis sic Montani Aprilla <m=N>(ater) <p=C>(onendum) curavit \n
EDCS-11001844.translation: To the divine shades. Aprilla, mother of Montanus, saw to the construction of this tomb for Aprillis.
EDCS-11001844.summary: A funerary dedication for Aprillis, arranged by her mother, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001845.translation: Sextus Donnius Vindex, centurion of Legio X Gemina Pia Fidelis Domitiana, and his fellow soldiers willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus.
EDCS-11001845.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and fellow soldiers of Legio X Gemina, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001846.translation: Caius Nigidius Aponinus, centurion of Legio X Gemina Pia Fidelis, and the fellow soldiers of the same legion willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximius and Hercules Saxanus.
EDCS-11001846.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus by a centurion and fellow soldiers of Legio X Gemina, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001847.translation: A detachment of the German Fleet, under the command of Rufrius Calenus, trierarch, and Julius Primus, fulfilled its vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus.
EDCS-11001847.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Hercules Saxanus by a detachment of the German Fleet, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001848.translation: Lucius Iulius Classicus, [centurion] of Legion XVI, and the standard-bearers [of the same legion], dedicated [this] to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Saxanus.
EDCS-11001848.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Saxanus by a centurion and standard-bearers of the 16th Legion, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001850.translation: Caius Domitius Rufinus, decurion of Cohors II Civium Romanorum Pia Fidelis Domitiana, and his fellow soldiers willingly, joyfully, and deservedly dedicated [this] as sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno, Mars, and Hercules.
EDCS-11001850.summary: A votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno, Mars, and Hercules by a decurion and fellow soldiers of Cohors II Civium Romanorum, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001852.translation: To the Nymphs, Iulius Crescens, a centurion (perhaps) of the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis Domitiana, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001852.summary: This inscription is a votive offering by a centurion of the 22nd Legion to the Nymphs, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001853.translation: To the Suleviae, Gaius Paccius Pastor, a veteran of the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis Domitiana, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001853.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated by a veteran of the 22nd Legion to the local deities called Suleviae, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001859.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, and to the Genius of the place, and to Juno Regina, Tertinius Severus, a soldier of the 8th Augustan Legion, a beneficiarius consularis, set this up in fulfillment of a vow and willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001859.summary: This dedicatory inscription to Jupiter, the Genius loci, and Juno Regina was set up by a soldier of the 8th Legion, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001860.text_edition: \n Finibus et Genio loci et Iovi Optimo Maximo milites legionis XXX Ulpiae victricis Marcus Massianius Secundus et Titus Aurelius Dosso votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-11001860.translation: To the boundaries and the Genius of the place and to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the soldiers of the 30th Ulpian Victorious Legion, Marcus Massianius Secundus and Titus Aurelius Dosso, willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-11001860.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by soldiers of the 30th Legion to deities associated with boundaries and the place, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001861.text_edition: \n Fortunae Conservatrici Caius Iulius Maianus |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11001861.translation: To Fortuna Conservatrix, Gaius Iulius Maianus, a centurion of the 8th Augustan Legion, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001861.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by a centurion of the 8th Legion to the protective goddess Fortuna, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001865.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Titionius Primus |(centurio) cohortis VII Raetorum equitatae votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001865.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and to Juno Regina, Titionius Primus, a centurion of the 7th Cohort of Raeti Equitatae, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-11001865.summary: This votive inscription to Jupiter and Juno Regina was made by a centurion of an auxiliary cavalry cohort, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001866.text_edition: \n omnibus dibus deabusque textor senex ex voto HITRA\n
EDCS-11001866.translation: To all the gods and goddesses, an old weaver from a vow to Hitra.
EDCS-11001866.summary: This dedication to all gods and goddesses is by an elderly weaver, possibly associated with a local deity named Hitra, and dates to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001872.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caius Iulius Fe cornicularius tribuni militum cohortis voluntariorum centuria Capitonis militavit annis XV C\n
EDCS-11001872.translation: To the spirits of the dead, Gaius Iulius Fe, a cornicularius (herald) to a military tribune of the cohort of volunteers, the century of Capito, served for 15 years.
EDCS-11001872.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaius Iulius Fe, a cornicularius in a cohort of volunteers, who served for 15 years, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11001877.translation: Here rests in peace, Rainovaldus, a beloved boy among his parents; a noble boy was brought into the nation by fate; death snatched him away from the world. He lived 35 years, died on the eleventh day of the month of October.
EDCS-11001877.summary: This epitaph commemorates Rainovaldus, a young boy who died at the age of 35 in October, likely dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-11001878.text_edition: \n Idus Octobres Genio horreorum numeri Brittonum Antoninianorum Ibliomarius Oppius posuit Titus Um Quintanensis posuit V Kalendas Novembres\n
EDCS-11001878.translation: On the Ides of October, to the Genius of the granaries of the Antonine Brittonum unit, Ibliomarius Oppius erected this; Titus Um erected this on the 5th day before the Kalends of November.
EDCS-11001878.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an offering to the Genius of the granaries by two individuals associated with a military unit called the Brittonum Antoninianorum, likely dating to the 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11001879.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio CITVR PVSEus actuarius numeri D<i=T>vitensis Grato et Seleuco consulibus votum solvit <l=E>(ibens) laetus merito \n
EDCS-11001879.translation: To the Genius of the divine house, Puseus, clerk of the Duitensis unit, freed from his vow willingly, gladly, deservedly, under the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus.
EDCS-11001879.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Puseus, a clerk of the Duitensis unit, to the Genius of the divine house, dated to the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus.

EDCS-11001881.text_edition: \n Genio tabularii numeri Brittonum Antoninianorum Vibius Mercurialis librarius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11001881.translation: To the Genius of the office of the Antonine unit of Britons, Vibius Mercurialis, a clerk, freed from his vow willingly, gladly, deservedly.
EDCS-11001881.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Vibius Mercurialis, a clerk, to the Genius of the office of the Brittonum unit, likely from the Antonine period.

EDCS-11001882.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio vexillariorum et imaginiferorum Attianus Coresi vexillarius Fortionius Constitutus imaginifer signum cum aedicula et tabulam marmoream dono dederunt dedicatum Imperatore domino nostro Gordiano Augusto et Aviola consulibus\n
EDCS-11001882.translation: To the Genius of the divine house, Attianus Coresi, standard-bearer, and Fortionius Constitutus, standard-bearer, dedicated this standard with a shrine and a marble tablet as a gift, under our Emperor Lord Gordianus Augustus and Aviola as consuls.
EDCS-11001882.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a military standard with shrine and a marble tablet by two officers to the Genius of the divine house, dated to the reign of Emperor Gordian III.

EDCS-11001883.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae baioli et vexillarii collegio Victoriensium signiferorum Genium de suo fecerunt VIIII Kalendas Octobres Praesente et Albino consulibus hi XIIII de suo restituerunt Paternus Prudens Marianus Dagovassus Cerialis Aturo Victor Satullus Sattara Macrinus Laetus Apollinaris Secundanus Ursus\n
EDCS-11001883.translation: To the Genius of the divine house, the porters and standard-bearers of the Victoriensium college of standard-bearers made this offering from their own funds on the ninth day before the Kalends of October, under Praesens and Albinus as consuls; these fourteen men restored it from their own funds: Paternus, Prudens, Marianus, Dagovassus, Cerialis, Aturo, Victor, Satullus, Sattara, Macrinus, Laetus, Apollinaris, Secundanus, Ursus.
EDCS-11001883.summary: This inscription records an offering made by the porters and standard-bearers of the Victoriensium college to their Genius, and the restoration of the monument by fourteen individuals, dated to the consulship of Praesens and Albinus.

EDCS-11001885.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Marti Praestanti Ulmionius Flio DONNOC IO \n
EDCS-11001885.translation: To the divine house, to the god Mars Praestans, Ulmionius Flio dedicated.
EDCS-11001885.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Mars Praestans by Ulmionius Flio, likely honoring the divine house.

EDCS-11001886.translation: To the household god Mercury, Iustus made this.
EDCS-11001886.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the household god Mercury by a person named Iustus.

EDCS-11201235.summary: This inscription seems to record a quantity or weight associated with Eutichius and the location of Naissus, possibly related to a transaction or inventory.

EDCS-11201811.text_edition: \n Deae Aventiae Cnaeus Iulius Marcellinus Equester de suo posuit\n
EDCS-11201811.translation: To the goddess Aventia, Cnaeus Iulius Marcellinus Equester dedicated from his own funds.
EDCS-11201811.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Aventia by Cnaeus Iulius Marcellinus Equester.

EDCS-11201812.translation: Publius Graccius Paternus ordered this to be set up by his will; his heir Scribonia Lucana took care to have it made.
EDCS-11201812.summary: This inscription records the posthumous dedication of a monument ordered by Publius Graccius Paternus and executed by his heir Scribonia Lucana.

EDCS-11201814.translation: To Anextlomara and Augustus, Publicius Aunus.
EDCS-11201814.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the deities Anextlomara and Augustus by Publicius Aunus.

EDCS-11201819.translation: To Mars. Marcus Maccius Sabinus, in accordance with a vision.
EDCS-11201819.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mars by Marcus Maccius Sabinus, likely after a divine vision, as indicated by 'ex visu'.

EDCS-11201820.text_edition: \n centuria Domiti todi Valerius Tertius <G=Q>enio legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis pullum votum solvit laetus libens merito \n
EDCS-11201820.translation: Valerius Tertius of the centuria of Domitius Todi in the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion fulfilled his vow for a fowl, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201820.summary: This inscription records a soldier, Valerius Tertius of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, fulfilling a vow for a fowl, likely in the 1st-3rd century AD.

EDCS-11201821.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Careius Certius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11201821.translation: Gaius Careius Certius fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, gladly, willingly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201821.summary: This inscription records a private dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Gaius Careius Certius, likely from the 1st-3rd century AD.

EDCS-11201822.translation: To Mars. Fidelis, freedwoman of Frontonis, fulfilled her vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201822.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Mars by Fidelis, a freedwoman, likely from the 1st-3rd century AD.

EDCS-11201823.text_edition: \n Lucius Petronius Secundus Marti votum cum suis libens merito\n
EDCS-11201823.translation: Lucius Petronius Secundus fulfilled his vow to Mars with his family, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201823.summary: This inscription records Lucius Petronius Secundus fulfilling a vow to Mars for himself and his family, likely from the 1st-3rd century AD.

EDCS-11201824.translation: Of Sextus Antistius Draconis, of the centuria of Lucius Valerius Terentius.
EDCS-11201824.summary: This inscription appears to be a boundary marker or a record of property division, possibly related to military land allocation.

EDCS-11201825.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with only partial names preserved, making its exact context uncertain.

EDCS-11201826.translation: [---] Verecundus, a ring-bearer, of the centuria of Satrienus, [son of] the military tribune Iuvenalis of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion.
EDCS-11201826.summary: This inscription records Verecundus, identified by his role as a ring-bearer and his family connections to a military tribune of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion.

EDCS-11201827.translation: [---] Sammo fulfilled his vow willingly [and deservedly].
EDCS-11201827.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a vow fulfilled by someone named Sammo, likely to a deity.

EDCS-11201828.text_edition: \n Marcus Luxsonius sic Marci filius Romilia Festus Ateste miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Atti Valentis annorum XXX stipendiorum Luxsonius sic legionis eiusdem Luxsonius! \n
EDCS-11201828.translation: Marcus Luxsonius Festus, son of Marcus, of the Romilia tribe, from Ateste, a soldier of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, centuria of Attius Valens, aged 30, with 30 years of service. Luxsonius [his] father of the same legion.
EDCS-11201828.summary: This inscription is a military dedication by Marcus Luxsonius Festus of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, including details about his father and service.

EDCS-11201832.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Statius Vegetus, possibly on a tombstone or monument.

EDCS-11201833.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cassius Secundus, likely on a tombstone or dedication.

EDCS-11201834.text_edition: \n Creiscenti Credani ad armamentarium Agili Credanus\n
EDCS-11201834.translation: Creiscentius to Credanus at the armory of Agilus Credanus.
EDCS-11201834.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Creiscentius to Credanus, mentioning an armory and Agilus Credanus.

EDCS-11201835.text_edition: \n Dab<i=E>s Vero centuria Adiutoris ama nos et vale \n
EDCS-11201835.translation: Dabies, of the century of Adiutor, our helper; love us and fare well.
EDCS-11201835.summary: This is a personal message or dedication from Dabies, a helper from Adiutor's century, asking for goodwill.

EDCS-11201836.translation: To Quintus Maius, soldier of the Legio XIII Gemina, hastatus in the third maniple.
EDCS-11201836.summary: This inscription records the military service of Quintus Maius, a soldier of Legio XIII Gemina.

EDCS-11201837.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Titus Pamius Satt(o)nus.

EDCS-11201840.translation: To Valerius Maturus and Gaius Adnamatius.
EDCS-11201840.summary: This is a dedication to Valerius Maturus and Gaius Adnamatius.

EDCS-11201841.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Gaius Valerius Onto.

EDCS-11201853.translation: To Apollo, Maria Patera willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow for the safety of her son Nobilianus.
EDCS-11201853.summary: This is a votive inscription to Apollo by Maria Patera for the health of her son Nobilianus.

EDCS-11201854.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Sucello Silvano Spart locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-11201854.translation: In honor of the divine house, the place was granted to the god Sucellus Silvanus by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11201854.summary: This inscription records the official granting of a place to the god Sucellus Silvanus in honor of the imperial family by the local council.

EDCS-11201855.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Soli Invicto Silvester votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11201855.translation: In honor of the divine house, Silvester gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow to the Unconquered Sun God as was deserved.
EDCS-11201855.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to the god Sol Invictus, likely dedicated by Silvester.

EDCS-11201860.translation: His wife Nia Severa arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11201860.summary: This inscription records that Nia Severa commissioned a monument or work, likely in memory of her husband.

EDCS-11201861.translation: In honor of the divine house, Venixamus, son of Meddil, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the goddess Victory.
EDCS-11201861.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Venixamus to the goddess Victoria, in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-11201862.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---] Caratullus, [---] Cyria.
EDCS-11201862.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning the deceased Caratullus and Cyria.

EDCS-11201863.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Eutichi sic Eutycho Eutiches sic Felix Eumenes Helius Carata filia\n
EDCS-11201863.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Eutichus, Eutichus, Eutiches, Felix, Eumenes, Helius, his daughter Carata.
EDCS-11201863.summary: This inscription lists several names, likely deceased individuals being honored, including Eutichus, Eutiches, Felix, Eumenes, Helius, and Carata.

EDCS-11201864.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Festio Victori Durra filia faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11201864.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Victori, daughter of Durra, arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11201864.summary: This funerary inscription records that Victori, daughter of Durra, commissioned a monument in honor of the deceased Festio.

EDCS-11201865.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Matutinus.
EDCS-11201865.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Matutinus.

EDCS-11201866.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His father arranged for this to be placed for Nantio, son of Natalis.
EDCS-11201866.summary: This funerary inscription records that the father of Nantio, son of Natalis, commissioned a monument for him.

EDCS-11201867.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sacurillae Sammonis filiae Carantillus Maturicis filius maritus ponendum curavit Dis Manibus Servando Carantilli filio\n
EDCS-11201867.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Carantillus, son of Maturicus, arranged for this to be placed for his wife Sacurilla, daughter of Sammon. To the spirits of the departed. For Servandus, son of Carantillus.
EDCS-11201867.summary: This inscription is a double funerary dedication, with Carantillus dedicating a monument for his wife Sacurilla, and also a monument for Servandus.

EDCS-11201874.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Marcus Valerius Florus et Ursa Sperati ex voto posuerunt\n
EDCS-11201874.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Marcus Valerius Florus and Ursa Sperati placed [this] in accordance with their vow.
EDCS-11201874.summary: This inscription records a votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Valerius Florus and Ursa Sperati.

EDCS-11201875.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, to Juno. Vitalis [---] / [---]
EDCS-11201875.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter and Juno, likely by an individual named Vitalis, with incomplete text.

EDCS-11201879.translation: To Diana. Martius Anullus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11201879.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Diana by Martius Anullus.

EDCS-11201880.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invihto sic Midhrae sic Materninius Faustinus carax sic fanum cum solo Invihto sic in suo fecit consacratus X Kalendas Februarias Fanus consacratus per Potentianum patrem consulibus Paulino et Iuliano libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11201880.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Invictus God, also Mithras, also Maternius Faustinus carax, dedicated a temple with its land to the Invictus God in his own property, consecrated on the tenth day before the Kalends of February. The temple was consecrated by Potentianus the father, under the consulship of Paulinus and Julianus, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201880.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple to the Invictus God (also identified with Mithras) by Maternius Faustinus, with specific consecration details and consular dating.

EDCS-11201882.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invihto sic Materninius Faustinus carax sic in suo posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11201882.translation: In honor of the divine house, Maternius Faustinus carax placed this willingly, joyfully, and deservedly to the Invictus God.
EDCS-11201882.summary: This inscription records Maternius Faustinus placing something in honor of the divine house and to the Invictus God.

EDCS-11201883.text_edition: \n Invi<c=H>to Faustinus c<o=A>rax votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-11201883.translation: Faustinus Carax willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to the Invictus God.
EDCS-11201883.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Invictus God by Faustinus Carax.

EDCS-11201885.summary: This fragmented inscription is a dedication to individuals named Ti[---] and Avitianus.

EDCS-11201886.summary: This is a very brief inscription that likely refers to a statue or image of Melausus.

EDCS-11201887.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Speratio Servando et Speratiae Ammossae et Speratiae \n
EDCS-11201887.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Speratio, to Servandus, and to Speratia Ammosa, and to Speratia.
EDCS-11201887.summary: This is a dedication to the Manes (spirits of the dead) for Speratio, Servandus, and Speratia Ammosa.

EDCS-11201892.translation: To the spirits of the departed: of Clementis, son of Aiassas the Rhodian, and Arruntius Cur[--] son of Curio.
EDCS-11201892.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Clementis, son of Aiassas, and Arruntius Cur[--], son of Curio.

EDCS-11201893.translation: To the Invictus God. Adiutorius Tertius.
EDCS-11201893.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the Invictus God by Adiutorius Tertius.

EDCS-11201894.translation: To Salverinus, from his wife Nov[---] Sal.
EDCS-11201894.summary: A dedication to a person named Salverinus, likely from his wife, of uncertain date.

EDCS-11201896.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae pro salute Iovi Optimo Maximo Materni Marciani Valeriana soror ex voto posuit laeta libens merito\n
EDCS-11201896.translation: In honor of the divine house, for health, Valeriana, sister of Materni Marciani, gladly, willingly, and deservedly set this up as a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-11201896.summary: A votive dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Valeriana, sister of Materni Marciani, likely from the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11201899.text_edition: \n Licinius Ob decurio civitatis Auderiensium et Messoria Tetrica coniux libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11201899.translation: Licinius Ob, decurion of the citizens of Auder, and his wife Messoria Tetrica, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly [set this up].
EDCS-11201899.summary: An inscription by Licinius Ob, a decurion, and his wife Messoria Tetrica, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201900.text_edition: \n Deo xancto sic Mercurio Priscinius Sedulius votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11201900.translation: Priscinius Sedulius gladly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to the holy god Mercury.
EDCS-11201900.summary: A votive offering to Mercury by Priscinius Sedulius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201901.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Priscinius Sedulius Primulus fratris sic votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11201901.translation: Priscinius Sedulius Primulus and his brother gladly, joyfully, and deservedly paid their vow to the unconquered god Mithras.
EDCS-11201901.summary: A votive offering to the god Mithras made by Priscinius Sedulius Primulus and his brother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201902.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Petronius Perpetuus ex iussu votum solvit libens l(aetus) merito\n
EDCS-11201902.translation: Petronius Perpetuus paid his vow to the unconquered god Mithras, as ordered, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201902.summary: A votive offering to Mithras by Petronius Perpetuus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201903.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Silvestrius Silvinus et Silvestrius Perpetuus et Silvinius Aurelius nepos votum solverunt libentes laeti merito Perpetuus frater artis sutoriae Silvinus artis quadratariae Aurelius donum dederunt Deo Soli Invicto Mithrae Silvestrius Silvinus et Silvestrius Perpetuus et Si<l=I>vinius Aurelius \n
EDCS-11201903.translation: Silvestrius Silvinus and Silvestrius Perpetuus and Silvinius Aurelius, his nephew, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly paid their vows; Perpetuus, a brother from the shoemaking trade; Silvinus, from the stonemasonry trade; Aurelius gave this gift to the unconquered Sun god Mithras; Silvestrius Silvinus and Silvestrius Perpetuus and Silvinius Aurelius.
EDCS-11201903.summary: A complex votive inscription to Mithras by several individuals, including a shoemaker and a stonemason, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201905.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Maiorius Urbicus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11201905.translation: Maiorius Urbicus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-11201905.summary: A votive offering to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Maiorius Urbicus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201909.translation: To the genius of the first century of Iucundus.
EDCS-11201909.summary: A dedication to the genius (guardian spirit) of a century named Iucundus, likely from a military context.

EDCS-11201918.text_edition: \n Messor gladiator voto soluto libens posuit Fortunae\n
EDCS-11201918.translation: Messor the gladiator gladly set this up, having fulfilled his vow, to Fortuna.
EDCS-11201918.summary: A dedication to Fortuna by a gladiator named Messor, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11201919.text_edition: \n Genio loci Eventui Bono Fortunae Conservatrici Titus Vindelicius Tertinus miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis strator consularis sacellum fecit libens sub cura Lib Primi |(centurionis) legionis eiusdem Imperatore Antonino II et Geta Caesare consulibus\n
EDCS-11201919.translation: To the Genius of the Place, to Beneficial Change, and to Fortune the Preserver, Titus Vindelicius Tertinus, soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, staff officer to the governor, made this shrine willingly, under the supervision of Lib(erius) Primus, centurion of the same legion, when Antoninus II and Geta Caesar were consuls.
EDCS-11201919.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a shrine to local deities and virtues by a soldier serving as a staff officer during the consulship of Antoninus II and Geta Caesar.

EDCS-11201922.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Teddiatius Temporinus placed this willingly, happily, and deservedly on his own property.
EDCS-11201922.summary: This inscription records the dedication of statues or a shrine to Jupiter and Juno by Teddiatius Temporinus.

EDCS-11201923.text_edition: \n Bello libertus magister II familiae donum dedit\n
EDCS-11201923.translation: Bello, a freedman and magistrate of the guild, gave this gift.
EDCS-11201923.summary: This inscription records a gift given by Bello, a freedman and a magistrate of a guild or association.

EDCS-11201924.text_edition: \n Lucio Valerio Luci filio Frontoni |(centurioni) misso honesta missione ex legione I adiutrici heredes filii eiusdem\n
