EDCS-11201924.translation: For Lucius Valerius Fronton, son of Lucius, centurion, discharged with an honorable discharge from the I Adiutrix Legion, his heirs.
EDCS-11201924.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the heirs of Lucius Valerius Fronton, a centurion honorably discharged from the I Adiutrix Legion.

EDCS-11201928.translation: Lucius Caliidius Primigenius, son of Lucius, freedman, from Pisaurum, aged 50, lies here. Zetus Suavis and his freedmen arranged for his burial.
EDCS-11201928.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lucius Caliidius Primigenius, a freedman from Pisaurum, noting his age and who arranged his burial.

EDCS-11201929.translation: To the departed spirits, to Haledona, aged 23, my dearest wife, and to myself, most reverent, Lucius Aetilius [arranged for this].
EDCS-11201929.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Haledona, wife of Lucius Aetilius, recording her age and intended for both of them.

EDCS-11201930.translation: For Tiberia Iulia Smeertuca, freedwoman of Tiberius Iulius Diviciacus, aged 27, from the Sebosiana cavalry unit, and for her son Speratus, her patron placed this.
EDCS-11201930.summary: This tombstone inscription is dedicated by a patron for Tiberia Iulia Smeertuca and her son Speratus, noting her age and origin from a cavalry unit.

EDCS-11201938.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Martialio Miccioni et Ibliomariae Bodicae patribus Miccionia Ammisia filia faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11201938.translation: To the departed spirits, Miccionia Ammisia, daughter, had this made for her parents, Martialio Miccioni and Ibliomaria Bodica.
EDCS-11201938.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by Miccionia Ammisia for her parents, Martialio Miccioni and Ibliomaria Bodica.

EDCS-11201943.translation: Here rests in the Lord Mauricia, an honorable woman, who lived 33 years; her husband and father(?) placed the monument.
EDCS-11201943.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Mauricia, an honorable woman who died at age 33, with the monument placed by her husband and father.

EDCS-11201946.translation: To the departed spirits, Gaius Solinius Protulus, son of Marcus, soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, aged 26, with 7 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-11201946.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaius Solinius Protulus, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia Pia Fidelis Legion, noting his age and years of service.

EDCS-11201947.translation: To the departed spirits, [3]rtius made this.
EDCS-11201947.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the maker of a tomb, identified only by a partial name.

EDCS-11201954.translation: Titus Julius Leon[--] / Leonis Leo [---] / fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11201954.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by an individual, likely named Leonis Leo, possibly of high status given the partial Roman names.

EDCS-11201955.text_edition: \n Herculi Saxsano sic vexillatio legionis XXX Ulpiae victricis et Iulius Verus optio\n
EDCS-11201955.translation: To Hercules Saxsanus, thus the vexillation of the XXX Ulpia Victrix legion and Julius Verus, optio, [dedicated this].
EDCS-11201955.summary: This is a dedication to the god Hercules Saxsanus by a military vexillation and an officer named Julius Verus.

EDCS-11201957.translation: Quodubis Masuaeta fulfilled her vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11201957.summary: This is a votive inscription by a woman named Quodubis Masuaeta, recording the fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-11201968.translation: Here rests in peace Garoaldus; he lived in this world for 5 years. His deposition was made in the month of December, the 14th day. Cherished by his own.
EDCS-11201968.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Garoaldus, his age, date of burial, and his familial affection.

EDCS-11201969.text_edition: \n Herculi Saxsano sic sacrum Celsus |(centurio) singularium peditum et commilitones singulares Licini Surae legati votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11201969.translation: To Hercules Saxsanus, thus dedicated: Celsus, centurion of the elite infantry, and his fellow soldiers, the elite of the staff of Legate Licinius Sura, fulfilled their vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-11201969.summary: This is a votive inscription to Hercules Saxsanus by a centurion and his elite troops, dedicated to the legate Licinius Sura.

EDCS-11201970.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo M(aximo) et Neptuno Caius Marius Maximus |(centurio) classis Germanicae piae fidelis pro se et suis commilitonibus qui sub eo sunt votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11201970.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Neptune, Gaius Marius Maximus, centurion of the pious and faithful German fleet, for himself and his fellow soldiers who are under him, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11201970.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter and Neptune by a naval centurion for himself and his subordinates.

EDCS-11201971.translation: Here rests in peace Pulevald, beloved by his parents; he lived in this world [---].
EDCS-11201971.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pulevald, noting his love from his parents and his lifespan in this world.

EDCS-11202053.text_edition: \n MATIO STOR ex iussu votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202053.translation: Matio Stor fulfilled his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly by order.
EDCS-11202053.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Matio Stor, executed by order.

EDCS-11202054.translation: In honor of the divine house: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the other gods and goddesses, Marcus Aurelius Titius Iulianus, a specialist subordinate to the consular governor, for his own health and that of his people, willingly set this up on the 15th day before the Kalends of August, during the reign of our lord Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus II.
EDCS-11202054.summary: This is a dedication to the imperial family and the gods by a military official, Marcus Aurelius Titius Iulianus, during the reign of Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus.

EDCS-11202055.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deabus Quadruvis Iovi Optimo Maximo dis deabusque omnibus Serenius Atticus beneficiarius consularis pro sua et suorum salute posuit IIII Kalendas Ianuarias Agricola et Clementino consulibus\n
EDCS-11202055.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and all the gods and goddesses of the crossroads, Serenius Atticus, aide of a consular governor, dedicated this for his own safety and that of his family, on the fourth day before the Kalends of January, when Agricola and Clementinus were consuls.
EDCS-11202055.summary: This is a dedication to the gods of the crossroads by Serenius Atticus for his well-being, dated to 396 AD.

EDCS-11202059.translation: To the genius of the first century of Iulius Maximus, Magius Bellianus.
EDCS-11202059.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of a centuria by Magius Bellianus.

EDCS-11202062.text_edition: \n Fronto Dregeni filius natione Ubius eques alae Indianae \n
EDCS-11202062.translation: Fronto, son of Dregentus, of Ubius by nationality, an equestrian of the ala Indiana.
EDCS-11202062.summary: This inscription records the name and origin of an equestrian soldier serving in the ala Indiana.

EDCS-11202063.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Ianuconius Vinco <ETV> et Avitia Apra et Vinconia Erepta votum ssolverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-11202063.translation: Ianuconius Vinco, and Avitia Apra, and Vinconia Erepta, gladly and joyfully paid their vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina as deserved.
EDCS-11202063.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Ianuconius Vinco, Avitia Apra, and Vinconia Erepta.

EDCS-11202064.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Cossus et I<u>noni Reginae votum libens laetus merito Caius Iulius\n
EDCS-11202064.translation: Caius Iulius paid his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, gladly, joyfully, and as deserved.
EDCS-11202064.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Caius Iulius.

EDCS-11202067.text_edition: \n Matribus Domesticis Cassius Fortunatus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202067.translation: Cassius Fortunatus gladly and deservedly paid his vow to the Domestic Mothers.
EDCS-11202067.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Matres Domesticæ by Cassius Fortunatus.

EDCS-11202157.translation: Gaius Licinius Crescens, soldier of the eleventh Claudian Pious Faithful legion, century of Coelius, paid his vow gladly, joyfully, and as deserved.
EDCS-11202157.summary: This is a votive dedication by Gaius Licinius Crescens, a soldier of the XI Claudia legion.

EDCS-11202160.translation: To the shades of the departed. Gaius Ennius Titus, son of Gaius, of the voting tribe Veturia, a soldier of the eleventh legion, century of Novius Castor, aged 36, with 9 years of service, lies here. His heirs arranged for this to be done according to his will.
EDCS-11202160.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gaius Ennius Titus, a soldier of the XI legion, who died at age 36 after 9 years of service.

EDCS-11202165.translation: To the shades of the departed. [---]
EDCS-11202165.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription.

EDCS-11202167.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iulio Sexto ex voto Amandi et Amatoris Nominatoris votum ssolverunt llibentes merito\n
EDCS-11202167.translation: Amandi and Amator Nominator paid their vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Iulius Sextus gladly and deservedly.
EDCS-11202167.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and Iulius Sextus by Amandi and Amator Nominator.

EDCS-11202168.text_edition: \n Apollini Granno Aulius Florius Gtus civis Trever vovit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202168.translation: To Apollo Grannus, Aulus Florius Gtus, a citizen of the Treveri, vowed willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-11202168.summary: A votive inscription to Apollo Grannus by a citizen of the Treveri.

EDCS-11202170.text_edition: \n Vosego Iulius Vitunis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202170.translation: Vosego Iulius Vitunis fulfilled his vow, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11202170.summary: A votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow by Vosego Iulius Vitunis.

EDCS-11202171.translation: Quint[---], soldier of the Legio VIII Augusta, beneficiary of a consul, on the Ides of [---] in the consulship of Mucianus and Fabius, fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11202171.summary: A military dedication, likely to a deity, by a soldier of Legio VIII Augusta, dated by consuls to the mid-3rd century CE.

EDCS-11202172.text_edition: \n Matri Deum Magnae et numinibus loci signum Dianae Gratinus rei publicae civitatis Vangionum servus arcarius et Decorata eius liberta publica ex voto posuerunt llibentes llaeti merito Imperatore domino nostro Traiano Decio Augusto et Grato consulibus\n
EDCS-11202172.translation: To the Mother of the Gods, Magna, and to the divine powers of the place, Gratinus, a slave and treasurer of the public affairs of the people of the Vangiones, and his freedwoman Decorata, a public freedwoman, set up this statue of Diana, willingly, gladly, and deservedly, during the reign of our lord Emperor Trajanus Decius Augustus and Gratus as consuls.
EDCS-11202172.summary: A dedication to the Mother of the Gods Magna and local deities, including Diana, by a slave and his freedwoman from the Vangiones, dated to 248 CE.

EDCS-11202173.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Flavius Primus in suo posuit libens laetus merito solvit\n
EDCS-11202173.translation: Flavius Primus set this up in his own property for Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-11202173.summary: A private dedication to Jupiter and Juno by Flavius Primus on his property.

EDCS-11202174.text_edition: \n Mercurio Augusto Vegetius Gattus ob honorem aedilitatis posuit\n
EDCS-11202174.translation: Vegetius Gattus set this up for Mercury Augustus in honor of his aedileship.
EDCS-11202174.summary: An honorary dedication to Mercury Augustus by Vegetius Gattus upon completing his term as aedile.

EDCS-11202175.text_edition: \n Virtuti Bellonae Bassiania Tacita votum solvit libens laeta merito sacerdotis Matris Deum Magnae\n
EDCS-11202175.translation: Bassiania Tacita, priestess of the Mother of the Gods Magna, fulfilled her vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly to Virtus and Bellona.
EDCS-11202175.summary: A votive inscription to Virtus and Bellona by Bassiania Tacita, a priestess of the Mother of the Gods Magna.

EDCS-11202177.text_edition: \n Gettonius Ursus Dossus legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis\n
EDCS-11202177.translation: Gettonius Ursus Dossus of the Legio XXII Primigenia, pious and loyal.
EDCS-11202177.summary: An inscription identifying Gettonius Ursus Dossus as a member of Legio XXII Primigenia.

EDCS-11202180.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio imparatore sic Lucio sic Septimio sic Severo sic vexillatio legionis XXII piae fidelis\n
EDCS-11202180.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the Genius, under the emperor, thus under Lucius, thus under Septimius, thus under Severus, by the detachment of the Legio XXII Pia Fidelis.
EDCS-11202180.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the Genius by a detachment of Legio XXII Pia Fidelis, dated during the Severan dynasty.

EDCS-11202181.translation: To Ostilius Genialis, from the corner of Quinilius (?), from Purpurio.
EDCS-11202181.summary: A dedication to Ostilius Genialis, possibly identifying a location or a gift from Purpurio.

EDCS-11202182.text_edition: \n Natalis miles legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis\n
EDCS-11202182.translation: Natalis, soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, loyal and faithful.
EDCS-11202182.summary: This is a tombstone for Natalis, a soldier of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11202185.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument for Annionius Securus, an individual from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11202186.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Maurus, likely a freedman, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11202187.translation: On the sixth day before the Ides of August.
EDCS-11202187.summary: This is a dating formula, possibly part of a larger inscription, indicating August 8th.

EDCS-11202191.summary: This inscription records the name Primus in his capacity as a magistrate, likely from a public building or a dedication.

EDCS-11202192.text_edition: \n III Idus Februarias Nominator Felicionis AN scri<b=R>it lapid III \n
EDCS-11202192.translation: On the third day before the Ides of February, Nominator Felicionis wrote on stone for the third time.
EDCS-11202192.summary: This inscription records an act of writing or commission by Nominator Felicionis on February 11th, possibly related to a funerary monument.

EDCS-11202199.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Silvanius Quintus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202199.translation: Silvanius Quintus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina.
EDCS-11202199.summary: This is a votive inscription by Silvanius Quintus dedicated to Jupiter and Juno, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11202200.translation: Titus Assonius Sappo arranged for this to be made during his lifetime for himself and his wife Aprilla, to the spirits of the departed.
EDCS-11202200.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Titus Assonius Sappo for himself and his wife Aprilla, indicating it was prepared while they were alive.

EDCS-11202201.text_edition: \n Cum sua aede Apollini deo Demionco Primius Poppillus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202201.translation: With his own shrine, Demioncus Primius Poppillus willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Apollo.
EDCS-11202201.summary: This is a votive inscription by Demioncus Primius Poppillus dedicating a shrine to Apollo, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11202204.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Misionius Victor Carmani Lugunnesi Cassi Martialis de suo posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202204.translation: Misionius Victor, son of Carmanus from Lugudunum, of Cassius Martialis, willingly, gladly, and deservedly placed this at his own expense and fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-11202204.summary: This is a votive inscription by Misionius Victor dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, likely from the Roman Imperial period, indicating his origin and patronage.

EDCS-11202205.text_edition: \n Apollini Granno Martius Senopatius Novellus dedicavit XV Kalendas Septembres Pisone et Iuliano consulibus\n
EDCS-11202205.translation: Martius Senopatius Novellus dedicated this to Apollo Grannus on the 18th day before the Kalends of September, during the consulship of Piso and Julianus.
EDCS-11202205.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Apollo Grannus by Martius Senopatius Novellus, dated to 152 AD.

EDCS-11202206.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription naming Sutta, daughter of Cantilius.

EDCS-11202209.text_edition: \n Mercurio Ianuarius Canti votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202209.translation: Ianuarius Canti gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-11202209.summary: This inscription records Ianuarius Canti fulfilling a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-11202210.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Dianae Avitus Candid votum solvit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-11202210.translation: In honor of the divine house, Avitus Candid gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the goddess Diana.
EDCS-11202210.summary: This inscription records a vow to Diana made in honor of the imperial family by Avitus Candid.

EDCS-11202211.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription possibly referring to a military unit or a centurion named Tet RA.

EDCS-11202212.translation: Troianus of Aquensis erected this to Mercury.
EDCS-11202212.summary: This inscription records Troianus of Aquensis setting up a monument to Mercury.

EDCS-11202214.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Iustus, son of Narcissus.
EDCS-11202214.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Iustus, son of Narcissus.

EDCS-11202215.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Deccio Magurio contubernalis liberta faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11202215.translation: Deccio Magurio, his fellow soldier, and the freedwoman arranged for this to be made.
EDCS-11202215.summary: This funerary inscription records that Deccio Magurio's contubernalis (fellow soldier or tent-mate) and a freedwoman arranged for his monument.

EDCS-11202216.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Flavius Bienus ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11202216.translation: Flavius Bienus erected this to Jupiter Best and Greatest in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11202216.summary: This inscription records Flavius Bienus erecting a monument to Jupiter Optimus Maximus in fulfillment of a vow.

EDCS-11202218.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Suationia Iustina Restituti f(ilia) v(otum) s(olvit) l(ibens) m(erito)\n
EDCS-11202218.translation: Suationia Iustina, daughter of Restitutus, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled her vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-11202218.summary: This inscription records Suationia Iustina fulfilling a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maxsimus.

EDCS-11202219.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Herecurae Iulius Verus pro se et suis posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202219.translation: In honor of the divine house, Julius Verus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly set this up for the goddess Hercules, for himself and his family.
EDCS-11202219.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Hercules by Julius Verus for his family, likely from the imperial period given the phrase 'domus divinae'.

EDCS-11202220.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Paterno Aprili<u>s Cresc<e>ns votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202220.translation: Aprilius Crescens gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest Paternos.
EDCS-11202220.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter by Aprilius Crescens, likely a private dedication.

EDCS-11202221.text_edition: \n Genio Dasagensium Magiatus et Flavius Senecianus de suo posuerunt\n
EDCS-11202221.translation: Magiatus and Flavius Senecianus set this up from their own funds for the Genius of the Dasagensians.
EDCS-11202221.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Magiatus and Flavius Senecianus to the Genius of the Dasagensians, likely a local community cult.

EDCS-11202222.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Aureliis Saluda et Regretho fratribus quondam equitibus novae alae firmae catafractariae AVR Aurelius Abdetathus frater eorum faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-11202222.translation: For the departed spirits of Aurelius Saluda and Regrethus, formerly brothers and cavalrymen of the new, firm, armored ala, their brother Aurelius Abdetathus had this made.
EDCS-11202222.summary: This is a funerary inscription for two brothers, Aurelius Saluda and Regrethus, who were cavalrymen, with the monument erected by their brother Aurelius Abdetathus.

EDCS-11202224.text_edition: \n co C Commodus ex voto posuit\n
EDCS-11202224.translation: Commodus set this up in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11202224.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Commodus in fulfillment of a vow, likely a private votive offering.

EDCS-11202225.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Av<i=T>tius Maiiorinus et Avitius Apollinaris decuriones civitatis Aureliae G S ex voto posuerunt \n
EDCS-11202225.translation: Avitius Maiiorinus and Avitius Apollinaris, decurions of the Aurelian community, set this up by vow for the god Mercury.
EDCS-11202225.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Mercury by two decurions of the Aurelian community, likely a public or semi-public offering.

EDCS-11202227.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Cobrunius Divixtus optio ex voto posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11202227.translation: In honor of the divine house, Cobrunius Divixtus, a optio, set this up by vow, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly, to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-11202227.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter by an optio named Cobrunius Divixtus, made in honor of the 'divine house' (imperial family), suggesting a period from the 1st century AD onwards.

EDCS-11202228.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Ateius Genialis civis Trever heres filius posuit\n
EDCS-11202228.translation: For the departed spirits of Ateius Genialis, a citizen of Trier, his heir, placed this.
EDCS-11202228.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ateius Genialis, a citizen of Trier, with the monument erected by his heir.

EDCS-11202229.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Diadumeno alumno vernae delicato suo nnorum XVI Felicionis liberti sui filio Marcus Ulpius Vannius |(centurio) legionis VIII Augustae patronus fecit hoc monumentum heredem non sequetur\n
EDCS-11202229.translation: For the departed spirits of Diadumenus, his cherished freedman pupil of sixteen years, son of Felicionis, Marcus Ulpius Vannius, a centurion of the Eighth Augustan Legion, his patron, made this monument; it will not pass to his heir.
EDCS-11202229.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Diadumenus, a young freedman pupil and son of Felicionis, commemorated by his patron Marcus Ulpius Vannius, a centurion, with a clause preventing inheritance.

EDCS-11202232.text_edition: \n Lucius Tanusius Luci Romilia Ateste annorum L stipendiorum XX Quintus Tanusius Luci Romilia Ateste annorum XXXX stipendiorum XX milites legionis XIIII geminae centuria C VoB \n
EDCS-11202232.translation: Lucius Tanusius Luci Romilia Ateste, aged 50, with 20 years of service, and Quintus Tanusius Luci Romilia Ateste, aged 40, with 20 years of service, soldiers of the XIV Gemina Legion, centuria C VoB.
EDCS-11202232.summary: This inscription records two soldiers, Lucius and Quintus Tanusius, of the XIV Gemina Legion, noting their ages and years of service, likely a tombstone or memorial.

EDCS-11202233.text_edition: \n Lucius Sterna Marci filius Scaptia Florentia nnum XXX miles legionis XVI stipendiorum \n
EDCS-11202233.translation: Lucius Sterna, son of Marcus, from the tribe Scaptia, Florentia, aged 30, a soldier of the 16th legion, with 30 years of service.
EDCS-11202233.summary: This inscription records the tombstone of Lucius Sterna, a soldier of the 16th legion, who died at the age of 30 after 30 years of service.

EDCS-11202235.text_edition: \n Paulla Tiberi Iuli Selvani sic ex cohorte Surorum nnrum XXIIX hic sita est hospes si vacuum est tumuli cognoscere cassus sic perlege nam mortis [] caussa sic dolenda fuuit sic dic rogo nunc iuvenis sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-11202235.translation: Paulla, wife of Tiberius Iulius Selvanus, here she lies, aged 28, formerly of the Cohors Surorum. Stranger, if you find this tomb empty, read on, for the cause of death was so pitiable. So, I beg you now, young man, may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11202235.summary: This inscription is a tombstone for Paulla, who died at age 28, with a plea to the reader to remember her pitiable death and wish her a peaceful rest.

EDCS-11202236.text_edition: \n Sterio Eximni filius Focunas miles nnorum XL stipendiorum XVI ex cohorte Raetorum et Vendelicorum sic hic situs est\n
EDCS-11202236.translation: Sterio Eximni, son of Focunas, aged 40, a soldier with 16 years of service, from the Cohors Raetorum et Vendelicorum, lies here.
EDCS-11202236.summary: This inscription records the burial of Sterio Eximni, a soldier of the Cohors Raetorum et Vendelicorum, who died at age 40 after 16 years of service.

EDCS-11202237.text_edition: \n Nunadus Sacri filius Runicas miles ex cohorte Raetorum et Vindelicorum nnrum XXXIIII stipendiorum XI hic situs est hered<e>s |(centuriones) Rufus et Munnius\n
EDCS-11202237.translation: Nunadus Sacri, son of Runicas, aged 34, a soldier with 11 years of service, from the Cohors Raetorum et Vindelicorum, lies here. His heirs are the centurions Rufus and Munnius.
EDCS-11202237.summary: This inscription records the burial of Nunadus Sacri, a soldier of the Cohors Raetorum et Vindelicorum, who died at age 34 after 11 years of service, with his heirs named.

EDCS-11202238.translation: [...]us Iucundus, a volunteer soldier of the 24th cohort, aged 50, with 21 years of service.
EDCS-11202238.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a soldier named Iucundus who served as a volunteer in the 24th cohort for 21 years, dying at age 50.

EDCS-11202239.translation: Liviae Livillae, freedwoman, Spendusa lies here. Crescens, freedman of Licina.
EDCS-11202239.summary: This inscription marks the burial place of Spendusa, freedwoman of Liviae Livillae, with Crescens, freedman of Licina, also mentioned, likely as a relation or benefactor.

EDCS-11202242.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus et perpetuae securitati Aproniae coniugi Antistius Aper PI Antistia Apra filia \n
EDCS-11202242.translation: To the divine spirits and eternal peace, for Apronia, wife, from Antistius Aper and Antistia Apra, daughter.
EDCS-11202242.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Antistius Aper and his daughter Antistia Apra to the divine spirits and for the eternal peace of Apronia, the wife and mother.

EDCS-11202245.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription mentioning a person named Tantius and their father.

EDCS-11202247.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus perpetuae securitati Quinto Avitio Hermeti medico coniugi TXE \n
EDCS-11202247.translation: To the divine spirits and eternal peace, for Quintus Avitius Hermetus, physician, husband.
EDCS-11202247.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a wife (indicated by TXE) to the divine spirits and for the eternal peace of her husband, Quintus Avitius Hermetus, a physician.

EDCS-11202248.translation: [...] Aurelius CO NIC [...] lived 21 years [...] O MA[---] / SPECIA [...] and Coblunius Ar[---] / [son of ...] of the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis, to his father [...] and to his most devoted brothers [...] and Cam() Vat[---] / veteran of the aforementioned legion, a man [...], by testament [...].
EDCS-11202248.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription is a testament dedicating property or honors to the deceased's father, brothers, and possibly other family members, mentioning military service in the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis.

EDCS-11202254.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ammosius Vitalis took care to have this made for Cassia Rufina and Iullinius Germanicus, who have died.
EDCS-11202254.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Ammosius Vitalis for Cassia Rufina and Iullinius Germanicus.

EDCS-11202255.summary: This fragment likely refers to a person named Provincialis, possibly part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-11202261.text_edition: \n Contuinda Esucconis fili-- Silvano Ategnissae filio heres ex testamento fecit\n
EDCS-11202261.translation: Contuinda, daughter of Esucconis, made this for her heir Silvanus, son of Ategnissae, according to the will.
EDCS-11202261.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by Contuinda for her heir Silvanus, as stipulated in a will.

EDCS-11202262.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Excingiorigiati et Rosmertae Caius Saturninius Viriaucus votum solvit libens laetus merito aedem donum dedit\n
EDCS-11202262.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Saturninius Viriaucus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to the god Mercurius Excingiorigiati and Rosmerta and dedicated this shrine as a gift.
EDCS-11202262.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a shrine to Mercury and Rosmerta by Caius Saturninius Viriaucus, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-11202263.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Dianae Victorius Amator votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11202263.translation: In honor of the divine house, Victorius Amator willingly and deservedly paid his vow to the goddess Diana.
EDCS-11202263.summary: This is a votive inscription to the goddess Diana by Victorius Amator, likely in the imperial period.

EDCS-11202264.translation: Here rests in peace Ragnoaldus the innocent, dear to his parents; he lived 7 years and departed from this world in February on the 7th day.
EDCS-11202264.summary: This is a Christian tombstone recording the death of Ragnoaldus at the age of 7 in February.

EDCS-11202265.translation: Here rests in peace Fredericus, who lived 50 years in this world; he died in peace in the month of June on the fifth day.
EDCS-11202265.summary: This is a Christian tombstone recording the death of Fredericus at the age of 50 in June.

EDCS-11202266.translation: Here rests in peace Gundoaldus, who lived [3] years in this world, and his burial was on the 20th of January.
EDCS-11202266.summary: This is a Christian tombstone recording the death of Gundoaldus, who lived an unknown number of years, with his burial on January 20th.

EDCS-11800685.translation: To the spirits of the departed for Martina [---] II
EDCS-11800685.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Martina.

EDCS-11800686.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Restitutus Ripani filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11800686.translation: Restitutus, son of Ripanus, willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-11800686.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Restitutus, son of Ripanus.

EDCS-11800746.translation: To Nigrus, [son of ---], in the capacity of [---]
EDCS-11800746.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely recording a dedication, possibly to a person named Nigrus.

EDCS-11800764.summary: This is an ownership mark from the workshop of Vitalis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11800771.summary: This is an ownership mark from the workshop of Caius Vibius (?), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801067.text_edition: \n Publio Annio Teretina Montano optioni et quaestori equitum interregi legionis XXI decurioni coloniae Equestris Annia Sabina flaminica Augustae patri\n
EDCS-11801067.translation: To Publius Annius Terentinus Montanus, junior officer and quaestor of the cavalry, interim commander of the 21st Legion, councilor of the colony of Equus, from Annia Sabina, priestess of Augusta, his father.
EDCS-11801067.summary: This is a dedication by Annia Sabina to her father, Publius Annius Terentinus Montanus, who held several military and civic positions, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801070.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld, Cintusmus son of Cintugnatus.
EDCS-11801070.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the departed soul of Cintusmus, son of Cintugnatus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801071.text_edition: \n Deo Apolloni Verilla Vei filia votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-11801071.translation: To the god Apollo, Verilla, daughter of Veius, gladly fulfilled her vow as deserved.
EDCS-11801071.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Apollo by Verilla, daughter of Veius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801073.text_edition: \n Quintus Sertorius Quinti filius Voltinia Vienna Quadratus hic situs est veteranus ex legione II Quintus Sertorius Soetrus libertus ex testamento fecit\n
EDCS-11801073.translation: Quintus Sertorius Quintus son Voltinia Vienna Quadratus, a veteran of the 2nd Legion, rests here; his freedman Quintus Sertorius Soetrus made this by his will.
EDCS-11801073.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintus Sertorius Quadratus, a veteran of the 2nd Legion, with a dedication by his freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801074.text_edition: \n Bibiae sic Tribiae sic Quadrubiae sic\n
EDCS-11801074.translation: To Bibia, so also to Tribia, so also to Quadrubia.
EDCS-11801074.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly recording multiple burials or dedications to women named Bibia, Tribia, and Quadrubia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801080.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Secco Secconianus Quartinus votum solverunt laeti libentes merito\n
EDCS-11801080.translation: In honor of the divine house, Secco and Secconianus Quartinus gladly fulfilled their vows as deserved.
EDCS-11801080.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating fulfillment of vows in honor of the imperial family, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801082.summary: This inscription records an action taken by Sempronianus, possibly in an official capacity related to the 21st legion or cohort, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11801083.text_edition: \n Salutabis meis verbis Fortunatum meum et Maximum meum BARIV VIIII Maias Dabis Ario eques turma Septumi sic\n
EDCS-11801083.translation: Greet my Salutis with my words, my Fortunatus and my Maximus. On the Ides of May, give to Arius, cavalryman of the troop of Septimius.
EDCS-11801083.summary: This is a personal letter, likely an epitaph or a dedication, mentioning individuals and a date.

EDCS-11801084.text_edition: \n Marcus Iulius Hermes Frontinianus PNNF FF\n
EDCS-11801084.translation: Marcus Julius Hermes Frontinianus, son of freedmen, son of freedmen.
EDCS-11801084.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely from a tombstone or similar monument, indicating lineage.

EDCS-11801087.text_edition: \n Mercurio et Maiiae sic Lucius Cavarius Ibliomarus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-11801087.translation: To Mercury and Maia, Lucius Cavarius Ibliomarus willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-11801087.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the gods Mercury and Maia by Lucius Cavarius Ibliomarus.

EDCS-12000412.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Viselliae Firmae Visellius Firminus et Iulia Secunda parentes infelicissimi vixit anno I diebus L\n
EDCS-12000412.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Visellius Firminus and Iulia Secunda, most unhappy parents, for their Visellia Firma, who lived 1 year and 50 days.
EDCS-12000412.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Visellia Firma, set up by her parents, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-12200133.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, likely a funerary dedication to a son named Musticius.

EDCS-12200135.summary: This is a dedication to the god Apollo by Otacilia.

EDCS-12200136.text_edition: \n Apollini et Marti Adventius Tocca votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12200136.translation: To Apollo and Mars, Adventius Tocca willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-12200136.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the gods Apollo and Mars by Adventius Tocca.

EDCS-12200137.text_edition: \n Marti Caturici et Apollini Gaius Iulius Belatullus de suo donum dedit\n
EDCS-12200137.translation: To Mars of Caturix and Apollo, Gaius Julius Belatullus gave this gift at his own expense.
EDCS-12200137.summary: This is a dedication to the gods Mars Caturix and Apollo by Gaius Julius Belatullus.

EDCS-12200139.text_edition: \n Marti Caturigi Silvano Pompeius Optatus et Augusto ex stipe R \n
EDCS-12200139.translation: To Mars of Caturix, Silvanus, and Augustus, Pompeius Optatus from the sacred offerings...
EDCS-12200139.summary: This is a dedication to the gods Mars Caturix, Silvanus, and Augustus by Pompeius Optatus, funded by offerings.

EDCS-12200140.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Cissonio Lucius C Paternus ex voto\n
EDCS-12200140.translation: To the god Mercury Cissonius, Lucius C. Paternus, according to his vow.
EDCS-12200140.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury Cissonius by Lucius C. Paternus.

EDCS-12200141.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be an offering or dedication to a deity or individual named Suleia Atumara.

EDCS-12200142.translation: Decimus Iulius Consors, son of Caius, of the Fabia tribe, priest of the Augustales, magistrate, curator of Roman citizens of the Helvetian assembly, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12200142.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Decimus Iulius Consors, an official of the Augustales and a curator, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200150.text_edition: \n Titus Crassicius Pattusius et Crassicius Magius Suleviis suis votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-12200150.translation: Titus Crassicius Pattusius and Crassicius Magius willingly and deservedly paid their vow to their Suleviae.
EDCS-12200150.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Titus Crassicius Pattusius and Crassicius Magius to their 'Suleviae', likely referring to female deities or perhaps deified ancestors, possibly from the 1st century CE.

EDCS-12200151.text_edition: \n Apollini Lucius Munatius Marci filius Teretina Gallus \n
EDCS-12200151.translation: Lucius Munatius Gallus, son of Marcus, of the Teretina tribe, [dedicated this] to Apollo.
EDCS-12200151.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Apollo by Lucius Munatius Gallus, a soldier, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200152.text_edition: \n Deum dearum aram posuit Marcus Masterna miles legionis XI Claudiae piae felicis centuria Crispi libens posuit\n
EDCS-12200152.translation: Marcus Masterna, a soldier of the 11th Claudia Pia Felix legion, of Crispus's centuria, willingly erected this altar to the gods and goddesses.
EDCS-12200152.summary: This inscription records Marcus Masterna, a soldier of the 11th Claudia Pia Felix legion, dedicating an altar to the gods and goddesses, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200153.text_edition: \n Fortunae Nyisus Publi servus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12200153.translation: Nyisus, the slave of Publius, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to Fortuna.
EDCS-12200153.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Fortuna by Nyisus, the slave of Publius, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200155.text_edition: \n Marti votum Tiberius Iulius Agilis gladiarius solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12200155.translation: Tiberius Iulius Agilis, the gladiator, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to Mars.
EDCS-12200155.summary: This inscription records a vow paid to Mars by Tiberius Iulius Agilis, a gladiator, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200156.text_edition: \n Marti Quintus Iulius Titullinus ex voto\n
EDCS-12200156.translation: Quintus Iulius Titullinus [fulfilled his vow] to Mars.
EDCS-12200156.summary: This inscription records Quintus Iulius Titullinus fulfilling a vow to Mars, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200157.translation: Caius Novellius Primus, veteran of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to Mars.
EDCS-12200157.summary: This inscription records Caius Novellius Primus, a veteran of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, fulfilling a vow to Mars, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200158.text_edition: \n Nymphis Caius Viselius Verecundus veteranus legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12200158.translation: Caius Viselius Verecundus, veteran of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow to the Nymphs.
EDCS-12200158.summary: This inscription records Caius Viselius Verecundus, a veteran of the 11th Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, dedicating an offering to the Nymphs, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12200159.text_edition: \n Silvano Lucius Flavius Burrus miles legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria Betuvi Silonis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12200159.translation: To Silvanus, Lucius Flavius Burrus, soldier of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion, from the century of Betuvius Silon, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12200159.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion fulfilling a vow to the god Silvanus.

EDCS-12200162.summary: This inscription is a very brief dedication or naming of Gaius Julius Severus.

EDCS-12200171.summary: This inscription refers to a specific centuria, the Valerian century, and possibly an imperial connection.

EDCS-12200173.text_edition: \n Lucius Rutilius Luci filius Sergia Macrinus Pi miles legionis |(centuriae) Provincialis stipendiorum \n
EDCS-12200173.translation: Lucius Rutilius Macrinus, son of Lucius, of the Sergia tribe, soldier of the Provincialis century, with [specified number of] years of service.
EDCS-12200173.summary: This inscription identifies Lucius Rutilius Macrinus, a soldier with service time in the Provincialis century.

EDCS-12200174.text_edition: \n Superi tribuni ex legione XI Claudia pia fideli\n
EDCS-12200174.translation: The tribunes from the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion.
EDCS-12200174.summary: This inscription lists tribunes who served in the XI Claudia Pia Fidelis legion.

EDCS-12200175.text_edition: \n centuria Arelli Flammae Caius Valerius Longus\n
EDCS-12200175.translation: From the century of Arellius Flamma, Gaius Valerius Longus.
EDCS-12200175.summary: This inscription names Gaius Valerius Longus and his association with the century of Arellius Flamma.

EDCS-12200176.translation: From the century of Lucius Serranus Attienus.
EDCS-12200176.summary: This inscription names Lucius Serranus Attienus and his association with a century.

EDCS-12200177.translation: From the century of Iulius Clementis.
EDCS-12200177.summary: This inscription names Iulius Clementis and his association with a century.

EDCS-12200178.translation: From the century of Postumius, Lucius Trosius.
EDCS-12200178.summary: This inscription names Lucius Trosius and his association with the century of Postumius.

EDCS-12200181.summary: This inscription is a brief naming or dedication of Gaius Trosius Spes.

EDCS-12300041.translation: With our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, perpetual emperors, built by Summa Rapida for the perpetual victors, under the supervision of [---], during the consulship of our lord Gratian II and Probus, a man of consular rank.
EDCS-12300041.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely commemorating a building project, possibly related to military infrastructure, from the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-12300042.translation: With our lords Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, perpetual emperors, the eighth legion Augustan built a fort at Raurica on the border, under the supervision of [---], prefect, during the consulship of our lord Gratian II and Flavius Probus, a man of consular rank.
EDCS-12300042.summary: This inscription records the construction of a fort at Raurica by the eighth legion Augustan, dedicated to the emperors Valentinian, Valens, and Gratian, likely dating to the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-12300043.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Eponae Lucius Sollius F Sollius \n
EDCS-12300043.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Sollius F Sollius dedicated to the goddess Epona.
EDCS-12300043.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Epona, honoring the imperial family, likely set up by Lucius Sollius F Sollius.

EDCS-12300044.text_edition: \n Tis Augusti dispensator horreorum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12300044.translation: Tis, steward of the granaries of Augustus, willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12300044.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by Tis, a steward of imperial granaries, likely during the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300045.text_edition: \n Heniochus de proprio dedit ponendum curavit Amor liberetus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12300045.translation: Heniochus gave this from his own resources and Amor liberetus arranged for its placement; he fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-12300045.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled and a monument dedicated by Heniochus and Amor liberetus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300051.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Rhenicio Regali Rhenicus pater vivus posuit\n
EDCS-12300051.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Rhenicus, his father, erected this for Rhenicio Regali while he was alive.
EDCS-12300051.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rhenicio Regali, set up by his father Rhenicus, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300052.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Lucius Succ [---]
EDCS-12300052.summary: This is a partial funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, likely for Lucius Succ, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300058.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Ageronius Maximus [---]
EDCS-12300058.summary: This is a partial funerary inscription dedicated to the spirits of the departed, likely for Ageronius Maximus, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300059.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae pro salute Sexti Maeni Pudentis\n
EDCS-12300059.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, for the safety of Sextus Maenius Pudentis.
EDCS-12300059.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mithras for the well-being of Sextus Maenius Pudentis, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300060.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sacer vixit nnos XXXIV\n
EDCS-12300060.translation: To the spirits of the departed: Sacer lived 34 years.
EDCS-12300060.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Sacer at the age of 34, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-12300061.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for Meluronus Spirnus.
EDCS-12300061.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Meluronus Spirnus, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-12300109.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Seuvo Seccali in suo ex voto posuit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-12300109.translation: Seuvo Seccali joyfully, willingly, and deservedly set this up in his own property in fulfillment of a vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina.
EDCS-12300109.summary: This is a votive inscription by Seuvo Seccali dedicated to Jupiter and Juno, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300110.text_edition: \n Marti Loucetio votum solvit libens laetus merito Fittio Condolli filius eques ala Petriana Treverorum\n
EDCS-12300110.translation: Fittius son of Condollus, a cavalryman of the Petriana ala of the Treveri, joyfully, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mars Loucetius.
EDCS-12300110.summary: This is a votive inscription by Fittius Condolli, a cavalryman, to the god Mars Loucetius, possibly dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300111.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Atti Cantinius Capell votum solvit libens laetus\n
EDCS-12300111.translation: In honor of the divine house, Cantinius Capell joyfully and willingly fulfilled his vow to the god Atti.
EDCS-12300111.summary: This is a votive inscription by Cantinius Capell dedicated to the god Atti, likely in honor of the imperial family, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300112.text_edition: \n Deo Cissonio Cittonius Pippausus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12300112.translation: Cittonius Pippausus joyfully, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the god Cissonius.
EDCS-12300112.summary: This is a votive inscription by Cittonius Pippausus to the god Cissonius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300113.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mithrae Caius Celsinius Matutinus veteranus legionis VIII Augustae Alexandrianae typum de suo repinxit\n
EDCS-12300113.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Celsinius Matutinus, a veteran of the Legio VIII Augusta Alexandriana, repainted the image from his own resources.
EDCS-12300113.summary: This is an inscription by Caius Celsinius Matutinus, a veteran, honoring the emperor and the god Mithras, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300114.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mithrae Caius Celsinius Matutinus veteranus legionis VIII Augustae Alexand[rianae typu]m de suo repinxit\n
EDCS-12300114.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Celsinius Matutinus, a veteran of the Legio VIII Augusta Alexandriana, repainted the image from his own resources.
EDCS-12300114.summary: This is an inscription by Caius Celsinius Matutinus, a veteran, honoring the emperor and the god Mithras, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300115.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mithrae Matto Gnati votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12300115.translation: In honor of the divine house, Matto Gnati joyfully, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Invincible God Mithras.
EDCS-12300115.summary: This is a votive inscription by Matto Gnati dedicated to the god Mithras and honoring the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300118.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Primus ASE votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12300118.translation: Primus ASE joyfully, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the Invincible God.
EDCS-12300118.summary: This is a votive inscription by Primus ASE to an Invincible God, likely Mithras, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300120.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mythrae sic Secu\n
EDCS-12300120.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Invincible God Mithras, Sic Secu...
EDCS-12300120.summary: This is an incomplete votive inscription dedicated to the god Mithras and honoring the imperial family, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12300131.translation: Marcus [?], of the [?] legion VIII Augusta, fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly.
EDCS-12300131.summary: This is a military dedication by an unknown soldier of the Legio VIII Augusta, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12300138.text_edition: \n Titus Albius Lemonia Bononia annorum XL stipendiorum XVII hic situs est\n
EDCS-12300138.translation: Titus Albius, from the Lemonia tribe, from Bononia, aged 40, with 17 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-12300138.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Albius, a soldier who served for 17 years, likely from the late 1st to early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12300227.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Vespasianus Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate VIIII imperator XVIIII pater patriae censor consul VIII designatus VIIII equitibus et peditibus qui militant in alis sex Noricorum et singularium et Moesica et Afrorum veterana et Siliana et Sulpicia et cohorte I Flavia Hispanorum quae sunt in Germania sub Quinto Iulio Cordino Rutilio Gallico qui quina et vicena stipendia aut plura meruerant quorum nomina subscripta sunt ipsis liberis posterisque eorum civitatem dedit et conubium cum uxoribus quas tunc habuissent cum est civitas iis data aut si qui caelibes essent cum iis quas postea duxissent dumtaxat singuli singulas ante diem XVII Kalendas Maias Decimo Novio Prisco Lucio Ceionio Commodo consulibus alae Moesicae cui praeest Titus Staberius Titi filius Quirina Secundus gregali Tertio Marci filio Treviro descriptum et recognitum ex tabula aenea quae fixa est Romae in Capitolio post casam Romuli Imperator Caesar Vespasianus Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate VIIII imperator XVIIII pater patriae censor consul VIII designatus VIIII equitibus et peditibus qui militant in alis sex Noricorum et singularium et Moesica et Afrorum veterana et Siliana et Sulpicia et cohorte I Flavia Hispanorum quae sunt in Germania sub Quinto Iulio Cordino Rutilio Gallioo sic qui quina et vicena stipendia aut plura meruerant quorum nomina subscripta sunt ipsis liberis posterisque eorum civitatem dedit et conubium cum uxoribus quas tunc habuissent cum est civitas iis data aut si qui caelibes essent cum iis quas postea duxissent dumtaxat singuli singulas ante diem XVII Kalendas Maias Decimo Novio Prisco Lucio Ceionio Commodo consulibus alae Moesicae cui praeest Titus Staberius Titi filius Quirina Secundus gregali Tertio Marci filio Treviro descriptum et recognitum ex tabula aenea quae fixa est Romae in Capitolio Auli Titini Iusti Cai Alfi Prisci Quinti Lolli Pietatis Manli Egnati Celeris Luci Aureli Potiti Luci Turrani Maximi Publi Atini Rufi\n
EDCS-12300227.translation: Emperor Caesar Vespasian Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 9th time, acclaimed imperator for the 19th time, father of the fatherland, censor, consul for the 8th time, designated consul for the 9th time, has granted citizenship and the right to marry to the cavalrymen and infantrymen serving in the six alae Noricorum, Singularium, Moesica, Afrorum Veterana, Siliana, and Sulpicia, and in the I Flavia Hispanorum cohort, which are in Germania under Quintus Julius Cordino Rutilius Gallicus, to those who had completed or would complete twenty-five years or more of service, to them, their children, and their descendants. And if they were unmarried, he granted them the right to marry the women they would subsequently take, provided each man took only one wife. This was done on the 17th day before the Kalends of May, under the consulship of Decimus Novius Priscus and Lucius Ceionius Commodus. For the ala Moesica, which is commanded by Titus Staberius Secundus, son of Titus, of the Quirina tribe, from Treveri, a regular soldier. This record and confirmation is taken from the bronze tablet fixed in Rome on the Capitol, behind the hut of Romulus. [List of witnesses follows.]
EDCS-12300227.summary: This is an imperial grant of citizenship and marriage rights by Emperor Vespasian to auxiliary soldiers who had completed 25 years of service, issued in 79 CE.

EDCS-12300240.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Vespasiani filius Domitianus Augustus Germanicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate X imperator XXI censor perpetuus consul XV pater patriae equitibus qui militant in alis quattuor I Flavia Gemina I Cannenefatium I singularium Scubulorum et peditibus et equitibus qui in cohortibus decem et quattuor I Flavia Damascenorum milliaria I Biturigum I Thracum I Aquitanorum veterana I Asturum II Aquitanorum II Cyrenaica II Raetorum III Delmatarum III et IIII Aquitanorum IIII Vindelicorum V Delmatarum VII Raetorum quae sunt in Germania superiore sub Lucio Iavoleno Prisco item dimissis honesta missione quinis et vicenis pluribusve stipendiis emeritis quorum nomina subscripta sunt ipsis liberis posterisque eorum civitatem dedit et conubium cum uxoribus quas tunc habuissent cum est civitas iis data aut si qui caelibes essent cum iis quas postea duxissent dumtaxat singuli singulas ante diem VI Kalendas Novembres Albio Pullaieno Pollione Cnaeo Pompeio Longino consulibus cohortis I Aquitanorum veteranae cui praeest Marcus Arrecinus Gemellus equiti Mucapori Eptacentis filio Thraci descriptum et recognitum ex tabula aenea quae fixa est Romae in muro post templum divi Augusti ad Minervam Imperator Caesar divi Vespasiani filius Domitianus Augustus Germanicus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate X imperator XXI censor perpetuus consul XV pater patriae equitibus qui militant in alis quattuor I Flavia gemina I Cannenefatium I singularium Scubulorum et peditibus et equitibus qui in cohortibus decem et quattuor I Flavia Damascenorum milliaria I Biturigum I Thracum I Aquitanorum veterana I Asturum II Aquitanorum II Cyrenaica II Raetorum III Delmatarum III et IIII Aquitanorum IIII Vindelicorum V Dalmatarum VII Raetorum quae sunt in Germania superiore sub Lucio Iavoleno Prisco item dimissis honesta missione quinis et vicenis pluribusve stipendiis emeritis quorum nomina subscripta sunt ipsis liberis posterisque eorum civitatem dedit et conubium cum uxoribus quas tunc habuissent cum est civitas iis da<t=I>a aut si qui caelibes essent cum iis quas postea duxissent dumtaxat singuli singulas ante diem VI Kalendas Novembres Albio Pullaieno Pollione Cnaeo Pompeio Longino consulibus cohortis I Aquitanorum veteranae cui praeest Marcus Arrecinus Gemellus equiti Mucapori <E=I>ptacentis filio Thraci descriptum et recognitum ex tabula aenea quae <f=E>ixa est Romae Quinti Muci Augustalis Luci Pulli Verecundi Cai Lucreti Modesti Cai Pompei Eutrapeli Cai Iuli Clementis Quinti Vetti Octavi Luci Pulli Ianuari \n
EDCS-12300240.translation: Emperor Caesar Domitian Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Vespasian, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 10th time, acclaimed imperator for the 21st time, perpetual censor, consul for the 15th time, father of the fatherland, has granted citizenship and the right to marry to the cavalrymen serving in the four alae I Flavia Gemina, I Cannenefatium, I Singularium Scubulorum, and to the infantrymen and cavalrymen serving in the fourteen cohorts, namely I Flavia Damascenorum milliaria, I Biturigum, I Thracum, I Aquitanorum Veterana, I Asturum, II Aquitanorum, II Cyrenaica, II Raetorum, III Delmatarum, III and IV Aquitanorum, IV Vindelicorum, V Delmatarum, VII Raetorum, which are in Germania Superior under Lucius Iavolenus Priscus, and also to those discharged with honorable dismissal after serving twenty-five or more years of service, to them, their children, and their descendants. And if they were unmarried, he granted them the right to marry the women they would subsequently take, provided each man took only one wife. This was done on the 6th day before the Kalends of November, under the consulship of Albius Pullaienus Pollio and Gnaeus Pompeius Longinus. For the I Aquitanorum Veterana cohort, which is commanded by Marcus Arrecinus Gemellus, to Mucapor, son of Eptacentis, a Thracian cavalryman. This record and confirmation is taken from the bronze tablet fixed in Rome on the wall behind the temple of the deified Augustus, near the temple of Minerva. [List of witnesses follows.]
EDCS-12300240.summary: This is an imperial grant of citizenship and marriage rights by Emperor Domitian to auxiliary soldiers who had completed 25 years of service, issued in 91 CE.

EDCS-12400226.text_edition: \n Imperatori Nervae Traiano Caesari Augusto Germanico divi Nervae filio pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae consuli II Ves<o=A>ntione milia passuum XXXXIIX \n
EDCS-12400226.translation: To Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Nerva, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul for the 2nd time. From Vesontio, 48 miles.
EDCS-12400226.summary: This is an milestone inscription indicating a road distance from Vesontio (Besançon) to an unknown destination, dating to Trajan's reign (98-117 CE).

EDCS-12400239.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Traiano Hadriano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli III patri patriae Aventicum milia passuum XXXXI\n
EDCS-12400239.translation: To Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrianus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the 3rd time, father of the fatherland. From Aventicum, 41 miles.
EDCS-12400239.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a road distance from Aventicum (Avenches) to an unknown destination, dating to Hadrian's reign (117-138 CE).

EDCS-12400302.translation: To Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland. From Augusta Treverorum, 88 miles.
EDCS-12400302.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a road distance from Augusta Treverorum (Trier), dating to Antoninus Pius' reign (138-161 CE).

EDCS-12400306.translation: The Restorers of the state, the Liberators of the fatherland, Valentinianus and Valens, victorious Emperors always, have made this at their own expense for the public good.
EDCS-12400306.summary: This inscription honors the emperors Valentinian I and Valens, likely commemorating a public work funded by them, dating to their joint rule (364-375 CE).

EDCS-12400313.translation: [Emperor Nerva] Caesar Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul for the 3rd time. From Mogontiacum, 60 miles.
EDCS-12400313.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a road distance from Mogontiacum (Mainz), dating to Nerva's reign (96-98 CE).

EDCS-12400314.translation: [Tiberius Claudius] Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 4th time, acclaimed imperator for the 8th time, consul designated for the 4th time, father of the fatherland. From Mogontiacum, 59 miles.
EDCS-12400314.summary: This is a milestone inscription indicating a road distance from Mogontiacum (Mainz), dating to Claudius' reign (41-54 CE).

EDCS-12400315.translation: To Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Nerva, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the country, consul for the second time, from Mogontiacum 59 miles.
EDCS-12400315.summary: This milestone records a road measurement from Mogontiacum commissioned by Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-12400317.text_edition: \n Marco Aurelio Numeriano nobilissimo Caesari a Mogontiaco leugas \n
EDCS-12400317.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Numerianus, most noble Caesar, from Mogontiacum [X] leagues.
EDCS-12400317.summary: This inscription records a road measurement from Mogontiacum dedicated to Caesar Marcus Aurelius Numerianus.

EDCS-12400336.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Claudio Tacito Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestare consuli proconsuli Aventico leugas LVI\n
EDCS-12400336.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Claudius Tacitus, Invictus Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, consul, proconsul, from Aventicum 56 leagues.
EDCS-12400336.summary: This milestone records a road measurement from Aventicum dedicated to Emperor Tacitus.

EDCS-12400337.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Nervae filio Nervae Traiano Augusto Germanico pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli II patri patriae designato III milia passuum LXXXV\n
EDCS-12400337.translation: To Emperor Caesar Nerva Trajan Augustus Germanicus, son of the deified Nerva, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, consul for the second time, father of the country, designated for the third time, 85 miles.
EDCS-12400337.summary: This milestone records a road measurement commissioned by Emperor Trajan, who held multiple consulships and tribunician powers.

EDCS-12400341.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, from the civitas of the Triboci.
EDCS-12400341.summary: This inscription dedicates a monument or marks a boundary for Emperor Valerian I by the civitas of the Triboci.

EDCS-12400342.text_edition: \n Caio Valenti Hostiliano Messio Quinto nobilissimo Caesari civitas Tribocorum a Vrocomago leugas \n
EDCS-12400342.translation: To Caesar Gaius Valens Hostilianus Messius Quintus, most noble Caesar, from Vrocomagus [X] leagues.
EDCS-12400342.summary: This inscription records a road measurement from Vrocomagus dedicated to Caesar Hostilian.

EDCS-12400344.translation: To Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus...
EDCS-12400344.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicated to Emperor Valerian I.

EDCS-12400345.text_edition: \n Caio Valenti Hostiliano Messio Quinto nobilissimo Caesari civitas Tribocorum a Vrocomago leugas\n
EDCS-12400345.translation: To Caesar Gaius Valens Hostilianus Messius Quintus, most noble Caesar, from Vrocomagus [X] leagues.
EDCS-12400345.summary: This inscription records a road measurement from Vrocomagus dedicated to Caesar Hostilian.

EDCS-12400347.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Cassianius Latinus Postumus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power for the ninth time, consul for the third time, father of the country, proconsul, from the civitas of the colony of Nemetes, 16 leagues.
EDCS-12400347.summary: This milestone records a road measurement from the colony of Nemetes dedicated to Emperor Postumus.

EDCS-12400348.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Carus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the country, proconsul, from the civitas of the Nemetes, 16 leagues.
EDCS-12400348.summary: This milestone records a road measurement from the Nemetes dedicated to Emperor Carus.

EDCS-12400349.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Valerius Licinius, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus; from the civitas Nemetum, 16 leagues.
EDCS-12400349.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Valerius Licinius, likely marking a distance of 16 leagues from the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400350.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius, the most noble Caesar; from the civitas Nemetum, 16 leagues.
EDCS-12400350.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius, likely marking a distance of 16 leagues from the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400351.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius, the Pious, Fortunate Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland; from Noviomagus, 16 leagues from the civitas Nemetum.
EDCS-12400351.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Trajan Decius, likely marking a distance of 16 leagues from Noviomagus to the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400352.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Valerio Licinianio sic Licinio nobilissimo Caesari civitas Nemetum leugas XIII\n
EDCS-12400352.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius, the most noble Caesar; from the civitas Nemetum, 13 leagues.
EDCS-12400352.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Valerius Licinianus Licinius, likely marking a distance of 13 leagues from the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400354.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Valerio Liciniano sic Licinio Pio Felici Invicto Augusto civitas Nemetum leugas II\n
EDCS-12400354.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus; from the civitas Nemetum, 2 leagues.
EDCS-12400354.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Valerius Licinianus Licinius, likely marking a distance of 2 leagues from the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400355.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Diocletiano Pio Felici invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae consuli civitas Nemetum leugas V\n
EDCS-12400355.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Diocletian, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul; from the civitas Nemetum, 5 leagues.
EDCS-12400355.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Diocletian, likely marking a distance of 5 leagues from the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400359.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Messio Quinto Traiano Deccio Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli patri patriae civitas Nemetum leugas\n
EDCS-12400359.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Messius Quintus Traianus Decius Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland; from the civitas Nemetum, [X] leagues.
EDCS-12400359.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Trajan Decius, likely marking an unstated distance in leagues from the civitas Nemetum.

EDCS-12400362.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Galerio Valerio Maximiano nobilissimo Caesari principi iuventutis civitas Vangionum leuga I\n
EDCS-12400362.translation: To our lord Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the most noble Caesar, prince of youth; from the civitas Vangionum, 1 league.
EDCS-12400362.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Caesar Galerius Valerius Maximianus, likely marking a distance of 1 league from the civitas Vangionum.

EDCS-12400363.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Publio Licinio Gallieno Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae consuli proconsuli civitas Vangionum\n
EDCS-12400363.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, proconsul; from the civitas Vangionum.
EDCS-12400363.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Gallienus, from the civitas Vangionum, likely for road maintenance or a boundary marker.

EDCS-12400364.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Caio Iulio Vero Maximino pio felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae consuli proconsuli et Caio Iulio Vero Maximo nobilissimo Caesari civitas Vangionum leugas\n
EDCS-12400364.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus, the pious, fortunate Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, proconsul, and to Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, the most noble Caesar; from the civitas Vangionum, [X] leagues.
EDCS-12400364.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperors Maximinus and his son Caesar Maximinus, likely marking an unstated distance in leagues from the civitas Vangionum.

EDCS-12400367.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring Emperor Caesar Marcus, likely part of a larger dedication. The date is inferable from the emperor's name but not fully determinable from this fragment alone.

EDCS-12400368.text_edition: \n nepoti Traiano Hadriano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate VI consuli III patri patriae ab Aquis Mattiacorum milia passuum VI\n
EDCS-12400368.translation: to the son of Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 6th time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, from the Aquis Mattiacorum, 6 miles.
EDCS-12400368.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the community of Aquis Mattiacorum, marking a distance of 6 miles to Emperor Trajan Hadrian Augustus, likely during his reign (117-138 AD).

EDCS-12400372.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Gaio Iulio Vero Maxsimino sic Pio Felici Augusto et Gaio Iulio Vero Maxsimo sic Caesari nobilissimo a Mogontiaco \n
EDCS-12400372.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, from Mogontiacum
EDCS-12400372.summary: This inscription dedicates a road or distance marker from Mogontiacum to Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximus Caesar, likely in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400373.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Antonio Gordiano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae civitas Sueborum Nicrensium leugam I\n
EDCS-12400373.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the country, the Suebi Nicrenses tribe, 1 league.
EDCS-12400373.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the Suebi Nicrenses tribe, marking a distance of 1 league to Emperor Gordian III Pius Felix Augustus, likely in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400375.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Caio Messio Quinto Troiano sic Decio Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae proconsuli civitas Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium\n
EDCS-12400375.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, father of the country, proconsul, the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe.
EDCS-12400375.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe to Emperor Decius Pius Felix Augustus, likely in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400376.text_edition: \n Quinto Herennio Etrusco Messio Decio nobilissimo Caesari civitas Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium\n
EDCS-12400376.translation: To Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius, most noble Caesar, the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe.
EDCS-12400376.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe to Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius, who was a Caesar and son of Emperor Decius, likely in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400377.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus Caessaribus Publio Licinio Valeriano et Publio Licinio Gallieno Piis Felicibus Auggustis civitas Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium\n
EDCS-12400377.translation: To the Emperors Caesars Publius Licinius Valerianus and Publius Licinius Gallienus, Pious Fortunate Augusti, the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe.
EDCS-12400377.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe to Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, dating to their joint rule in the mid-3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400378.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Severi nepoti divi Antonini Magni filio Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate iterum consuli III patri patriae proconsuli civitas Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium devotissima posuit a Lopoduno leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400378.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of divine Severus, son of great divine Antoninus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the second time, consul for the 3rd time, father of the country, proconsul, the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe, most devoted, placed this from Lopodunum, 4 leagues.
EDCS-12400378.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium tribe to Emperor Caracalla, marking a distance of 4 leagues from Lopodunum, likely in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400379.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Severo Alexandro Pio Felici Augusto civitas Sueborum Nicrensium a Lopoduno leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400379.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, the Suebi Nicrenses tribe, from Lopodunum, 4 leagues.
EDCS-12400379.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the Suebi Nicrenses tribe to Emperor Severus Alexander, marking a distance of 4 leagues from Lopodunum, likely in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400380.text_edition: \n I<m=N>peratori Caesari Caio Iulio Vero Maximino Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli partri patriae proconsuli et Gaio Iulio Vero Maxi<m=N>o nobilissimo Caesari civitas Sueborum Nicrensium leugas IIII \n
EDCS-12400380.translation: To Emperor Caesar Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the country, proconsul, and Gaius Julius Verus Maximus, most noble Caesar, the Suebi Nicrenses tribe, 4 leagues.
EDCS-12400380.summary: This inscription records a dedication by the Suebi Nicrenses tribe to Emperors Maximinus Thrax and his son Maximus Caesar, marking a distance of 4 leagues, likely in the early 3rd century AD.

EDCS-12400381.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Antonio Gordiano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae civitas Sueborum Nicrensium leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400381.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, the community of the Suebi Nicrenses [grants] 4 miles.
EDCS-12400381.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles by the Suebi Nicrenses to Emperor Gordian III, likely dating to his reign (238-244 CE).

EDCS-12400382.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Iulio Philippo Pio Felici Augusto tribunicia potestate II patri patriae consuli et Marco Iulio Philippo nobilissimo Caesari civitas Sueborum Nicrensium leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400382.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, and to Marcus Julius Philippus, most noble Caesar, the community of the Suebi Nicrenses [grants] 4 miles.
EDCS-12400382.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles by the Suebi Nicrenses to Emperor Philip the Arab and his son, Caesar Philip, likely dating to their joint rule (c. 247-249 CE).

EDCS-12400383.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Gaio Messio Quinto Troiano sic Decio Pio Felici Invicto Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate patri patriae proconsuli civitas Sueborum Nicrensium leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400383.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Gaius Messius Quintus Traianus Decius Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, proconsul, the community of the Suebi Nicrenses [grants] 4 miles.
EDCS-12400383.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles by the Suebi Nicrenses to Emperor Decius, likely dating to his reign (249-251 CE).

EDCS-12400384.text_edition: \n Quinto Herennio Etrusco Messio Decio nobilissimo Caesari civitas Sueborum Nicrensium leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400384.translation: To Quintus Herennius Etruscus Messius Decius, most noble Caesar, the community of the Suebi Nicrenses [grants] 4 miles.
EDCS-12400384.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles by the Suebi Nicrenses to Caesar Quintus Herennius Etruscus, likely dating to his co-rule with his father Decius (c. 250-251 CE).

EDCS-12400385.text_edition: \n Impperatoribus Caessaribus Publio Licinio Valeriano Pio Felici Invicto Augusto et Publio Licinio Gallieno Augusto civitas Ulpia Sueborum Nicrensium a Lopoduno leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400385.translation: To the Emperors Caesars Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus and Publius Licinius Gallienus Augustus, the Ulpian community of the Suebi Nicrenses [grants] 4 miles from Lopodunum.
EDCS-12400385.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles from Lopodunum by the Ulpian community of the Suebi Nicrenses to Emperors Valerian and Gallienus, likely dating to their joint reign (253-260 CE).
