EDCS-12400387.text_edition: \n Imperatore Caesare Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felice Augusto Parthico maximo Britannico maximo pontifice maximo patre patriae consule IIII proconsule civitas Aquensis ab Aquis leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400387.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, Parthicus Maximus, Britannicus Maximus, chief priest, father of the fatherland, consul for the 4th time, proconsul, the community of the Aquenses [grants] 4 miles from Aquae.
EDCS-12400387.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles from Aquae by the Aquenses to Emperor Caracalla, dating to his consulships and honours (c. 202-217 CE).

EDCS-12400388.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Severi nepoti divi Antonini Magni filio Marco Aurelio Antonino [Pio Felici Augusto pontifici] [maximo tribunicia potestate] III consul III patri patriae proconsuli civitas Aurelia Aquensis ab Aquis leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400388.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Severus, son of the deified Antoninus Magnus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus [Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest], [holder of tribunician power] III, consul III, father of the fatherland, proconsul, the community of the Aurelian Aquenses [grants] 4 miles from Aquae.
EDCS-12400388.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles from Aquae by the Aurelian Aquenses to Emperor Elagabalus, dating to his third tribunician power and consulship (c. 215-217 CE).

EDCS-12400389.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Severi Pii nepoti divi Antonini Magni Pii filio Marco Aurelio Severo Alexandro Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribuniciae sic potestas sic consul patri patriae civitas Aurelia Aquensis ab Aquis leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400389.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Severus Pius, son of the deified Antoninus Magnus Pius, Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, the community of the Aurelian Aquenses [grants] 4 miles from Aquae.
EDCS-12400389.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles from Aquae by the Aurelian Aquenses to Emperor Severus Alexander, dating to his consulship and tribunician power (c. 222-235 CE).

EDCS-12400390.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Antonio Gordiano Pio Felici Augusto pontifici tribunicia potestate patri patriae consul proconsuli restitutori orbis ab Aquis leugas IIII\n
EDCS-12400390.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antonius Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, father of the fatherland, consul, proconsul, restorer of the world, [the community] from Aquae [grants] 4 miles.
EDCS-12400390.summary: This inscription records a grant of 4 miles from Aquae to Emperor Gordian III, likely dating to his reign (238-244 CE).

EDCS-12400392.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Severi Pii nepoti divi Antonini Pii Magni filio Marco Aurelio Severo Alexandro Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribuniciae potestatis consuli patri patriae civitas Aurelia Aquensis ab Aquis leugas XVII\n
EDCS-12400392.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, grandson of the deified Severus Pius, son of the deified Antoninus Pius Magnus, Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, holder of tribunician power, consul, father of the fatherland, the community of the Aurelian Aquenses [grants] 17 miles from Aquae.
EDCS-12400392.summary: This inscription records a grant of 17 miles from Aquae by the Aurelian Aquenses to Emperor Severus Alexander, dating to his consulship and tribunician power (c. 222-235 CE).

EDCS-12400393.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Antonino Pio Felici Augusto Parthico maximo Britannico maximo pontifici maximo patri patriae consuli IIII proconsuli \n
EDCS-12400393.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of Parthia the greatest, conqueror of Britain the greatest, chief priest, father of the country, consul for the fourth time, proconsul.
EDCS-12400393.summary: This inscription is a titulature for Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely part of a larger dedication or honorific monument.

EDCS-12400395.text_edition: \n Imperatori Marco Iulio Philippo Pio Felici Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli patri patriae et Marco Iulio Philippo Caesari a Portu leugae V\n
EDCS-12400395.translation: To Emperor Marcus Julius Philippus Pius Felix Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul, father of the country, and to Marcus Julius Philippus Caesar, from the Port, 5 leagues distant.
EDCS-12400395.summary: This inscription records the titulature of Emperor Philip the Arab and his son, likely marking a road or milestone.

EDCS-12400398.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Traiani Parthici filius divi Nervae nepos Traianus Hadrianus Augustus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XIII consul III pater patriae a Sumelocenna milia passuum XXVIIII\n
EDCS-12400398.translation: To Emperor Caesar Traianus Hadrianus Augustus, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 13th time, consul for the third time, father of the country, from Sumelocenna, 29 miles distant.
EDCS-12400398.summary: This inscription is the titulature of Emperor Hadrian, indicating a distance marker from Sumelocenna.

EDCS-12400399.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Tito Aelio Antonino Augusto Pio pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate consuli III patri patriae Aventico milia passuum XXXVIII\n
EDCS-12400399.translation: To Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Antoninus Augustus Pius, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the third time, father of the country, from Aventicum, 38 miles distant.
EDCS-12400399.summary: This inscription is the titulature of Emperor Antoninus Pius, indicating a distance marker from Aventicum.

EDCS-12400402.text_edition: \n Nobilissimo Caesari Caio Galerio Maximiano nostri Augusti filio\n
EDCS-12400402.translation: To the most noble Caesar Gaius Galerius Maximianus, son of our Augustus.
EDCS-12400402.summary: This inscription is an honorific dedication to Caesar Galerius Maximian, likely erected by someone acknowledging his imperial status.

EDCS-12400407.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus Parthicus maximus Britannicus maximus pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XVI imperator II consul IIII proconsul princeps iuventutis fortissimus felicissimusque Magnus princeps pacator orbis vias et pontes vetustate collapsos restituit Aventico XXVI\n
EDCS-12400407.translation: Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, conqueror of Parthia the greatest, conqueror of Britain the greatest, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 16th time, imperator for the second time, consul for the fourth time, proconsul, prince of the youth, the most courageous and fortunate, the great prince, pacifier of the world, restored roads and bridges collapsed by age, at Aventicum, 26 [miles distant].
EDCS-12400407.summary: This extensive titulature and achievement record for Emperor Marcus Aurelius details his restoration of infrastructure and marks a distance of 26 miles from Aventicum.

EDCS-12500038.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the eternal memory of the once incomparable matron Florentina, who lived 37 years, 5 months, and 14 days. Iunius Eudemus had this made for his most rare wife.
EDCS-12500038.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Florentina, commissioned by her husband Iunius Eudemus, providing her age and dates of life.

EDCS-12500039.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---] Viralirae Lucer[---] [---] matron[a?] [---] unfortunat[e?].
EDCS-12500039.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely for a matron named Viralirae Lucer[---], possibly lamenting an unfortunate fate.

EDCS-12500040.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Porcius Crescens, freedman of Marcus, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his wife Porcia Mansueta. Marcus Porcius Verecundus, freedman and heir, had this made.
EDCS-12500040.summary: This funerary epitaph records a self-commissioned tomb by Marcus Porcius Crescens for himself and his wife, completed by his freedman and heir.

EDCS-12500043.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Crescens, the most dutiful son, set up [this monument] from his own resources for Urision, his father, and Moriēna, his mother.
EDCS-12500043.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where Crescens dedicates a monument to his parents, Urision and Moriēna.

EDCS-12500051.translation: To Mercury, Esunertus, son of Sounis, willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-12500051.summary: A dedication to Mercury by Esunertus, son of Sounis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500062.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcianus Avitianus, a soldier of the 8th Augusta legion, willingly and joyfully and deservedly placed this in fulfillment of a vow for the health of his wife, Iassa Titiola.
EDCS-12500062.summary: A military dedication to the imperial family and goddesses by Marcianus Avitianus, a soldier of the 8th Augusta legion, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12500065.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Bellatullus, the heir, placed this by their will.
EDCS-12500065.summary: A tomb inscription by Bellatullus, the heir, for his deceased relatives, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500066.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for perpetual security. Bellica Pro(?). Bellicius Sonsiciosus.
EDCS-12500066.summary: A tomb inscription from Bellicius Sonsiciosus for Bellica Pro(?), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500068.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The heirs took care to place this for Cantognatus, son of Mainus.
EDCS-12500068.summary: A tomb inscription by the heirs for Cantognatus, son of Mainus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500069.summary: An incomplete inscription, likely a tombstone, identifying an individual named Caracus.

EDCS-12500070.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [---]onnur, son of [---]om[---]. // To the spirits of the departed. Carro.
EDCS-12500070.summary: A fragmented tomb inscription that mentions at least two individuals, possibly related, named [---]onnur and Carro.

EDCS-12500071.translation: To the spirits of the departed. AV[---]us, son of Tiberius [---]. // To the spirits of the departed. Carana, [daughter?] of C[---]PLIA.
EDCS-12500071.summary: A fragmented tomb inscription mentioning individuals with names like AV[---]us, Tiberius, Carana, and C[---]PLIA, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500072.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caranto, son of Floridus. Florinus, son of [---], took care to place this.
EDCS-12500072.summary: A tomb inscription indicating that Florinus, son of [---], arranged for the burial of Caranto, son of Floridus.

EDCS-12500073.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caraisioun, son of Cornitus, his son took care to place this. // To the spirits of the departed. Caia, daughter of Crobus, her son took care to place this. // To the spirits of the departed. Carasus, son of Cara[---]. // To the spirits of the departed. Carasius, son of Cara[---].
EDCS-12500073.summary: Multiple fragmented tomb inscriptions likely from the Roman Imperial period, commemorating individuals named Caraisioun, Caia, Carasus, and Carasius.

EDCS-12500074.translation: To Carantodia Ianuaria, daughter, and to Maternio [---]tianus and Secundanus Felix, sons. Secundanus Carantodi, husband and father, most unhappy, had this set up.
EDCS-12500074.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a grieving husband and father for his wife and sons.

EDCS-12500075.translation: To the departed spirits. Pugnus Carantus arranged for this to be placed; his heir arranged for it to be set up.
EDCS-12500075.summary: This is a funerary inscription indicating that Pugnus Carantus commissioned a burial monument, which was then set up by his heir.

EDCS-12500076.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying Caratodius as the son of Carathoun.

EDCS-12500077.translation: To the departed spirits. Augustus Caratus and Carantodius [set this up].
EDCS-12500077.summary: This funerary inscription records that Augusts Caratus and Carantodius dedicated a monument to the departed spirits.

EDCS-12500078.translation: To the departed spirits. His heirs took care to have this made according to the will of Publius Carisius Paternus and Suadullius Aventinus Matrainnus Nobilis, son.
EDCS-12500078.summary: This funerary inscription states that the heirs of Publius Carisius Paternus and Suadullius Aventinus Matrainnus Nobilis had a monument erected in accordance with their will.

EDCS-12500079.translation: To the departed spirits. Catulianus [set this up] for his wife, and Africanus, son of Catulianus.
EDCS-12500079.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Catulianus for his wife and Africanus, son of Catulianus.

EDCS-12500080.translation: Capurillus, his son, placed this for Catullinus, son of Catullus.
EDCS-12500080.summary: This is a funerary inscription erected by Capurillus for his son, Catullinus.

EDCS-12500081.translation: To the departed spirits. [---]llus, son of Uc[---], [set this up] for Coberatus, son of Maximinus.
EDCS-12500081.summary: This funerary inscription dedicates a monument to Coberatus, son of Maximinus, by [---]llus, son of Uc[---].

EDCS-12500082.translation: To the departed spirits. For Cossianus, son of Cossus.
EDCS-12500082.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Cossianus, son of Cossus.

EDCS-12500084.translation: To the departed spirits. Secundina, his sister, arranged for this to be set up for Divicianus.
EDCS-12500084.summary: This funerary inscription records that Secundina, sister of Divicianus, arranged for his monument to be erected.

EDCS-12500085.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Duroti Carantus, her heir, arranged for this to be set up for his wife Divixta.
EDCS-12500085.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated to Divixta by her husband Carantus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500086.translation: To the spirits of the departed and to the eternal security of Iulia Blandula. Her husband, Cornelius Iuvenilis, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-12500086.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by Cornelius Iuvenilis for his wife Iulia Blandula, probably during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500087.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Capurrilla, mother, for Iustinus.
EDCS-12500087.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a mother named Capurrilla for her son Iustinus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500088.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gnatus, grandson of Mainni son of Gnatillus, made this at his own expense.
EDCS-12500088.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Gnatus, the grandson of Mainni, set up this monument at his own expense, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500089.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Maioris son of Ocicus. They arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-12500089.summary: This funerary epitaph records that a monument was set up for Maioris, son of Ocicus, by unspecified individuals, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500090.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Malia, daughter of Senior. Her husband Caratacus arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-12500090.summary: This funerary epitaph states that Caratacus, the husband of Malia, arranged for this monument to be erected in her memory, probably dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500091.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Masn[3]onse[3] Toonni. Secundinus, his brother, arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-12500091.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Secundinus, brother of Masn[3]onse[3] Toonni, arranged for this monument, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500092.translation: To the spirits of the departed, in memory of Mamertina, daughter of Senetus.
EDCS-12500092.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commemorating Mamertina, daughter of Senetus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500093.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Mainnus, father, arranged for this to be set up for Mivinu(a).
EDCS-12500093.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Mainnus, the father, arranged for this monument for his daughter Mivinu(a), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500094.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Natali, son of Caranti, and his son. They arranged for this to be set up.
EDCS-12500094.summary: This funerary epitaph records that a monument was set up for Natali, son of Caranti, and his son, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-12500095.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Petra, daughter of Mainnus, erected this, her heir saw to its placement.
EDCS-12500095.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Petra, daughter of Mainnus, whose heir placed the monument.

EDCS-12500096.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Pugnus, son of Cinerus.
EDCS-12500096.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Pugnus, son of Cinerus.

EDCS-12500098.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To [---]aporius, son of Loculus [---], and [---]ulla, his daughter.
EDCS-12500098.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription possibly commemorating two individuals, possibly father and daughter.

EDCS-12500099.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To [---]AVN[---], a beneficiary of Vitianus [---], son of [---], his heir NI[---]OIEVT placed this.
EDCS-12500099.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription for a beneficiary of Vitianus, whose heir placed the monument.

EDCS-12500101.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, possibly funerary, recording a placement by someone named Regina.

EDCS-12500104.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo s Lucius veteranus cohortis XXIIII voluntariorum civium Romanorum fecit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12500104.translation: In honor of the divine house. Lucius, a veteran of the twenty-fourth cohort of Roman citizens, gladly and willingly made this for Jupiter Optimus Maximus, as is deserved.
EDCS-12500104.summary: This is a dedication of a monument to Jupiter by Lucius, a veteran of the 24th cohort, likely during the imperial period.

EDCS-12500105.summary: This is a fragmented dedication to Mercury and Maia by Nigrinus.

EDCS-12500106.translation: Secundinius Attillus and Divilla, by vow, [dedicated] the temple.
EDCS-12500106.summary: This is a votive dedication of a temple by Secundinius Attillus and Divilla.

EDCS-12500114.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Aunoro(?), son, while he was alive.
EDCS-12500114.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aunoro(?), son, set up by himself while alive.

EDCS-12500117.text_edition: \n Mercurio sacrum Gentilis Africani filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12500117.translation: Sacred to Mercury. Gentilis, son of Africanus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12500117.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury by Gentilis, son of Africanus, who fulfilled his vow.

EDCS-12500118.translation: Matrona Tertio and Libo set this up to Mercury as a vow.
EDCS-12500118.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury by Matrona Tertio and Libo.

EDCS-12500120.translation: Tatianus Accepti set this up, a gift to the goddess Diana, as a willing, happy, and deserved vow.
EDCS-12500120.summary: This is a votive dedication to Diana by Tatianus Accepti.

EDCS-12500122.translation: Attonius Tertullus set this up for Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-12500122.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Attonius Tertullus.

EDCS-12500123.text_edition: \n Me\xc4\x91\xc4\x91illio Rufi filio et Vanataxtae et Ioincorigi coniux Pacata et Vitalis fecerunt\n
EDCS-12500123.translation: Pacata and Vitalis made this for their son Meddillius, son of Rufus, and for Vanataxta and Ioincorigi.
EDCS-12500123.summary: This is a dedication by Pacata and Vitalis for family members.

EDCS-12500124.translation: To the divine shades for eternal rest and eternal security. Barbat[i]us Silvester, decurion of the civitas Nemetum, and his brothers Arbirius, Silvanus, and Silvio[n]i, and their nephew Rusticius arranged for this to be made for their dearest father.
EDCS-12500124.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a father, set up by his sons and nephew, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-12500126.text_edition: \n Mercurio Samus essus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12500126.translation: Samus essus fulfilled his vow to Mercury, willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-12500126.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury by Samus essus.

EDCS-12500130.translation: Amandus and Victorina [set this up] for Diana for the health of Tucius Verus, Roman equestrian, and of Tert[3] Romana.
EDCS-12500130.summary: This is a dedication to Diana for the health of Tucius Verus and Tert[3] Romana by Amandus and Victorina.

EDCS-12500132.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio et Rosmertae Marcus Adiutorius Memmor decurio civitatis St ex voto posuit libens merito\n
EDCS-12500132.translation: Marcus Adiutorius Memmor, decurion of the civitas St, set this up to the god Mercury and Rosmerta as a willing, happy, and deserved vow.
EDCS-12500132.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury and Rosmerta by Marcus Adiutorius Memmor, a local official.

EDCS-12500133.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Defensori sacrum Maximin-- V L Felicio V L Leontius de pecunia sua et suorum votum solverunt libentes merito\n
EDCS-12500133.translation: To the god Mercury the Defender. Maximin--, V L Felicio, V L Leontius fulfilled their vow from his own money and that of his family, willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-12500133.summary: This is a votive dedication to Mercury the Defender by Maximin--, V L Felicio, and V L Leontius.

EDCS-12500134.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marcus Adiutorius Memor decurio civitatis St ex voto solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12500134.translation: In honor of the divine house. Marcus Adiutorius Memor, decurion of the civitas St, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-12500134.summary: This is an inscription honoring the imperial family, set up by Marcus Adiutorius Memor, a local official.

EDCS-12500136.translation: To the divine shades of Septimia Restituta, aged 17. Her mother Septimia Atuqua [made this].
EDCS-12500136.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Septimia Restituta, set up by her mother.

EDCS-12500137.translation: [Name illegible] paid his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-12500137.summary: This is a votive inscription mentioning a dedicant fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-12500139.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Poppausio Cossetioni et coniugi eius et filio defuncto heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-12500139.translation: The heir had this made for Poppausius Cossetion, his spouse, and his deceased son.
EDCS-12500139.summary: This is a funerary inscription where an heir commissioned a monument for family members.

EDCS-12500148.translation: To the Deae Quadriviae, Maternus willingly and joyfully paid his vow for the health of Donata.
EDCS-12500148.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Deae Quadriviae by Maternus for the health of Donata.

EDCS-12500149.text_edition: \n Leubius Claupi filius eques missicius ala Sebosiana annorum LXXV hic situs est Gratus filius miles ex testamento fecit\n
EDCS-12500149.translation: Leubius, son of Claupius, a cavalryman discharged from the Sebosian ala, aged 75, is buried here. His son Gratus, a soldier, made this according to his will.
EDCS-12500149.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Leubius, a veteran cavalryman, commissioned by his son Gratus.

EDCS-12500150.translation: Victorius Quintianus had this made for his dearest wife Felicia Felicula.
EDCS-12500150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by Victorius Quintianus for his wife Felicia Felicula.

EDCS-12600012.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Valerius Aprilis bucinator votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12600012.translation: Valerius Aprilis, a trumpeter, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-12600012.summary: This is a votive inscription by Valerius Aprilis, a bucinator, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.

EDCS-12600013.text_edition: \n Minervae Caius Valerius Romulus miles legionis XIIII votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12600013.translation: Caius Valerius Romulus, a soldier of the 14th legion, paid his vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly to Minerva.
EDCS-12600013.summary: This is a votive inscription by Caius Valerius Romulus, a soldier of the Legio XIV, to Minerva.

EDCS-12600014.text_edition: \n Minervae Veranius Secundus et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12600014.translation: Veranius Secundus and his family paid their vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly to Minerva.
EDCS-12600014.summary: This is a votive inscription by Veranius Secundus and his family to Minerva.

EDCS-12600015.text_edition: \n Visunae Lucius Salvius Similis Salvi Similis filius Mediomatricus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-12600015.translation: Lucius Salvius Similis, son of Salvius Similis, a Mediomatrician, paid his vow willingly and deservedly to Visuna.
EDCS-12600015.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Salvius Similis, a member of the Mediomatrici tribe, to the deity Visuna.

EDCS-12600019.text_edition: \n Caius Veturius Cai filius Veturia Dexter Placentia miles cohortis XXVI voluntariorum civium Romanorum centuria Victoris annorum XXXX stipendiorum XVI heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-12600019.translation: Gaius Veturius Dexter, son of Gaius, of the Veturia tribe, from Placentia, a soldier of the 26th cohort of Roman citizen volunteers, in the centuria of Victor, aged 40, with 16 years of service, erected this.
EDCS-12600019.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Veturius Dexter, a soldier, erected by his heir.

EDCS-12600020.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iuco Iuniani sibi et matri suae\n
EDCS-12600020.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Iucundus for himself and his mother, daughter of Iunius.
EDCS-12600020.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Divine Spirits by Iucundus for himself and his mother.

EDCS-12600031.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo in honorem domus divinae Titus Aelius Victor votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12600031.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, in honor of the divine house, Titus Aelius Victor gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-12600031.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Titus Aelius Victor, dedicated in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-12600032.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo in honorem domus divinae Titus Aelius Victor quod voverat visu dei monitus posuit votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12600032.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, in honor of the divine house, Titus Aelius Victor placed this, which he had vowed after being warned by a vision of the god; gladly and joyfully he fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-12600032.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Titus Aelius Victor, dedicated in honor of the imperial family, mentioning a divine vision.

EDCS-12700145.text_edition: \n Quinto Maio militi legionis XIII geminae |(centuriae) Statii Nana\n
EDCS-12700145.translation: For Quintus Maius, a soldier of the 13th Gemina legion, in the centuria of Statius Nana.
EDCS-12700145.summary: This is an epitaph for Quintus Maius, a soldier of the 13th Gemina legion.

EDCS-12700230.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae anus Secundus votum solverunt libentes laeti merito\n
EDCS-12700230.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and Juno Regina, the old women Secundus gladly and joyfully fulfilled their vow as was deserved.
EDCS-12700230.summary: This is a votive inscription to Jupiter and Juno by a group identified as 'anus Secundus' (old women Secundus).

EDCS-12700231.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Claudiae Quartae annorum XXXXV coniugi rarissimae et Mirioni filio annorum IIII Lucius \n
EDCS-12700231.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Claudia Quarta, aged 45, a most rare wife, and for our son Mionius, aged 4, Lucius...
EDCS-12700231.summary: This is a funerary inscription by Lucius for his wife Claudia Quarta and son Mionius.

EDCS-12700232.text_edition: \n Secundus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700232.translation: Secundus fulfilled his vow gladly and joyfully as was deserved.
EDCS-12700232.summary: This is a votive inscription by Secundus, likely a fulfillment of a personal vow.

EDCS-12700234.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Respecto Beri annorum XXIII civi Suebo Nicrensi exploratori Candidus Beri frater procuravit\n
EDCS-12700234.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Respectus, aged 23, a Suebian citizen from Nicra, an explorer, his brother Candidus Beri procured this.
EDCS-12700234.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Respectus, a Suebian explorer, procured by his brother Candidus Beri.

EDCS-12700235.translation: Marovus, son of Bricto, a citizen of the Treveri...
EDCS-12700235.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Marovus, son of Bricto, as a citizen of the Treveri.

EDCS-12700236.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Pacus Bervi fratribus monimentum posuit Secundo Bervi et Masuetincae coniugi et Mattio et P<l=I>acidiae neptiae fi<l=I>iae S<e=I>cundi de sua pecunia Ungario locum dedit \n
EDCS-12700236.translation: To the departed spirits. Secundus Bervius erected this monument for his brothers Pacus and Bervius, and for his wife Masuetinca, and his granddaughter Mattia, and his daughter Placidia, at his own expense; Ungarius provided the place.
EDCS-12700236.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Secundus Bervius for his relatives, with land provided by Ungarius.

EDCS-12700237.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Vigellius Nonni annorum XVII Iulio Tertio et Calliae coniugi suae Nonnus Blandi faciendum curavit filio et suae coniugi piissimae de sua pecunia\n
EDCS-12700237.translation: To the departed spirits. Nonnus Blandi had this made at his own expense for his son Vigellius Nonni, aged 17, and for his wife Callia, and for himself, a most devoted son and wife.
EDCS-12700237.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Nonnus Blandi for his son Vigellius Nonni and wife Callia.

EDCS-12700243.text_edition: \n Sulevis sororibus Lucius Gallionius Ianuarius decurio alae I nnatium votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700243.translation: Lucius Gallionius Ianuarius, decurion of the 1st wing of the Unti, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the sisters Sulevia.
EDCS-12700243.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Gallionius Ianuarius to the goddesses Sulevia.

EDCS-12700244.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Annio Ianuario Anni Postumi liberto Vervicia mater faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-12700244.translation: To the departed spirits. Vervicia, mother, had this made at her own expense for her freedman Annio Ianuarius, of Annius Postumius.
EDCS-12700244.summary: This is a funerary monument commissioned by Vervicia for her freedman Annio Ianuarius.

EDCS-12700246.summary: This is a very brief inscription identifying Claudia Daernus as a veteran.

EDCS-12700247.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Quintius Vitalis et Quintii Antistii Respectus Av \n
EDCS-12700247.translation: In honor of the divine house. Lucius Quintius Vitalis and Quintii Antistii Respectus Av [fulfilled their vow] to Jupiter Optimus Maximus.
EDCS-12700247.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Quintius Vitalis and Quintii Antistii Respectus Av in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-12700249.text_edition: \n Abnobae sacrum Marcus Proclinius Verus stator votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700249.translation: A sacred offering to Abnobae. Marcus Proclinius Verus, stator, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12700249.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Abnobae by Marcus Proclinius Verus.

EDCS-12700251.text_edition: \n Venidius Germanus miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis pro se et suos sic posuit Mamertino et Rufo consulibus\n
EDCS-12700251.translation: Venidius Germanus, miles beneficiarius consularis of the 8th Augustan Legion, placed this for himself and his family under the consulship of Mamertinus and Rufus.
EDCS-12700251.summary: This is an inscription by Venidius Germanus, a soldier of the 8th Legion, recording his dedication during the consulship of Mamertinus and Rufus.

EDCS-12700252.summary: This is a simple epitaph recording the lifespan of Ingenuus.

EDCS-12700253.translation: Attia (?) and Ipati (?) Anidiania (?) Erius and Roato (?) [erected this monument?].
EDCS-12700253.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning several names, possibly indicating family members.

EDCS-12700254.text_edition: \n Collegio Matisonensium Iulius Venussimus <f=E>ilius optio collegii supra scripti ei dono dedit \n
EDCS-12700254.translation: Julius Venussimus, son of Aelius, optio of the aforementioned college, gave this as a gift to the college of the Matisonenses.
EDCS-12700254.summary: This inscription records a gift made by an optio to his college, likely in the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700256.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Salvonius Domitianus de suo posuit\n
EDCS-12700256.translation: Salvonius Domitianus erected this at his own expense to the god Mercury.
EDCS-12700256.summary: This inscription records a private dedication to the god Mercury, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12700259.text_edition: \n Fortunae sacrum ex voto Giamillius Ianuarius votum solvit libens laetus merito Falcone consSule\n
EDCS-12700259.translation: Giamillius Ianuarius willingly, happily, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Fortuna, during the consulship of Falcone.
EDCS-12700259.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow made to the goddess Fortuna, dated by the consulship of Falcone.

EDCS-12700263.text_edition: \n Nymphis pro salute et victoria Imperatoris Commodi Antonini Augusti Pii Felicis iussu Clementis Dextriani legati Augusti pro praetore quod aqua non esset induxit per Iulium Demetrianum |(centurionem) legionis VIII Augustae piae fidelis constantis Commodae per pedes Crispino et Aeliano consulibus\n
EDCS-12700263.translation: By order of Clementis Dextrianus, legate of the emperor with praetorian power, for the health and victory of the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Pius Felix, because there was no water, this was brought through Julius Demetrianus, centurion of the 8th Augustan Legion, pious, faithful, constant, under the feet of the consuls Crispinus and Aelianus.
EDCS-12700263.summary: This inscription records the construction of an aqueduct for the Nymphs by a legionary legate and centurion, to ensure the health and victory of Emperor Commodus.

EDCS-12700264.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12700264.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae aquam Alexandrianam cohorti I Septimiae Belgarum Al<e=D>xandrianae sub cura Cati Clementini consularis perduxit Lucius Valerius Optatus praefectus dedicata X Kalendas Augustas Pompeiano et Paeligniano consulibus \n
EDCS-12700264.translation: In honor of the divine house, the Alexandrian water was brought to the 1st Cohort of Belgae Septimiae Alexandrianae under the supervision of Catius Clementinus, consul, by Lucius Valerius Optatus, prefect, dedicated on the tenth day before the Kalends of August, during the consulship of Pompeianus and Paelignianus.
EDCS-12700264.summary: This inscription records the completion of an aqueduct for a cohort of Belgae under the supervision of a consular official and a prefect, dedicated in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-12700265.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Nymphis perennibus aquam Gordianam cohorti I Septimiae Belgarum Gordianae multo tempore intermissam sub cura ani cons(ularis) Caius Iulius Rogatianus eques Romanus praefectus cohortis eiusdem novo aquaeductu perduxit per pedes Vquinque milia DCCCCVII quam salere instituit in praetorium et in balineum dedicata pridie Nonas Decembres Imperatore domino nostro Gordiano Augusto II et Pompeiiano sic consulibus\n
EDCS-12700265.translation: In honor of the divine house, Caius Iulius Rogatianus, a Roman knight and prefect of this same cohort, brought the Gordian water to the 1st Cohort of Belgae Septimiae Gordianae with a new aqueduct, which had been interrupted for a long time, covering a distance of 5907 paces, which he established for the praetorium and the bath, dedicated on the day before the Nones of December, during the consulship of our lord Emperor Gordianus Augustus II and Pompeianus.
EDCS-12700265.summary: This inscription details the restoration of a water supply to a cohort by its prefect, Caius Iulius Rogatianus, under Emperor Gordian III.

EDCS-12700267.translation: For the safety of our lord, the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Augustus [lacuna]...
EDCS-12700267.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription dedicated to Emperor Severus Alexander, likely for his health, dating to his reign (222-235 CE).

EDCS-12700273.text_edition: \n pro salute cohortis III Aquitanorum pius Iulianus medicus cohortis supra scriptae bene merentibus de suo posuit Saturnino et Gallo consulibus libens merito\n
EDCS-12700273.translation: For the health of the 3rd Cohort of Aquitani, Iulianus, the physician of the aforementioned cohort, set this up at his own expense for those deserving it, willingly, happily, and deservedly, during the consulship of Saturninus and Gallus.
EDCS-12700273.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a cohort physician for the health of his unit, dated by the consuls Saturninus and Gallus.

EDCS-12700276.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, and to the other Cassii, and to the immortal gods and goddesses, Cupitus [lacuna]...
EDCS-12700276.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription honoring Jupiter Optimus Maximus, other deities, and the imperial family, dedicated by a person named Cupitus.

EDCS-12700277.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Queen Juno and the Genius of the place, the beneficed officials of Germania Superior, Petronius Senilis, a soldier of the 8th Augustan Legion, a beneficed official of the consul, fulfilled his vow willingly, happily, and deservedly for his safety and that of his family, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January, during the consulship of Pompeianus and Paelignianus.
EDCS-12700277.summary: This inscription records a soldier of the 8th Legion fulfilling a vow to Jupiter, Juno, and the Genius loci for his own and his family's well-being, dated by the consuls Pompeianus and Paelignianus.

EDCS-12700278.translation: To the goddesses of the crossroads and of the four crossroads.
EDCS-12700278.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription dedicated to the goddesses of the crossroads, likely from an ancient roadside shrine.

EDCS-12700281.translation: To the supreme and mighty goddess, Fortunata, Sacconius Iustus Ambaxtus built the temple with its altar at his own expense, fulfilling his vow willingly, gladly, and deservedly, under the consulship of Asprus and Asprus, on the Ides of October.
EDCS-12700281.summary: This inscription records the dedication of a temple and altar to the goddess Fortunata by Sacconius Iustus Ambaxtus, an ex-slave, during the consulship of Asprus and Asprus.

EDCS-12700282.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Herculi ino Adnamatius Superst<e=I>s decurio cohortis II Hispanorum votum solvit libens laetus merito \n
EDCS-12700282.translation: In honor of the divine house, Adnamatius Superstes, decurion of the Second Cohort of Spaniards, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-12700282.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Hercules by Adnamatius Superstes, a decurion in a cohort of Spaniards, likely from the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-12700285.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno cohors I Aquitanorum veterana equitata cui praeest Titus Fabius Liberalis praefectus votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-12700285.translation: The First Aquitanian Veteran Cavalry Cohort, commanded by Titus Fabius Liberalis, its prefect, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled its vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-12700285.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled by the First Aquitanian Veteran Cavalry Cohort to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.

EDCS-12700287.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Lucius Caecilius Caecilianus praefectus cohortis I Aquitanorum domo Thaenis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700287.translation: Lucius Caecilius Caecilianus, prefect of the First Aquitanian Cohort, from the town of Thaenae, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-12700287.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus by Lucius Caecilius Caecilianus, prefect of the First Aquitanian Cohort, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century AD.

EDCS-12700288.translation: Lucius Caecilius Caecilianus, son of Lucius, of the tribe Quirina, prefect of the First Aquitanian Cohort, from the town of Thaenae in Africa, [dedicated this to] Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-12700288.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus by Lucius Caecilius Caecilianus, prefect of the First Aquitanian Cohort, originating from Thaenae in Africa.

EDCS-12700290.translation: To Minerva, Papias, standard-bearer of the First Aquitanian Veteran Cavalry Cohort.
EDCS-12700290.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Minerva by Papias, a standard-bearer in the First Aquitanian Veteran Cavalry Cohort.

EDCS-12700291.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae et Soli socio Argata votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700291.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras and his companion Sol, [dedicant's name] willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12700291.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to the god Mithras and Sol, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century AD.

EDCS-12700292.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Cauti et Cautopati Florius Florentius et Ancarinius Severus nepos votum solverunt libentes laeti merito Faustino et Rufino consulibus\n
EDCS-12700292.translation: In honor of the divine house, Florius Florentius and his grandson Ancarinius Severus willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Cautes and Cautopates, during the consulship of Faustinus and Rufinus.
EDCS-12700292.summary: This inscription records a vow fulfilled to Cautes and Cautopates by Florius Florentius and his grandson Ancarinius Severus, likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-12700293.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Pa Perpetuus haruspex de suo posuit\n
EDCS-12700293.translation: To the Unconquered God Mithras, Perpetuus the haruspex dedicated this from his own resources.
EDCS-12700293.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Mithras made by Perpetuus, a haruspex, at his own expense.

EDCS-12700294.text_edition: \n Deo Invicto Mithrae Mercurio Quintus P Gemellus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700294.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, to Mercury, Quintus P. Gemellus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12700294.summary: This is a votive inscription from Quintus P. Gemellus to the gods Mithras and Mercury, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12700297.text_edition: \n Deo Orienti Titus Martialius Candidus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700297.translation: To the Eastern god, Titus Martialius Candidus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12700297.summary: This is a votive inscription from Titus Martialius Candidus to the Eastern god, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12700298.text_edition: \n Deo Occidenti Titus Martialius Candidus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700298.translation: To the Western god, Titus Martialius Candidus gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12700298.summary: This is a votive inscription from Titus Martialius Candidus to the Western god, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-12700308.text_edition: \n Eponae Titus Flavius Claudianus tribunus militum legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis ex Syria Antiochia aram posuit curante Valerio Tertio beneficiario eius votum solvit libens\n
EDCS-12700308.translation: Titus Flavius Claudianus, military tribune of the 22nd Legion Primigenia, the Pious, the Faithful, from Antioch in Syria, set up this altar in honor of Epona, at the care of his beneficiary Valerius Tertius, and gladly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-12700308.summary: This inscription records an altar dedicated to Epona by Titus Flavius Claudianus, a military tribune, with the assistance of his beneficiary Valerius Tertius, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12700309.translation: To the genius of the century, Publius Naunius M.I.
EDCS-12700309.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of a centuria by Publius Naunius M.I., likely from the Roman army.

EDCS-12700314.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Herculi posuit Marcus Murr<a>nius Patiens manticularius\n
EDCS-12700314.translation: Marcus Murronius Patiens, a travelling salesman, set this up in honor of the divine house to Hercules.
EDCS-12700314.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Hercules and the imperial family by Marcus Murronius Patiens, a travelling salesman.

EDCS-12700315.inscription_type: tituli fabricationis, tituli honorarii, tituli sacri
EDCS-12700315.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo pro salute Neronis Claudi Caesaris Augusti Imperatoris canabari publice Publio Sulpicio Scribonio Proculo leg(ato) Augusti pro praetore cura et impensa Quinti Iuli Prisci et Quinti Iuli Aucti Samus et Severus Venicari filii sculpserunt\n
EDCS-12700315.translation: For the safety of Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Imperator, the canabarii (barrack dwellers) publicly dedicated this to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, under the care and expense of Quintus Julius Priscus and Quintus Julius Auctus. Samus and Severus, sons of Venicarius, carved it.
EDCS-12700315.summary: This inscription is a public dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by the canabarii for the safety of Emperor Nero Claudius Caesar, commissioned by Quintus Julius Priscus and Quintus Julius Auctus and carved by Samus and Severus, likely dating to Nero's reign (54-68 CE).

EDCS-12700316.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Quintus Iulius Priscus et Quintus Iulius Auctus\n
EDCS-12700316.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Quintus Julius Priscus and Quintus Julius Auctus.
EDCS-12700316.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Quintus Julius Priscus and Quintus Julius Auctus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12700317.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Aufidius Victorinus legatus Augustorum pro praetore\n
EDCS-12700317.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Caius Aufidius Victorinus, imperial legate with praetorian authority.
EDCS-12700317.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Caius Aufidius Victorinus, a Roman imperial legate, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700318.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo sacrum Lucius Cassius Primigenius et Lucius Cassius Secundus filius de sua pecunia Iovi sacrum Lucius Cassius Primigenius et Lucius Cassius Secundus \n
EDCS-12700318.translation: Sacred to Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Lucius Cassius Primigenius and his son Lucius Cassius Secundus from their own money. Sacred to Jupiter. Lucius Cassius Primigenius and Lucius Cassius Secundus.
EDCS-12700318.summary: This inscription is a dedication of sacred property to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Lucius Cassius Primigenius and his son Lucius Cassius Secundus, funded by their own money, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-12700319.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Dolicheno Domitius Asclepiades domo Arethusa Suriae sic |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae Antoninianae votum solvit\n
EDCS-12700319.translation: In honor of the divine house, Domitius Asclepiades from Arethusa in Syria, a centurion of the Twenty-second Primigenia Antoniniana legion, fulfilled his vow to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus.
EDCS-12700319.summary: A centurion of the XXII Primigenia legion dedicated an offering to Jupiter Dolichenus in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-12700320.text_edition: \n I(ovi) O(ptimo) M(aximo) Dolicheno Gaius Iulius Maternus negotiator iubente deo posuit Praesente et Extricato consulibus X Kalendas Iunias per Valentem sacerdotem\n
EDCS-12700320.translation: Gaius Iulius Maternus, a merchant, set this up to Jupiter Optimus Maximus Dolichenus by the god's command. On the 22nd day before the Kalends of June, through the priest Valens, with Praesens and Extricatus as consuls.
EDCS-12700320.summary: A merchant dedicated an offering to Jupiter Dolichenus, initiated by divine command, and dated by the consuls Praesens and Extricatus.

EDCS-12700324.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Minervae et ceteris dis immortalibus Quintus Tarronius Iulianus |(centurio) legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis pro salute sua et suorum iussus ex visu libens laetus posuit\n
EDCS-12700324.translation: Quintus Tarronius Iulianus, a centurion of the Twenty-second Primigenia pious and faithful legion, placed this willingly, happily, and deservedly for his own well-being and that of his family, having been commanded by a vision, to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Juno Regina, Minerva, and the other immortal gods.
EDCS-12700324.summary: A centurion of the XXII Primigenia legion erected a monument for his family's well-being, dedicated to several deities, after receiving a divine command.

EDCS-12700325.inscription_type: tituli honorarii, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12700325.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Libero Patri Publius Urvinus ex monitu dei aram in suo posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-12700325.translation: In honor of the divine house, Publius Urvinus dedicated an altar in his own property to Liber Pater, on the god's advice, willingly, happily, and deservedly.
EDCS-12700325.summary: Publius Urvinus dedicated an altar to Liber Pater in honor of the imperial family, based on divine advice.

EDCS-12700326.text_edition: \n Marti Camulo sacrum Fronto TEoni filius dono dedit\n
EDCS-12700326.translation: Fronton, son of Teon, gave this sacred offering to Mars Camulus.
EDCS-12700326.summary: Fronton, son of Teon, made a sacred offering to Mars Camulus.

EDCS-12700328.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Lucius Potens beneficiarius consularis aedem vetustate conlapsam restituit\n
EDCS-12700328.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Potens, a *beneficiarius consularis*, restored this temple, which had collapsed from age, to the god Mercury.
EDCS-12700328.summary: Lucius Potens, a *beneficiarius consularis*, restored a temple to Mercury in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-12700329.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Ursulia Victorina ex voto posuit libens laetus merito Sabino II et Venusto consulibus\n
EDCS-12700329.translation: In honor of the divine house, Ursulia Victorina dedicated this altar to the god Mercury, fulfilling her vow willingly, happily, and deservedly. With Sabinus II and Venustus as consuls.
EDCS-12700329.summary: Ursulia Victorina dedicated an altar to Mercury in honor of the imperial family, fulfilling a vow during the consulship of Sabinus II and Venustus.

EDCS-12700330.translation: To the goddess Minerva, Gaius IEVNV.
EDCS-12700330.summary: Gaius IEVNV dedicated an offering to the goddess Minerva.

EDCS-12700331.translation: To the goddesses of the crossroads, Ammonius.
EDCS-12700331.summary: Ammonius dedicated an offering to the Deae Quadrubiae (goddesses of crossroads).

EDCS-12700335.text_edition: \n NTINA Mogontiacensis vici navaliorum et Carinius Victor et Carinia Iustina filii votum solverunt libentes laeti merito Imperatore domino nostro Maxim[ino] Augusto et Africano consulibus\n
EDCS-12700335.translation: The inhabitants of the docklands district and Carinius Victor and his children Carinia Iustina fulfilled their vow willingly, happily, and deservedly to NTINA of Mogontiacum, during the reign of our lord Emperor Maxim[in]us Augustus and with Africanus as consul.
EDCS-12700335.summary: The inhabitants of the naval district and the Carinius family dedicated an offering to NTINA of Mogontiacum during the reign of Emperor Maximinus and the consulship of Africanus.

EDCS-12700338.translation: Caletio Similis gave this as a gift.
EDCS-12700338.summary: This is a dedication by Caletio Similis, possibly for a religious or public offering.

EDCS-12700342.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Nicasi Liberalini Victoris viri centenarii adsessoris ferrariarum s<e=I>(rvi) \n
EDCS-12700342.translation: To the departed spirits. Nicasius Liberalinus, the husband of Victoris, a centenarian assessor in the ironworks service.
EDCS-12700342.summary: A funerary epitaph for Nicasius Liberalinus, who held a position related to the iron industry, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12700343.text_edition: \n Aureliae Iuliae siveco coniugi castissimae et pientissimae quae vixit nnos menses VI dies et innocenti spirito sic Aelio Marcellino scholastico equiti Romano qui vixit nnos X menses II dies XI Aelius Martinus |(centurio) legionis XXII EI FIEICII et Marciae ti socrui quae vixit nnos LXV menses VI\n
EDCS-12700343.translation: To Aurelia Julia, my most chaste and dutiful wife, who lived X years, VI months, and [--] days, and to the innocent spirit. Aelius Marcellinus, a scholasticus, Roman eques, who lived X years, II months, and XI days. Aelius Martinus, a centurion of Legio XXII Primigenia, and Marcia, my mother-in-law, who lived LXV years, VI months.
EDCS-12700343.summary: A complex funerary inscription for multiple family members, including a wife, son, and mother-in-law, set up by a centurion of Legio XXII Primigenia, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700345.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Epigonus annorum XXV servos sic Aeli Maximi |(centurionis) legionis XXII Primigeniae\n
EDCS-12700345.translation: To the departed spirits. Epigonus, aged 25 years, slave of Aelius Maximus, a centurion of Legio XXII Primigenia.
EDCS-12700345.summary: A funerary epitaph for Epigonus, a slave of a centurion in Legio XXII Primigenia, dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700346.text_edition: \n Lucius Refidius Luci filius Terbassus domo Venafro |(centurio) legionis XVI nnum XXXV hic situs est\n
EDCS-12700346.translation: Lucius Refidius Terbassus, son of Lucius, from Venafrum, a centurion of Legio XVI, aged 35 years, lies here.
EDCS-12700346.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Refidius Terbassus, a centurion of Legio XVI, who died at age 35, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700358.translation: Legio I Adiutrix / the century of Vetus / Verus
EDCS-12700358.summary: A fragmentary military record or dedication from Legio I Adiutrix, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700359.text_edition: \n Valerius filius Claudia Crispus Savaria miles legionis I adiutricis annorum XXXII stipendiorum XIIII hic situs est testamento fieri iussit heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-12700359.translation: Valerius Crispus, son of Valerius and Claudia, from Savaria, a soldier of Legio I Adiutricis, aged 32 years, with 14 years of service, lies here; he ordered this to be made by his will, and his heir had it made.
EDCS-12700359.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valerius Crispus, a soldier in Legio I Adiutricis, who died at 32 after 14 years of service, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700360.text_edition: \n Caius Attius Cai filius Pupinia Maxsimus sic Baeterris miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum XXXVII stipendiorum XVII hic situs est heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-12700360.translation: Gaius Attius Maximus, son of Gaius, of the Pupinia tribe, from Baeterrae, a soldier of Legio IV Macedonica, aged 37 years, with 17 years of service, lies here; his heir had this made.
EDCS-12700360.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Attius Maximus, a soldier in Legio IV Macedonica, who died at 37 after 17 years of service, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700361.text_edition: \n Claudia Rusticus Teurnia miles legionis IIII Macedonicae annorum \n
EDCS-12700361.translation: Claudia Rusticus, from Teurnia, a soldier of Legio IV Macedonica, aged...
EDCS-12700361.summary: A fragmentary funerary epitaph for Claudia Rusticus, a soldier in Legio IV Macedonica, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700365.text_edition: \n Caius Cassius Luci filius Geminus Oufentina Mediolano miles legionis XV Primigeniae annorum XX stipendii I hic situs est\n
EDCS-12700365.translation: Gaius Cassius Geminus, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe, from Mediolanum, a soldier of Legio XV Primigeniae, aged 20 years, with 1 year of service, lies here.
EDCS-12700365.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Cassius Geminus, a soldier in Legio XV Primigeniae, who died at 20 after 1 year of service, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-12700366.text_edition: \n Lucius Cornelius Luci filius Colinus Pollia Eporedia miles legionis XV annorum XXII stipendii I hic situs est\n
EDCS-12700366.translation: Lucius Cornelius Colinus, son of Lucius, of the Voltinia tribe, from Eporedia, a soldier of the 15th legion, aged 22, with 1 year of service, is buried here.
EDCS-12700366.summary: This is a soldier's tombstone from the 15th legion, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-12700367.text_edition: \n Lucius Varius Luci filius Oufentina Sacco Mediolano miles legionis XV Primigeniae annorum XXV stipendii I hic situs est\n
EDCS-12700367.translation: Lucius Varius Sacco, son of Lucius, of the Oufentina tribe, from Milan, a soldier of the 15th Primigenia legion, aged 25, with 1 year of service, is buried here.
EDCS-12700367.summary: This is a tombstone for a soldier of the 15th Primigenia legion, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-12700369.text_edition: \n Caius Atilius Cai filius miles legionis XVI stipendiorum XIIII Scruttari hic situs est Marcus Annius Marcellus heres faciundum curavit\n
EDCS-12700369.translation: Caius Atilius, son of Caius, a soldier of the 16th legion with 14 years of service, a Scruttarius, is buried here. Marcus Annius Marcellus, the heir, saw to its construction.
EDCS-12700369.summary: This tombstone commemorates a soldier of the 16th legion and records that his heir commissioned the monument.

EDCS-12700370.text_edition: \n Caius Pompeius Cai filius Oufentina Mediolano miles legionis XVI nnorum XXXIV stipendiorum XIV hic situs est heres ex testamento\n
EDCS-12700370.translation: Caius Pompeius, son of Caius, of the Oufentina tribe, from Milan, a soldier of the 16th legion, aged 34, with 14 years of service, is buried here, as per his will.
EDCS-12700370.summary: This is a tombstone for a soldier of the 16th legion, erected according to his will, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-12700371.text_edition: \n Marci filius Voltinia Viana miles legionis XVI nnrum XL stipendiorum XIX hic situs est\n
EDCS-12700371.translation: A soldier of the 16th legion, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Viana, aged 40, with 19 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-12700371.summary: This is a tombstone for a soldier of the 16th legion, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-12700372.text_edition: \n Marcus Iulius Marci filius Voltinia Adiutor Apta miles legionis XXII Primigeniae annorum XXXVI stipendiorum XXII hic situs est ex testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-12700372.translation: Marcus Iulius Adiutor, son of Marcus, of the Voltinia tribe, from Apta, a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia legion, aged 36, with 22 years of service, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-12700372.summary: This tombstone commemorates a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia legion who made arrangements for its construction in his will.

EDCS-12700373.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco M M veterano legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis naupego et filio Ianuario ponendum curavit Quarta Saturnina coniux in suo sibi\n
EDCS-12700373.translation: To the departed spirits. Quarta Saturnina, his wife, saw to the construction of this monument for Marcus M M, a veteran of the 22nd Primigenia legion, pious and loyal, a boatman, and for their son Ianuarius, in her own plot.
EDCS-12700373.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by a wife to her veteran husband and son, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12700374.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lucaniae Lucillae matri karissimae et Novaniis Augusto et Aprili fratribus et Honoratiis Lupo et Afro filiis dulcissimis et Servandiae Primitivae coniugi obsequentissimae Novianius Honoratus bucinator legionis XXII Primigeniae piae fidelis\n
EDCS-12700374.translation: To the departed spirits. Novianius Honoratus, a bucinator (horn blower) of the 22nd Primigenia legion, pious and loyal, [erected this] for his most cherished mother Lucania Lucilla, and for his brothers Novanius Augustus and Aprilis, and for his most obedient wife Servandia Primitiva.
EDCS-12700374.summary: This funerary monument is dedicated by a soldier of the 22nd Primigenia legion to his family members, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-12700375.text_edition: \n Marcus Servilius Marci filius Pollia Firmus Parma miles legionis P \n
EDCS-12700375.translation: Marcus Servilius Firmus, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, from Parma, a soldier of the P [legion]...
EDCS-12700375.summary: This is a fragment of a tombstone for a soldier of an unspecified legion, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-12700379.translation: ...us, son of Marcus, of the Lem[onia?] tribe, from Bononia...
EDCS-12700379.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a tombstone, with missing information about the individual and their context.

EDCS-12700380.translation: Valerius, son of [---], of the Pomptina tribe, a soldier [---]
EDCS-12700380.summary: This incomplete inscription likely records a soldier named Valerius, including his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-12700382.text_edition: \n <G=C>enialis Clusiodi filius imaginifer ex cohorte VII Raetorum annorum XXXV stipendiorum XIII hic positus \n
EDCS-12700382.translation: Genialis, son of Clusiodus, an imaginifer (standard-bearer) from the 7th Cohort of Raetians, aged 35, with 13 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-12700382.summary: This is a tombstone for Genialis, a soldier of the 7th Cohort of Raetians, detailing his age and service length.

EDCS-12700384.text_edition: \n Surus Cocae filius natione Dansala miles e \n
EDCS-12700384.translation: Surus, son of Cocaeus, of the Dansala tribe, a soldier [---]
EDCS-12700384.summary: This fragmentary inscription identifies Surus, a soldier from the Dansala tribe.

EDCS-12700389.text_edition: \n Antullus Nigri filius annorum II hic situs est Urbana mater posuit\n
EDCS-12700389.translation: Antullus, son of Niger, aged 2 years, is buried here. His mother Urbana placed this.
EDCS-12700389.summary: This tombstone records the burial of a young child, Antullus, set up by his mother Urbana.

EDCS-12700391.text_edition: \n Bonicia Artonis filia viva sibi et Sincorillae filiae annorum XXX hic sita est\n
EDCS-12700391.translation: Bonicia, daughter of Arto, alive, placed this here for herself and for her daughter Sincorilla, aged 30.
EDCS-12700391.summary: This funerary inscription records Bonicia's provision for her own burial and that of her daughter Sincorilla.

EDCS-12700392.translation: Calpurnius [---]aro, son of [---]no, Adbugius [---]vo, by his will.
EDCS-12700392.summary: This fragmented inscription likely refers to a burial or funerary arrangement made by will, possibly involving individuals named Calpurnius and Adbugius.

EDCS-12700394.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marci Euvodi Marcia Festina et Marcia Iulia filiae heredes faciendum curaverunt\n
EDCS-12700394.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcia Festina and her daughter Marcia Iulia, the heirs, have taken care to have this made.
EDCS-12700394.summary: This tombstone, dedicated to the Divine Shades, was erected by Marcia Festina and her daughter Marcia Iulia, who were the heirs.

EDCS-12700396.text_edition: \n Ianuarius annorum VII hic situs est\n
EDCS-12700396.translation: Ianuarius, aged 7 years, is buried here.
EDCS-12700396.summary: This is a tombstone for a young child named Ianuarius, who died at the age of 7.

EDCS-12700398.summary: This is a very fragmented inscription that may record the maker or subject of a monument, possibly named Marcellinus or Sulpicianus.

EDCS-12700399.text_edition: \n Mercatorio Mercatori liberto Mercatorius Victorinus pro meritis fecit\n
EDCS-12700399.translation: Mercatorius Victorinus erected this for his freedman Mercatorio, son of Mercator, for his merits.
EDCS-12700399.summary: This inscription records a monument erected by Mercatorius Victorinus for his freedman Mercatorio, acknowledging his merits.

EDCS-12700400.summary: This inscription is fragmentary and appears to record names, possibly of a funerary context, with incomplete restorations.

EDCS-12700401.summary: This is a short funerary epitaph recording that Primus Crescens placed the monument.

EDCS-12700403.text_edition: \n Respectus natione Tr<e=F>(vir) annorum VIII Veranius natione Tr<e=F>(ir) nnrum III filii Samocna natione Tr<e=F>(vir) annorum II filia Praesens pater filiis suis posuit ob pietatem hic siti sunt \n
EDCS-12700403.translation: Respectus, a Trevir by nation, aged 8; Veranius, a Trevir by nation, aged 3; Samocna, a Trevir by nation, aged 2; Praesens, his daughter. The father placed this for his children, who are buried here, out of piety.
EDCS-12700403.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father for his young children, who were Trevirs by nation and are buried here.

EDCS-12700404.text_edition: \n Rhodine Pollentina annorum XX qum sic natis II hic sita est Caius Rulius Cai Pollia Pollentia Rhodine ancillae suae et natis II posuit sit grata requies quem pia qura sic tegit hospes qui casus legisti nostros et precor ut dicas sit tibi Rhcodine terra levis\n
EDCS-12700404.translation: Rhodine Pollentina, aged 20, who died 2 days after birth, is buried here. Caius Rulius Cai, Pollia Pollentia, and Rhodine, his slave, and his two children placed this for their slave Rhodine and their two children. May rest be granted to you. May the earth lie lightly on you, stranger, who have read our misfortunes, and I beg that it may be said that the earth lies lightly on Rhodine.
EDCS-12700404.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Rhodine, a slave, placed by her owner and his family, with a plea for rest and a wish for the earth to lie lightly upon her.

EDCS-12700405.translation: Saturninus... and for himself... he made.
EDCS-12700405.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the construction of a monument or tomb by Saturninus, possibly for himself and others.

EDCS-12700406.translation: Lucius Seblasius Amandus, freedman of Lucius, is buried here.
EDCS-12700406.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the burial of Lucius Seblasius Amandus, a freedman.

EDCS-12700407.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to be a funerary epitaph, possibly naming the deceased and their age.

EDCS-12700408.translation: To the departed spirits. Superina or Viventio.
EDCS-12700408.summary: This is a dedication to the Manes (departed spirits), likely for a tomb, naming Superina or Viventio.

EDCS-12700410.translation: Trophimus, slave of Marcus Marius Rusticus, aged 20, is buried here. His mother grieving Trophimus without end. This is a fatal flaw, to spare the child.
EDCS-12700410.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Trophimus, a slave, placed by his grieving mother, lamenting the fate that took him.

EDCS-12700420.translation: ...25 years... months... Zontius... lived for years
EDCS-12700420.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph recording the age of the deceased, Zontius, with incomplete details.

EDCS-12700437.translation: Bonosus, sweetest and most loving son, who lived...
EDCS-12700437.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a beloved son named Bonosus.

EDCS-12700438.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-12700438.translation: Crispinus placed this monument for his sweetest wife Maura, who fulfilled the decree of kinship in our one marriage for 12 months and 27 days, who lived 17 years, 9 months, and 20 days. Crispinus placed this monument for his wife Maura in Christ Jesus.
EDCS-12700438.summary: A funerary inscription by Crispinus for his wife Maura, detailing their marriage duration and her lifespan, likely from the Christian period.

EDCS-12700439.translation: Here rests Genuarius, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-12700439.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death of Genuarius at the age of 25.

EDCS-12700440.translation: Here rests in peace Leoncia, who lived 68 years. Blessed, she rested on Monday. Here rests [---]iova, who lived [---] days 10 days. Blessed rested [---]es, on Friday, at the [---] hour. He/She delighted the Lord. [He/She] deigned to have one monument.
EDCS-12700440.summary: A fragmented Christian funerary inscription for Leoncia and another individual, recording their ages and dates of death.

EDCS-12700442.translation: Here lies Saturnus. He lived well. His pious father placed [this].
EDCS-12700442.summary: A funerary inscription for Saturnus, who lived 9 years, erected by his father.

EDCS-12700445.translation: Ursus lived in peace for 3 years and 3 months.
EDCS-12700445.summary: A funerary inscription for Ursus, indicating he lived for 3 years and 3 months.

EDCS-12700469.text_edition: \n Gai Rai Manibus Atrectus Nani filius cohortis IIII Vindelicorum centuria Muraesi heres secun<d>us de suo fecit\n
EDCS-12700469.translation: For the spirits of Gaius Raes, Atrectus son of Nanus, second heir of the century of Muraesus in the 4th Cohort of the Vindelici, made at his own expense.
EDCS-12700469.summary: A funerary epitaph for Atrectus, a soldier of the 4th Cohort of Vindelici, indicating he was a second heir and the monument was self-funded.

EDCS-12700482.translation: In the reign of Emperor Commodus Augustus. From the century of Victor in the 32nd Volunteer Cohort. Dasius Masuri.
EDCS-12700482.summary: A military inscription from the time of Emperor Commodus, mentioning Dasius Masuri from the 32nd Volunteer Cohort.

EDCS-12700485.summary: A fragmented inscription likely related to a military tent-group (contubernium).

EDCS-12700490.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo cohors IIII Aquitanorum equitata civium Romanorum cui praeest Caius Tettius Secundus praefectus votum solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-12700490.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest. The 4th Cohort of Aquitani, an equestrian unit of Roman citizens, commanded by Gaius Tettius Secundus, its prefect, fulfilled its vow willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-12700490.summary: A dedication by the 4th Cohort of Aquitani, an equestrian unit, to Jupiter, thanking their prefect Gaius Tettius Secundus for fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-12700493.translation: Syrian, a soldier of the I cohort of sagittarii, aged 50 years, with 11 years of service, lies here.
EDCS-12700493.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a Syrian soldier serving in the I cohort of archers.

EDCS-12700494.translation: Aetherius the presbyter is covered by this tomb, dear to all in his character and grace, but especially proven in Christ's faith and religion.
EDCS-12700494.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aetherius, a presbyter, highlighting his Christian devotion.

EDCS-12700506.text_edition: \n centuria Sabini Leubacciorum Germani<c=S>orum centuria Gemelli Mansueti AIITIS centuria P Flavini Primi \n
EDCS-12700506.translation: Centuria of Sabinus of the Leubacci, Germani; centuria of Gemellus of Mansuetus; centuria of P. Flavinius Primus.
EDCS-12700506.summary: This inscription lists the names of three centurions, likely related to military units or land divisions.

EDCS-12700508.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the divine power of Augustus(?), to Mars Smertrius and Vindoridus Boudna, Gnaeus Domitius, son of Gnaeus(?)...
EDCS-12700508.summary: This is a dedication honoring the imperial family, Mars Smertrius, Vindoridus Boudna, made by Gnaeus Domitius.

EDCS-12700509.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Numini Aug(usti) Marti Smertrio et Vindoridio Boudnae Cnaeus Domitius C qui burgum aedificaverunt Lup Amminus praefectus Sab Acceptio Vid Perpetuus Flavius Tasgillus Co Lepidus Minucius Luppus cum Ces Ursulus paratus est Victorino Augusto et Sancto consulibus X Kalendas Iunias\n
EDCS-12700509.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the divine power of Augustus, to Mars Smertrius and Vindoridus Boudna, Gnaeus Domitius, and Amminus, prefect of the Cohors Equitata Acceptio, built the burgus. Vid. Perpetuus, Flavius Tasgillus, Lepidus, Minucius Luppus, with Ursulus, were prepared. In the consulship of Victorinus and Sanctus, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-12700509.summary: This inscription records the construction of a fortified settlement (burgus) by Gnaeus Domitius and Amminus, dedicated to the imperial family and deities, with a specific date provided.

EDCS-12700510.summary: This is a fragmented inscription mentioning the construction or dedication of a temple by Caius Sextius.

EDCS-12700511.text_edition: \n Tessiato Titiliae filio et Taticoni Iblissae filiae uxsori sic et Saturninae filiae eorum\n
EDCS-12700511.translation: To Tessiatus, son of Titilia, and to Taticon, daughter of Iblissa, his wife, and also to their daughter Saturnina.
EDCS-12700511.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Tessiatus, his wife Taticon, and their daughter Saturnina.

EDCS-12700513.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Genio capsariorum numeri Divitiensium Gordianorum Titus Flavius Processus medicus hordinarius sic sub Caio Vibio Vitale praefecto numeri supra scripti donum posuit\n
EDCS-12700513.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Genius of the capsarii (orderlies) of the Gordiani Divitienses unit, Titus Flavius Processus, the ordinary doctor, placed this gift under Gaius Vibius Vitalis, the prefect of the aforementioned unit.
EDCS-12700513.summary: This is a dedication by Titus Flavius Processus, a doctor, to the Genius of the capsarii unit, under the prefecture of Gaius Vibius Vitalis.

EDCS-13302673.text_edition: \n VVGSA REMVLOSVNIAEQVE ORBVTERAVO N TOSRMEGIGEEVRDAD OETLRI CANANIE entos ex condemnatione Iuventi Caesiani legati felicissimi Augusti legionis octavae Augustae piae fidae legatos Secundio Secundi filio Prifernio Victorino |(denarios) quingentos faeneratos ntos sebtuaginta sic sex denarios reliquos sescentos sebtuaginta sic tres creditos denarios ENVDIARDVSi vindicaret ni traderet in quam rem pari examine actum municipio Aris pridie Nonas Augustas Imperatore Marco Aurelio Commodo Antonino Augusto Felice quinquies et Manio Acilio Glabrione bis consulibus tributis et intributionibus omnibus ex ea summa e census \n
EDCS-13302673.translation: For the VVGSA, for Remulosunia, and for the whole of Oebuteravus, the consuls Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Augustus Felix (for the fifth time) and Manius Acilius Glabrio (for the second time) granted from the census, on the day before the Nones of August, the sum of five hundred denarii, lent out, seventy-seven denarii, and the remaining six hundred and seventy-three denarii, credited, in order that NVDIARDVS might claim them, if they were not handed over, concerning which matter an action was taken with equal judgment in the municipality of Aris, from all tributes and impositions from that sum.
EDCS-13302673.summary: This is a complex legal or financial document from the municipality of Aris, detailing a loan and its repayment terms, issued during the consulship of Marcus Aurelius Commodus Antoninus Felix and Manius Acilius Glabrio.

EDCS-13303287.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Domitius Lucinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-13303287.translation: To the god Mercury, Domitius Lucinus gladly paid his vow, as deserved.
EDCS-13303287.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mercury by Domitius Lucinus.

EDCS-13303288.text_edition: \n Biraca Sabini filia hic sita annorum VIIII\n
EDCS-13303288.translation: Biraca, daughter of Sabinus, lies here, aged 9 years.
EDCS-13303288.summary: This is a tombstone for a young girl named Biraca, who died at the age of nine.

EDCS-13303289.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Lillutius, son of Cantianus.
EDCS-13303289.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirits for Lillutius, son of Cantianus.

EDCS-13303300.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Camulat(i)a, aged 80 years.
EDCS-13303300.summary: This epitaph records the death of Camulat(i)a, who lived to be 80 years old.

EDCS-13303307.translation: Firminius Augustio, Adamatius Taurinus, Sabinianus Diginianus, Ioinus Honoratus, Felix, Iinius Victor.
EDCS-13303307.summary: This inscription lists several individuals, likely part of a dedication or a funerary monument, with fragmented names and cognomina.

EDCS-13303313.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. The heir made (this) for Loconi and Crobius, sons of Tutulus.
EDCS-13303313.summary: This is a funerary dedication for two brothers, Loconi and Crobius, sons of Tutulus, erected by their heir.

EDCS-13303314.translation: To the spirits of the underworld for Marcellinus and Paulina.
EDCS-13303314.summary: This is a dedication to the departed spirits for Marcellinus and Paulina.

EDCS-13303315.translation: While alive, [he set this up] for Biliuretus in that place.
EDCS-13303315.summary: This inscription indicates a monument erected during the lifetime of Biliuretus.

EDCS-13303316.translation: Died(?) Tuteua, daughter of Dagillus, aged 60 years. To the spirits of the underworld. Drucicarus, aged 20 years.
EDCS-13303316.summary: This inscription records the death of Tuteua, aged 60, and Drucicarus, aged 20, with an unclear initial word possibly referring to death.

EDCS-13303317.translation: For Attius Silvinus, a veteran of the legion, and for Attiola, his wife, and for Silvester, his son, who lived 16 years, and for Lea, his daughter-in-law, who passed away, and for Ianus, their grandson. Silvinius Victor, while alive, [erected this] for himself and his family.
EDCS-13303317.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Silvinius Victor for his family, including his wife, son, daughter-in-law, and grandson, as well as a veteran named Attius Silvinus.

EDCS-13303318.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the goddess Fortuna. Dentilianus Divicianus erected (this) willingly, gladly, deservedly, in accordance with a vow.
