EDCS-13303318.summary: This inscription records a votive offering made by Dentilianus Divicianus to the goddess Fortuna in honor of the imperial family.

EDCS-13303321.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Ianuarius, the freedman, took care to have this made for Lucius Capitonius Paternus.
EDCS-13303321.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman for his patron, Lucius Capitonius Paternus.

EDCS-13303330.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His children took care to place this for Ianuarius Cattus.
EDCS-13303330.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by the children for Ianuarius Cattus.

EDCS-13303334.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sedata, daughter of Seranus.
EDCS-13303334.summary: This is an incomplete funerary epitaph for Sedata, daughter of Seranus.

EDCS-13303335.translation: To the spirits of the departed. His children took care to place this for Marcus Virius Paternus, son of Sextus.
EDCS-13303335.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by the children for Marcus Virius Paternus.

EDCS-13303353.summary: This is a very brief funerary epitaph possibly indicating the name of the deceased and the person who set it up.

EDCS-13400078.translation: Gemellianus made this at the Aquis Helveticis (Baden, Switzerland).
EDCS-13400078.summary: This is an inscription recording the construction of something at the Roman baths of Aquis Helveticis by Gemellianus.

EDCS-13400158.translation: The 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis. Sempronius Fronto.
EDCS-13400158.summary: This inscription likely records the name of a soldier, Sempronius Fronto, belonging to the 22nd Legion Primigenia Pia Fidelis.

EDCS-13400239.summary: This inscription refers to a military unit, possibly indicating ownership or a boundary marker of the century of Quintus Voltius.

EDCS-13600439.text_edition: \n centuria Cnaei TaCexati Marci Popili Postumi cohortis X Caius Sertorius |(centurio) M Naibilius sic centuria Tii\n
EDCS-13600439.translation: The century of Gnaeus Ta[---]exatus, son of Marcus Popilius Postumus, of the 10th cohort. Caius Sertorius, centurion. Naibilius. This century of Tii.
EDCS-13600439.summary: This inscription details military organization, naming centurions and possibly a cohort and century, likely related to a boundary or ownership marker.

EDCS-13900085.translation: Marcus A. C. of the 22nd Legion Pia Fidelis.
EDCS-13900085.summary: This inscription records the name of Marcus A. C., a soldier belonging to the 22nd Legion Pia Fidelis.

EDCS-13900130.translation: The troop of Postumus Lepontius, an equestrian.
EDCS-13900130.summary: This inscription records a cavalryman named Lepontius who served in the troop of Postumus.

EDCS-13900131.text_edition: \n Cicollus Brixsa Cunn Cicollus Brixsa Cunn\n
EDCS-13900131.translation: Cicollus, Brixsa, Cunn. Cicollus, Brixsa, Cunn.
EDCS-13900131.summary: This inscription appears to be a repetition of personal names, possibly a dedication or memorial, with no further context.

EDCS-13900132.translation: Quintus Septimius Licinus, centurion of the Spanish cohort.
EDCS-13900132.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Septimius Licinus, a centurion in a Spanish cohort.

EDCS-13900134.summary: This inscription likely commemorates Valerius, a trumpeter, possibly on a tombstone.

EDCS-13900135.text_edition: \n Dabis Aninio Moderato militi legionis XXI rapacis centuria Vindicis\n
EDCS-13900135.translation: Dabis, to Aninius Moderatus, a soldier of the 21st Rapax legion, in the century of Vindicis.
EDCS-13900135.summary: This is a dedication to Aninius Moderatus, a soldier in the 21st Rapax legion, in Vindicis' century.

EDCS-13900137.text_edition: \n AL C F C AA Auli Vetti Prisci legati Augusti DX\n
EDCS-13900137.translation: For his father, the son of Aulus Vettius Priscus, legate of Augustus, for the 30th time.
EDCS-13900137.summary: This inscription is a dedication by the son of Aulus Vettius Priscus, who served as legate of Augustus multiple times.

EDCS-13900520.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Publius Atton<i>us Patrinus aram de suo in in suo posuit laetus libens merito Imperatore domino nostro Severo Alexandro III et Dione consulibus\n
EDCS-13900520.translation: In honor of the divine house, Publius Attonius Patrinus gladly, willingly, and deservedly dedicated an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus at his own expense on his own land, during the consulship of our emperor Severus Alexander for the third time and Dio.
EDCS-13900520.summary: This inscription records the dedication of an altar to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Publius Attonius Patrinus during the consulship of Severus Alexander and Dio.

EDCS-13900607.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo vicani Salodurenses publice magistris vici io Vikano sic II Tito Pedio Mallusio\n
EDCS-13900607.translation: In honor of the divine house, the villagers of Salodurum publicly dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, under the magistracies of the vicus, to the vicus teacher II, Tito Pedio Mallusio.
EDCS-13900607.summary: This inscription records a public dedication by the villagers of Salodurum to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, honoring their vicus teacher Tito Pedio Mallusio.

EDCS-13900610.text_edition: \n Iullus Adcomargi Decmus Brutti de s<u>o dederunt\n
EDCS-13900610.translation: Iullus and Adcomargus and Decmus Brutti gave from their own property.
EDCS-13900610.summary: This inscription records a gift or dedication of property by Iullus, Adcomargus, and Decmus Brutti.

EDCS-14800072.summary: This inscription likely records the name of Marcus Afranius Professus, possibly on a tomb or dedicatory monument.

EDCS-14800074.translation: The 21st Legion, under the supervision of Victoris.
EDCS-14800074.summary: This inscription records a statement by the 21st Legion, overseen by Victoris.

EDCS-14800075.summary: This inscription is a dedication or ownership mark belonging to Lucius Cornelius Priscus.

EDCS-14800076.summary: This inscription records that Camillius Torquatus created the object or monument.

EDCS-14800079.text_edition: \n Deo Mercurio Iulius Sextus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800079.translation: To the god Mercury, Iulius Sextus gladly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800079.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mercury, dedicated by Iulius Sextus.

EDCS-14800088.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Augusto Iulianus Bioxxi filius donum solvit votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800088.translation: To Lord Mars Augustus, Iulianus, son of Bioxxi, presented a gift and gladly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800088.summary: This is a votive inscription to Lord Mars Augustus, dedicated by Iulianus, son of Bioxxi.

EDCS-14800089.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Berexe Sembi filia votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800089.translation: To Lord Mars Berexe, Sembi, daughter of [?], gladly paid her vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800089.summary: This is a votive inscription to Lord Mars Berexe, dedicated by Sembi, daughter of [?].

EDCS-14800090.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Augusto Tittullius Avitinus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800090.translation: To Lord Mars Augustus, Tittullius Avitinus gladly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800090.summary: This is a votive inscription to Lord Mars Augustus, dedicated by Tittullius Avitinus.

EDCS-14800091.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Augusto Iulianus Bioxxi filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800091.translation: To Lord Mars Augustus, Iulianus, son of Bioxxi, gladly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800091.summary: This is a votive inscription to Lord Mars Augustus, dedicated by Iulianus, son of Bioxxi.

EDCS-14800092.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Gracilia Severa votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800092.translation: To Lord Mars, Gracilia Severa gladly paid her vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800092.summary: This is a votive inscription to Lord Mars, dedicated by Gracilia Severa.

EDCS-14800093.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Andos Leurisi votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800093.translation: To Lord Mars, Andos Leurisi gladly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-14800093.summary: This is a votive inscription to Lord Mars, dedicated by Andos Leurisi.

EDCS-14800094.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Augusto Gaius Valerius Sabinianus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800094.translation: To the lord Mars Augustus, Gaius Valerius Sabinianus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800094.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars by Gaius Valerius Sabinianus.

EDCS-14800095.text_edition: \n Marti domino Xalinis Salixi votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800095.translation: To the lord Mars Xalis, Salixus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800095.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars by Salixus.

EDCS-14800096.summary: This is a short inscription recording a dedication to the god Mars.

EDCS-14800097.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a dedication by Verecundus to a deity named Belex.

EDCS-14800098.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Andossus Obbelexxi filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800098.translation: To the lord Mars Andossus, Obbelexxi's son, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800098.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars Andossus by the son of Obbelexxi.

EDCS-14800099.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Porcius Trofumus sic votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800099.translation: To the lord Mars, Porcius Trofumus thus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800099.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars by Porcius Trofumus.

EDCS-14800100.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Xembus Bambixxi votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800100.translation: To the lord Mars Xembus, Bambixxi willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800100.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars Xembus by Bambixxi.

EDCS-14800101.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Flaminia Festiba sic votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800101.translation: To the lord Mars, Flaminia Festiba thus willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-14800101.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars by Flaminia Festiba.

EDCS-14800102.translation: Ciurxos, son of Doxxus, [made] a vow to Mars.
EDCS-14800102.summary: This is a votive inscription recording a vow made to the god Mars by Ciurxos, son of Doxxus.

EDCS-14800103.text_edition: \n Votum solvit libens merito domino Marti Bambixxus Sembeocci\n
EDCS-14800103.translation: Bambixxus, son of Sembeocc, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the lord Mars.
EDCS-14800103.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Mars by Bambixxus, son of Sembeocc.

EDCS-14800104.summary: This inscription appears to be a very brief dedication or naming inscription, likely for Severus Iuvalis.

EDCS-14800105.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Bonxus Sembedonis Iuli libertus\n
EDCS-14800105.translation: To Lord Mars, Bonxus, freedman of Sembedo, willingly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800105.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars, dedicated by Bonxus, a freedman, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800106.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Fuscus Iustini filius votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800106.translation: To Lord Mars, Fuscus, son of Justinus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800106.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars, dedicated by Fuscus, son of Justinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800107.summary: This inscription appears to be a very brief dedication or naming inscription, likely for Verinus Octo.

EDCS-14800109.translation: To Lord Mars, Iustinus, [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-14800109.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars, dedicated by Iustinus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800110.translation: Silixius Carerdonis to his lord Mars, [fulfilled his vow].
EDCS-14800110.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars, dedicated by Silixius Carerdonis, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800111.text_edition: \n Xembesus Hissi domino Marti votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800111.translation: Xembesus Hissi to his lord Mars, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800111.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars, dedicated by Xembesus Hissi, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800112.text_edition: \n Domino Marti Augusto Iulius Bonnoxus votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-14800112.translation: To Lord Mars Augustus, Iulius Bonnoxus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-14800112.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars Augustus, dedicated by Iulius Bonnoxus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800115.text_edition: \n Iuliana Handos domini sic Marti votum\n
EDCS-14800115.translation: Iuliana Handos to her lord Mars, [fulfilled her vow].
EDCS-14800115.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Mars, dedicated by Iuliana Handos, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-14800117.summary: This inscription appears to be a very brief dedication or naming inscription, likely for Andossus Banbixi.

EDCS-14800121.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication naming the dedicator, Victor Sembius Victor.

EDCS-14800122.text_edition: \n Maria Corisilla ex vissu sic voto sic solvit libens laeta merito\n
EDCS-14800122.translation: Maria Corisilla, in accordance with a vision, thus paid her vow, gladly and joyfully, as was deserved.
EDCS-14800122.summary: This is a votive inscription where Maria Corisilla fulfilled a vow after a vision, likely dedicated to a deity.

EDCS-14800126.text_edition: \n Herequrae sic Ritie Victoris votum solvit libens\n
EDCS-14800126.translation: Herequra, and Ritie Victoris, paid her vow gladly.
EDCS-14800126.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Herequra and Ritie Victoris.

EDCS-14800127.text_edition: \n Mogontiaci A V akippi sic |(denarios) ducentos Nonis Aprilibus Catullino et Apro consulibus N M \n
EDCS-14800127.translation: At Mogontiacum, A. Vakip(p)ius paid two hundred denarii on the Nones of April, when Catullinus and Aper were consuls.  To the departed spirit.
EDCS-14800127.summary: This is a financial record or dedication from Mogontiacum, specifying a payment of two hundred denarii on a specific date during the consulship of Catullinus and Aper.

EDCS-15300321.text_edition: \n Legio XI Claudia pia fidelis |(centuria)? P(ubli) Orci\n
EDCS-15300321.translation: From the legion XI Claudia pia fidelis, from the century of Publius Orcus.
EDCS-15300321.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary stone or identifies a standard belonging to a century within the XI Claudia legion.

EDCS-15300322.text_edition: \n Legio I Flavia Minervia |(centuria)? Sesti Phoebi\n
EDCS-15300322.translation: From the legion I Flavia Minervia, from the century of Sextus Phoebus.
EDCS-15300322.summary: This inscription likely marks a boundary stone or identifies a standard belonging to a century within the I Flavia Minervia legion.

EDCS-15300323.translation: From Dabis, from the century of Frontinus Caius.
EDCS-15300323.summary: This inscription likely identifies a boundary stone or a standard belonging to a century named after Frontinus Caius.

EDCS-15300325.summary: This is likely a dedication or memorial inscription in honor of Aulus Maranius Silicius.

EDCS-15300327.text_edition: \n Caio Aemilio Luperco militi legionis XI Claudiae piae fidelis centuria \n
EDCS-15300327.translation: To Gaius Aemilius Lupercus, soldier of the legion XI Claudia pia fidelis, from the century.
EDCS-15300327.summary: This is likely a dedication or memorial inscription for Gaius Aemilius Lupercus, a soldier of the XI Claudia legion.

EDCS-15300331.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription for Eurylo or his slave.

EDCS-15300332.text_edition: \n Dabes sic Sexto Calvio militi legionis \n
EDCS-15300332.translation: You will give [it] to Sextus Calvius, a soldier of the legion.
EDCS-15300332.summary: This is a payment or delivery instruction to Sextus Calvius, a legionary soldier, likely from a tablet or record.

EDCS-15300333.text_edition: \n Dabis Quinto Attio Basso Dabis Quinto V D centuria Saturnini\n
EDCS-15300333.translation: You will give [it] to Quintus Attius Bassus, from the century of Saturninus.
EDCS-15300333.summary: This is a payment or delivery instruction to Quintus Attius Bassus, specifying his centurion and century, likely from a tablet or record.

EDCS-15300335.text_edition: \n Dabis Annio Luciano qui est in giro ecestri sic Vindoinsa\n
EDCS-15300335.translation: You will give [it] to Annius Lucianus, who is in the *giro ecestri*, to Vindoinsa.
EDCS-15300335.summary: This is a payment or delivery instruction to Annius Lucianus, mentioning a specific group or location (*giro ecestri*), likely from a tablet or record.

EDCS-15300337.translation: To Primigenius of Oclatius, from the century of Primigenius Imber.
EDCS-15300337.summary: This inscription records a dedication or assignment to Primigenius, identifying his centurion and century.

EDCS-15700042.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Marti Severus Alexandri miles legionis XXII Primigeniae Antoninianae piae fidelis custos castelli figlinarum cives sic T<hr=RH>ax ex voto posuit Imperatore domino nostro A[ntonino] Augusto III et Valerio Comasonte sic consulibus dedicavit VII Kalendas Apriles \n
EDCS-15700042.translation: In honor of the divine house, Severus, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia Antoniniana Pia Fidelis legion, keeper of the Figlinae fortress, a citizen of T(h)rax, set this up as a votive offering; he dedicated it under our lord the Emperor Antoninus Augustus III and Valerius Comasonte as consuls, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April.
EDCS-15700042.summary: This is a military dedication to Mars, set up by Severus, a soldier of the XXII Primigenia legion, during the consulship of Antoninus Augustus III and Valerius Comasonte, likely in the early 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15700115.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Soli Invicto Mithrae aram Privatii Secundinus et Tertinus et Confinis ex voto Privati Tertini votum solverunt laeti libentes merito\n
EDCS-15700115.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Unconquered Sun Mithras, Privatus Secundinus, Tertinus, and Confinis fulfilled a vow for Privatus Tertinus; they happily, willingly, and deservedly completed the vow.
EDCS-15700115.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to Sol Invictus Mithras, fulfilling a vow by several individuals, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15700132.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Deo Invicto Mytrhe sic aram ex voto dei de suo impendio instituerunt Aulus Gratius Iuvenis pater sacrorum et Aulus Gratius Potens miles legionis XXII matricarius fratres dedicaverunt consule Africano\n
EDCS-15700132.translation: In honor of the divine house, to the Unconquered God Mithras, they erected this altar as a votive offering from their own expense: Aulus Gratius Iuvenis, father of the sacred rites, and Aulus Gratius Potens, a soldier of the XXII legion, a matricularius, his brother, dedicated it during the consulship of Africanus.
EDCS-15700132.summary: This is a dedication of an altar to the god Mithras, sponsored by Aulus Gratius Iuvenis and his brother Aulus Gratius Potens, a soldier of the XXII legion, during the consulship of Africanus, likely in the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-15800327.summary: This is a simple owner's mark or ownership inscription, likely on a piece of property or an object.

EDCS-15800328.text_edition: \n QE Quinti Postumi Hermetis chloron ad epiphoras Quinti Postumi Hermetis pelaginum sic ad claritatem O TA\n
EDCS-15800328.translation: From Quintus Postumius Hermes's chloron for afflictions, Quintus Postumius Hermes's pelaginum for clarity.
EDCS-15800328.summary: This inscription lists two medicinal preparations, 'chloron' and 'pelaginum', associated with Quintus Postumius Hermes for treating ailments and improving clarity.

EDCS-15900061.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Amminio Adnamato defuncto Restia coniux faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-15900061.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Amminius Adnamatus, who has died; Restia, his wife, saw to its construction.
EDCS-15900061.summary: This is a tombstone inscription (dis manibus) for Amminius Adnamatus, commissioned by his wife Restia.

EDCS-15900366.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Olitio Gaipori et Primiae Secundae uxsori sic heredes fecerunt\n
EDCS-15900366.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. The heirs of Olitios, son of Gaipor, and of Prima Secunda, his wife, erected this.
EDCS-15900366.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Olitios and his wife Prima Secunda, erected by their heirs, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-15900367.translation: Here lies Sarmanna, the healer. She lived more or less 70 years. Pientius Pientinus, her son, and Honorata, her daughter-in-law, placed this tombstone in peace.
EDCS-15900367.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sarmanna, a female healer, stating her age and identifying the relatives who erected the monument, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-15900368.summary: A very brief inscription, likely an ownership mark or a dedication, possibly related to craftsmanship or a building, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-16000507.translation: Under the emperor Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, in his 12th consulship, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the 7th time, consul for the 4th time, father of the country, [Quintus Curtius Rufus, imperial legate pro praetore], [Marcus Licinius Senecio, imperial legate], [the 21st Legion Rapax].
EDCS-16000507.summary: This inscription is a fragment of a larger dedication, listing imperial consuls and legates, and mentioning a legion, likely dating to the reign of Claudius (41-54 AD).

EDCS-16100259.text_edition: \n centuria Murrae Marci centuria Flori Marci Iuli Celeris Legionis IIII centuria Rufini centuria Flavi Aper sic centuria Flori Iuli\n
EDCS-16100259.translation: The century of Murra, son of Marcus; the century of Florus, son of Marcus Iulius Celer; the century of Rufinus; the century of Flavius Aper; thus the century of Florus, son of Iulius.
EDCS-16100259.summary: This inscription lists several centuries, possibly within a Roman legion or administrative division, identified by the names of their centurions or associated figures, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-16100424.summary: A brief inscription identifying a 'century of Numerius', likely a military or administrative unit, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-16100426.translation: Dabis for Belica against the bathhouse.
EDCS-16100426.summary: This inscription seems to record a dispute or a legal proceeding concerning a bathhouse, possibly related to property or rights, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-16200765.translation: Garum from Hispania, belonging to Frontonius the steward.
EDCS-16200765.summary: This is an inscription related to commerce, specifically identifying a product (garum, a fermented fish sauce) and its owner or producer, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16200767.text_edition: \n Potitus Fusci adversarius Ivisum Valli Marullum Pusionis Maxsumus sic Priuni Nervinum Paterni Maturum Suavis Turicum Macri Sulpicium Secundani Prudentem Solvendi Mensor Marulli Novimarum Marulli servos sic Secundam ES litis vanus est datur\n
EDCS-16200767.translation: Potitus, adversary of Fuscus, against Ivisus, son of Vallius Marullus, son of Pusionus; Maxsumus; thus Priunius Nervinus, son of Paternus; Maturus; Suavis; Turicus, son of Macr(i)us; Sulpicius Secundanus; Prudentem Solvendi; Mensor, son of Marullus; Novimarum, son of Marullus; slaves, thus Secunda. [---] is vain. It is given.
EDCS-16200767.summary: This complex inscription appears to record a legal dispute, listing various individuals, possibly as plaintiffs, defendants, or witnesses, in a dispute concerning slaves, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-16200865.text_edition: \n Tiberi C<l=I>(audi) Peregrini dialepidos ad cicatrices Tiberi C<l=I>(audi) Peregrini diabsoricum sic ad claritatem \n
EDCS-16200865.translation: Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus's oil for scrofula; Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus's depilatory, for clarity.
EDCS-16200865.summary: This inscription advertises two medicinal preparations, an oil for scrofula and a depilatory, both attributed to Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-16200866.text_edition: \n Tiberi Claudi Peregrini aniceton ad aspritudines et claritatem Tiberi Claudi Peregrini cinnaminum ad suppurationem Tiberi Claudi Peregrini diamisus ad aspritudines Tiberi Claudi Peregrini diasmyrnes ad sedata\n
EDCS-16200866.translation: Of Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus: Aniceton for harshness and clarity; cinnamomum for suppurations; diamisus for harshness; diasmyrnes for settled conditions.
EDCS-16200866.summary: This inscription lists medicinal preparations by Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus, likely for sale or personal use, perhaps dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200867.text_edition: \n Tiberi Claudi Peregrini diapsoricum ad aspritudines Tiberi Claudi Peregrini cnnum ad caliginem Tiberi Alpi Soterichi cinnaminum ad caliginem Tiberi Alpi Soterichi diapsoricum ad c<l=I>aritatem \n
EDCS-16200867.translation: Of Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus: Diapsoricum for harshness; cinnamomum for cloudy vision; of Tiberius Alpus Soterichus: cinnamomum for cloudy vision; diapsoricum for clarity.
EDCS-16200867.summary: This inscription records medicinal preparations by Tiberius Claudius Peregrinus and Tiberius Alpus Soterichus, possibly for sale or personal use, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200870.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial for Valerius, a shield-bearer, possibly related to military service or a funerary context.

EDCS-16200873.translation: To Veranius, soldier of the XIII Legion, of Vasio.

EDCS-16200875.summary: This short inscription records a dedication by Marcus M. S. to the god Mars, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200876.text_edition: \n centuria Claudi Primi Quinti ConDati Secundi\n
EDCS-16200876.translation: Century of Claudius Primus, Quintus Condatus, Secundus.
EDCS-16200876.summary: This inscription lists names associated with a century, possibly belonging to officers or members of a military unit, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16200878.text_edition: \n Sexti Antisti Draconis Luci Valeri centuria Terenti\n
EDCS-16200878.translation: Of Sextus Antistius Dracon, Lucius Valerius, century of Terentius.
EDCS-16200878.summary: This inscription lists individuals associated with a century, likely indicating membership in a military unit or a specific group.

EDCS-16200882.text_edition: \n centuria Antei Salonini Cai Calvi Me<r>katoris sic\n
EDCS-16200882.translation: Century of Anteius Saloninus, Caius Calvus, the merchant.

EDCS-16200951.summary: This is a dedication by Belliccus to Vasiona.

EDCS-16201165.text_edition: \n Q<ua=AV>drubiis sic Mansuaeta sic votum solvit libens merito \n
EDCS-16201165.translation: Mansueta, freed from her quadruped, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-16201165.summary: This records a votive offering made by Mansueta.

EDCS-16201218.translation: Here will rest in peace the matron named Remicus, together with her sons Duccio and Dersto Dadilo, with their sons; they set up this tombstone.
EDCS-16201218.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Remicus and her descendants, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16201219.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deo Mercurio Cimbriano aedem cum signo Tettius Perpetuius Carus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-16201219.translation: In honor of the divine house, Tettius Perpetuius Carus willingly, happily, and deservedly dedicated this temple with its statue to the god Mercurius Cimbrianus.
EDCS-16201219.summary: This is a dedication of a temple and statue to the god Mercurius Cimbrianus by Tettius Perpetuius Carus.

EDCS-16201609.translation: Samus and Severus, sons of Venicarius, carved this.
EDCS-16201609.summary: This records the work of stonecutters Samus and Severus.

EDCS-16201683.text_edition: \n Honesti Lautini dialepidos ad aspritudines Honesti Lautini diamisus ad veteres cicatrices Honesti Lautini dialibanum ad impetum lippitudinis Honesti Lautini diagesamias ad suppurationes\n
EDCS-16201683.translation: Honestus Lautinus's balm for roughness, Honestus Lautinus's oil for old scars, Honestus Lautinus's incense for the onset of dimness of sight, Honestus Lautinus's incense for suppuration.
EDCS-16201683.summary: This lists several medicinal preparations made by Honestus Lautinus.

EDCS-16201999.translation: Detachment of the legion LOG[...], to Flavius Af[...], the legate.

EDCS-16300110.text_edition: \n Cai Flamini Marcionis nardinum ad impetum\n

EDCS-16500040.translation: To Mars the Soldier, Lucius Priscius Messor.

EDCS-16600270.text_edition: \n Cai Iuli Potentini collyrium crocodem sic Cai Iuli Potentini collyrium stactum crocodes ad claritatem Cai Iuli Potentini diamisus ad veteres cicatrices Aureli Amphionis penicillum ex ovo\n
EDCS-16600270.translation: Caius Iulius Potentinus's crocodile eye salve for clarity; Caius Iulius Potentinus's oil of myrrh salve for old scars; Aurelius Amphion's brush of egg.

EDCS-16600471.text_edition: \n Luci Iuli Senis crocodes ad aspritudines\n
EDCS-16600471.translation: Lucius Iulius Senis's crocodile eye salve for roughness.
EDCS-16600471.summary: This inscription records a medicinal preparation, likely an eye salve, for treating skin roughness, created by Lucius Iulius Senis.

EDCS-16600472.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti Genio Victoriae signiferi ob immunitatem omnem eis concessam a vicanis veteribus consistentibus Castello Mattiacorum Novianius Mogetius Ianuarius Perpetuus Domatius Bodico Seglatius Statutus Atessanius Montanus Senecianius Florentinus Martionius Fortio Cossius Nertinus Nertinius Quintus Germanus Ibliae Isidorius Severus Claudius Firmus Giamonius Adiutor Iustus Censorini\n
EDCS-16600472.translation: In honor of the divine house, for Mars, the Genius, and Victory, the standard-bearer, because of all the immunity granted to them by the old villagers residing at the fort of the Mattiaci: Novianius Mogetius Ianuarius Perpetuus Domatius Bodico Seglatius Statutus Atessanius Montanus Senecianius Florentinus Martionius Fortio Cossius Nertinus Nertinius Quintus Germanus Ibliae Isidorius Severus Claudius Firmus Giamonius Adiutor Iustus Censorini.
EDCS-16600472.summary: This is a collective dedication made by villagers residing at the fort of the Mattiaci to honor the emperor's family and deities, in gratitude for granted immunity, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16700219.text_edition: \n Fortunae Cnaeus Calpurnius Verus praefectus cohortis VII Raetorum equitatae\n
EDCS-16700219.translation: For Fortune. Gnaeus Calpurnius Verus, commander of the Seventh Cohort of Raeti, cavalry.
EDCS-16700219.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Fortuna by Gnaeus Calpurnius Verus, a military officer commanding a cavalry cohort, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16700266.text_edition: \n Ammius Saturninus rusticus de suo peculio histud sic scribsit sic\n

EDCS-16800312.translation: Of Xanthos's brush for inflammation; of Xanthos's oil of myrrh for roughness.

EDCS-20500400.translation: Marcus Valerius Rufus, son of Marcus, of the Stellatina tribe, a veteran of 43 years, for himself and for his brothers out of duty, [dedicated this] to Lucius Valerius Niger, son of Lucius, of the Stellatina tribe, [and to] Lucius Valerius, son of Lucius, of the Stellatina tribe.

EDCS-20601073.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Novanius Augustus in suo <p=R>(osuit) \n
EDCS-20601073.translation: In honor of the divine house, Novanius Augustus placed [this] for Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina on his own property.

EDCS-20601074.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo aram Augustus posuit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-20601074.translation: Augustus erected this altar to Jupiter Best and Greatest, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
