EDCS-29100921.summary: This inscription records a high-quality type of garum and its owner, Claudius Valerius Caldonius Domesticus, who served as an imperial legate.

EDCS-29100924.translation: Laccatum, belonging to C. Aemilius Marci.
EDCS-29100924.summary: This inscription, with many illegible parts, likely records a product named Laccatum and its owner, C. Aemilius Marci.

EDCS-29100925.translation: Excellent old sharp Cordyla, belonging to Caius Crispus Salvius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-29100925.summary: This inscription describes a high-quality type of fish or condiment called Cordyla and lists its owner, Caius Crispus Salvius.

EDCS-29100926.translation: Excellent old Lixitanian Cordyla, belonging to Proculus and Urbicus, their household slave.
EDCS-29100926.summary: This inscription describes a high-quality type of fish or condiment called Cordyla, mentioning its owners Proculus and Urbicus and a household slave.

EDCS-29100927.translation: Old, sharp Cordyla, from the pantry, abundant, 70; L. Uritius Verecundus, 53.
EDCS-29100927.summary: This inscription likely records the sale or measure of goods, possibly wine or oil, with quantities and a vendor's name.

EDCS-29100928.translation: Old, sharp Cordyla, from the pantry, excellent, abundant; L. Uritius Verecundus, domestic, 31, 5, 6.
EDCS-29100928.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of goods, possibly wine or oil, with quality indicators and quantities, associated with L. Uritius Verecundus.

EDCS-29100930.summary: This inscription likely refers to a product named Cordyla, its quantity, and associated with L. Uritius Verecundus.

EDCS-29100931.summary: This inscription mentions two individuals, Proculus and Urbicus, with a numerical value, possibly related to accounts or a transaction.

EDCS-29100935.translation: Cordyla, I carry; 70; M. Faustus; T. B. S. 20; GFCCLX.
EDCS-29100935.summary: This inscription lists a product (Cordyla) and numerical values, possibly indicating a sale or inventory, with names of individuals.

EDCS-29100937.translation: Old Nymph, 80; Domitius; L. G. I. V. Argynus.
EDCS-29100937.summary: This inscription seems to record a product, likely wine or oil (Nymph), its quantity, and the names of individuals, potentially a purchase or ownership record.

EDCS-29100938.translation: Alex? recent, read; Q. Stattius Rufi Hastici et Numidae; L. C. S. CE. B.
EDCS-29100938.summary: This inscription lists names of individuals and possibly a description of a read document or item, with abbreviations that are difficult to decipher.

EDCS-29100939.translation: Garum; 60; Theudas; college of the Fulvii; M. C. F. 10.
EDCS-29100939.summary: This inscription mentions garum (fish sauce), a name (Theudas), a college (likely a guild or association), and numerical values, indicating a transaction or membership record.

EDCS-29100942.summary: This inscription contains a number and a name, 'Veri', possibly related to an account, measurement, or ownership.

EDCS-29100943.summary: This inscription records a numerical value and the name Sextus Magis, likely related to a transaction, measurement, or an inventory.

EDCS-29100949.summary: This inscription likely records an age or duration related to Gaius Aemilius Vastus, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-29100961.summary: This inscription contains fragmented personal names, possibly from a funerary or dedicatory context.

EDCS-29100969.translation: To the god Mercury, Marcus Valerius Silvester [dedicated this].
EDCS-29100969.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury by Marcus Valerius Silvester, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-29601393.translation: Here lie the great [members?] of Ancaratus, who with great strength, kind love in a pious breast.
EDCS-29601393.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a poetic epitaph for Ancaratus, praising his strength and kindness.

EDCS-29601394.translation: Here rests, well remembered, Badegiselus the priest, who lived in peace 50 years happily.
EDCS-29601394.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the peaceful death and lifespan of Badegiselus, a priest.

EDCS-29601395.translation: [---] to [his?] most beloved [---] mother Optovalda, to Forando her son, who was born after the passing of his father.
EDCS-29601395.summary: This epitaph commemorates a son named Forandus, born after his father's death, and mentions his mother Optovalda.

EDCS-29601396.translation: In this tomb rests, well remembered, Gaereholdus, who lived in peace [---] years.
EDCS-29601396.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Gaereholdus and mentions his lifespan in peace.

EDCS-29601397.summary: This is a fragmented epitaph stating that Landulfus rests and is well remembered.

EDCS-29601398.translation: Here lie in marble the remains, the worship of Leutegondes, who was taken [away?] in glory; her soul rests in Christ; father and bones of the most pious [---] founded this monument.
EDCS-29601398.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Leutegondes, whose soul rests in Christ, and was founded by her parents.

EDCS-29601399.translation: In this tomb rests the girl named Munetrudis, who lived 21 years.
EDCS-29601399.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the burial and lifespan of a young girl named Munetrudis.

EDCS-29601400.translation: In this tomb rests, of good memory, Panto, who lived twenty years. Died in peace, happily.
EDCS-29601400.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Panto, a person who lived twenty years and died peacefully.

EDCS-29601401.translation: Here rests, of good memory, Pertrammus Abba, who lived in peace for thirty-four years.
EDCS-29601401.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Pertrammus Abba, who lived for thirty-four years.

EDCS-29601402.translation: Rusticus, faithful boy, who lived for two years, two months, and [3] days, sweet to his parents.
EDCS-29601402.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Rusticus, a young boy who lived for two years and two months, and was dear to his parents.

EDCS-29601404.translation: On this monument rests the daughter of the illustrious patron Macthildis, whose name was Bertichildis, who died. She lived in peace for a short time, twenty years and one month. She lived with her husband Ebregisilus for five years. She was snatched away on Saturday at the eighth hour by divine power, loved by the people, a widow, an orphan, and for the poor she gave alms for her sin. Death takes what it cannot return.
EDCS-29601404.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bertichildis, daughter of Macthildis, who lived twenty years and one month, and was a generous donor to the poor.

EDCS-29601405.translation: Purity, modesty, chastity, which adorn women, excelled you here, Nomidia, a laurel. After death, your merits will not die. Agrippina, your sister, marks this monument with solace.
EDCS-29601405.summary: This is a funerary inscription praising Nomidia for her virtues and her sister Agrippina's memorialization of her.

EDCS-29601406.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for someone named Runaquiu.

EDCS-30100967.text_edition: \n Ianuarius Kalendae Nonae Idus Februarius Kalendae Nonae Idus Martius Kalendae Nonae Idus aequinoctium Aprilis Kalendae Nonae Idus Maius Kalendae Nonae Idus Iunius Kalendae Nonae Idus solstitium VIII Kalendas Iulias Iulius Kalendae Nonae Idus Augustus Kalendae Nonae Idus September Kalendae Nonae Idus aequinoctium October Kalendae Nonae Idus November Kalendae Nonae Idus December Kalendae Nonae Idus bruma Mapilius Mapilianus subpraefectus aquarum dei Borvonis ex aere fracto et excitatoriam fecit ex voto solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-30100967.translation: January: Kalends, Nones, Ides. February: Kalends, Nones, Ides. March: Kalends, Nones, Ides. Equinox. April: Kalends, Nones, Ides. May: Kalends, Nones, Ides. June: Kalends, Nones, Ides. Solstice. The eighth day before the Kalends of July. July: Kalends, Nones, Ides. August: Kalends, Nones, Ides. September: Kalends, Nones, Ides. Equinox. October: Kalends, Nones, Ides. November: Kalends, Nones, Ides. December: Kalends, Nones, Ides. Winter Solstice. Mapilius Mapilianus, subprefect of the waters, made this from bronze and an excitatrium, fulfilling a vow freely and deservedly.
EDCS-30100967.summary: This inscription lists the days of the Roman calendar and records a dedication by Mapilius Mapilianus, subprefect of the waters, for a bronze structure and an excitatrium, likely related to water management, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-30101045.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a dedication or a personal mark, with the initials L. D. P.

EDCS-30101050.summary: This inscription seems to be a personal statement or a dedication, possibly related to Pegasus or a similar concept, with repetitive elements.

EDCS-30101051.summary: This inscription appears to be a personal statement or dedication, similar to EDCS-30101050, with a repeated mention of Pegasus.

EDCS-30101052.summary: This is an inscription recording a payment of one litra by Eisanus of Thessalonica.

EDCS-30101053.summary: This is an inscription recording a payment of one litra by Eunetius of Thessalonica.

EDCS-30101054.summary: This is an inscription recording a payment of one litra by Pausilypus of Thessalonica.

EDCS-30101055.summary: This is an inscription recording a payment of one litra by Zosimus of Thessalonica.

EDCS-30101056.text_edition: \n R IIISIP Serdicae Terent pondo I\n
EDCS-30101056.summary: This inscription records 33 pounds originating from Serdica.

EDCS-30101059.translation: From the auspice, from the storehouse.
EDCS-30101059.summary: This inscription likely records goods or a payment from a storehouse under divine favor (auspice).

EDCS-30101060.translation: From the auspice, from the storehouse.
EDCS-30101060.summary: This inscription likely records goods or a payment from a storehouse under divine favor (auspice).

EDCS-30101061.text_edition: \n Hemeteri AVRS Marcelliani tribuni pondo undecim et uncias duas Pondo XI |(uncias) II Avi trib(uni) pondo XI |(uncias) II\n
EDCS-30101061.translation: Hemeterius, military tribune, 11 pounds and 2 ounces. Avi, military tribune, 11 pounds and 2 ounces.
EDCS-30101061.summary: This inscription records the weight of 11 pounds and 2 ounces, possibly of grain or another commodity, associated with two military tribunes, Hemeterius and Avi.

EDCS-30101063.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly a name associated with a monument or object.

EDCS-30101064.summary: This is a simple dedication or maker's mark by Reginus.

EDCS-30101067.translation: Casuri donated the stone to my Casuri.
EDCS-30101067.summary: This is a dedication of a stone by someone named Casuri to another Casuri, likely a personal or familial dedication.

EDCS-30101070.translation: From the silver mines, one pound weight of refined silver from Nais(s)us.
EDCS-30101070.summary: This inscription records the weight and origin of refined silver, likely an accounting or delivery note from a mining operation.

EDCS-30101089.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Flavio Valerio Constantino Pio nobilissimo Caesari divi Constanti Pii Augusti filio\n
EDCS-30101089.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the Pious, the most noble Caesar, son of the deified Constantius Pius Augustus.
EDCS-30101089.summary: This is a formal imperial titulature, likely part of a larger inscription honoring Emperor Constantine the Great.

EDCS-30101091.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely the beginning of a dedication or ownership statement by Caius Iulius Vasilius.

EDCS-30101093.summary: This inscription identifies a workshop belonging to someone named Crestus, likely related to a craft or trade.

EDCS-30101094.summary: This inscription identifies a workshop belonging to someone named Frontinus, likely related to a craft or trade.

EDCS-30101107.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Ver Verrinus in suo votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-30101107.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Ver Verinus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow on his own property.
EDCS-30101107.summary: This is a votive inscription by Ver Verinus to Jupiter and Juno, indicating the fulfillment of a religious vow.

EDCS-30101108.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription, possibly referring to a consular official, M. C., and the date or period of his consulship.

EDCS-30101109.text_edition: \n Campestribus sacrum Lucius Petronius Luci filius Stellatina Florentinus domo Saldas sic praefectus cohortis IIII Aquitanorum Commodianae equitatae civium Romanorum votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-30101109.translation: Sacred to the Campestres. Lucius Petronius Florentinus, son of Lucius, of the Stellatina tribe, from Saldas, prefect of the Fourth Cohort of Aquitanians, Commodianae, cavalry, of Roman citizens, gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was fitting.
EDCS-30101109.summary: This is a detailed votive inscription by Lucius Petronius Florentinus, a prefect of an auxiliary cavalry cohort, dedicating his fulfilled vow to the Campestres deities.

EDCS-30400058.translation: From the estates of Faustina Augusta, tile work from the larger Domitian kilns.
EDCS-30400058.summary: This inscription records the origin of tile work, specifying it comes from the estates of Faustina Augusta and was produced in the Domitian kilns.

EDCS-31300138.text_edition: \n Lucius fecit ad cantunas novas Lucius fecit\n
EDCS-31300138.translation: Lucius made the new gutters, Lucius made them.
EDCS-31300138.summary: This inscription records Lucius making new gutters, possibly as a dedication or as a record of repair.

EDCS-31300141.translation: Severianus and Gemellus made them both.
EDCS-31300141.summary: This is a dedication or record of construction made by Severianus and Gemellus.

EDCS-31300142.summary: This inscription records Severianus as the maker of molds.

EDCS-31600135.translation: Here rests in peace. John January lived 100 years in this world. Hunudrec made this tomb.
EDCS-31600135.summary: This is a tomb inscription recording the death and lifespan of John January, with Hunudrec as the maker of the monument.

EDCS-31600141.translation: Gibuald died and was buried on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-31600141.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Gibuald and the date of his burial.

EDCS-31700429.translation: Tiles of the Decian Number, from the workshops of Asinius Pollio.
EDCS-31700429.summary: This is a maker's mark on roof tiles, indicating they belong to the Decian estate and were produced by Asinius Pollio's workshops.

EDCS-31800073.translation: Of Caius Claudius Immunis: an ointment for brightness // Of Caius Claudius Immunis: a salve for the attack of dimness, from egg // Of Caius Claudius Immunis: a plaster for roughness and brightness // Of Caius Claudius Immunis: a scented ointment after the attack of dimness, from egg.
EDCS-31800073.summary: This inscription lists various cosmetic or medicinal preparations attributed to Caius Claudius Immunis, likely for sale or use.

EDCS-31800078.translation: Of the partnership of Spurius, son of Titus, and Lucretius.
EDCS-31800078.summary: This inscription records the names of partners in a business or association.

EDCS-32300395.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Connius Covventinus libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-32300395.translation: To Jupiter, Best and Greatest, Connius Covventinus willingly, gladly, and deservedly dedicated this.
EDCS-32300395.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating something to Jupiter, made by Connius Covventinus.

EDCS-32300398.summary: This is a maker's inscription, stating that Ramung created the object.

EDCS-32300404.text_edition: \n Minervae aram Solitus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-32300404.translation: To Minerva, Solitus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-32300404.summary: This is a votive altar dedicated to Minerva by Solitus, who gladly fulfilled his vow, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300406.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae Caius Vettius Connougus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-32300406.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina, Caius Vettius Connougus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-32300406.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus and Juno Regina by Caius Vettius Connougus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300409.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Quintus Volu[---] [---] altar [---]
EDCS-32300409.summary: This is a fragmented inscription to Jupiter Optimus Maximus, likely an altar dedicated by Quintus Volu[---], dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300413.text_edition: \n Deanae Iulius Fraternus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-32300413.translation: To Deana, Iulius Fraternus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-32300413.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Deana (a local form of Diana) by Iulius Fraternus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300414.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Titus Bassienius Agnus votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-32300414.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus, Titus Bassienius Agnus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-32300414.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Titus Bassienius Agnus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300418.translation: To Mercury, Lucius Cassius Manlius, a soldier of the I Adiutrix legion from the century of Aemilius Seranus, gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow as was deserved.
EDCS-32300418.summary: This is a votive inscription to Mercury by Lucius Cassius Manlius, a soldier of the I Adiutrix legion, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300419.translation: To Minerva, Valerius Perimus, architect of the cohort, and Vittalis, a stonecutter, [fulfilled their vow] according to the vow and for themselves and the stonecutters.
EDCS-32300419.summary: This is a votive inscription to Minerva by Valerius Perimus (an architect) and Vittalis (a stonecutter), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300923.translation: Albucius's eyebrow ointment for darkening of the eyebrows; Albucius's eye-salve as a tear-remover from smoky dust; Albucius's balm for all darkening and as a tear-remover; Albucius's wheat [ointment?] for brightness.
EDCS-32300923.summary: This inscription lists several cosmetic products from a maker named Albucius, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32300982.summary: This inscription contains a Greek personal name and a Christian acclamation, likely from late antiquity or the early Christian period.

EDCS-32300984.translation: Septimius Theodolus, corrector of Venice and Istria, tax collector.
EDCS-32300984.summary: This is a career inscription for Septimius Theodolus, who held the administrative position of corrector for Venice and Istria, likely from the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-32300990.summary: This inscription identifies Crispus, a noble Caesar, likely on a coin or official document.

EDCS-32301035.translation: Under the consulship of Apronianus and Paetus, from the potteries of Annius Verus, by Publius, son of Publius, from Salaria.
EDCS-32301035.summary: This inscription records a consignment from the potteries of Annius Verus, dating to the consulship of Apronianus and Paetus.

EDCS-32301036.translation: From the Saenian potteries, by Caelius Julianus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-32301036.summary: This inscription indicates the origin of pottery from the Saenian potteries, attributed to Caelius Julianus.

EDCS-32701087.text_edition: \n Deo Soli Invicto Lucius Fabius Anthimus votum solvit libens laetus merito medicus coh(ortis) IIII Vin(delicorum)\n
EDCS-32701087.translation: Lucius Fabius Anthimus, a doctor of the 4th cohort of the Vindelicans, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to the unconquered god Sol.
EDCS-32701087.summary: This is a votive inscription to the god Sol Invictus by Lucius Fabius Anthimus, a doctor serving in the military.

EDCS-33500469.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to name an individual, possibly Arsacidas, and part of another name ending in -anus.

EDCS-33800040.summary: This inscription is a brief statement possibly referring to a local designation or practice related to the Capratine region.

EDCS-33800042.summary: This is a simple inscription bearing the name Privatus Classicus, likely identifying an individual or a property.

EDCS-33800044.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Tutillus Cai Iuli Tuti filius sacerdos Augustorum statuam ex testamento poni iussit ex HS nummum XXXXVIII |(milibus) Marti Cicollui\n
EDCS-33800044.translation: Gaius Julius Tutillus, son of Gaius Julius Tutillus, ordered a statue to be erected in memory of the Augusti, at his death, costing 48,000 sesterces, to Mars Cicollus.
EDCS-33800044.summary: This inscription records the posthumous erection of a statue costing 48,000 sesterces to Mars Cicollus, commissioned by Gaius Julius Tutillus in his will.

EDCS-33900053.text_edition: \n Deum maxsime sic Atthis Tyranne totumque duodecatheum commendo deabus iniurium fas ut me vindicetis a Priscilla Caranti quae nuberi erravit per Matrem deum vestrae ut vindicate sacra Paterni Priscilla pereat Per Matrem deum dies C cito vindicate numen vestrum magnum a Priscilla quae detegit sacra Priscillam usquam nullam numero nupsit gentem tremente Priscilla quam errante\n
EDCS-33900053.translation: I commend to you, greatest gods, and to the entire council of twelve gods, Atthis the Tyrant, and the goddesses; it is right that you avenge me from Priscilla Caranti, who wrongly married; by your Mother of the Gods, avenge the sacred rites of Paternus; may Priscilla perish; by the Mother of the Gods, quickly for 100 days, avenge your great divinity from Priscilla who has exposed the rites, Priscilla nowhere, she married no one, a trembling nation, Priscilla while erring.
EDCS-33900053.summary: This is a complex and curses-laden inscription imploring the gods to avenge the speaker against Priscilla for revealing sacred rites and a wrongful marriage.

EDCS-33900054.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae deae Fortunae Ceionius Primitius ex voto fecit laetus libens merito\n
EDCS-33900054.translation: In honor of the divine house, Ceionius Primitius made this vow to the goddess Fortuna, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-33900054.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicating a work to the goddess Fortuna in honor of the imperial family by Ceionius Primitius.

EDCS-33900055.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Lucius Vibunnius Vindex beneficiarius consularis votum solvit laetus libens merito Avito et Maximo consulibus\n
EDCS-33900055.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Lucius Vibunnius Vindex, a beneficiarius consularis, gladly, willingly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow, Avitus and Maximus being consuls.
EDCS-33900055.summary: A vow fulfilled to Jupiter by Lucius Vibunnius Vindex during the consulship of Avitus and Maximus.

EDCS-33900056.summary: This inscription likely marks a funerary monument or a boundary stone belonging to the century of Germanus Genialis.

EDCS-33900058.text_edition: \n Pro salute Augustorum senatus populique Romani et exercitus Matri Magnae Claudia Augusti liberta Icmas et Vitulus Caesaris sacerdote Claudio Attico liberto\n
EDCS-33900058.translation: For the safety of the Augusti, the Senate and People of Rome, and the army, Claudia, freedwoman of Augustus, Icmas, and Vitulus, priest of Caesar, and Claudius Atticus, freedman, dedicated this to the Great Mother.
EDCS-33900058.summary: A dedication to the Great Mother for the safety of the emperors and the Roman state, made by Claudia, Icmas, Vitulus, and Claudius Atticus.

EDCS-33900059.text_edition: \n Pro salute Augustorum et senatus populique Romani et exercitus Isidi Pantheae Claudia Augusti liberta Icmas et Vitulus Caesaris sacerdote Claudio Attico liberto\n
EDCS-33900059.translation: For the safety of the Augusti, the Senate and People of Rome, and the army, Claudia, freedwoman of Augustus, Icmas, and Vitulus, priest of Caesar, and Claudius Atticus, freedman, dedicated this to Isis Panthea.
EDCS-33900059.summary: A dedication to Isis Panthea for the safety of the emperors and the Roman state, made by Claudia, Icmas, Vitulus, and Claudius Atticus.

EDCS-33900060.text_edition: \n Insidi! Linus votum solvit libens laetus\n
EDCS-33900060.translation: Linus gladly and joyfully fulfilled his vow to Isis.
EDCS-33900060.summary: A personal vow fulfilled to Isis by Linus.

EDCS-33900061.text_edition: \n Isidi Reginae Grania Quartilla Hastae legati Augusti voto succepto sic sua pecunia libens merito\n
EDCS-33900061.translation: Grania Quartilla, from Hasta, priestess of the Queen Isis, willingly and deservedly fulfilled her vow with her own money.
EDCS-33900061.summary: A vow fulfilled to Isis Regina by Grania Quartilla using her own funds.

EDCS-33900063.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae signum Genii Lucius Vettonius Secundus decuriae III pausariorum de suo libens laetus\n
EDCS-33900063.translation: In honor of the divine house, Lucius Vettonius Secundus of the third cohort of pausarii willingly and joyfully dedicated the statue of the Genius at his own expense.
EDCS-33900063.summary: Lucius Vettonius Secundus dedicated a statue of Genius to honor the imperial family and the cohort of pausarii.

EDCS-33900064.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae decuriae I pausariorum Valerius Liberalis ob immunitatem sibi ab eis concessam de suo donum dedit\n
EDCS-33900064.translation: In honor of the divine house, Valerius Liberalis of the first cohort of pausarii gave this gift at his own expense for the tax exemption granted to him by them.
EDCS-33900064.summary: Valerius Liberalis made a gift to honor the imperial family and the first cohort of pausarii in exchange for a tax exemption.

EDCS-33900065.text_edition: \n Genio pausariorum vexsillationis sic veteranorum Primus Andami servus donum dedit libens laetus\n
EDCS-33900065.translation: Primus, a slave of Andami, gladly and joyfully gave this gift to the Genius of the vexillation of pausarii veterans.
EDCS-33900065.summary: A gift was given to the Genius of the veteran pausarii vexillation by Primus, a slave.

EDCS-33900067.text_edition: \n PRI Prima Aemilia Narcissi agat quidquid conabitur quidquid aget omnia illi inversum sit sic illa nuncquam sic quicquam florescat amentita surgat amentita suas res agat quidquid surget omnia interversum surgat <P=T>rima Narcissi agat comodo! haec carta nuncquam sic florescet \n
EDCS-33900067.translation: May everything Prima Narcissi attempts, everything she does, turn out in reverse; may she never flourish, may she rise confused and attend to her own affairs, may everything she undertakes be reversed; may this paper never flourish.
EDCS-33900067.summary: This is a malediction or curse directed at Prima Narcissi, wishing her ill fortune and failure.

EDCS-33900068.text_edition: \n Avitam novercam dono tibi et Gratum dono tibi EMESMANT\n
EDCS-33900068.translation: My stepmother Avita, I give you as a gift and I give you as a gift, EMESMANT.
EDCS-33900068.summary: This is a personal inscription, likely a dedication or an expression of affection from one person to their stepmother, Avita.

EDCS-33900069.text_edition: \n Bone sancte Atthis sic tyranne adsis advenias Liberali iratus per omnia te rogo domine per tuum Castorem Pollucem per cistas penetrales des et malam mentem malum exitum quandius sic vita vixerit ut omni corpore videat se emori praeter oculos Neque se possit redimere nulla percunia nullaque re neque abs te neque ab ullo deo nisi ut exitum malum hoc praesta rogo te per maiestatem tuam\n
EDCS-33900069.translation: Good, holy Atthis, come to me, Liberalis, like a tyrant, be angry, I beg you, my lord, by your Castor and Pollux, and by the sacred chests, grant me a wicked mind and a wicked end, as long as he lives this life, may he see himself dying in every limb, nor can he redeem himself with any money or by any means, neither from you nor from any god, unless you grant this wicked end, I beg you by your majesty.
EDCS-33900069.summary: This is a curse inscription, likely a private imprecation seeking divine retribution against an unknown enemy.

EDCS-33900072.text_edition: \n Cemeno Attonis TOC Tauri |(denarium) semissem CON TRA TRA\n
EDCS-33900072.translation: Cemenus, son of Atto, for Taurus, half a denarius.
EDCS-33900072.summary: This is a record of a transaction, possibly related to a debt or payment, involving Cemenus, Atto, and Taurus.

EDCS-33900073.text_edition: \n Col pondo I Atilius Servandus pondo IIII |(denarium) I Crispinus Cast |(denarium) semissem\n
EDCS-33900073.translation: Col, weighing 1 pound. Atilius Servandus, weighing 4 pounds. Crispinus, son of Cast, 1/2 denarius.
EDCS-33900073.summary: This inscription records weights and possibly payments, likely from a commercial or administrative context.

EDCS-34100106.text_edition: \n Pondo II pondo IIII Caletus Canti Secun sarca Tauri pondo II\n
EDCS-34100106.translation: Weighing 2 pounds, weighing 4 pounds. Caletus, son of Cantius, for Secundus, 2 pounds of Taurus.
EDCS-34100106.summary: This inscription details quantities of goods, possibly a record of trade or delivery, involving Caletus, Cantius, Secundus, and Taurus.

EDCS-34100107.text_edition: \n |(denari--) Atticus sarca IINI Secund pondo VIII Iulia Apium |(sestertium) I pondo II |(semis)\n
EDCS-34100107.translation: From Atticus, 1 sarcina. Secundus, 8 pounds. Iulia Apium, 1 sestertius, 2 pounds, 1/2.
EDCS-34100107.summary: This inscription lists quantities of goods or payments, possibly related to trade or a financial transaction, involving Atticus, Secundus, and Iulia Apium.

EDCS-34100109.translation: Licinius Successus, 1 and a half denarii for Taurus.
EDCS-34100109.summary: This is a record of a payment or debt, involving Licinius Successus and Taurus.

EDCS-34100110.translation: LVS Launus, son of Surus, sarcina for Castus.
EDCS-34100110.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of goods or a delivery, involving Launus, Surus, and Castus.

EDCS-34100111.text_edition: \n Ruliasus Totti pondo II Tauri |(denarium) semissem\n
EDCS-34100111.translation: Ruliasus, son of Tottus, 2 pounds. Half a denarius for Taurus.
EDCS-34100111.summary: This inscription records quantities and a payment, possibly related to a commercial transaction, involving Ruliasus, Tottus, and Taurus.

EDCS-34100112.text_edition: \n crispa pondo XIII Cantius Saturnini BAN\n
EDCS-34100112.translation: Crispa, 13 pounds. Cantius, son of Saturninus, BAN.
EDCS-34100112.summary: This inscription records a weight and a name, possibly related to a delivery or a financial record.

EDCS-34100116.translation: In a word, I say happy, whoever.
EDCS-34100116.summary: This inscription is a fragment that records a personal sentiment or dedication.

EDCS-34600024.text_edition: \n Caius Saufeius Titi filius Fabia Patavio miles legionis XIIII geminae annorum XXXV stipendiorum XXII hic situs est rtus et \n
EDCS-34600024.translation: Gaius Saufeius, son of Titus, of the Fabia tribe, from Patavium, a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, aged 35, with 22 years of service, is buried here.
EDCS-34600024.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a soldier of the 14th Gemina legion, providing his name, tribal affiliation, origin, age, and service length.

EDCS-34800095.translation: To Priscus, the medicus, the manipularis (?).
EDCS-34800095.summary: This is a dedication to an individual named Priscus, possibly a medicus or a soldier.

EDCS-35000001.translation: Quintus... and Marcus... this inscription... Decia Ra[...]
EDCS-35000001.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record names and possibly a dedication or funerary monument.

EDCS-35200291.translation: Antonia, freedwoman of Lucius, the young [ulla]... Lucius Antonius, freedman of Lucius [3]lus, lived [3] years. Lucius Antonius, freedman of Lucius P[3], made this for himself and his family. Father, this for his children, innocent. Behold, the final...
EDCS-35200291.summary: This is a funerary inscription for members of the Antonii family, likely a tombstone set up by a freedman for himself and his family, with references to his father and children.

EDCS-36100001.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo diis sic deabusque omnibus Fortunae Reduci et Genio loci Nertinius Festus miles legionis VIII Augustae beneficiarius consularis pro salute sua suorumque posuit Idibus Ianuariis Iuliano et Crispino consulibus\n
EDCS-36100001.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, to all the gods and goddesses, to Fortune the Bringer-Back, and to the Genius of the place, Nertinius Festus, a soldier of the 8th Augusta legion, a beneficiarius consularis, erected this for his own safety and that of his family, on the Ides of January, during the consulship of Iulianus and Crispinius.
EDCS-36100001.summary: This is a dedication to various deities by Nertinius Festus, a soldier and beneficiarius consularis, for his well-being and that of his family, dated to 165 CE.

EDCS-36100002.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Genio loci Lucius Augustinius Hibernus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito Aproniano et Bradua consulibus\n
EDCS-36100002.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to the Genius of the place, Lucius Augustinius Hibernus, a beneficiarius consularis, gladly, joyfully, and deservedly fulfilled his vow, during the consulship of Apronianus and Bradua.
EDCS-36100002.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter and the Genius loci by Lucius Augustinius Hibernus, a beneficiarius consularis, dated to 167 CE.

EDCS-36100003.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Caius Iulius Avitus beneficiarius consularis Claudia Cemenelo\n
EDCS-36100003.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Gaius Iulius Avitus, a beneficiarius consularis, [dedicated this] to Claudia Cemenela.
EDCS-36100003.summary: This is a dedication to Jupiter by Gaius Iulius Avitus, a beneficiarius consularis, possibly related to Claudia Cemenela.

EDCS-36100004.text_edition: \n Caius Antenius Mercator beneficarius consularis aquam perduxit sibi et collegiis suis\n
EDCS-36100004.translation: Gaius Antenius Mercator, a beneficiarius consularis, brought water for himself and his guilds.
EDCS-36100004.summary: This inscription records an action by Gaius Antenius Mercator, a beneficiarius consularis, who arranged for the supply of water for himself and his associations.

EDCS-36100006.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Sittonius Maternus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-36100006.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Sittonius Maternus, a beneficiarius consularis, gladly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-36100006.summary: This is a votive dedication to Jupiter by Sittonius Maternus, a beneficiarius consularis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-36100007.text_edition: \n Decimus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-36100007.translation: Decimus, a military officer serving under a consular legate, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-36100007.summary: This is a votive inscription by Decimus, a beneficiarius consularis, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-36100008.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Iulius Marinus beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-36100008.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest, Iulius Marinus, a military officer serving under a consular legate, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-36100008.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulius Marinus, a beneficiarius consularis, dedicating to Jupiter.

EDCS-36100009.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Titus Flavius Victor beneficiarius consularis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n
EDCS-36100009.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno, Titus Flavius Victor, a military officer serving under a consular legate, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-36100009.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titus Flavius Victor, a beneficiarius consularis, dedicating to Jupiter and Juno.

EDCS-36100010.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Iovi Optimo Maximo Iunoni Reginae Minervae Marti Victoriae Genio loci et Geniis praesidium Marcus Aurelius Iulius Super beneficiarius consularis pro se et suis votum solvit libens laetus merito Idibus Iuliis Imperatore domino nostro Antonino IIII et Balbino consulibus\n
EDCS-36100010.translation: In honor of the divine house, to Jupiter Best and Greatest, Juno Regina, Minerva, Mars, Victoria, and the Genius of the place and the Geniuses, Marcus Aurelius Iulius Super, a military officer serving under a consular legate, for himself and his family, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow on the Ides of July, during the consulship of our Emperor Antoninus IIII and Balbinus.
EDCS-36100010.summary: This is a detailed votive inscription by Marcus Aurelius Iulius Super, a beneficiarius consularis, dedicating to multiple deities and the imperial family under specific consuls.

EDCS-36100026.summary: A fragmentary inscription likely dedicating to Jupiter, possibly by a person named -inus Titu[---].

EDCS-36100028.translation: [---] his images, Caius / [---]ceptus and / [---]ecundinus / [---]a Suarica / [---]isia the mother / placed [in fulfillment of a vow].
EDCS-36100028.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription mentioning multiple individuals and possibly a vow.

EDCS-36100049.translation: Here rests in peace Daniulfus, dear to his parents, who lived in this world for 65 years. He died in peace. He deserved to have a tomb in the portico of Saint Peter. His burial.
EDCS-36100049.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Daniulfus.

EDCS-36100050.translation: Here rests in peace Santa, a notary, who extended kindness to many. She deserved honor. She had a tomb in the portico of the saints. She lived in this world for 40 years. She died in peace on the 10th day before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-36100050.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription recording the death of Santa, a notary, and her burial.

EDCS-36100051.translation: Here rests in peace Austroaldus, who lived in this world for 30 years. Under God / purchased (?)
EDCS-36100051.summary: This is a fragmentary early Christian funerary inscription recording the life and possible purchase of burial for Austroaldus.

EDCS-36100052.translation: [Here] rests in peace Adelbertus, dear to his parents, who lived in this world for 30 years. His burial, which was made in the month of May on the twelfth day.
EDCS-36100052.summary: This is an early Christian funerary inscription recording the death and burial of Adelbertus in May.

EDCS-36100053.translation: Here may rest Aunebredus in peace. He lived 35 years and 5 days.
EDCS-36100053.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aunebredus, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36100054.translation: Here may Ermelenus rest in peace. He lived 200 years.
EDCS-36100054.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Ermelenus, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36100055.translation: Here may Berctefredus the youth rest in peace. He lived in the world for 2 years. He departed on the Kalends of April.
EDCS-36100055.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan and date of departure of Berctefredus, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36100056.translation: Here may Erdemulis, dear to his parents, rest in peace. He lived for 30 years in the world. His deposition was in September.
EDCS-36100056.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Erdemulis and the month of his deposition, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36100057.translation: May the innocent Maxixus, dear to his parents, rest in peace. He died in peace. He lived for 3 years and 2 months.
EDCS-36100057.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Maxixus, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36100060.translation: Here is laid Auricula, wife of Innocentius. She died in peace. This occurred in the month of October, seven days.
EDCS-36100060.summary: A funerary inscription recording the death date of Auricula, wife of Innocentius, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36100062.translation: Here may Aisoena rest in peace. She lived 50 years.
EDCS-36100062.summary: A funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Aisoena, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36200554.summary: A fragmentary inscription with names and letters, likely funerary, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36200564.text_edition: \n Numisiae Ferocillae coniugi incomparabili pietate quae vixit nnos XXVII menses IIII dies XXVII Aurelius Philumenus maritus Ferocilla filia VI fecerunt\n
EDCS-36200564.translation: To Numisia Ferocilla, incomparable wife, who lived 27 years, 4 months, 27 days. Aurelius Philumenus her husband and Ferocilla her daughter made this.
EDCS-36200564.summary: A funerary epitaph for Numisia Ferocilla, dedicated by her husband and daughter, dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36200567.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription (Dis Manibus), dated to the Roman period.

EDCS-36300059.translation: Lucius Laenas, freedman of Lucius, is buried here.
EDCS-36300059.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Laenas, a freedman, indicating his burial location.

EDCS-36300074.translation: Here rests in peace. Aunobertus lived for 13 years and died in peace on the Ides of November.
EDCS-36300074.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aunobertus, recording his age at death and the date of his passing.

EDCS-36300076.summary: This fragmentary inscription likely records the name and age of a deceased individual, possibly related to a 'Varus'.

EDCS-36400016.text_edition: \n Signis cohortis I <A=E>quitanorum Bironius evincus beneficiarius \n
EDCS-36400016.translation: Bironius, beneficiarius of the standards of the I Equitanorum cohort, conquered.
EDCS-36400016.summary: This inscription likely refers to a military achievement or status of Bironius within the I Equitanorum cohort.

EDCS-36400018.text_edition: \n Rogo te domina Mater Magna ut tu me vindices de bonis Flori coniugis mei qui me fraudavit Ulattius Severus quemadmodum hoc ego averse scribo sic illi Omnia quidquid agit quidquid aginat omnia illi aversa fiant ut sal et aqua illi eveniat quidquid mi abstulit de bonis Flori coniugis mei rogo te domina Mater Magna ut tu de eo me vindices\n
EDCS-36400018.translation: I beg you, Mistress Mater Magna, that you defend me concerning the property of Florus, my husband, who defrauded me. Ulattius Severus, just as I write this to him averted, may all that he does, all that he undertakes, turn out averted for him, may it happen to him as salt and water (i.e., misfortune) for whatever he took from the property of Florus, my husband. I beg you, Mistress Mater Magna, that you defend me concerning him.
EDCS-36400018.summary: This is a curse inscription addressed to the goddess Mater Magna, requesting divine retribution against Ulattius Severus for defrauding the writer concerning her husband Florus's property.

EDCS-36400021.text_edition: \n Tiberius Claudius Adiutor in megaro eum rogo te Mater Magna megaro tuo recipias et Attis domine te precor ut hunc hostiam acceptum habiatis sic et quit sic aget aginat sal et aqua illi fiat ita tu facias domina it sic quid cor eoconora sic caedat Devotum defictum sic illum menbra sic medullas AA nullum aliud sit Attis Mater Magna\n
EDCS-36400021.translation: Tiberius Claudius Adiutor, I beg you, Mater Magna, to receive me into your megaron (sanctuary/temple) and Attis, my lady. May you accept this offering. Just as he does, may it happen to him as salt and water (i.e., misfortune). May you do this, my lady. And thus may he be cut down (spiritually/physically), may his limbs, his marrow, be nothing else. Attis, Mater Magna.
EDCS-36400021.summary: This is a vow or curse inscription to Mater Magna and Attis, invoking divine punishment upon someone named Tiberius Claudius Adiutor, requesting they be received into a sanctuary and face misfortune.

EDCS-36400038.translation: Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 2nd time, granted citizenship and the right of marriage with the wives whom they then had (or would later have if single) to those who served in the fleet praetorian at Misenum, which is under Lucius Iulius Fronton, having completed twenty-six years of service and been honorably discharged, whose names are inscribed below, to them, their children, and their descendants. Recorded and confirmed from a bronze tablet which is fixed in Rome on the wall behind the temple of the deified Augustus near the Minerva. Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, son of the deified Trajan the Parthian, grandson of the deified Nerva, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 2nd time (!), consul for the 2nd time (!), to those who served in the fleet praetorian at Misenum, which is under Lucius Iulius Fronton, having completed twenty-six years of service and been honorably discharged, whose names are inscribed below, granted citizenship and the right of marriage with the wives whom they then had (or would later have if single) to them, their children, and their descendants. Tiberius Iulius Urbanus, Tiberius Claudius Menander, Quintus Fabius [?], Publius Vigellius Priscus, Aulus Cascellius Proculus, Publius Atinius Crescens, Lucius Pullius Verecundus.
EDCS-36400038.summary: This is an imperial rescript from Emperor Hadrian granting citizenship and marriage rights to honorably discharged veterans of the Misenum fleet, dated to the consulship of Gaius Herennius Capella and Lucius Coelius Rufus, with a list of names appended.

EDCS-36400068.summary: This is a maker's signature on a monument or artifact, identifying Marcellus as the creator.

EDCS-36400069.summary: This is a maker's signature on a monument or artifact, identifying Suadius Iunior as the creator.

EDCS-36400126.translation: Achifracius rests here in peace. He lived for 5 years.
EDCS-36400126.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Achifracius, recording his name, burial, and age at death.

EDCS-36500046.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo et Iunoni Reginae vicani Salutares Lucius Valerius Fronto Lucius Helvius ongio Lucius Iuventius Ocellio Titus Helvius Fuscus Caius Iulius Crescens Caesius Celer Marcus Mucius Septimus Marcus Flavius Philetus Lucius MagiLli(us) Victor Marcus Clodius Optatus Quintus Fabricius Threptus Quintus Lupinius Festus Lucius Valerius I Donius Ianuarius Iunius Marcus SuII Marcus SuTINQIIXTX Ixius AtIXTO Publius Iulius Saturninus NOLIIONANILOII ETAECICIIVI Quintus nn Severus Tatius MuI-v Lucius Helvius II Sextus Aimilius sic Verus Domitius IA Lucius O Lucius IuLius Stabius I Lucius Iscensius Iustio VeIatun AVIIAI A Marcus AIAP ISC Victoria Augusti\n
EDCS-36500046.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest and to Juno Regina, the residents of the Salutares district, Lucius Valerius Fronto, Lucius Helvius Ongio, Lucius Iuventius Ocellio, Titus Helvius Fuscus, Caius Iulius Crescens, Caesius Celer, Marcus Mucius Septimus, Marcus Flavius Philetus, Lucius Magillius Victor, Marcus Clodius Optatus, Quintus Fabricius Threptus, Quintus Lupinius Festus, Lucius Valerius Donius Ianuarius, Iunius Marcus, Lucius Ixius, Publius Iulius Saturninus, Noliionaniloii, Etaeciciuvi Quintus, Severus Tatius, Lucius Helvius, Sextus Aimilius, Verus Domitius, Lucius, Lucius Iulius Stabius, Lucius Iscensius Iustius, Veiatunus, Marcus, Victoria Augusti, dedicate this.
EDCS-36500046.summary: This is a dedication by residents of the Salutares district to Jupiter and Juno, listing numerous names, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-36700002.summary: This is a memorial inscription for Drusus Germanicus, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-37700254.text_edition: \n Titus Silius Lucusta Mercurio et Apollini votum solvit libens merito\n
EDCS-37700254.translation: Titus Silius Lucusta willingly and deservedly paid his vow to Mercury and Apollo.
EDCS-37700254.summary: This is a votive inscription by Titus Silius Lucusta dedicating a payment to Mercury and Apollo, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38000284.text_edition: \n Quintum in hac tabula depono aversum se suisque rationibus vitaeque male consummantem ita uti galli bellonarive absciderunt concideruntve se sic illi abscissa sit fides fama faculitas nec illi in numero hominum sunt neque ille sit quomodi sic et ille mihi fraudem fecit sic illi sancta Mater Magna et relegisti cuncta ita uti arbor siccabit se in sancto sic et illi siccet fama fides fortuna faculitas tibi commendo Attihi sic d<o>mine ut me vindices ab eo ut intra annum vertentem exitum illius vilem malum\n
EDCS-38000284.translation: I place Quintus on this tablet, estranged from his affairs, his resources, and his life, which he has badly wasted, just as galli or bellonae have cut themselves off or fallen, so may his trust, reputation, ability, and livelihood be cut off; may he not be counted among men, nor may he be like him, just as he defrauded me, so may the Holy Mother Magna and your careful consideration, as a tree dries up in the sacred place, so may his reputation, trust, fortune, and ability dry up. I commend him to you, my lord, that you may vindicate me against him, so that within the coming year his end may be worthless and bad.
EDCS-38000284.summary: This is a curse tablet invoking the Magna Mater to bring misfortune upon Quintus for defrauding the author, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38000285.text_edition: \n Mando et rogo religione ut mandata exagatis Publium Cutium et Piperionem et Placida et Sacra filia eius sic illorum membra liquescant quatmodum sic hoc plumbum liquescet ut eorum exsitum sic sit\n
EDCS-38000285.translation: I command and implore you by religious duty that you carry out the instructions concerning Publius Cutius and Piperio and Placidus and his daughter Sacra, that their bodies may dissolve just as this lead will dissolve, so that their end may be thus.
EDCS-38000285.summary: This is a curse tablet invoking religious duty to cause the dissolution of Publius Cutius, Piperio, Placidus, and Sacra, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38000286.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Trutmo, son of Florus Clitmo, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38000287.summary: This inscription likely refers to a military unit or a land division identified by the name Severus Popai, possibly from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38300454.summary: This inscription probably refers to land division or a measurement related to Silvanus, with 'XXX s(emis)' indicating thirty and a half units, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38300476.summary: This fragmentary inscription mentions a 'Petroni' and possibly 'Martis' (Mars), suggesting a dedication or reference to a person and a deity, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-38300591.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that mentions 'Va/tia', possibly part of a name or place, its context and date are uncertain.

EDCS-38300798.summary: This is a personal name inscription, likely a funerary marker or dedication, for Virtirus, son of Veriugus.

EDCS-38301302.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly graffiti, indicating someone named [...]inus is drinking.

EDCS-38301304.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription containing personal names, likely part of a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-38301523.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to record the name of a person, Minuti, and possibly another name or possessive, Pixto[...].

EDCS-38301652.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that mentions Augustus and a goddess, possibly indicating a dedication.

EDCS-38700260.text_edition: \n Fibulam Gnatae qui involavit aut qui melior est animi consci<u=O>(s) ut illum aut illam aversum faciant dii sicut hoc est aversum et qui res ill<i=AE>us sustulit \n
EDCS-38700260.translation: May the gods make the fibula of Gnata, whoever stole it or whoever has a clearer conscience, turn away from him or her, just as this is turned away, and whoever took his things.
EDCS-38700260.summary: This inscription invokes divine punishment on anyone who stole a fibula belonging to Gnata or had malicious intent, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-38700304.text_edition: \n Marius nnm sic suus sic et eum qui exin conciliavit aequa a vita\n
EDCS-38700304.translation: Marius, thus his own, thus also the one who reconciled him fairly from life.
EDCS-38700304.summary: This inscription seems to be a personal statement or epitaph for Marius, referencing reconciliation and life.

EDCS-38700306.summary: This is a very brief inscription possibly recording the handover or dedication of an object or person named Hermēs.

EDCS-38900292.text_edition: \n in dies XXX et quacumque ducitur ibi sortem et usuras probas recte dari stipulatus est Sextus Carisius Maximus quo spopondit Lucius Haterius Marius aes reddam tibi aut procuratori aut heredi tuo actum Vindonissae hibernis legionis XI VIII Kalendas Februarias Imperatore Domitiano Vespasiani filio Augusto Germanico XV Marco Cocceio Nerva II consulibus Caius Catilius Scaeva signifer centuria Orgi Lucius Carisius Sanctus centuria Gavini Caius Petronius Rutilianus centuria S Tauri Caius Gabinius Duccenus custos armorum centuria Tauri Titus Gavius Supero equiti alaes sic I Flavies \n
EDCS-38900292.translation: For 30 days, and wherever it is led, Sextus Carisius Maximus stipulated that the proper share and interest be given, for which Lucius Haterius Marius promised 'I will return the money to you or your procurator or heir.' Acted at Vindonissa in the winter quarters of the legion XI, on the 8th day before the Kalends of February, when Emperor Domitian Vespasian's son Augustus Germanicus was consul for the 15th time and Marcus Cocceius Nerva was consul for the 2nd time. Gaius Catilius Scaeva, standard-bearer of the century of Orgi. Lucius Carisius Sanctus, of the century of Gavini. Gaius Petronius Rutilianus, of the century of S. Tauri. Gaius Gabinius Duccenus, keeper of arms, of the century of Tauri. Titus Gavius Supero, to a cavalryman of the ala I Flavia.
EDCS-38900292.summary: This is a detailed legal and military record from Vindonissa dated to 81 AD, documenting a financial agreement and listing military personnel and units.

EDCS-44500196.text_edition: \n Mando et rogo liberta Cerialis ut ea extra IPIVTI faciatis ut se plangat velit se quatmodum sic archigalli se COLI sibi settas faciatis ita menses duos ut eorum ixsitum sic audiam diliquescant quatmmodi sic hoc liquescet \n

EDCS-46400786.text_edition: \n Humanum quis sustulit Verionis palliolum sive res illius qui illius minus fecit ut illius mentes memorias deiectas sive mulierem sive eas cuius Verionis res minus fecit ut illius manus caput pedes vermes cancer vermitudo interet membra medullas illius interet\n
EDCS-46400786.translation: Who has taken away the cloak or property of Verionis, so that his mind's memories are diminished, or the woman, or she to whom Verionis's property has been diminished, so that his hands, head, feet, worms, cancer, canker, her limbs, her marrow, are destroyed.

EDCS-46600122.text_edition: \n In honorem domus divinae Marti Loucetio et Victoriae Nemetonae Marcus Aurelius Senillus Severus beneficiarius legati urnam cum pedibus et phiala ex voto posuit libens laetus merito Grato et Seleuco consulibus X Kalendas Maias\n
EDCS-46600122.translation: In honor of the divine house, Marcus Aurelius Senillus Severus, a beneficiary of the legate, willingly, joyfully, and deservedly set up this urn with feet and a phiale to Mars Loucetius and to Victoria Nemetona, under the consulship of Gratus and Seleucus, ten days before the Kalends of May.
EDCS-46600122.summary: This is a dedication to Mars and Victoria by Marcus Aurelius Senillus Severus, likely a military official, around the late 2nd or 3rd century CE, indicated by the consuls and dedication to the imperial family.

EDCS-46600123.translation: Here rests in peace Aigttheus, who lived for 21 years. Aso and Alhi set up this monument out of affection.

EDCS-46600124.text_edition: \n Matri Deum Magnae et viribus Patrici Cybelici Pacatia Pacata filia Pacati Pacatini decurionis civitatis Treverorum consummata per Servandium Maternum sacerdotem deum Matris III Idum Novembrium Perpetuo et Corneliano consulibus\n
EDCS-46600124.translation: To the Great Mother of the Gods and the powers of Patricius Cybelius, Pacatia Pacata, daughter of Pacatus Pacatinus, a decurion of the city of the Treveri, completed this, through Servandius Maternus, priest of the Mother of the Gods, on the third day before the Ides of November, during the consulship of Perpetuus and Cornelius.
EDCS-46600124.summary: This is a dedication to the Mother Goddess Cybele by Pacatia Pacata, daughter of a Treveran decurion, through her priest Servandius Maternus, dated to November 11, 197 CE.

EDCS-46600125.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo Mes Iblionis votum solvit libens laetus merito\n

EDCS-59500319.text_edition: \n Mater Magna te rogo per tua sacra et numen tuum Gemella fibulas meas qualis sustulit sic et illam REQVIS adsecet ut nusquam sana sit quomodo galli se secarunt sic eam velis nec se secet sic uti planctum habeat quomodo et sacrorum deposierunt in sancto sic et tuam vitam valetudinem Gemella neque hostiis neque auro neque argento rediimire possis a Matre deum nisi ut exitum tuum populus spectet Verecundam et Paternam sic illam tibi commendo Mater deum magna rem illorum in AECRVMO DEO VIS quale rogo consummentur quomodo et res meas viresque fraudarunt nec se possint redimere nec hosteis lanatis Nec plumibis nec auro nec argento redimere a numine tuo nisi ut illas vorent canes vermes adque alia portenta exitum quarum populus spectet tamquam quae C FORRO L auderes commendo duas tam quam ius C aversso sic scriptis istas AE RISS ADRICIS S LON a illas si illas cistas caecas aureas FECRA EILOAS OVEIS mancas A\n
EDCS-59500319.translation: Great Mother, I beg you through your sacred rites and your divinity that Gemella's fibulae, as she has removed them, so may she be beset by the quest for them, that she may never be well, just as the Galli cut themselves, may you wish that she not cut herself, so that she may have mourning, just as they placed their sacred offerings in the holy place, so too your life and health Gemella, neither with sacrifices nor with gold nor with silver may you be redeemed, except that the people may witness your end. Verecunda and Paternus, I commend her to you like their offering in a sacred vessel may they be consumed, just as my possessions and strength have defrauded them, nor may they be able to redeem themselves, nor with fleeced, nor with leaden, nor with gold, nor with silver may they be redeemed from your divinity, except that dogs and worms and other portents may devour them, the end of which the people may witness, just as I commend two people who dared C FORRO L, like your C aversso, so these writings AE RISS ADRICIS S LON, and those, if those chests golden blind FECRA EILOAS OVEIS lame A.
EDCS-59500319.summary: This is a long and complex curse inscription, likely from the Roman Imperial period, invoking the Great Mother goddess against an individual named Gemella, and also referring to others and their possessions.

EDCS-64100411.text_edition: \n Inimicos Sexti ut hic non possint contra Sexti facundiam nec agere O quicquam possint ut sic vani et muti quomodi et illi qui in hoc monumento iacent In illo tum loqui Valentinus et tuto et Ripanus et Le et Iuventinum et Lucius et Carum et Frontonem alii adversarii sint vani et muti quomodi sic ista garrula avis\n
EDCS-64100411.translation: May Sextus' enemies not be able to act against Sextus' eloquence here, nor be able to do anything, so that they are vain and mute, just like those who lie in this tomb, unable to speak in that place. Valentinus and Tuto and Ripanus and Le and Iuventinum and Lucius and Carus and Fronto, may other adversaries be vain and mute, just like this chattering bird.
EDCS-64100411.summary: This is a funerary inscription containing a curse against enemies, invoking silence and ineffectiveness upon them, attributed to Valentinus and others.
